subject: ACC
title: Introduction to Accounting I
description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part I.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ACC
title: Introduction to Accounting II
description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part II.

subject: ACC
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
description: Accounting process and the application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of cash, receivables, inventories, property plant and equipment, depreciation and depletion, intangibles, and current liabilities.
prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210 , or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- or better )

subject: ACC
title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
description: Application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of long-term liabilities, investments, contributed capital, retained earnings, accounting changes and errors, income recognition, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and statement of cash flows.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Internship
description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Term paper and meetings with faculty advisor required.

subject: ACC
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research of a special area in major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: ACC
title: Federal Individual Income Taxation
description: Examines federal income tax concepts, such as gross income, exclusions, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits, especially for sole proprietors. Introduces taxation of property transactions. Development of professional writing skills is integral to this course.
prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210 , or BUS 624 (with a minimum grade of C- or better).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- or better )

subject: ACC
title: Taxation of Business Entities
description: A survey of the general concepts, rules, and practices involved in the taxation of sole-proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, and subchapter S corporations.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Information Systems
description: Accounting systems analysis, control and design in manual and computerized environments. Knowledge and skills of information technology for auditing AIS systems. Hands-on experience with microcomputers and a computerized accounting system.
prereq_raw: ACC 323 (with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 (with C or better).

children.text: ( with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 ( with C or better)

subject: ACC
title: Law for the Accountant
description: Intensive study of areas of law of importance to accountants. Particular attention is given to principles of law relating to contracts, sales, commercial paper, secured transactions, property, legal entities, agency, securities, and accountant’s legal liability.

subject: ACC
title: Advanced Financial Accounting
description: Accounting topics relating to consolidation requirements and introduction to the fundamentals of fund accounting, including the general fund, restricted funds, debt service funds, enterprise funds, general long-term account group, general fixed assets accounting group, and accounting entries for encumbrances.

subject: ACC
title: Special Topics in Accounting
description: Addresses current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

subject: ACC
title: Auditing
description: Auditing concepts including standards, objectives and ethics for external auditors. Emphasis on reporting standards, internal control, evidence, statistical sampling, IT audits and assurance. Development of professional writing skills is an integral part of this course.
prereq_raw: ACC 323 and ACC 409 , both with C- or better.

subject: ACC
title: Forensic Accounting
description: Theoretical and real life aspects of forensic accounting. Includes discussions of the legal environment, types of forensic engagements such as, lost earnings, business valuations, fraud, and real world forensic cases.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ACC
title: (Alpha) Accounting Capstone
description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems.
prereq_raw: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Capstone: Managerial Accounting-Tax-Ethics
description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems.
prereq_raw: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Capstone: Financial Accounting-Auditing-Accounting Information Systems
description: Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Lectures, discussions, case analysis. (B) managerial-tax-ethics; emphasis on instruction in writing; (C) financial-auditing-accounting information systems.
prereq_raw: ACC 401 (or concurrent) and ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (B); ACC 418 (or concurrent) for (C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-Audit and Attestation
description: Auditing and Attestation (AUD) section covers the entire auditing process, including auditing procedures, generally accepted auditing standards, standards related to attest engagements, and the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Business Environment and Concepts
description: The Business Environment and Concepts (BEC) section focuses on business concepts and the significance of a CPA’s professional duties and responsibilities within the larger context of the business environment.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Financial Accounting and Reporting
description: The (FAR) section focuses on U.S. GAAP, including concepts and standards for financial statements, typical items in financial statements, specific types of transactions and events, accounting and reporting for governmental and other entities.

subject: ACC
title: CPA Review-The Regulation
description: The Regulation section focuses on federal taxation, especially taxation of business entities; individuals, and property taxation, but also tests on business law, business ethics, and professional and legal responsibilities.

subject: ACC
title: International Corporate Governance
description: Understanding of complex and critical issues of international corporate governance, financial reporting, and ethical conduct. Includes corporate governance in the U.S., major European markets, and Asia. Emphasis on internal and external stakeholders, regulators, and gatekeepers.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Theory and Development
description: History and theoretical background of accounting standards. Including accounting theories, formulating and testing theories; scientific, pragmatic, syntactic and semantic theories; normative and positive theories. Literature supportive and critical of accounting theories and standards.
prereq_raw: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Information and Assurance and Analytics
description: Focus on auditing processes, standards, and guidance specific to IT risks. Exposure to advanced IT audit software and its practical application and real world IT audit issues.
prereq_raw: ACC 418 with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Global Accounting
description: Theory and fundamental causes of international variations in accounting. Special emphasis on problems such variations create for financial reporting, control, and decision-making within multinational business enterprises.
prereq_raw: ACC 323 with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Accounting and Tax Research
description: In-depth examination of tax and accounting research, IRC, and SEC procedures. Extensive practice in issue identification, reading and analyzing primary authority, and communicating results. Business Administration students only.
prereq_raw: ACC 460E (or concurrent) with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Tax of Partners/Partnerships
description: Examines advanced topics in federal taxation of partners and partnerships regarding the contribution, operation, and distribution from partnerships and transfers of partnership interests.
prereq_raw: ACC 407 with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Advanced Public Sector Accounting
description: Provides the tools necessary for understanding the principles of fiscal accountability and reporting in governmental and not-for-profit organizations.
prereq_raw: ACC 415 with C- or better, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Estate and Gift Taxation and Planning
description: Examines estate and gift tax provisions and basic estate planning techniques to save taxes and avoid probate. Overviews generation-skipping transfer taxes and income taxes on estates and trusts.
prereq_raw: ACC 401 with C- or better, or consent.

children.text: with C- or better, or consent

subject: ACC
title: Multijurisdictional Taxation
description: Examines international, state, and local tax issues. Topics include U.S. International taxation of in- and out-bound transactions, sourcing of income and deductions and nexus.

subject: ACC
title: Financial Statements Analysis
description: Analyses of a firm’s profitability, liquidity, and solvency using ratios and common size financial statements. Students are expected to find strengths and weaknesses of the firm based on their analysis.

subject: ACC
title: Data Analytics for Accountants
description: Introduction to visual analytics. Tableau and Power BI for Excel. Introduction to data processing and blending, data visualization and other visualization techniques. Introduction to PowerQuery, PowerPivot, PowerView, and PowerMap.

subject: ACC
title: Analysis and Decision-Making
description: Integrates learning through analysis and communication of comprehensive business problems. Stresses research, critical thinking, and analytical and communication skills applied to contemporary accounting and tax issues.
prereq_raw: ACC 625 with C- or better (or concurrent), no waiver.

children.text: with C- or better (or concurrent) , no waiver

subject: ACC
title: Current Topics in Accounting
description: Concentration on current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

subject: ACC
title: Accounting Internship
description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Necessary evaluation reports and meetings with faculty advisor required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: Thesis Research
description: Required for Plan A candidates only; six credit hours required, one must be taken during semester that degree is being awarded.
prereq_raw: MAcc student and School of Accountancy Director approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ACC majors only.

subject: ACC
title: Financial Accounting Research
description: Provides an overview of financial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Managerial Accounting Research
description: Provides an overview of managerial accounting research. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Behavioral Accounting
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in behavioral accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Accounting Information Systems
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in accounting information systems topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc. PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: ACC
title: Research in Auditing and International Accounting
description: Provides an overview of accounting research in Auditing and International Accounting topics. Specific research studies are examined as to their theoretical basis, design, implications, methodology, relevance, etc.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: ACC
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in an area of accounting under the direction of faculty member(s).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD students in Business Administration only.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies
description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: America and the World
description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Institutions and Movements
description: Emergence and transformation of laws, ideologies, institutions, and social movements from the 17th-21st centuries. Emphasis on relationships among structures of power, representational practices, belief systems, and social action. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
description: Literature and modern media; visual and performing arts; material culture and architecture; foodways and ritual as meaning-making processes that have shaped the diverse identities, spaces, and communities of the Americas. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Domestic Issues
description: Current debates in the U.S. over individual rights and nationalism; civil rights, citizenship, and sovereignty; sexuality, law, and religion; economic, racial, and gender equality; public health and environmental justice. Writing emphasis, interdisciplinary perspectives.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Global Issues
description: Interdisciplinary and transnational perspectives on global issues including international law and diplomacy; war, diaspora, and refugees; economic underdevelopment and environmental racism; globalization, race, and the feminization of poverty. Writing emphasis.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: Histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples in U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, Samoans. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi and its relationship to other Indigenous nations.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: Histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of Indigenous peoples in U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, Samoans. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi and its relationship to other Indigenous nations.

subject: AMST
title: Art and Social Change
description: Emphasis on students’ oral and written responses to literary, visual, and performing arts, including poetry, visual art, music, film, and dance, with particular attention to the influence of art upon social and political movements.

subject: AMST
title: Hip-Hop and American Culture
description: Survey tracing hip-hop from its Afro-Carribean musical beginnings to contemporary adaptations and interpretations. Students will analyze various materials and will pay attention to the relationships between hip-hop and contemporary social forms.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Justice and Asian America: Social Movements and the Law in American History
description: Examination of demands for and the changing nature of justice, historical and contemporary, through court cases, legislation, presidential orders, and social movements that address legal, social, and political definitions of Asian America. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: History, Culture, Lifestyles
description: Explores experiences of Japanese Americans in Hawaiʻi and the U.S.: historical and cultural heritage, biographical portraits, changing family ties, ethnic lifeways, gender relations, local identity, and the future of island living. Emphasis: oral communication skills.

subject: AMST
title: African Americans: Issues, Culture, History
description: Traces the history and culture of African Americans and outlines contemporary issues. Topics include: slavery and racism, community formation and resistance, cultural expression, African American diversity, civil rights, gender and class relations.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

subject: AMST
title: American Music and Culture
description: Analysis of a variety of American musical genres and histories through focused writing assignments (record and performance reviews, personal narratives, interviews, research proposals, research papers).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: second year standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. Emphasis on ethics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: America, Hawaiʻi and World War II
description: Examines WWII as a watershed in American and Hawaiʻi history and culture. Topics include: Pearl Harbor, Japanese American internment, sex and racial tensions, Anti-Semitism and the Holocaust, and the dawn of the Atomic Age.

subject: AMST
title: American Environments: Survey
description: Survey of social, political, and cultural relations in diverse, contemporary American environments, including: island societies, urban centers, suburbs, Indian reservations, farming communities, and national parks. Special emphasis on contemporary environmental issues in Hawaiʻi.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
description: Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or higher standing, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: Digital America: Online Communities and Virtual Worlds
description: Seminar on the impact of the digital revolution and virtual communities on American culture and society, with an emphasis on questions of identity and participatory democracy. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: one DH, DA, or DL course, sophomore standing, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Religions in America
description: Examination of American religious traditions, both historical and contemporary, with an emphasis on the principles of religious liberty, non-establishment, and pluralism. Emphasis on writing and ethics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: War and Media
description: Examination of a range of media, including photography, film, print journalism, television, video games, and the internet, as they have shaped popular representations and experiences of war in America from the Civil War through the present.

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship with the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of Reconstruction.

subject: AMST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of AMST 343 - American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century .
prereq_raw: AMST 150 or AMST 201 or AMST 202 or AMST 211 or AMST 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152 ; or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: American Design: An Historical Survey
description: Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Open to all class standings.

subject: AMST
title: Contemporary American Design
description: Investigates design in contemporary American culture. Graphic, industrial, urban, and user-interface design practices are situated within broader social and economic forces. Modes of design practice, production, and consumption studied as reflection of American society today.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Open to all class standings.

subject: AMST
title: Culture and the Arts in America
description: Study of the role of the arts in American society and diverse cultural practices in historical and contemporary contexts.

subject: AMST
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Lands and Waters
description: Examines indigenous practices born of and located in Indigenous places. Analyzes how indigenous knowledge of place informs Indigenous cultural, linguistic, intellectual, and political survivance and sovereignty, and resistance.

subject: AMST
title: American Travel Writing
description: Survey examines the roles that travel writing plays in American identity- and nation-formation, from early colonial history to the present.
prereq_raw: AMST 110 , AMST 150 , AMST 201 , AMST 202 , AMST 211 , or AMST 212 .

subject: AMST
title: American Cinema
description: Introductory history of American cinema from the silent to the digital era, with an emphasis on criticism, genre and style, as well as cultural and sociopolitical context.

subject: AMST
title: American Empire
description: Examines an “American culture of empire” in the context of Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific, exploring ethical issues of settler colonialism and decolonial movements. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing.

subject: AMST
title: Critical Research Methods
description: Overview of methods and methodologies drawn from various fields (including history, politics, literature, art, law and race, Indigenous, gender, and sexuality studies) for conducting interdisciplinary research. Models of writing from AMST faculty; emphasis on writing.

subject: AMST
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Literature and Film
description: Interdisciplinary, comparative course examining native literary texts (novels, short fiction, poetry), films, etc. that address issues of representation and how native peoples actively resist colonial ideology.

subject: AMST
title: Asian American Music Cultures
description: An exploration of how Asian American music making is related to community formation, labor migration, and cultural sensibilities throughout the 20th century.

subject: AMST
title: Japanese Americans: Research Topics
description: Research and thematic seminar on Japanese American culture, issues, and history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: Regionalism: The South
description: Definition of a Southern identity and its relation to the larger U.S. culture, using literary and polemical works of 19th- and 20th-century.

subject: AMST
title: Hawaiʻi’s Multiculturalism
description: A multidisciplinary examination of the dynamics of the Hawaiian Islands’ racial and cultural diversity from the perspectives of historical trends, social processes, and contemporary political, social, and economic issues as they impact interracial relations.

subject: AMST
title: American Ideas of Nature
description: The natural world in American thought from Native Americans to modern ecologists.

subject: AMST
title: History of American Architecture
description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

subject: AMST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: AMST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

subject: AMST
title: Islands, Empires, and the Arts
description: Colonialism, neocolonialism, and cultures of resistance in the Caribbean and its North American diaspora through literature, film, and the arts. Focus on political dissent; nation building; historical memory; construction of gender, race. Writing emphasis. Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: Politics in Hawaiʻi
description: Discussion of modern politics against the background of recent history and major contemporary issues.

subject: AMST
title: History of Crime and Punishment
description: History of American crime and punishment from 18th century to the present. Topics: changing crime patterns, evolving punishment methods, penal reform movements, convict resistance, growth of prison industrial complex, racism, class, and gender.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 381 , or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
prereq_raw: one of AMST 310 , AMST 316 , AMST 318 , AMST 373 , AMST 455 , POLS 339 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 ; or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

subject: AMST
title: Social Movements
description: Examination of mass mobilization in U.S. history from the Revolution forward, including abolitionism, feminism, civil rights, labor, and more. Concludes with analysis of various community organizing efforts today.

subject: AMST
title: Racism, American Culture and Film/ Media
description: An exploration of the critique of racial ideologies in American film. The course also examines how aggrieved communities develop cultural sensibilities, aesthetic choices and politicized identities through film, video and media work.

subject: AMST
title: Gender in Action Cinema
description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: AMST
title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence: Studies in American Melodrama
description: Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity.

subject: AMST
title: Popular Culture
description: Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

subject: AMST
title: The ‘20s and ‘30s
description: Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

subject: AMST
title: Culture, Society, and Literature
description: Literary and non-fictive exploration of the intellectual and moral response of Americans to institutions and culture of 20th-century marketplace economy.

subject: AMST
title: Fashioning America
description: Examines linkages between American identity, representation, labor and capital through fashion theory, clothing discourses and other practices of textile production over history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

subject: AMST
title: Art of the United States
description: Emphasis on the 18th and 19th centuries.

subject: AMST
title: Museum Interpretations
description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Emphasizes written communication and strategies of interpretive engagement with ethical and social justice issues.

subject: AMST
title: Film in American Culture
description: Comprehensive survey of varieties of film experience from historical and contemporary points of view. Significant attention paid to the development of writing skills and to ethical issues.

subject: AMST
title: Sports in America
description: Sports as reflected in literature, films, and TV.

other_notes: Focus on ethical dimensions of sports and sporting cultures; writing emphasis.

subject: AMST
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

subject: AMST
title: America’s World Role
description: Examination of America’s role in modern world affairs, against the background of history, perceptions, and values.

subject: AMST
title: America and Africa
description: American attitudes toward Africa, as well as how Africa has functioned within the dynamics of American culture and history.

subject: AMST
title: American Experience in Asia
description: Examination of various forms of U.S. engagement with Asia, with particular attention to the role of Hawaiʻi as the site, agent, and object of engagement. Emphasis on developing critical reading and expository writing skills.

subject: AMST
title: Religion, Sex, and Gender in the U.S.
description: Examines religious and ethical conflicts about sexuality and gender nonconformity in contemporary America. Students gain knowledge, practical wisdom, and communication skills to negotiate moral disagreement in a pluralistic society.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Preservation: Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific
description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/ Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: AMST, ARCH, and HIS majors only.

subject: AMST
title: Senior Research and Community Project
description: Guides students through a substantial research or community project. Required for AMST majors and open to any student interested in conducting an original project related to American history, society, and culture.

subject: AMST
title: World Maritime History
description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

subject: AMST
title: (Alpha) Topics in American Studies
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent for (D).

subject: AMST
title: Topics in American Studies: social structure and interaction
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent for (D).

subject: AMST
title: Topics in American Studies: arts and environment
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies undergraduate courses, focused within these areas: (B) social structure and interaction; (D) arts and environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent for (D).

subject: AMST
title: Readings in American Studies
description: Directed readings and research for majors.

subject: AMST
title: Approaches to American Studies
description: Introductory survey of methodological issues underlying research in American studies and professional academic practices.

subject: AMST
title: Patterns of American Cultures
description: Survey of key texts in American Studies, focusing on cultural origins and development, and advancing professional development.

subject: AMST
title: Early America
description: Interdisciplinary approach to understanding early American culture and history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Asian America
description: The Asian American experience from an interdisciplinary and humanities perspective. Asian American history, literature, media, and theater arts. Comparative study of Hawaiʻi and the Continental U.S.

subject: AMST
title: Women in American Culture
description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

subject: AMST
title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
description: Graduate seminar designed to introduce history students to the multidisciplinary theories that are appropriate to cultural studies.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: American West
description: Examination of the U.S. colonization of the American West. Topics include: European-indigenous relations, migration and labor, regional literature, frontier ideology, ethnic conflict, and new community formation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: AMST
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

subject: AMST
title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: AMST
title: Social and Cultural Diversity in America
description: Examination of selected subcultures in America.

subject: AMST
title: American Sexualities
description: Aspects of sexual identity within the context of American culture.

subject: AMST
title: Slavery and Modern Memory
description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Identity
description: Interdisciplinary and comparative focus on how Indigenous identity is constructed, negotiated, asserted, ascribed, and deconstructed within and without Indigenous communities with attention to the U.S.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

subject: AMST
title: Wilderness in America
description: American wilderness as both physical setting and social construction.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Material Culture
description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

subject: AMST
title: Environment and Society
description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

subject: AMST
title: Mass Media
description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

subject: AMST
title: Technologies of War and Media
description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Public History and Commemoration
description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various ways in which historic memory is constructed in sites such as museums, memorials, and theme parks.

subject: AMST
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics in American History: Foreign Relations
description: Seminar in advanced research and readings: foreign relations.

subject: AMST
title: Writing for Publication
description: Advanced seminar designed to convert graduate research projects into publishable scholarly articles.

subject: AMST
title: Revolutions and Social Movements
description: Examines the role of social movements in transforming American society and culture.

subject: AMST
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Social/Cultural/ Intellectual
description: Readings and research on American social and intellectual history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: Business/Labor/ Technology
description: Readings and research on American business, labor, and technological history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: AMST
title: American Intellectual Traditions
description: Examination of intellectual figures and movements in American history.

subject: AMST
title: Field Mastery
description: Prepares students to achieve specialization in an American Studies-related academic field.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Topics in American Cinema
description: Investigation of the formal, social, and industrial development of American cinema, alongside key critical and methodological approaches to the impact and significance of film as a cultural medium.

subject: AMST
title: Arts in America: Modern to Post-Modern
description: Survey of the literature of the field.

subject: AMST
title: Transpacific Studies
description: Critical analysis of regional formation in and across the Pacific and the role of the U.S. therein; migrations within and across the Pacific; political, military, economic, cultural, and environmental dynamics of transpacific exchanges.

subject: AMST
title: Globalization and Transnationalism
description: Examines the socioeconomic and cultural meanings of globalization and transnationalism. Emphasis on how the deployment and flows of power beyond the nation-state have an impact on regional, national, and/or local communities and cultures.

subject: AMST
title: Advanced Topics: America and the World
description: Historical and contemporary issues in America’s global relationships.

subject: AMST
title: Comparative Methods in American Studies
description: Examines approaches to American studies that use comparison as a primary method. Comparison of histories, institutions, of phenomena between the U.S. and another country as well as among communities in the U.S. Graduate standing only.
coreq_raw: AMST 600 or AMST 601 or AMST 602, or consent.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Curation and Museums: Practice Meets Theory
description: Seminar explores the history, evolution, and contemporary movement towards indigenous curation within museums, emphasis on the Americas and Oceania, as shaped by colonialism, globalization, multiculturalism, self-determination, and nationalism.

subject: AMST
title: 20th Century U.S. Literature
description: Selected works of 20th-century literature as cultural documents.

subject: AMST
title: African American Literature
description: Cultural and social imagination of blacks and whites as revealed in literature, poetry, and drama.

subject: AMST
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

subject: AMST
title: Historic Building Technology
description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600-c.1960.

subject: AMST
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes, and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

subject: AMST
title: Museums: Theory, History, Practice
description: History and theory of museums and related institutions (art galleries, historic houses, zoos, parks). Relationship between museums, collections, and communities. Introduction to governance, planning, legal, and ethical concerns.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Collections
description: Work of museums and professionals (registrars, collections managers, conservators, curators and others) in the care of collections, interpretive studies of museum displays; field trips.

subject: AMST
title: Museums and Education
description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects.

subject: AMST
title: Museum Studies Practicum
description: Applies coursework in museum studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Museum studies certificate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Indigenous Studies Practicum
description: Applies course work in Indigenous studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: AMST
title: Research Seminar
description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies graduate courses; emphasis upon research methods.

subject: ANAT
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Anatomy Electives
description: Advanced study of human anatomy by dissection and individual observation of surgical procedures. (C) topics in reproductive biology.
prereq_raw: FMCH 531, MED 531, OBGN 531, PED 531, PSTY 531, SURG 531 or FMCH 532 , MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532 , PSTY 532 , SURG 532 ; or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Unit VII Anatomy Electives: topics in reproductive biology
description: Advanced study of human anatomy by dissection and individual observation of surgical procedures. (C) topics in reproductive biology.
prereq_raw: FMCH 531, MED 531, OBGN 531, PED 531, PSTY 531, SURG 531 or FMCH 532 , MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532 , PSTY 532 , SURG 532 ; or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: (Alpha) Independent Study in Anatomy
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

subject: ANAT
title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Human Gross Anatomy
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

subject: ANAT
title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Histology
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

subject: ANAT
title: Independent Study in Anatomy: Research in Anatomy and Developmental Biology
description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

subject: ANAT
title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: ANAT
title: Human Embryology
description: Systematic study of human development, including implantation, placentation, basics of development of each organ system with reference to pertinent congenital anomalies and their surgical repair.
prereq_raw: ANAT 603 or ANAT 604 . Recommended: gross anatomy course.

subject: ANAT
title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS.
repeatable_raw: 8 times per alpha, up to 32 credits

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
description: Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social importance. Topics include physiology, genetics, nutrition, reproduction, behavior, care, and management to achieve productivity, performance, and welfare. (lecture, discussion, and field trips)

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.
prereq_raw: ( ANSC 200 (or concurrent), CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L or higher) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Anatomy of Domestic Animals
description: Micro and gross anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany ANSC 301 , with an emphasis on teaching scientific and technical writing. Dissection and identification of anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Applied Animal Nutrition
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of the principles of nutrition to feeding of farm animals; composition and nutritional value of feed stuffs; nutritional requirements of beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, and swine.
prereq_raw: ( ANSC 201 (or concurrent), and ANSC 244 or FSHN 244 ) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 or FSHN 181 or FSHN 185 .

subject: ANSC
title: Horses and Horsemanship
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin of species, breeds, nutrition, care, management. Lab on management practices with work on light horses.

subject: ANSC
title: Laboratory Skills in Animal Science
description: Provides students with basic and essential laboratory skills required in various fields of animal science such as nutrition, genetics, reproductive physiology, meat science, clinical pathology, parasitology, and animal handling.
prereq_raw: ( ANSC 200 or ANSC 201 , and BIOL 171 and BIOL 171L and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of D-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors only.

subject: ANSC
title: Poultry Production
description: Students will learn about poultry health and hygiene, husbandry, production, biosecurity, hands-on skills, and recent advances in poultry farming systems for meat and egg production.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANSC
title: Beef Production
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of economic beef production, including beef breeds, selection, breeding, management systems, feeding, and marketing under tropical conditions.
prereq_raw: ( ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 ) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: ANSC
title: Swine Production
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of efficient pork production, including comparative breed evaluation, breeding, feeding, management, marketing, and business aspects. Problems and practices associated with tropical environment emphasized.

subject: ANSC
title: Tropical Dairying
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles involved in economical milk production in the tropics, including management, recordkeeping, breeds, breeding, selection, culling, feeding, housing, milking, quality control, and raising young animals.

subject: ANSC
title: Genetics and Animal Breeding
description: Review and application of genetic principles to livestock, poultry, companion, aquatic, and laboratory research animals. Current practices and future developments.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or ZOOL 101 / ZOOL 101L , and MATH 140X or higher) with a minimum grade of C. Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent.

children.text: Recommended: biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

subject: ANSC
title: Genes and Animal Biology
description: An understanding of animal biology at the level of genes and their regulations; emphasis on gene structure, recombinant DNA, transgenic animals and functional genomics being used for agricultural, nutritional and biomedical sciences. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: ( ANSC 301 , BIOL 171 or ZOOL 101 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production
description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

subject: ANSC
title: Physiology of Domestic Animals
description: Functions and relationships of organs and organ systems of domestic animals excluding reproduction and lactation. Problem-based learning and case studies are emphasized.
prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or consent

subject: ANSC
title: Animal Diseases and Their Control
description: Disease problems of livestock, poultry, and companion animals; their economic significance, causes, public health implications, and control.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200 (or concurrent), and BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or ZOOL 101 / ZOOL 101L .

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology
description: Development, growth, function, carcass evaluation of muscle tissue.

subject: ANSC
title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Livestock and poultry slaughter, carcass evaluation, meat chemistry, muscle physiology and biochemistry, meat microbiology, and meat processing.

subject: ANSC
title: Companion Animals and Society
description: Explore human and companion animal relationships in biological, social, cultural, economic, legal, health, and welfare contexts to prepare students for careers in the various animal-related fields in Hawaiʻi, the Pacific rim, and worldwide. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

subject: ANSC
title: Biology and Culture of Shrimp and Prawns
description: Aspects of the biology and culture of the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii and marine shrimp Penaeus (sp) species. Scientific research results and case studies presented and analyzed.

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination
description: Introductory exploration of anatomy, development, and physiology of reproduction of domestic animals and artificial insemination.
prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: ANSC
title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination Lab
description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, estorus synchronization, breeding soundness, and artificial insemination laboratory, field trips. One week off-island field trip.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Production Laboratory
description: Intensive, hands-on course involving the culture of larvae and juveniles of marine shrimp, freshwater prawns, molluscs, fish, and their food. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing and flexible time for continuous live animal care. Lab fee required.

subject: ANSC
title: Comparative Endocrinology
description: Structure and function of endocrine systems across vertebrate groups, surveying how hormones mediate adaptive responses to dynamic environments and coordinate key aspects of growth, development, metabolism, osmoregulation, and stress.
prereq_raw: ANSC 301 (with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: ANSC
title: Aquaculture Business Planning and Entrepreneurship
description: Practical aspects of planning and developing an aquaculture business from conceptualization to a final business plan. Topics include species/technology, project planning, business structuring, permitting, contracts, production plans, financial planning and analysis, market/competition analysis, capital acquisition, intellectual property and legal issues.
prereq_raw: ANSC 450 or OCN 450 . Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care.

children.text: Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

subject: ANSC
title: Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

subject: ANSC
title: Field Experience
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior standing in ANSC.

subject: ANSC
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

subject: ANSC
title: The Science of Food Systems
description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Experimental Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Seminar in Animal Sciences
description: Topics of current interest and current research related to nutrition, genetics, and physiology.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Animal Nutrition
description: An advanced course in the nutrition of mono-gastric, ruminant, avian, and aquatic species. Topics include digestive system structures, utilization of nutrients, energy metabolism, and experimental techniques used in the study of animal nutrition.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Physiology of Reproduction
description: Comparative differentiation, development, growth, and function of the reproductive systems of mammals and birds; external factors that influence response; artificial insemination.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Growth Biology of Meat Animals
description: Growth and development of meat-producing animals; skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone; protein turnover, lipid metabolism, and bioenergetics; regulation of animal growth.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Entomophagy
description: This advanced course examines the scientific, technological, and socio-economic dimensions of entomophagy–the use of insects and insect-derived materials as sustainable sources of food and feed for an expanding global population.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ANSC
title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

subject: ANSC
title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only; others with consent.

subject: ANSC
title: Micronutrients: Vitamins and Minerals
description: Covers selected vitamins and minerals, their discovery history and research use, why selected animal models are chosen for studying micronutrients, how micronutrients are metabolized within the body, their interactions, and environmental concerns.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FSHN, CMB, ASNC, MB, and MBBE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Topics in Animal Sciences
description: Advanced topics in animal sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues and critical analysis of current research literature.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors only.

subject: ANSC
title: Advanced Laboratory Techniques
description: (1 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.
prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent and MBBE 402 / MBBE 402L , and FSHN 477 ; or BIOC 441 .

subject: ANSC
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Plan B students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend before a three-person faculty committee a report of work the student has produced in the project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANSC majors only.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, credit earned up to 9 credits.

subject: ANTH
title: Emerging Humanity
description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Open to nonmajors, recommended for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Emerging Humanity
description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Humanity
description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors, required for ANTH majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Humanity
description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Surf Culture
description: Examines environmental and cultural factors in the development of Polynesian surf culture, surfing’s decline due to Western influence, and its revitalization as a modern recreational activity. Business practices of the surfing industry are critically analyzed.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Surf Culture Field Lab
description: Surfing sites are visited, ancient and modern Polynesian surfing practices and surfboard design and technology are discussed. Shoreline assessments emphasize ocean safety. Social issues surrounding surfing sites in Hawaiʻi are analyzed.

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Ecology of Hawaiʻi
description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology
description: Introduction to prehistoric archaeology; methods and techniques of excavation and laboratory analysis; brief survey of theory in relation to change and diversity in prehistoric human groups.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
description: Human evolution, primatology, human genetics, biological variation, human adaptability, growth and development.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology Laboratory
description: Laboratory to accompany ANTH 215 .

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Reasoning for Anthropologists
description: Achieve basic quantitative literacy and to familiarize them with statistical reasoning so that they are prepared to carry out anthropological (and other social science) research.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Sports
description: Explores sports from anthropological viewpoint: biological, cultural, linguistic, and archaeological. Open to nonmajors. Sophomore standing only.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Love
description: Explores love from multiple anthropological viewpoints: biological, cultural, archaeological.

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Social Issues
description: Contemporary issues in the field of anthropology and in society, including race, ethnicity, gender, inequality, colonialism and decolonization, health disparities and environmental change, from the perspective of cultural anthropology, biological anthropology and archaeology.

subject: ANTH
title: Culture and Health
description: Social and cultural aspects of medicine; the relationship of medicine to the beliefs, social systems, ecological adaptations, and cultural changes of human groups.

subject: ANTH
title: Evolutionary Medicine
description: Using an evolutionary perspective, examines how diseases and other medical issues came to be and how they can be prevented or treated.

subject: ANTH
title: Human Origins
description: Theory of evolution, evolutionary systematics, and taxonomy; evolutionary biology of primates; fossil records for primate and human evolution. Laboratory included.

subject: ANTH
title: Visual Anthropology
description: Historical development of documentary films of non-Western peoples; critical examination of ways in which ethnographic films represent different cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Sex and Gender
description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual differences; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Tourism
description: Anthropological perspectives on the subject of the global phenomenon of tourism. Includes issues of cultural performance, identity, and commoditization. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Origins of Pacific peoples; chronology of settlement; sequences of culture in Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Origins of Cities
description: Combined lecture/ discussion on the emergence and development of ancient cities in comparative perspective and the dynamics of (pre)modern urban life. Examples are drawn from the Near East, Mediterranean, Africa, India, China, and the Americas.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: American Folklore and Folklife
description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnohistory
description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e., the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

subject: ANTH
title: Food Origins, Food Culture
description: Lectures and discussion offer an anthropological introduction to how humans created and transformed food through time. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples and Cultures of North America
description: Survey of Indigenous peoples of North America. Integrates documentary records, ethnography, and archaeology to explore variability among native communities. Contemporary topics include political recognition and self-determination, health and education, and natural resources and economic development.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Surfing
description: Applies cultural anthropology to assess surfing as an indigenous Hawaiian and modern globalized activity. Discusses the history of surfing, surfing culture, and the impacts of surfing tourism on coastal development, reef ecology, and ocean safety.

subject: ANTH
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future.

subject: ANTH
title: Society and Environment
description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

subject: ANTH
title: Historical Ecology
description: Examines the recursive relationship between humans and the environment across deep time.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Virtual Worlds
description: Anthropological study of computer mediated interaction. Focus on the ethnography of massively multiplayer online games, text-based chat rooms, and blogs.

subject: ANTH
title: Aggression, War, and Peace
description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

subject: ANTH
title: Pacific Island Cultures
description: Introduction to cultures of Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia from time of first settlement to emergence of modern nation states.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
description: As primates are our closest living relatives, studying the range of variation in areas like life history, diet, communication, and social systems within the order primates can inform on how we ourselves evolved.

subject: ANTH
title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Household Archaeology
description: Focuses on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between households that comprised ancient communities and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnographic Field Techniques
description: Problems and techniques of social-cultural anthropological fieldwork; ethnographic literature; work with informants.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Indigenous Peoples of Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Mesoamerica
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Andean South America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Race and Human Variation
description: Human genetic and physical variation; latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal variation across human populations; history of racism; contemporary issues in race and racism.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend ANTH 152 and ANTH 215 ; or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Practicum
description: Students will gain practical archaeological experience (e.g., materials processing, analysis, documentation, conservation) under the direction of practicing archaeological professionals in the local community and in collaboration with supervising archaeological faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANTH majors or minors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Lab Techniques
description: Laboratory analysis and evaluation of field data; preservation and restoration of artifacts. Preparation for publication.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Field Techniques
description: Archaeological survey and excavations; field trips, mapping, photography. May focus on terrestrial or underwater. May be taught entirely in the field at a national or international archaeological site.

subject: ANTH
title: How Archaeology Works
description: Uses archaeological examples to illustrate social science research techniques. Students learn how to create, analyze, and evaluate data through lab-based exercises, and examine ethical issues inherent in anthropological practice.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology
description: Introduction to the human skeleton and methods for analyzing archaeological human remains including age, sex, ethnicity, paleodemography, skeletal and dental variation, paleopathology, population studies.

subject: ANTH
title: Skeletal Biology Laboratory
