description: Laboratory to accompany ANTH 384 .

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Undergraduate Seminar
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar: archacology
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar: ethnography
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate SeminarD social anthropoloogy
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar: applied
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar: psychological
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar: biological
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) ethnography; (D) social anthropology; (E) applied; (F) psychological; (G) biological.

subject: ANTH
title: Directed Reading or Research
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: major or minor in Anthropology.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethics in Anthropology
description: Seminar surveying ethical cases, problems, issues and questions from the inception of anthropology to the present. Junior standing or higher or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Language and Gender
description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

subject: ANTH
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

subject: ANTH
title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
description: Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: Political Anthropology
description: Character of political institutions and their development in non- Western and non-industrial societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Anthropology
description: Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the changing contexts of anthropological practice as calls for reflexivity lead anthropology of all backgrounds to bring insights from their “homes.” Issues include the question of objectivity, the emicetic distinction, and the ethics of different kinds of anthropological research and the role of anthropologists in indigenous self-determination.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

subject: ANTH
title: Social and Cultural Change
description: Various approaches to examples of social and cultural change in non-literate societies; evolution, diffusion, acculturation, revolution, etc. Historical features and social processes of colonialism.

subject: ANTH
title: Islands as Model Systems: Human Biogeography of the Pacific
description: Applying the concept of islands as “model systems;” explores the impacts of human populations on the natural ecosystems of oceanic islands, and the reciprocal effects of anthropogenic change on human cultures.

subject: ANTH
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Food, Health, and Society
description: How human groups identify, collect, create, and transform foods; how they shape those into dietary behaviors, and the influence of those behaviors on health.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of the Body
description: Exploration of the history and development of theories of the body via topics such as phenomenology, perception, bodily rituals, gender, sex, race, colonialism, power, pain, medicalization, immunology, reproductive health and cyborgs.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Consumer Cultures
description: Examines the practices and meanings of consumption in the contemporary world. Topics include social class, branding, fandom, global-local nexus.

subject: ANTH
title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: The Agriculture of Identity: Food and Farming in Anthropological Perspective
description: Exploration of agriculture from the perspective of anthropology, with a focus on alternatives to industrial agriculture, especially in the context of Hawaiʻi. Readings include academic writing and also literary non-fiction and journalism.

subject: ANTH
title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
description: Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism.
prereq_raw: ANTH 152 or ANTH 301 or ASAN 202 or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

subject: ANTH
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Sacred Places
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Cultures
description: Cultures of Southeast Asia from hunting and gathering groups to high civilizations; kinship, economic, political, and religious systems; recent developments.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Polynesian Cultures
description: Analysis of Polynesian cultures from their origins to contemporary states.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Melanesia
description: Close study of cultures of Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji through anthropological ethnography.

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology Through South Africa
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology explored through the archaeology and ethnography of South Africa. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Forensic Anthropology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of physical anthropology to problems in human identification. Determination of age, sex, ancestry, etc., of the skeleton and preparation of reports for legal medicine.

subject: ANTH
title: Extinctions
description: An extraordinary number of plants and animals have gone extinct. Delves deeply into the primary literature that focuses on extinction and conservation from the beginning of the earth to the present day.

subject: ANTH
title: Asian Paleoanthropology
description: Neogene- Quaternary paleoenvironmental reconstructions; human evolution in East Asia during the Pleistocene; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend ANTH 310 , or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: East Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of China, Japan, and Korea from earliest human occupation to historic times. Geographical emphasis may vary between China and Japan/Korea.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Health and Development
description: Seminar explores the definitions and histories of development and global health initiatives in developing countries from an anthropological perspective. Reading materials include scholarly and popular texts that propose and critique solutions to global poverty. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Hawaiian Archaeology
description: Archaeological perspective in Hawaiʻi’s past; origins of Hawaiians; early settlement and culture change; settlement patterns and material culture; historic sites preservation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing and consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Quantitative Archaeology
description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANTH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine. This course develops written communication skills.
prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, ANTH 152 , or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Field Mapping
description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Lithic Artifact Assemblage Analysis
description: Combined lecture/lab on the manufacture and analysis of stone tools. Students work with experimental collections and engage in stone tool production. The ways in which lithics enlighten us about past human behavior are discussed.

subject: ANTH
title: Faunal Analysis in Archaeology
description: Analysis of archaeologically recovered faunal collections with emphasis on identification and interpretation of nonhuman vertebrate remains.

subject: ANTH
title: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology
description: Introduction to the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics in archaeological research. Topics include: map creation; spatial database management; spatial analysis; image processing, data reporting; and data display. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: ANTH 466 or ANTH 666 , or instructor approval.

subject: ANTH
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Anthropology
description: The application of anthropological methods and concepts to solving practical human problems such as homelessness, domestic violence, maternal morbidity, conflict over resources, and the loss of indigenous languages. Includes a significant service-learning component.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Culture and Behavior
description: Sociocultural factors in Japanese behavior. Social structure; traditional institutions.

subject: ANTH
title: Japanese Popular Culture
description: Explores contemporary Japanese popular culture through themes such as gender, consumerism, globalization and nostalgia. Rather than a survey of popular culture genres, the course is organized thematically around issues and problematics.

subject: ANTH
title: Pre-European Hawaiʻi
description: Pre-European society and culture from an anthropological viewpoint.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Peoples of Hawaiʻi
description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawaiʻi using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Chinese Culture: Ethnography
description: Critical interpretations of ethnographic and biographic texts depicting individual and family lives in different socioeconomic circumstances, geographical regions, and historical periods of modern China.

subject: ANTH
title: History of Anthropology
description: Development of anthropological ideas, focusing on theoretical issues concerning culture, society, and human nature. Required of majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History: Monuments and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. Monuments and nationalism in Southeast Asia.

subject: ANTH
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis I
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. First semester of a two-semester sequence with ANTH 496 . May be taken concurrently with ANTH 496 . Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Senior Thesis II
description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. Second semester of a two-semester sequence with ANTH 495 . May be taken concurrently with ANTH 495 . Optional for majors.

subject: ANTH
title: Ethnology
description: Survey, in historical perspective, of theory in social and cultural anthropology, from the origin of anthropology to 1976. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Linguistic Anthropology
description: Investigation of mutual influences of linguistic theory and methodology and anthropological theory and methodology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology
description: Development of critical and analytical skills in assessment of archaeological literature; emphasis on the science, theory, explanation, and paradigms that comprise archaeology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Biological Anthropology Core
description: Human evolution and human variability in extant and previously existing populations; emphasis on history of physical anthropology, evolutionary systematics, primate biology and behavior, paleontology, anthropological genetics, climatic adaptation, growth, and nutrition. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Discursive Practices
description: Emphasizes linguistic, semantic, and interactional aspects of culture, exploring ways that discourse constructs social action and social realities, examining processes by which culture is produced as meaningful behavior in actual situations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Infectious Disease
description: The role of human behavior, including its social and cultural determinants, in understanding the distribution of infectious diseases and in shaping preventive and therapeutic strategies.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: History and Memory
description: History and collective memory as culturally formed and politically contested realities. The role of narrative, ritual, and media technologies in shaping representations of the past.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawaiʻi, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

subject: ANTH
title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
description: Graduate seminar that examines the history of theory in sociocultural anthropology from 1960 to present. Designed to be taken in sequence after ANTH 601 .

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Theory in Social and Cultural Anthropology
description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

description: Major theoretical problems in (B) kinship; (C) cognitive systems; (D) religion; (E) political institutions; (F) law and social control; (G) economics; (H) ecology; (I) other to be announced.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Pacific Islands Archaeology
description: Advanced theoretical and methodological examination of archaeological research in Oceania, a region including the islands of Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Methods and Theory in Archaeology
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: analytical
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: environment/landscape
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: applied archaeology
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: economic/resources
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Methods and Theory in Archaeology: survey/locational
description: Focused seminars pertaining to distinct areas of archaeological method and theory. (B) analytical; (C) environment/landscape; (D) applied archaeology; (E) economic/resources; (F) survey/locational.

subject: ANTH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

subject: ANTH
title: Decolonizing Anthropology
description: Decolonizing approaches to anthropology with a focus on South Africa and its relevance for the Pacific and U.S. Topics include race, inequality, nationalism, migration, heritage, and violence.

subject: ANTH
title: Advances in Extinctions
description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and conservation broadly speaking, with particular emphasis on the 6 mass extinction events, including the Anthropocene.

subject: ANTH
title: Paleoanthropology of Asia
description: Survey of the Asian paleoanthropological record, particularly in its paleoenvironmental setting; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing and relevant background in anthropology or related field.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Perspectives on Southeast Asia
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia, and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
prereq_raw: background in archaeology or Southeast Asian history or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Global Aid
description: Examines ideologies of development, humanitarian, and global health interventions from an anthropological perspective. Explores the disjuncture between discourses that portrays global aid as easing suffering and those that accuse it of maintaining relationships of domination.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Hawaiian Archaeology
description: An advanced theoretical and methodological examination of past and current archaeological research in the Hawaiian Islands.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeological Data Analysis
description: Advanced introduction to the fundamental principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data.

subject: ANTH
title: Biomedicine and Culture
description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies, and practices of modern medicine.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Archaeology Field Methods
description: (5 7-hr Lab) Laboratory and field training in the principles and practice of methods of archaeology-survey, mapping, excavation, conservation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Advanced Household Archaeology
description: Focus on the differences in the composition, activities, roles, and relationships to be observed archaeologically between the households that comprised ancient communities, and how these differences inform us about the dynamics of social change.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Archaeology Practicum
description: Applies course work in archaeology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. MA track in Applied Archaeology students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Method and Theory in Hawaiian Archaeology
description: Graduate seminar focused on method and theory in the practice of applied archaeology in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology
description: Theory, methods, and results of application of cultural anthropological concepts to practical problems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ANTH
title: Applied Cultural Anthropology Practicum
description: Applies course work in cultural anthropology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ANTH majors only.

subject: ANTH
title: Professional Skills Develop in Anthropology
description: Seminar prepares graduate students for entry into profession, including employment opportunities, research, presentations, ethics and outreach. Required of all Plan B students.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Thesis Research

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Methods in Cultural Anthropology
description: Ethnographic research methods. Introduction to the approaches and techniques of participatory research, including the collection, analysis, and interpretation of social and cultural data. Politics and ethics of research practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in anthropology or consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Seminar in Research Design and Proposal Writing
description: Research design and proposal writing. For students preparing for advanced research.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: ANTH
title: Anthropology of Japan
description: Japan examined through three dimensions of cultural anthropology: cultural/symbolic, social/organizational, and individual/psychological. Selected topics analyzed and interpreted in terms of conjunctions of these dimensions.

subject: ANTH
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar: Archaeology
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar: medical
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar: ethnography
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar: social
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ANTH
title: Research Seminar: biological
description: Selected problems in current research. (B) archaeology; (C) medical; (D) ethnography; (E) social; (G) biological.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed to provide students with basic knowledge of Modern Standard Arabic. Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language, as well as formal spoken Arabic.

subject: ARAB
title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
description: Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language as well as formal spoken Arabic. It introduces a wide range of situation-based texts and topics that build vocabulary, grammar, and general communicative competence.

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed for students who have successfully completed a year of Elementary Arabic. Focus is on acquisition of more complex grammatical structures, expanding vocabulary, and developing competence in a wide range of communicative situations.

subject: ARAB
title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
description: Designed for students who have successfully completed three semesters of Arabic. Focus is on intensive practice of interactive functional skills such as listening comprehension and fundamental conversation strategies.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic I
description: Develop proficiency in reading/listening comprehension in Modern Standard Arabic. The instructional materials consist of authentic written, visual and audio materials. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: ARAB
title: Third-Level Arabic II
description: Continuation of third-level Arabic I. Emphasis on developing writing and interaction ability at advanced levels of proficiency. Course includes extensive reading, composition exercises, listening skills, conversation practice and extensive review of Arabic grammar. Developing fluency is the main objective of this course. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to the Built Environment
description: Introduction to the breadth of design in today’s global culture. Exploration of human responses to place, climate, culture, communication, and technology, with emphasis on the impact of scientific knowledge on environmental design. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio I
description: Introduction to creative design processes focusing on the investigation of composition within defining perceivable space. Hands-on exploration of materials and structures as an introduction to design processes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Fundamentals Studio II
description: Continued exploration of design processes. Introduction to CAD technologies, material exploration, and creative exploration including the relationship between digital, physical, and materials aspects of design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio I
description: Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Beginning Design Studio II
description: Development of designs and processes to study precedents and explore solutions responding to human needs in built and natural environments. Analysis and representation of architectonic space and form using hand and computer techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Tectonics for Environmental Design: Materials & Methods
description: Introduction to essential knowledge, terminology, and techniques related to materials, processes, and systems used in the construction of built environments, with a focus on applications in design practices.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EnvD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems A
description: Introduction to building systems, including structural, environmental, life-safety, building envelope, building materials and building assemblies. Development of design skills with emphasis on elevating skills in assessing and selecting appropriate building systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism A
description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture in the world’s major cultural regions, from early agricultural settlements to 1500 C.E. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: World Architecture and Urbanism B
description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture from the 15th century C.E. to the present. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Introduction to Environmental Systems B
description: Introduction to environmentalism; focusing on the impact of building systems of the global environment; the role of environmental regulations/certifications, and understanding of sustainable principles (economic, social, and natural systems).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Tectonics for Environmental Design: Integrated Systems
description: Application of fundamental structural principles and systems, materials and assemblies, building envelope systems, and environmental control systems, with an emphasis on their integration within the built environment through project-based exercises.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio I
description: Building and site design with emphasis on site development, analysis, and climatic response. Introduction to sustainable design, land use ordinances, description and delineation of property and land features, and urban and community design influences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Intermediate Design Studio II
description: Architectural design with emphasis on space planning, building materials, technology, climatic responses, and codes including complex functional requirements, multistory design issues, vertical transportation, structure, and finishes. Production of complete schematic design documents. Detailed writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architecture History
description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Graphics Studio
description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Theory
description: Examination of theories, movements, and periods in architectural history focusing on contemporary issues. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of writing, and three oral communication assignments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landform and Water
description: Essential topographic site design concepts and skills needed to reshape the land for human use, circulation, water management, and resilience. Topics will be reinforced through problem sets and analytical, computational, graphical, and technical exercises.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Directed Work
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Concentration Design Studio
description: Professional experience combined with scholarly and research activity occurring in an off-campus location with a focus on architectural concentration areas.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Studio
description: Studio focused on advanced critical issues related to architecture and the built environments with an emphasis on collaborative or immersive place-based projects in local or global contexts.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Capstone Design Studio
description: Culminating design studio with focus on the development of a comprehensive design project integrating all major aspects of prior environmental design education.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Practice Law and Ethics
description: Knowledge of professional standards and a broad understanding of the practice of architecture, including professionalism; ethical conduct; public, client, consultant, contractor, and government relations; project administration, contracts, procedures, and compensation; land use and construction law.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Digital Design Synthesis
description: Investigation of processes for generating architectonic form using current digital technologies. Making advanced geometric models including investigation of morphological transformations. Study of design optimization, digital fabrication, information modeling, and generative algorithms.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Exchange
description: Seminar centered on academic and cultural exchanges, focused on advanced topics related to the design of built environments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, and sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: History of American Architecture
description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific
description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ARCH
title: Urban Ecological Analysis and Design
description: Applied urban and landscape ecology principles and strategies for analysis, design, and management of urban regions and sites; emphasis on structure, functions, and processes that form urban landscapes at multiple scales and in diverse contexts.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Plants in Design
description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics
description: Selected topics in any aspect of architecture. Content to be announced.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture History
description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Explore Furniture Design
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice and an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BEnvD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Writing
description: Reading, research, and work on topics in architecture and design. Includes an intensive writing component. May include specialized research and/ or studio experience in architecture, design, and the history and theory of architecture and design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENVD majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: American Architecture
description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

subject: ARCH
title: Design Communication for Landscape Architects
description: Theory and application in design communication, including drawing and presentation skills; emphasis on the design process and critical thinking through analog and digital media, diagramming, three-dimensional modeling, and various other presentation techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
description: Introduction to the use of computers in landscape architecture, emphasizing two- and three-dimensional computer-aided drawings and graphics suitable to landscape architectural design and practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawaiʻi and the tropics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Materials and Construction
description: Examination of materials and methods of landscape construction from source, extraction, and manufacturing, to use and reuse. Assignments include drawing standard construction details and a report on the history of material use, properties, and qualities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Landscape Architectural Professional Practice
description: Introduction of practices and core methods of the landscape architecture profession. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, professional relationships, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Land Use Planning
description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation
description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawaiʻi and the region.

subject: ARCH
title: Vernacular Architecture
description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

subject: ARCH
title: Fundamentals of Landscape Design Studio
description: Theory and application of foundational landscape design principles, programming, and physical analysis to site-based design problems. Visual, formal, spatial, and functional design principles are applied to ecological and cultural influences in landscape design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Site Design Studio
description: Landscape project design at the site scale; from concept development through detailed design. Synthesis of foundational skills into more complex, layered spatial, and functional problems. Emphasis on site research and design methods.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND and TPSS majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Seminar
description: Provides participants with basic knowledge of the field of historic preservation as well as the fundamental knowledge of how to document, conserve, and preserve both tangible and intangible cultural properties.

subject: ARCH
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation Planning
description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

subject: ARCH
title: Elements of Style
description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Building Technology
description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600-c.1960.

subject: ARCH
title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Preservation Field Study
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable up to 18 credits.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Study: Hawaiʻi
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable up to 18 credits.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Study: Asia
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable up to 18 credits.

subject: ARCH
title: Preservation Field Study: Pacific
description: On-site historic preservation field study. Site will rotate. Academic and hands-on preservation training. (B) Hawaiʻi; (C) Asia; (D) Pacific.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable up to 18 credits.

subject: ARCH
title: Historic Preservation Practicum
description: Applies course work in historic preservation to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and University faculty. Historic preservation certificate students only.
prereq_raw: ARCH 628 / PLAN 675 and ARCH 645 / ANTH 645 / AMST 645

subject: ARCH
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar on a wide range of architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
description: Specialized investigation at an advanced level of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
description: Intensive work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Furniture Design and Fabrication
description: Exploration of design and building principles as related to furniture. Emphasis on fundamentals of practice, an understanding of materials and structure, with an intensive hands-on building experience. Additionally, a survey of 20th Century furniture design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. ARCH and LAND majors only, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ARCH
title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Directed Work
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: MLA Thesis
description: Landscape architectural thesis research and design inquiry. Limited to MLA students under Plan A.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Asia-Pacific Architectural History and Theory
description: Study of the history and theory of culture and the built environment with particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture and Urban Design Theory
description: Detailed investigation of major theories in architecture and urban design and examination of their impact on contemporary architectural practice in varied geo-political contexts.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems I: Introduction to Systems
description: Study of building materials, assemblies, and integrated design including structural, environmental, life-safety, and building envelope systems. Development of ability to design, analyze and assess appropriate systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems II: Qualitative Bioclimatic and Structural Performance
description: Introduction to the theory of bioclimatic principles and structural systems and the ability to analyze, assess, select, design, and integrate them as initial determinants into the building design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate status.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems III: Quantitative Structural Analysis and Design
description: Introduction to procedures and wood, steel, concrete, and masonry material properties used for structural analysis and design of individual structural elements and building structural systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems IV: Environmental Technology, Sustainability, and Analysis
description: Application and analysis of high-performance building design principles. Emphasis on climate-appropriate passive design, energy-efficient lighting and conditioning strategies, innovative water systems, and renewable energy production.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Systems V: Building Systems Integration
description: Properties, evolution, and range of building materials, assemblies, and systems and their applications in integrated high-performance building design with a focus on the role of detail and systems in the design process.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication I
description: Exploration of digital technologies, their relationship to design, and their application to architectural analysis, conceptualization, design processes, communication, representation, and construction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communication II
description: An interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to digital technology and its applications to current developments in practice and research within architecture and design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Forms and Frames of Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice within the global context with emphasis on the Asia Pacific region. Exploration of information technology systems, materials and design process research, construction technology, computer aided manufacturing, and entrepreneurial approaches.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Design Communications III
description: Interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to architectural presentation techniques, particularly oral and written, to current developments in architectural practice.

subject: ARCH
title: Research Methods Seminar
description: Comprehensive assessment of objectives and function of research in architecture and landscape architecture. Lecture, seminar, independent work with emphasis on research project topic and proposal development.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio I: Intro to Design
description: Design theories and systematic analytic and synthetic methodologies applied to creation of building and site spaces responsive to environmental and human needs. Several individual projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio III
description: Design of complex, large scale building and site engaging social, cultural, code, sustainable systems, and acoustic issues. Production of schematic and design development documents.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio IV: Urban Design
description: Urban design focused on Asian cities investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH and LAND majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Architecture Studio V: Comprehensive Design
description: Design and programming for a moderately complex building and site. Production of design development and partial construction documents describing sustainable building assemblies and construction cost.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: Advanced Practice
description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only.

subject: ARCH
title: (Alpha) Professional Studio
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) practicum; (T) China.
prereq_raw: ARCH 744 , and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726 , ARCH 744 , ARCH 745 , ARCH 750G , and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Studio: business
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) practicum; (T) China.
prereq_raw: ARCH 744 , and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726 , ARCH 744 , ARCH 745 , ARCH 750G , and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Studio: community design
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) practicum; (T) China.
prereq_raw: ARCH 744 , and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726 , ARCH 744 , ARCH 745 , ARCH 750G , and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

subject: ARCH
title: Professional Studio: alternative experience
description: Scholarly and research activity combined with professional experience occurring in an off-campus location. (B) business; (C) community design; (E) alternative experience; (G) global; (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) practicum; (T) China.
prereq_raw: ARCH 744 , and ARCH 750C or ARCH 750G for (B), (G), and (T); ARCH 744 and ARCH 745 for (H); ARCH 726 , ARCH 744 , ARCH 745 , ARCH 750G , and ARCH 781 for (C), (E), and (P).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ARCH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only for (G), (H), and (T).

subject: ARCH

subject: ART

subject: ART
title: Sculpture of China
description: Thematic introduction to sculpture in China from the Neolithic period through the present day.

subject: ART

description: Introduction to the art and architecture of Southeast Asia from prehistory through the 21st century.

subject: ART

subject: ART

subject: ART

subject: ART

description: Introduction to the methods and approaches of art history. Students will develop skills in perception and comprehension of visual art forms, and a critical mastery of art-historical methods, with an emphasis on writing.

description: Examination of the role of the artist in society, the artist as self, as community member, as teacher. Professional Practice skills in the arts; planning, grantsmanship, fundraising, budgeting, marketing, outreach, and media relations.

grade_option_raw: CR/NC only. To be taken during the semester prior to expected graduation.

subject: ART
title: BFA Capstone Seminar/Studio
description: In conjunction with the production of art for the BFA annual exhibition, this seminar will examine, critique, and evaluate the student’s art within the context of contemporary art, professional practices, exhibition theory, and integrate theoretical and practical issues in the life of an artist.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BFA majors only.

subject: ART
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis.

subject: ART
title: Installation/Performance-Material in Context
description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools.

subject: ART
title: Early 20th Century American Art
description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ART

prereq_raw: ART 365 , ART 365L , and ART 366 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BFA majors only.

title: Design: Studio III Lab
description: Advanced instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including software and peripheral devices. Instruction in image manipulation and editing still video images for the web, CD, DVD, and portable interface devices.
prereq_raw: ART 365 , ART 365L , and ART 366 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BFA majors only.

subject: ART
title: Design: Typography III
description: Advanced typographic design. Exploration of 2D, 3D, electronic, and intermedia. Emphasis on contemporary typographic models.
prereq_raw: ART 365 , ART 365L , and ART 366 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BFA majors only.

subject: ART
title: Design: Production Techniques
description: Advanced techniques in design production from printed and digital media.

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BFA majors only.

subject: ART

subject: ART

description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Emphasizes written communication and strategies of interpretive engagement with ethical and social justice issues.

subject: ART

description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning.

subject: ART

description: History of contemporary art in Hawaiʻi: the institutions, artists, critics, and historians that have shaped it. Strong focus on oral history of Hawaiʻi artists.

subject: ART
title: Traditional Chinese Painting
description: Stylistic and historic development of two-dimensional arts; painting and calligraphy from prehistory through 18th century. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ART

description: Introduction to the arts of China in the modern and contemporary periods, in all media and genres, from 1840 to the present. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ART

subject: ART

description: Explores the physical, historical, symbolic, and contextual capacity of materials, as well as the mutually constitutive roles of artist and materials within the creative process.

subject: ART

subject: ART

subject: ART

subject: ART
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: AS
title: United States Air Force Heritage and Values I
description: Develops Department of the Air Force writing, speaking, and briefing skills while examining warfare, joint operations, command structures, and professionalism, enabling students to communicate clearly in operational military environments across the force.

subject: AS
title: Initial Military Training I
description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to all majors.

subject: AS
title: Competition and Security
description: Introductory-level exploration of national security, encompassing a broad perspective on the military’s involvement in all facets of national security, ranging from cooperation to armed conflict.

subject: AS
title: Initial Military Training II
description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to all majors.

subject: AS
title: Team and Leadership Fundamentals I
description: Provides a fundamental understanding of both leadership and team building. The course flow is designed to prepare students for field training and leadership positions.
prereq_raw: AS 101 and AS 101L and AS 102 and AS 102L ; or instructor approval.

subject: AS
title: Basic Cadet Leader I
description: Laboratory consists of preparing second-year AFROTC cadets with the skills needed to successfully complete AFROTC Field Training. Students will learn basic military skills, Field Training skills, and participate in physical fitness training.

subject: AS
title: Team and Leadership Fundamentals II
description: Continuation of AS 201 . Provides a fundamental understanding of both leadership and team building. This course is designed to prepare students for field training and leadership positions.

subject: AS
title: Basic Cadet Leader II
description: Continuation of AS 201L .

subject: AS
title: Leading People and Effective Communication I
description: Utilizes students’ field training experience to take a more in-depth look at leadership. Special emphasis placed on enhancing communication skills and refining ethical thought as a leader. Leadership and management techniques implemented in supervised environment.

subject: AS
title: Intermediate Cadet Leader I
description: Laboratory consists of demonstration of leadership and management skills needed to successfully function as an Air Force officer. Instruction will include lessons covering planning, organizational and communication skills, and the ability to use available resources to complete an assigned task.
prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

subject: AS
title: Leading People and Effective Communication II
description: Continuation of AS 301 . Takes a more in-depth look at leadership, with special emphasis on enhancing communication skills and its relationship to leadership, developing leadership and management techniques in a supervised environment.

subject: AS

description: Continuation of AS 301L .
prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent.

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

prereq_raw: AS 301 and AS 301L and AS 302 and AS 302L ; or instructor approval.

subject: AS

subject: AS

description: Continuation of AS 401 . Provides college seniors guidance in their role as military officers and how they are tied to US national security, over-viewing complex social and political issues facing the military profession.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies
description: Introductory course focuses on change and continuity in the history, culture, values, and political institutions of South, East, and Southeast Asia, and the region’s interrelationships with the rest of the world.

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description: Introduction to research and writing in Asian Studies provides a structured overview of the research and writing process from an interdisciplinary perspective, focused on Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: East Asia
description: Understanding East Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to Asian Studies: South/ Southeast Asia
description: Understanding South and Southeast Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

subject: ASAN
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

subject: ASAN
title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
description: Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization.

subject: ASAN
title: Career Pathways in Asian Studies
description: Explore the range of careers related to Asian Studies and develop skills and materials to build your academic success into a meaningful career. Students create a job search portfolio they can share with prospective employers.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Political Economy
description: Interdisciplinary analysis of the social and political issues in China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, relationships between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: The Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

subject: ASAN
title: Chado-the Way of Tea Practicum
description: Practice Japanese tea ceremony as host and guest. Learn to sit and move in the tearoom, how to serve and receive sweets and tea. Active participation in every class, including performing for classmates, is required.

subject: ASAN
title: (Alpha) Japanese Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Japanese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts. (B) 1900-1960; (C) 1960-present; (D) special topics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Media, Advertising & Desire in East Asia
description: Examines concepts of beauty and desire in East Asian cultures within historical and contemporary media contexts. Uses critical theory and in-depth case studies to explore how images, language, and branding work in contemporary Asian societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts.

subject: ASAN
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course.

subject: ASAN
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ASAN
title: Buddhist Philosophy
description: Survey of central thinkers and schools.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
description: This course explores traditional and modern Southeast Asian literature, focusing on key texts from various periods and genres. It emphasizes developing written communication skills through writing instruction.

subject: ASAN
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.
