subject: ASAN
title: Modern Philippines
description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

subject: ASAN
title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawaiʻi
description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ASAN
title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher.

subject: ASAN
title: Korean Cinema
description: Develop an understanding of Korean culture and society through visual, narrative, and contextual analysis of Korean films. Topics include post-Korean War experience, compressed modernity, authoritarianism, and post-authoritarian transformation. Special attention to independent films.

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues Korea and Japan
description: In-depth understanding of Korean-Japanese relations in the past and present by examining conflicting views and interpretations by Japanese, Korean, and Western scholars on important issues that divide the people of East Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.
prereq_raw: ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 or PLAN 310 , or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Statecraft and Diplomacy in East Asia
description: Examines the history and architecture of diplomacy and statecraft in East Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
prereq_raw: ASAN 310 or PLAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Contested Issues in Contemporary Japan
description: Familiarizes students with public discourse in Japan by analyzing key current issues widely debated in the Japanese media and in public forums in light of their political, historical, cultural, social and economic contexts.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Previous course work related to Japan or Asia will be helpful.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g., with class, religion, ethnicity).

subject: ASAN
title: K-pop and J-pop: Korean and Japanese Popular Music and Society
description: Examines modern Japan and South Korea through popular music. Examines genres from early popular music, today’s K-pop and J-pop music.

subject: ASAN
title: Japan Cool: Anime, Manga, and Film
description: Focus on Japanese anime, manga, and films with an emphasis on oral communication. What can one learn about Japanese issues of gender, national identity, and race?

subject: ASAN
title: Transpacific Youth Pop Culture: From K-pop to Tiktok
description: Examines ties between East Asian and Asian American digital media, including comics, movies, TV shows, music, and video games, to examine the dreams, fears, and aspirations of young Asians and Asian Americans.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture-Chinese Diaspora
description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course.

subject: ASAN
title: Perspectives on Chinese Cinema
description: Introduction to Chinese cinema studies, with emphasis on the theoretical and critical approaches to Chinese film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Political Violence in Modern Southeast Asia
description: Why do Southeast Asian governments and political movements engage in mass killings? How do their perpetrators justify these atrocities? How do survivors deal with their trauma and get their voices heard?

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Chinese Development
description: Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.

subject: ASAN
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

subject: ASAN
title: Food, Culture, and Politics in Asia
description: Examines Asia’s role in the development of global foodways. Topics include the relationship between spices and imperialism, global popularity of Asian cuisines, Asian-influenced “hapa” cuisine in Hawaiʻi, McDonaldization in Asia, and food security and sustainability.

subject: ASAN
title: Religions of Island Southeast Asia
description: A comparative, interdisciplinary examination of indigenous beliefs, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism in island Southeast Asia, and how they have been adjusted because of economic and social change.

title: (Alpha) Approaches to Asian Studies
description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. subject: ASAN
title: Advanced Research and Writing in Asian Studies
description: Provides a structured overview of research and writing process, focused on Asia. Topics include research questions, abstracts, literature reviews, arguments, conceptualization, incorporating evidence, research ethics, and style. Students are required to produce a research paper.

subject: ASAN
title: Politics and Development: China
description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

subject: ASAN
title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

subject: ASAN
title: Problems/Issues of Contemporary Asia
description: Analysis from multidisciplinary perspective: rural development, urbanization, international relations, ethnicity, religion, language, etc.

subject: ASAN
title: Gender in Asian Performing Arts
description: Performance is a rich site for gender construction, critique, and articulation in Asia. This seminar examines gender reflected in traditional music, dance, and theatre, including character role and performer persona; approaches of performance and culture studies, and an “Asian way.”

subject: ASAN
title: Culture and Colonialism
description: Analysis of theories and debates (cultural studies, feminist writings, post-colonial issues). Case studies of the transformation and creation of “traditional” cultures under colonialism.

subject: ASAN
title: Capitalism in Contemporary Asia
description: Historically grounded theoretical examination of capitalism in 20th-century Asia; multidisciplinary approach to fundamental change in political and economic structures and institutions, prospects for the future.

subject: ASAN
title: Ethnic Nationalism in Asia
description: Contemporary theories of ethnic and cultural nationalism from perspective of Asia. Issues of nation-state, power hierarchies, modernity, and identity in contemporary societies.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Security Cultures
description: Comparative study of conceptualizations, practices and institutions of national security in Asia in light of their geographic and historic contexts.

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asia Now
description: Examines the ways global influences are shaping the cultural developments in the diverse societies of contemporary Southeast Asia.

subject: ASAN
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Japanese Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics in Japanese literature, primarily of the modern period. English translations of original texts will be provided whenever available.

subject: ASAN
title: Contemporary Chinese Documentary: Record, Expression, Cultural Space
description: Introduction to contemporary Chinese independent documentary with these goals: to achieve in-depth understanding of Chinese society through documentary; be familiar with theoretical debates on documentary form; and understand documentary as a cultural discourse.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

subject: ASAN
title: Marriage and Family in East Asia
description: Examines gendered/generational practices, expectations, and ideologies of marriage, childrearing, and caregiving; state’s role in legitimizing certain kinds of families; how transnational marriage migration is changing notions of belonging, relatedness, and national identity in East Asia. Graduate standing or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: East Asia Now
description: Views East Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic and political themes including various experiences with the West. Focus upon present state of the region.

subject: ASAN
title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature.

subject: ASAN
title: South Asia Now
description: Views South Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic, and political themes, including global interactions. Focus upon present state of the region.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Telecom and the Internet in East Asia
description: Offers interdisciplinary approach to study of internet and telecommunications in East Asia. Examines growth and development of telecommunications networks in China, Japan, South and North Korea. Focuses on contemporary social media and government policy.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical socio-cultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

subject: ASAN
title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.
repeatable_raw: 2 times in different topics, but need consent for second repeat.

subject: ASAN
title: Southeast Asia and its Neighbors
description: Examines how Southeast Asian nations have recalibrated their international relationships in accordance with past experience and new concerns, focusing on interactions with Japan, China, and India, while integrating both global and domestic imperatives.

subject: ASAN
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

subject: ASAN
title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Chinese Foreign Policy
description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.
prereq_raw: ASAN 600 , ASAN 608 , or POLS 645C , or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: International Relations in Asia
description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues interact with domestic politics? Covers Japan, China, Korea, ASEAN nations, India, and touches on Russia, Australia, and New Zealand.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Field Study in Asia
description: With prior consent and supervision of an Asian Studies faculty, students design, conduct, and write the results of a field research project.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASAN
title: Topics in Buddhist Studies
description: Seminar on selected topics in Buddhist studies.
prereq_raw: PHIL 360 , PHIL 406 , REL 475 , or REL 490 ; or consent.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Studies Master’s Plan B Culminating Experience
description: Students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend a portfolio of work produced in seminars before a three-person faculty committee.
prereq_raw: any ASAN 600(Alpha) or ASAN 601 with a minimum grade of B-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASAN majors only.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: ASAN
title: Directed Research
description: Individual problems and research.

subject: ASAN
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Bibliography, reference tools, and research methods in sources on Asia in Western and Asian languages. Discussion of published and archival repositories.

subject: ASAN
title: MAIA Capstone
description: Capstone experience for MAIA students that emphasizes practical applications of Asia knowledge. Should be taken in final semester or after completion of all or most of MAIA core requirements.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MAIA majors only.

subject: ASAN
title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ASL
title: Elementary American Sign Language I
description: Development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Elementary American Sign Language II
description: Continued development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Intermediate American Sign Language I
description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Intermediate American Sign Language II
description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

subject: ASL
title: Advanced American Sign Language I
description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

subject: ASL
title: Advanced American Sign Language II
description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy
description: Introduction to the astronomical universe: sky and celestial objects, planetary motion, planets and the Solar System, Sun and stars, the Milky Way and galaxies, cosmology and the universe.

subject: ASTR
title: Survey of Astronomy Laboratory
description: Observations of constellations and the night sky, the sun and moon, planets, stars, and deep-sky objects; laboratory and observational experiments illustrating basic concepts in astronomy.

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Archaeoastronomy
description: Astronomy and celestial lore in ancient cultures: Neolithic Europe, Mayan, Mesoamerican, Egyptian, Mesopotamian, American Indian, Chinese, and Polynesian. Concepts of the cosmos, calendars, eclipse predictions, motion of celestial bodies, and navigation. Construction of simple observing tools.

subject: ASTR
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

subject: ASTR
title: Introduction to Astronomical Research
description: Introduction to astronomical research, including literature resources, basic computing skills, software tools, data analysis, scientific communication, and research opportunities. Prepares students for effective internships and directed research projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR and ASTP majors only.

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astronomy
description: A rigorous overview of modern astronomy: solar system, stellar, galactic and extragalactic astronomy and cosmology.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: For science and engineering students.

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics I: The Solar System
description: Solar system astrophysics. Dynamics of planets, satellite systems, asteroids and comets; planetary atmospheres and internal structure; thermal balance; the Sun as a star. Introduces numerical computing.
prereq_raw: PHYS 170 , MATH 242 or MATH 252A , and PHYS 272 (or concurrent).

subject: ASTR
title: Foundations of Astrophysics II: Galaxies and Stars
description: Stellar and galactic astrophysics. Stellar magnitudes, colors, distances, and spectra. Galactic structure and evolution, active nuclei, large-scale structure, Big-Bang cosmology. Stellar interiors, nuclear “burning,” main-sequence and evolved stars. Introduces computer programming.
prereq_raw: ASTR 241 , PHYS 274 (or concurrent), and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

subject: ASTR
title: Evolution of the Universe
description: The Big Bang, origin of the elements, formation and evolution of galaxies and stars.
prereq_raw: ASTR 110 or ASTR 210 or ASTR 241 or ASTR 242 , or consent

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology
description: Are we alone in the universe? Astronomical, biological, and geological perspectives on this fundamental question. Course discusses with a writing emphasis: habitability, resources, space exploration, searches for life on Mars, solar system moons, and exoplanets.

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy
description: Principles and techniques of optical and near-infrared astronomical observation. Astronomical coordinate systems. Telescopes, cameras, spectrographs, and detectors. Astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of astronomical objects.
prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
description: Optical and near-infrared astronomy laboratory. Error analysis, properties of light, data, and image processing. Astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic measurement.
prereq_raw: ASTR 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; PHYS 152L or PHYS 274L ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

subject: ASTR
title: Observational Astronomy Projects
description: Astronomical observational research projects. Students use astronomical data and process telescopic observations to produce scientific results, and present these orally and in writing. Students prepare for independent research projects and present research plans orally.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Spectroscopy
description: Introduction to astronomical spectroscopy. Stellar atmospheres, line formation, elements of radiative transfer. Phases of interstellar medium. Emission line diagnostics. Doppler shift and kinematics.
prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

subject: ASTR
title: Modern Extragalactic Astronomy
description: Use of astronomical surveys to map large-scale distribution of galaxies. Internal structure & dynamics of galaxies. Evolution of galaxy populations over cosmic time. Theoretical understanding of galaxy formation in context of modern Big Bang cosmology.
prereq_raw: ASTR 210 or ASTR 242 ; and ASTR 300 (or concurrent); and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 . Recommended: ASTR 280

subject: ASTR
title: History of Cosmology and Scientific Thought
description: History and intellectual context of astronomical discovery; the evolution of ideas of space, time, and motion from the Babylonians to relativistic cosmologies; emphasis on the interaction of astronomy with the history of ideas.

subject: ASTR
title: Directed Study
description: Individual reading, observation, or experimentation in astronomy and astrophysics.

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Astrophysics
description: Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies & Cosmology
description: Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation.
prereq_raw: ASTR 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A .

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discovery of other planetary systems; solar activity.
prereq_raw: ASTR 300 ; and PHYS 152 or PHYS 274 ; and MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A .

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: ASTR 242 .

subject: ASTR
title: Senior Research Project
description: Seminar focusing on development of professional skills for astronomical research, and on scientific writing as a tool for organizing research. A final paper describing a supervised research project is required.
prereq_raw: ASTR 301 , ASTR 399 (or concurrent) or PHYS 399 (or concurrent).

subject: ASTR
title: Being a Professional Astronomer
description: Seminar for beginning graduate students focusing on professional skills needed for astronomy and discussing possible research opportunities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: The Interstellar Medium
description: Astrophysics of diffuse matter, HII regions, molecular clouds, etc.

subject: ASTR
title: Stellar Interiors and Evolution
description: Structure and evolution; energy sources, radiative processes; relations to observables.

subject: ASTR
title: Galaxies
description: Observations and stellar dynamics of elliptical and spiral galaxies including our galaxy, globular clusters, and dark matter. Galaxy formation and evolution.

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology
description: Geometry and evolution of the universe. Dark matter. Early universe. Formation of large-scale structure, galaxies, and clusters. Cosmological models.

subject: ASTR
title: The Solar System
description: Survey of observational data and physical concepts on planets and smaller bodies; formation of planetary systems; solar activity.

subject: ASTR
title: Radiative Transfer Stellar Atmospheres
description: Excitation, ionization, and radiative transfer in stellar atmospheres; model atmospheres, formation of line and continuum radiation.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrophysical Techniques
description: Telescopes, positional astronomy, photon detection, error analysis, photometry, spectroscopy.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomical Instrumentation
description: Design and operation of astronomical instrumentation. Physics of optical and infrared detectors. Wavefront sensors and adaptive optics. Radio and infrared interferometry. Optical design: methods and software.
prereq_raw: ASTR 633 (with a minimum grade of B-).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- )

subject: ASTR
title: Fundamentals of Astrophysics
description: Applications of fundamental physics to astrophysical situations. Elements of general relativity. Basics of hydrodynamics and shock waves. Radiative processes, high energy astrophysics. Modern dynamics.

subject: ASTR
title: General Relativity
description: Introduction to gravity and general relativity. Tensor basics, classical scalar, vector and tensor field theories. Exact symmetric Einstein equation, gravito-magnetic weak field, and radiation solutions.

subject: ASTR
title: Active Galaxies
description: Phenomenology of active galactic nuclei, black holes, accretion flows and jets, emission mechanisms, host galaxies, and cosmic evolution.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

subject: ASTR
title: Exoplanet Astronomy
description: Accelerated survey of exoplanet astronomy and planetary systems using data from the field’s leading edge, introduction to key theoretical concepts, application of analytic and numerical tools, and development of teamwork, presentation and publishing skills.
prereq_raw: ASTR 633 with a minimum grade of B, or instructor permission.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar I
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar II
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astronomy Seminar III
description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

subject: ASTR
title: Astrobiology Seminar: Origin, Evolution and the Role of Water for Life in the Universe
description: Interdisciplinary research topics in astrobiology as they relate to the theme of water: formation in space, role in creating pre-biotic molecules, delivery to earth, and terrestrial planet habitability.
prereq_raw: graduate level sciences and ideas, or consent.

subject: ASTR
title: Scientific Grant Writing
description: Principles of scientific grant writing are taught by working on draft proposals through a mix of lectures, discussions, and hands on activities. The final proposal will be reviewed and evaluated via a review panel.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Programming and Algorithms for Astronomers
description: Distillation of modern computer science fundamentals and paradigms, with applications to astronomy. Common algorithms and essential programming techniques. Assignments include extensive Python programming practice. Open to graduate students in any physical science.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ASTR
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR.

subject: ASTR
title: Star Formation
description: Molecular clouds, collapse processes, physics of circumstellar disks and accretion, properties of young stars, outflows and jets, formation of binaries, extrasolar planets and planet formation, meteorites and the early solar system.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ASTR
title: Astro-ph Seminar
description: Seminar discussions of the most recent research papers covering all areas of astronomy. Students lead discussion sessions and discuss papers of their choice during the semester.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR majors only.

subject: ASTR
title: Cosmology Seminar
description: Students and researchers will review and discuss the most important and exciting cosmological results in depth.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR and PHYS majors only.

subject: ASTR
title: Stars and Planets Lunch and Talks (SPLAT) Seminar
description: Seminar for graduate students and researchers discussing the latest results on solar, stellar, and exoplanet research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ASTR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
description: Introductory physical science course for all undergraduates in any major. A non-mathematical introduction to basic atmospheric variables, Earth’s past climates, global warming, air pollution, El Nino, hurricanes, tornadoes, and forecasting weather in Hawaiʻi.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Exercises with meteorological data and measurement systems. Characteristics of Hawaiian winds, temperatures, and rainfall.

subject: ATMO
title: Pacific Climates and Cultures
description: Highlights the interface between the observed weather and climate of the Pacific and the past and future culture of the people of the Hawaiian and Pacific islands.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman and sophomore standing only.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
description: Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, thermodynamics, conservation laws, dynamic approximations, clouds and precipitation, convection, atmospheric circulations, mid-latitude and tropical weather systems, forecasting, climate.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Energy and Circulation
description: Conceptual introduction to atmospheric structure and motion, focusing on thermodynamics and dynamics. Emphasizes physical intuition, real-world examples, and visual tools over math. Topics include cloud formation, atmospheric stability, wind systems, and weather patterns.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Physics
description: Energy and thermodynamics, statics and stability, physical processes of cloud formation, radiation and Earth-atmosphere heat balance, kinetic theory, optical effects.
prereq_raw: ATMO 200 , MATH 242 , and PHYS 272 ; or consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Scalar and vector development of basic laws of hydrodynamics, equations of motion, kinematics, divergence and vorticity, viscosity and turbulence, introduction to numerical weather prediction, general circulation.

subject: ATMO
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi. ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Instruments and Observations
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Each week targets a different meteorological instrument and culminates in a lab exercise and report. The focus is on accurate measurement and scientific-style writing.

subject: ATMO
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Delve into global environmental change issues such as geometric population growth, food production, plastic waste, and global warming that are of growing interest and importance to our society. Designed for non-GES majors.
prereq_raw: ATMO 200 , OCN 201 , or similar environmental/ natural sciences course.

subject: ATMO
title: Programming for Meteorologists
description: Scientific programming in Fortran 77, graphics software and meteorological applications.
prereq_raw: ATMO 302 (or concurrent) and MATH 241 ; or consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior/ senior standing and consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Directed Reading
description: Individual reading in Atmospheric Sciences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior and senior standing only.

subject: ATMO
title: Applied Atmospheric Dynamics
description: Advanced concepts in dynamics: vorticity, cyclogenesis, jet streams, fronts, mesoscale circulations.

subject: ATMO
title: Synoptic Satellite Meteorology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Satellite applications to synoptic meteorology and forecasting, including orbital elements, ephemerides, viewing geometry, radiation, satellite sensors, and interpreting satellite data.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Meteorology
description: History; tropical clouds and hydrometeors; typhoons; monsoons; local and diurnal effects.

subject: ATMO
title: Meteorological Analysis Lab
description: (2 4-hr Lab) Techniques and methods of forecasting extratropical systems with analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems. Students will be instructed on how to communicate and discuss a weather forecast and how to present a research paper.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Analysis Lab
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in tropical and equatorial regions; forecasting tropical systems.

subject: ATMO
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis, and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

subject: ATMO
title: Special Topics in Weather & Climate
description: Concentrated studies on selected weather and climate topics.

subject: ATMO
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Capstone for senior Meteorology majors. Undergraduate thesis project includes literature review, experiment or research design, data collection and analysis, technical writing of a final thesis paper and oral presentation of the paper. Junior and senior standing only.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics I
description: Governing equations for moist atmospheric motions, approximations, basic theoretical models, boundary layer dynamics, atmospheric waves, quasi-geostrophic theory for mid-latitudes.
prereq_raw: ATMO 402 , and either MATH 402 or MATH 405 ; or consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
description: Overview of dynamic meteorology, numerical weather prediction, geophysical fluid instabilities, approximate dynamical systems, atmospheric general circulation, stratospheric dynamics.

subject: ATMO
title: Cumulus Dynamics
description: Dynamics of convective systems: tornadoes, waterspouts, squall lines. Interactions with synoptic scale.

subject: ATMO
title: Mesoscale Meteorology
description: Scale analysis. Observational and theoretical aspects of mesoscale circulation systems.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Climate and Weather
description: Climate and general circulation of the tropics; El Niño and Southern Oscillation; intraseasonal oscillation; trade winds; tropical weather systems; energy balance; typhoons.

subject: ATMO
title: Satellite Data Applications
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Principles and practices of satellite remote sensing as used in the atmospheric sciences, specifically clouds, aerosols, precipitation, ocean and land cover datasets from various satellites. Develop skills including data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using Matlab.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Cyclones
description: Lecture covering fundamentals of tropical cyclone structure, motion, and impacts on society. Observations from satellites, aircraft, ships and buoys, and numerical simulations focusing on storm structure and track. Some forecasting exercises.

subject: ATMO
title: Monsoon Meteorology
description: Synoptic components of monsoons, regional and temporal variability, numerical models, research exercises.

subject: ATMO
title: Physical Meteorology
description: Molecular kinetics, atmospheric thermodynamics, cloud physics, precipitation processes, atmospheric electricity, scattering and absorption of solar radiation, absorption and emission of infrared radiation, radiative transfer.

subject: ATMO
title: Radar Meteorology
description: (2 Lec, 1-3 hr. Lab) Radar hardware, electromagnetic propagation and scattering, radar equation, signal processing, precipitation estimation and polarimetric applications, Multi- Doppler wind synthesis, mobile and spaceborne radars, forecasting, and data assimilation applications.
prereq_raw: ATMO 620 (with a minimum grade of B- or higher) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- or higher ) or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Statistical Meteorology
description: Probability; frequency distributions of atmospheric variables; linear models; time series analysis (frequency and time domain); principal component analysis; statistical weather forecasting and verification.

subject: ATMO
title: Advanced Statistical Methods in the Geosciences
description: Methods for numerous multivariate analyses will include singular spectrum, extended empirical orthogonal function, singular-value decomposition, canonical correlation, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other advanced topics include wavelet analysis, statistical downscaling and Bayesian analysis.

subject: ATMO
title: Paleoclimate Model-Proxy Synthesis
description: Basics of Earth System Model development, parameterizations, intermodel variability and design of paleoclimate simulations. Types of proxies, tools and techniques for paleoclimate record development and reconstructions. Hypothesis testing and methods for proxy-model comparison studies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GEO, EPET, NREM, OCN, and ORE majors only.

subject: ATMO
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent.

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent

subject: ATMO
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Niño/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

subject: ATMO
title: Numerical Weather Prediction
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental methods and techniques in numerical weather prediction: time differencing, spatial finite differencing, spectral methods, numerical stability, explicit and implicit methods. Modern operational and research forecast models. Hands-on laboratory includes simple to complex dynamic models, with a term project.
prereq_raw: ATMO 600 or OCN 620 ; MATH 407 or MATH 408 ; or consent.

subject: ATMO
title: Climate and Climate Variability
description: Physical basis of climate, numerical climate models, paleoclimatic indicators, modern instrumental climate records, assessment of human impact on climate, predictions of future climate.

subject: ATMO
title: Tropical Climate Dynamics and Modeling
description: Overview of current progress in tropical climate dynamics with a particular focus on large-scale atmosphere-ocean interactions; introduction of basic numerical techniques for students to construct and run immediate tropical atmosphere and ocean models.

subject: ATMO
title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
description: Theory, observations, large-scale analyses, and global model simulations that describe characteristic largescale circulation of the Earth’s atmosphere. Includes zonally averaged climatology, asymmetric features of the general circulation, and El Nino-Southern Oscillation phenomenon.

subject: ATMO
title: Special Topics in Meteorology
description: Concentrated studies on selected atmospheric problems.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable two times, up to nine credits.

subject: ATMO
title: Seminar in Meteorology
description: Participation in departmental seminars and presentation of a seminar on research results. Includes written critiques of departmental seminars.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Sustainable Engineering
description: Sustainability and its social and technical significance; global population growth; resource management and quantification; designs for sustainable society; challenges interfacing technology and culture/religion; green and ecological engineering; life cycle analyses; engineering ethics; selected case studies.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Quantitative Biology
description: Quantitative approach to applied topics in biology including synthesis and metabolism, kinetics, physiological systems, cellular processes and signaling, informatics, and emerging technologies for health, biological production/processing, and discovery.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) and CHEM 162 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Biological Engineering
description: Discussion and experimental investigation of physical and chemical principles underlying representative biological processes and systems. Bioproduction, energy conversion processes, physiological systems, biological treatment, biosensors, biomechanics, and related natural and engineered systems.

subject: BE
title: Introduction to Applications in Biological Engineering
description: Discussion and investigation of special topics, problems and applications of biological engineering.

subject: BE
title: Mass and Energy Balances
description: Introduction of the principles of mass and energy conservation; development of systematic approaches to apply these principles in calculations for design and analysis of biochemical, chemical, and physical processes.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , PHYS 170 , and MATH 242 or MATH 252A ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling
description: Introduction to analytical and numerical solutions for systems of differential equations. Modeling and computer simulation of representative dynamic systems encountered in biological engineering.
prereq_raw: ( BE 260 , ECE 110 or ECE 160 , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , CEE 270 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Dynamic Systems Modeling Laboratory
description: Industry field trips and lab experiences to illustrate behavior of representative dynamic systems in biological engineering. Data acquisition and model validation.

subject: BE
title: Transport Phenomena
description: Fundamental principles and applications relating to mass, momentum, and energy transfers in biosystems and other systems for engineers and scientists.
prereq_raw: BE 260 , CEE 270 , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , ME 311 (or concurrent).

subject: BE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or ECON 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, ECE, and ME majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or ECON 130 ( with a minimum grade of C- ) , and senior standing

subject: BE
title: Biomass Conversion to Biofuels and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production; fundamental concepts in biofuel/bioenergy production; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel/ bioenergy; biodiesel production; environmental impacts, economics and life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies.
prereq_raw: BE 373 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or consent

subject: BE
title: Food Engineering
description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 , CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A , MATH 243 or MATH 253A , PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Environmental Biotechnology
description: Environmental impact and control; the micro-organism and its nutrition and growth conditions; microbial growth and substrate removal kinetics; bioreactors; biological treatment systems; biodegredation of xenobiotic organic chemicals; case studies.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Unit Operations
description: Introduction to unit operations in biological, environmental, food, and manufacturing processes. Integration of biology and chemistry into engineering using basic concepts in mass and energy conservation and transport in reacting and non-reacting systems.
prereq_raw: BE 373 ; and either CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: BE
title: Bioremediation: Principles and Practices
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Soil environment, fate and transport of contaminants; microbial ecology, metabolism, and energy production; biodegradation of selected compounds. In situ treatment, solid-phase bioremediation, slurry-phase bioremediation, and vapor-phase biological treatment. Open to nonmajors.

subject: BE
title: Artificial Intelligence for Bioprocesses
description: Explores how artificial intelligence can be integrated with bioprocess techniques. Using real-world data and hands-on coding, delves into how machine learning can be used to generate practical insights.
prereq_raw: ( MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A and ECE 110 or ECE 160 or ICS 111 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
prereq_raw: BE 373 or CEE 320 or ME 322 ; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Bioprocess Design and Analysis
description: Combined lecture/computer lab on theory and practice of bioprocess design and analysis, involving biological basics and engineering principles of bioprocessing, computer-aided unit operations, process integration, and economic evaluation.
prereq_raw: BE 373 , or BE 437 (or concurrent) or BE 460 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design I
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) First course in a two-semester major open-ended design experience for senior students in biological engineering, with heavy emphasis on teaching written/oral engineering communication. Design process; project management; methodology; modeling; optimization; engineering economics.
prereq_raw: ( BE 350 / BE 350L , BE 373 , CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent), ME 311 , ECE 211 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Senior Engineering Design II
description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Continuation of BE 481 with emphasis on written/oral communication and engineering ethics. Properties of biological materials; risk and reliability; guest lectures on design by engineers; project completion with submission of a final design report. A-F only. Pre: 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.
prereq_raw: BE 481 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or consent

subject: BE
title: Biological Engineering Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: BE
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

subject: BE
title: Directed Research
description: Research in the area of biosystems engineering.

subject: BE
title: Instrumentation and Measurement
description: Measurement concepts and operating principles applied to the selection and use of instruments important to scientists and engineers dealing with biological systems, including automatic data acquisition and processing.
prereq_raw: CHEM 151 , MATH 241 , and ME 311 ; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Biofuel and Bioenergy
description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production, biorefinery concept; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel; biodiesel production; algal-biofuel; environmental impacts, life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies; term paper and presentation.

subject: BE
title: Experimental Methods in Cause-Effect Modeling
description: Factorial designs and fractional factorial designs for screening variable and response optimization. Response surface methodology. Experimental designs appropriate to building and testing multi-variable behavior relationships. Sequential experimental designs.

subject: BE
title: Biological Instrumentation
description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

subject: BE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

subject: BE
title: Biosystems Modeling
description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system models, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
prereq_raw: one of MATH 215 , MATH 241 , MATH 251A ; or consent.

subject: BE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

subject: BE
title: Seminar
description: Use of computer and video technology in technical presentation, review of current biosystems engineering research.

subject: BIOC
title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
description: Biological chemistry stressing integration of concepts of general, inorganic, and biochemistry and application to life chemistry.
prereq_raw: beginning algebra and high school science.

subject: BIOC
title: Elements of Biochemistry
description: Biochemical principles and concepts as applied to living systems, including sufficient organic chemistry to understand these principles.

subject: BIOC
title: Basic Biochemistry
description: Principles of biochemistry, applicable to medicine and real-life situations, involving metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Taught by biomedical researchers. Evaluated based on exams, quizzes, homework, and group presentation.

subject: BIOC
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: Independent research or selected reading of current literature in the area of biochemistry and biophysics.

subject: BIOC
title: Topics in Biochemistry
description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students take an in-depth study of selected topics in biochemistry.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: fourth-year medical student or consent.

subject: BIOC
title: Highlights of Organ-System Biochemistry
description: Provides highly interactive, small group discussions on concepts of biochemistry important to the various organ systems; such as cardiac, respiratory, hematology, gastrointestinal, endocrine, musculoskeletal and neurological systems, and relevant to clinical medicine.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD majors only.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology and Society
description: Characteristics of science, historical development of scientific concepts, and interaction of society with science illustrated by topics from biological science. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawaiʻi. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Option Program Seminar
description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Current Topics in Biomedical Research Seminar
description: Overview of contemporary laboratory- and population-based studies of disease. Discussion of career pathways in human health sciences. Public health and epidemiology of cancer.

subject: BIOL
title: Hawaiian Environment Science
description: Characteristics of science and interaction with society illustrated by topics in geology, astronomy, oceanography, and biology of Hawaiian Islands. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I
description: Introductory biology for all life science majors. Cell structure and chemistry; growth, reproduction, genetics, evolution, viruses, bacteria, and simple eukaryotes.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 171 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, and BIOL 171 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II
description: Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 172 .
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 131 , CHEM 151 , CHEM 161 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A ) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biostatistics
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or BOT 101 ; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
description: Principles of ecology and evolution for life science majors stressing integrated approach and recent advance.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 , BIOL 172L (or concurrent).

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 265 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 (or concurrent).

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology
description: Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L and CHEM 272 .

subject: BIOL
title: Cell and Molecular Biology Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory for Cell and Molecular Biology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 (or concurrent) and CHEM 272 .

subject: BIOL
title: Service Learning for Biology Majors
description: Directed participation on tutorials and related activities in public schools and approved community and UH Mānoa organizations.
prereq_raw: BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L , BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L , and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution
description: Ecological and evolutionary factors creating and maintaining patterns of biological diversity in major marine ecosystems. Emphasis on the biphasic life histories of many marine organisms. The development of quantitative skills and critical thinking.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 , BIOL 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBIO majors only.

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Ecology and Evolution Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 301 . A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBIO majors only.

subject: BIOL
title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Ecology
description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology
description: Introduction to animal and human ethology and sociobiology; emphasis on social and interspecific behavior, its causes and adaptive significance. Lab optional.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 171L and BIOL 172 and BIOL 172L or ANSC 201 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Ethology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of methods in the study of animal behavior by demonstrations, labs and projects.

subject: BIOL
title: Environmental Issues
description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
prereq_raw: one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 , or GEO 101 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates
description: Introduction to the evolution and systematics of vertebrates, with emphasis on comparative morphology, physiology, and ecology.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Vertebrates Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 325 .

subject: BIOL
title: Marine Mammal Biology
description: Overview of marine mammal science, significance and roles of marine mammals in their ecosystems, and marine conservation issues. Current research topics in marine mammal science will also be covered.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , and BIOL 265 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent.

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

subject: BIOL
title: Parasitology
description: Animal parasites of man, and domestic and wild animals; systematics, comparative morphology, life history, pathology, treatment, control.

subject: BIOL
title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

subject: BIOL
title: Island Ecosystems
description: Characteristics of island biota; examples from Hawaiʻi and the Pacific. Impact of island and continental cultures; policy and ecosystem endangerment; contemporary legislation, policy, and management practices.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological science or consent. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: BIOL
title: Biological Field Studies
description: Biological survey, collection, and analysis techniques will be reviewed and applied through field studies. Students will be introduced to the uniqueness of the Hawaiian environment and its diversity of life. Emphasis on diversity, evolution and ecology.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics
description: Genetic concepts at advanced undergraduate level; genetic transmission, recombination, gene action, mutation, population and evolutionary genetics.

subject: BIOL
title: Genetics Laboratory
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments with a variety of organisms to illustrate principles discussed in BIOL 375 .
prereq_raw: BIOL 275L / BIOL 275 , BIOL 375 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Communicating in Biological Sciences
description: Combined lecture/lab impart essential knowledge and skills in technical writing, poster design, and oral presentations for effective communication for life science majors. Research papers, lab reports, project proposals, conference presentations are covered.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , and ENG 100 .

subject: BIOL
title: (Alpha) Teaching Internship
description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

subject: BIOL
title: Teaching Internship: general
description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

subject: BIOL
title: Teaching Internship: oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication
description: Teaching internship in the Life Sciences that includes the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments or classroom activities. (B) general; (C) oral emphasis, includes emphasis on instruction in oral communication.

subject: BIOL
title: Ocean Internships and Research
description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance.
prereq_raw: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal.

children.text: in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent , project proposal

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology
description: General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Biotechnology Lab-Gene Editing by CRISPR/Cas9
description: (1-hr Lec, 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany BIOL 401 . Students learn advanced gene editing techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9 to engineer prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
prereq_raw: BIOL 275L or BIOL 375L , or MBBE 304 , or MBBE 375 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Principles of Biochemistry
description: Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants, and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L , and CHEM 273 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Field Problems in Marine Biology
description: Integrated program of intensive lectures, laboratory experiments, and field research that focus on the biological processes that shape the lives of marine organisms. Limited space enrollment by consent; GPA considered.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 / BIOL 301L and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Topics in Marine Biology
description: Current themes in marine biology and experience in scientific assessment. Emphasis on teaching writing and oral communication.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 301 / BIOL 301L or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBIO majors only.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of Marine Organisms
description: Biology, physiology, and ecology of marine organisms and marine ecosystems, and the physical and chemical factors, which influence them. Cannot be used to satisfy BS-MB major requirements. Credit granted for only one of ZOOL 200 , BIOL 301 , or BIOL 406. Junior standing or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Cell Biology I
description: Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and CHEM 273 , or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 407 ; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
description: (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany BIOL 407 and BIOL 408 .

subject: BIOL
title: Human Role in Environmental Change
description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 or GEO 101 and either BIOL 310 or GEO 322 ; or consent.

children.text: with a minimum grade of B

subject: BIOL
title: Corals and Coral Reefs
description: The biogeography, evolution, ecology, and physiology of corals and coral reefs, and the application of this information to the management of coral reefs. Emphasis will be placed on processes such as dispersal, the evolution and operation of mutualisms, calcification, reproduction, and the maintenance of diversity.

subject: BIOL
title: Wildlife and Plant Conservation
description: Principles of conservation biology and wildlife management techniques, illustrated with animal, plant, and ecosystem examples. Examination of ethical, cultural, legal, political, and socio-economic issues impinging on conservation policy and practice. Group project and field trips.
prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 172 or BOT 201 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

subject: BIOL
title: Psychoactive Drug Plants
description: Taxonomy, ecology, biochemistry, distribution, cultural history, and contemporary use of mind-altering drug plants; examples from primitive, traditional, and modern societies.
prereq_raw: junior standing, one semester of biological science, and either ANTH 200 or GEO 151; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

subject: BIOL
title: Fish Diversity
description: Survey of fish biodiversity focusing on major lineages, their phylogenetic relationships, and their geographic distribution in light of evolutionary history.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Fish Diversity Laboratory
description: (2 2-hr Lab) Overview of the major orders and families of fishes of the world; introduction to local Hawaiian fishes; coverage of basic fish anatomy; introduction to field and laboratory techniques in fish research.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: The Rise of Fishes: An Evolutionary History
description: The origins and early evolution of fishes, with a focus on morphological innovations that have led to lineage divergence and adaptive radiation, and the nature of underlying processes associated with novel character trait evolution.

subject: BIOL
title: Evolutionary Biology
description: Process of evolution: genetic basis, natural selection, population genetics, speciation, the fossil record.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 , and BIOL 172 or BOT 201 . Recommended: a BIOL, ZOOL, or BOT course at 300 or 400 level.

children.text: Recommended: a BIOL, ZOOL, or BOT course at 300 or 400 level

subject: BIOL
title: The Biology of Cancer
description: Integrative study of the molecular basis of cancer, progression of disease, current treatments, and ethical implications of research. Analysis of published studies through written and small group discussions. Structured training in writing scientific review papers.
prereq_raw: BIOL 407 (or concurrent) and BIOL 408 (or concurrent) or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MCB or BIOL majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: BIOL
title: Cancer Research Laboratory
description: Project-based training in molecular cell biology techniques focused on cancer. Application of scientific method in study design, experimentation, and data analysis. Development of competency reading scientific literature. Strengthening written and oral skills through scientific presentations.

subject: BIOL
title: Life in the Soil Environment
description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
prereq_raw: BIOL 375 or PEPS 371 / SUST 371 / TPSS 371 , or MICR 351 , or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany BIOL 480 . Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171L and BIOL 172L , or MICR 351L , or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 (or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent)) with a minimum grade of C , or consent

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Invertebrates
description: Body plans, development, cellular construction, physiological integration, natural history, and ecology of invertebrate animals. Emphasis on marine species, especially local ones.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology of the Invertebrates Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab)

subject: BIOL
title: Biogeography and Evolution
description: Study of the fundamental role that geography plays in evolution and maintenance of species diversity.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and one of BIOL 172 or BOT 101 .

subject: BIOL
title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher and consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biological Directed Research
description: Development and completion of a research project under the direction of a faculty advisor.
prereq_raw: 2.5 GPA minimum, written proposal and consent.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable three times, up to 12 credits; up to 6 credits apply towards BA and BS BIOL major requirements.

subject: BIOL
title: (Alpha) Biology Workshop for Science Teachers
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: biotechnology
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: ecology, evoloution and conservation
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: marine biology
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

subject: BIOL
