title: Biology Workshop for Science Teachers: general biology
description: Principles taught in a conceptual and/ or hands-on manner either in a laboratory setting or in the field. (B) biotechnology; (C) ecology, evolution and conservation; (D) marine biology; (F) general biology.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , in-service teachers; or consent.

subject: BIOL
title: Life Sciences Colloquium
description: Seminars presented with the School of Life Sciences; topics will vary across the biological sciences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT, MBIO, MICR, ZOOL majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only.

subject: BIOL
title: Molecular Ecology
description: Practical introduction to molecular methods used to address ecological and evolutionary questions. Advanced undergraduate/graduate level. Focus on methods and application to independent research project.
prereq_raw: BIOL 265 / BIOL 265L (or equivalent) or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L (or equivalent), and BIOL 375 / BIOL 375L , and consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L ( or equivalent), and BIOL 375 / BIOL 375L , and consent

subject: BIOL
title: Population Genetics
description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.
crosslisted_raw: CMB 650 Professional Development Courses for Science Teachers

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research and Reading
description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Research Review
description: Research elective for medical students.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD students only.

subject: BIOM
title: Global Health and Medicine: Emerging Problems and Impact
description: Analysis of emerging problems and impact in countries on a multidimensional perspective.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BIOM, NURS, PH, SPA majors only.

subject: BIOM
title: Introduction to Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141 or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

children.text: ( or higher ) or PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141 or consent

subject: BIOM
title: Legal and Regulatory Issues and Bioethics
description: Ethical dilemmas in clinical research are identified and resolved in cases, research on human subjects regulation are discussed. Research misconduct is defined. Ethical considerations in protocol developed in the Designing Clinical Research course are resolved.

subject: BIOM
title: Clinical Protocol Development
description: Provides training in proposal development. Governance structures of funding agencies; funding opportunities and decisions; review processes; NIH application and processes; reading RFAs; compliance issues; cultural sensitivity; and types of questions using databases are addressed.

subject: BIOM
title: Foundations of Biomedical Ethics
description: Explores the foundations of biomedical ethics via small group seminars and discussion, presentations. Enrolled in MS or PhD in Biomedical Sciences program only.

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Ethics in Biomedical Research II
description: Develop biomedical ethics through case studies to incite discussions on topics such as gene therapy, gene enhancement, genetic counseling, informed consent, health care professional/patient and investigator/student participant communication, advanced directives and living wills, clinical research in developing countries, clinical research in ethnic minority and socio-economically disadvantaged populations, and non-discrimination in health care and research settings.

subject: BIOM
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research II
description: Explore topics in cultural competence in greater depth, encouraging trainees to address issues from a unified yet flexible conceptual framework. Involves building knowledge, skills and action plans to address a range of learning styles and to appreciate and benefit from diversity.

subject: BIOM
title: PhD Team Building Seminar
description: Seminar focuses on teaching participants to work independently and collaborate in order to accomplish specific results. Students will be exposed to group dynamics, communication, healthy competition, conflict resolution, and innovative means of crossing boundaries between departments, organizations, industries and disciplines.

subject: BIOM
title: Mentored Research Practicum
description: Conduct research under the direction of a mentor. Participants will be responsible for submission of a proposal, acquisition of IRB approval, and conduct of the project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BIOM students only.

subject: BIOM
title: Advanced Biostatistics for Clinical Research
description: Current methods for analyzing longitudinal and clustered, clinical data through lectures, discussions, and a group analysis. Topic areas include multi-level, multi-state, multi-process, and structural equation models.

subject: BIOM
title: Directed Research
description: Students may register on approval of department.

subject: BIOM
title: Disasters and Pandemics: Medical and PH Management and Risk Communication
description: Assess impact on health in disasters and diseases. Enhances research skills related to management and communication.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BIOM, PH, NURS, and SPA majors only.

subject: BIOM
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: BLAW
title: Legal Environment of Business
description: Introduction to the legal environment of business operations with particular attention to business law and ethics and to principles of law relating to contracts, agency, partnerships, and corporations.

subject: BLAW
title: Business Enterprise and Government
description: Critical study of the legal environment of business administration including competition, monopolies, mergers, securities, taxation, and regulatory agencies.

subject: BLAW
title: International Business Law
description: Overview of international and national law as it applies to international trade. Readings and case studies focus on the legal environment of selected areas in the Asia Pacific region and strategies for doing business overseas.

subject: BLAW
title: Social and Legal Aspects of Management
description: Study of the legal environment of management with particular attention to the sources, principles, and form of the law; contracts, business organizational structures, agency, and partnership.

subject: BOT
title: Freshman Seminar
description: Discussion of hot topics in botany, including conservation of rare plants, invasive species, marine botany, ethnobotany, poisonous plants, evolution in action, fungal networks, and careers in botany with emphasis on Hawaiian examples. Students should enroll in BOT 100 and BOT 101 / BOT 101L , or BOT 100 and BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L .

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany
description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

subject: BOT
title: General Botany Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab observations and experiments illustrating basic principles of plant biology.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Plants, People, and Culture
description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance
description: Introduction to the native flora of Hawaiʻi, its origin, evolution and ecology, and the observation, identification, and systematics of the Hawaiian flora.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance Lab
description: The exploration of concepts and the process of science through hands-on experience in studying Hawaiian and introduced plants, their ecology, and cultural significance.

subject: BOT
title: Magical Mushrooms and Mystical Molds
description: Impact of fungi in nature and on humankind. Selected historical events in which fungi played a significant role, their activities as decomposers and pathogens, and their uses as sources for mind altering drugs in religious ceremonies and in food and beverage production in various societies.

subject: BOT
title: Campus Plants
description: Nontechnical course emphasizing recognition of the many interesting tropical plants seen on campus; origin, status in Hawaiʻi, and cultural and economic uses of campus plants.

subject: BOT
title: Sophomore Seminar
description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
description: Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

subject: BOT
title: Biostatistics
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
prereq_raw: BOT 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 ; MATH 134 or higher, or MATH assessment exam.

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-in-practice in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

subject: BOT
title: Ecology
description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

subject: BOT
title: Field Botany
description: Combined lecture-laboratory with intensive field experience for observational and experimental field work in native/impacted Hawaiian ecosystems. Field experience typically held during spring break. Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine habitats considered.

subject: BOT
title: Resource Management and Conservation in Hawaiʻi
description: Management of native Hawaiian organisms and terrestrial ecosystems with particular attention to strategies, planning, research, and management actions necessary to control alien influences and promote native species.

subject: BOT
title: Tropical forest Ecology
description: Introduction to the ecological processes and principles of tropical ecosystems, and to conservation issues facing tropical forests, with a particular emphasis on the neotropics.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; and BIOL 265 .

subject: BOT
title: Senior Seminar
description: Current research themes in botany presented in discussion format; reading current research papers. Oral presentations of primary research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing and consent.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Form and Function
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture/laboratory to examine the anatomy, physiology, morphology, and functional ecology of plants. Labs will develop skills in microscopy, experimental techniques for studying plant physiology, and basic functional ecology.

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
prereq_raw: BOT 201 or BIOL 172 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

subject: BOT
title: Medical Ethnobotany
description: Survey and theory of plants used as medicines, cultural perspectives of herbal medicine, and the botanical/chemical basis of allopathic and naturopathic medicine. Lecture/ discussion, term paper or project.

subject: BOT
title: Biocultural Ecology and Conservation
description: Examines some perspectives on ecology within the context of Indigenous and Local Knowledge systems, and some approaches to conservation by Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities.
prereq_raw: BIOL 265 or BIOL 301 or BIOL 305 / BOT 305 or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

subject: BOT
title: Plant-Animal Interactions
description: Interdependence of plants and animals, emphasizing the influence of animals on plant fitness and evolution. Topics include pollination, fruit/seed dispersal, herbivory, and ant-plant mutualisms.

subject: BOT
title: ʻĀina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

subject: BOT
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O’ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

subject: BOT
title: Systematics of Vascular Plants
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) “Hands-on” experience with Hawaiʻi’s unique tropical flora; emphasis on recognition and identification of vascular plant families and the principles and methodologies that define them; evolution of biodiversity.

subject: BOT
title: Plant Ecology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecological principles and process that determine patterns of plant distribution and abundance. Lectures cover theory and examples from primary literature. Labs cover study design, descriptive and experimental techniques, field skills, and data analysis and interpretation.

subject: BOT
title: Algal Diversity and Evolution
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of algal diversity, structure, and evolution. Identification of common Hawaiian algae. Develops written communication skills with significant attention paid to developing writing skills and emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: one of BOT 101 , BIOL 172 , MICR 351 , ZOOL 101 ; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Grant Writing and Your Career in Science
description: Scientific grant writing from inception through management to completion; students will write a DDIG and participate in a panel. Professional skills including “rules,” job applications, interviews, transitioning from graduate student to academic or non-academic job.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: current standing as a graduate student, or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Foundations of Current Botany I
description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in history of science, plant diversity, plant interactions with the environment, and plant integration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in BOT or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature.
prereq_raw: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: BOT
title: Botanical Seminar
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in botany.

subject: BOT
title: Advanced Botanical Problems
description: Investigation of any botanical problem; reading and laboratory work.

subject: BOT
title: Ethnoecological Methods
description: Field techniques for assessing the ecological effects of cultural uses of plants. Emphasis on documenting traditional and local patterns of plant use and measuring the effects on plant individuals, populations, communities, and landscapes.
prereq_raw: previous course work in anthropology or biology.

subject: BOT
title: Population Biology
description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
prereq_raw: one of BOT 456 , NREM 680 , PEPS 671 , ZOOL 620 , ZOOL 623 ; or consent.

subject: BOT
title: Ecological Statistics with R
description: Learn how to choose appropriate statistical methods to test hypotheses in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology and applications using R as a platform. Lecture/ discussion, term paper.

subject: BOT
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

subject: BOT
title: High Throughput Sequencing Approaches to Ecology and Evolution
description: Fundamentals of experimental design, lab techniques and data analysis to conduct research using high throughput sequencing. Students will work in groups to conduct an amplicon sequencing study with ten samples.

subject: BOT
title: Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution
description: Molecular approaches to evolution, phylogenetics, and systematics. Basic use of chloroplast DNA, mitochondrial DNA, nuclear DNA, and electrophoresis. Phylogenetic analysis using parsimony, distance, and comparative methods.

subject: BOT
title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only.

subject: BOT
title: Marine Macrophytes Seminar
description: Discussion of current literature in physiological ecology, cellular and molecular adaptations to environmental factors by marine plants.

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants
description: Discussion of current studies in morphological, physiological, cellular, and molecular adaptation to marine environments by macroalgae, phytoplankton, and seagrasses.
prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, BOT 480 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: upper division ecology class recommended, BOT 480 (

subject: BOT
title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants Lab
description: Field and laboratory research techniques and projects in the physiological ecology of algae and seagrasses.
prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, BOT 470 (or equivalent), BOT 480 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: upper division ecology class recommended, BOT 470 (

subject: BOT
title: Conservation Biology
description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution, and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.

subject: BOT
title: Directed Research
description: Research preliminary to thesis or dissertation research.

subject: BOT
title: Thesis Research
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for MS degree and approval of thesis proposal.

subject: BOT
title: Topics in Conservation Biology
description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology.

subject: BOT
title: Dissertation Research
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD and approval of dissertation proposal.

subject: BUS
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR and BUS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen only.

subject: BUS
title: Introduction to Business
description: Introduction to each of the functional areas of business. Intends to help students understand the interrelationships of business functional areas and the role of business in society. Stresses written communication in business.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BUS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman or sophomore standing only.

subject: BUS
title: Written Communication in Business
description: An interactive writing class stressing persuasive writing in the context of memos, letters, and business reports.
prereq_raw: ACC 200 or ACC 210 , and ENG 100 . Students may not earn credit for both BUS 209 and ENG 209 .

children.text: Students may not earn credit for both BUS 209 and ENG 209

subject: BUS
title: Applied Math in Business
description: Provides problem-solving and quantitative skills essential in business. Reviews algebra, mathematics of finance, calculus in business applications, probability, introductory statistics, and hypothesis testing.

subject: BUS
title: Statistical Analysis for Business Decisions
description: Problem recognition and formulation; stress on cross-disciplinary complex problem solving and communication; computer intensive. Coverage of descriptive statistics, probability and hypothesis testing with emphasis on quality, productivity, and regression analysis. Must be taken in first semester of BBA program.

subject: BUS
title: Information Systems for Global Business Environment
description: Skills and strategies for using information resources applied to local and global business issues; advanced skills in computer-based analytical techniques and information management; impact of information technology on business operations and business strategies. Must be taken in first semester of BBA program.
prereq_raw: ICS 101 , or LTEC 112 and LTEC 113 , or equivalent, or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Principles of Marketing
description: Concepts, problems, and opportunities in marketing within its competitive, political-legal, economic, social and global environments. Social responsibility and ethics. Marketing research. Consumer and business-to-business segmentation and positioning. Strategic marketing planning. Students may not earn credit for BUS 312 and TIM 304 .

subject: BUS
title: Economic and Financial Environment of Global Business
description: International trade, financial flows, and direct investment. Public and private institutions including government policies and capital markets. Emphasis on Asia Pacific issues, with attention to the cultural differences among countries.

subject: BUS
title: Business Finance
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of financial management: analysis and decision making for asset management, capital budgeting, capital structure, and dividend policy. Prerequisite for all other finance courses.
prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210 , ECON 130 and ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Global Management and Organizational Behavior
description: Analysis of theories and concepts underlying domestic and global organizational management, including behavioral and personnel issues. Emphasis on leadership, team-work, cultural differences in the Asia Pacific region. Prerequisite to all other advanced management courses. Students may not receive credit for BUS 315 and TIM 303 .

subject: BUS
title: Strategic Management
description: Applications of strategy to domestic and global business problems using an interdisciplinary approach. Emphasis on Asia-Pacific business, assessment of risk, integration of all business core disciplines. Extensive writing expected.
prereq_raw: all core courses and graduating senior standing.

subject: BUS
title: Data Analytics for Business
description: Introduction to data analytics techniques and tools, builds on foundational business analysis and quantitative methods knowledge. Modules include preparing relevant data, conducting analysis, visualizing results, and storytelling with data.

subject: BUS
title: Asia Pacific Business
description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study of businesses, governmental entities, and nongovernmental organizations in specific geographic areas in non-U.S. settings.

subject: BUS
title: Asia Pacific Field Trip
description: Analysis of business environment and business issues through study and direct observation of businesses, governmental entities, and non-governmental organizations in non-U.S. settings. Involves group travel to selected international business cities. Travel sites will vary.

subject: BUS
title: Dynamics of Asian Finance
description: Analysis of selected key industries of Asian countries: business/ economic trends, shifting product mix, technological changes, joint ventures, international competition, and productivity strategy, including contrasting management styles, worker/management relationships, and decision-making processes under different cultural settings. Industry observations conducted in Asian countries for three weeks during the summer.
prereq_raw: 6 credit hours of economics or business, PAMI participant; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Professional Development
description: Professional development course designed to focus and improve the career development and leadership skills of MBA students. Students learn from guest speakers through site visits, intensive workshops, and hands-on experience. MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Sustainable Business Management
description: Overview of sustainable business management in the firm’s functional areas, including sustainable strategic planning, climate risk assessment, sustainable asset financing, supply chain management, fair trade, and green/ethical consumption behavior management.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: BUS
title: Data Analytics and Statistics for Business
description: Data analytical and statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on descriptive and predictive quantitative analytical methods, including time series and regression. Completing an additional six contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Micro- and Macro-economic Foundations for Managers
description: Applications of micro- and macro-economic principles to managerial decisions. Microeconomic focuses on economic foundations of business strategies. Macroeconomics focuses on the external economic environment including regulatory and international trends and issues. Admission to MBA program. Complete an additional 3 contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Business Statistics
description: Statistical tools for the MBA with emphasis on quality control, time series, and forecasting using regression.

subject: BUS
title: Economic Foundations of Strategy
description: Microeconomic principles that provide structure to solve managerial problems, and to suggest strategies for success. Evaluation of the microeconomic competitive environment in which organizations operate.

subject: BUS
title: Marketing Management
description: Concepts and issues in marketing within the global environment of business. Ethical dimensions and social responsibilities; market research; consumer segmentation and positioning. Strategic marketing planning. MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Accounting for Decision-making
description: Accounting tools for business professionals focusing on the role of accounting information in capital markets, managerial decision-making and corporate governance. Completing an additional 12 contact-hour tutorial will be required and incorporated into the class schedule. With instructor approval, the tutorial requirement may be waived if student has successfully completed an accounting course (ex. ACC 200 (with a minimum grade of C-)) or ACC 201 (with a minimum grade of C-) or an approved online tutorial.

subject: BUS
title: Digital Transformation with Information Systems and Technology
description: Practices, techniques, and tools for managing digital innovation in markets, firms, and enterprise systems through information technologies and applications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Leadership and Organizational Behavior
description: Personal leadership and communications development and the contributions of the behavioral sciences to understanding human behavior in organizations with a focus on leading organizations in times of change. MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Business, Government, and External Environment
description: Important issues related to the external environment of business. This includes international trade and finance, regulatory environment, social impacts of business.

subject: BUS
title: Ethics
description: Assists students in developing an awareness of major ethical issues which affect business decisions, and encourages a socially responsible consideration of those issues and being able to express their views.

subject: BUS
title: Managerial Finance
description: Financial management theories and tools for business professionals; asset management; capital budgeting; capital structure and dividend policies. MBA students only or advisor approval.
prereq_raw: BUS 619 , BUS 620 , and BUS 624 ; or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Managing Information Technology for Strategic Advantage
description: Theory, practices, techniques for managing information technology resources for innovation and for strategic advantage in global business environment.

subject: BUS
title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Theory, practices, techniques for managing operations and supply chains for global integration of firms and organizations.

subject: BUS
title: Business Policy and Strategy
description: Integration of learning through analysis of comprehensive business problems, resolution of policy issues, and the study of competitive strategies in the international setting.
prereq_raw: MBA core courses completed or taken concurrently; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA students only or advisor approval.

subject: BUS
title: Business Study Abroad
description: Study abroad experience emphasizing international business issues. Content varies depending on course of study and educational institution selected. Course qualifies as an international business elective(s).
prereq_raw: business core or permission of academic advisor.

subject: BUS
title: International Business Topics
description: Analysis of the business environment and business issues through study of businesses, governmental entities, and/or nongovernmental organizations in specific geographic areas, in non-U.S. settings.

subject: BUS
title: International Business Field Experience
description: Analysis of the business environment and business issues through study and direct observation of businesses, governmental entities, and/or nongovernmental organizations in non-U.S. settings. Involves group travel to selected international business cities.

subject: BUS
title: Field Study in Asia
description: Industry observations conducted entirely in Asian countries for three and a half weeks.

subject: BUS
title: Internships
description: On-the-job experience in the business community. Project paper and meetings with faculty advisor required.

subject: BUS
title: MBA Consulting Practicum
description: Final MBA requirement for those candidates not writing a thesis. Candidates will form consulting teams to perform a meaningful, strategic study for a client organization.
prereq_raw: BUS 632 and at least 12 credits of MBA electives.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA students only or advisor approval.

children.text: at least 12 credits of MBA electives

subject: BUS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Outline (including methodology or sources, results expected and means of measurement) must be prepared by student and approved by supervisor and chair of graduate programs before registration.

subject: BUS
title: Thesis Research
description: Required for Plan A candidates only; six credit hours required, one of which must be taken during semester in which degree is awarded.

subject: BUS
title: Advanced Research Methods
description: Analysis of current theories in international business; design research studies in areas of possible dissertation research through application of scientific method; includes formation of research questions and testable hypothesis, identification of data sources, and analysis.
prereq_raw: two graduate level courses (six credits) in statistics and methodology, or consent.

children.text: two graduate level courses ( six credits) in statistics

subject: BUS
title: Research Seminar in Business
description: Covers research topics including research projects currently underway by Shidler College faculty, advanced PhD students, distinguished visiting faculty, and research contemplated by new PhD students.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: student status in PhD in business administration or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Seminar in International Business
description: Developing research and teaching skills in international business, preparation for teaching college-level courses in “international business,” give presentation on recent research in most selective business journals, integrating expectations of university teaching, research, and service.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: student status in PhD in business administration or consent.

subject: BUS
title: Dissertation Research
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: CAAM
title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction
description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. No experience necessary.

subject: CAAM
title: Clinical Nutrition
description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations, and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions.
prereq_raw: CHEM 151 (or higher) or PHYL 141 or BIOL 171 or approval from instructor; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing and higher.

children.text: ( or higher ) or PHYL 141 or BIOL 171 or approval from instructor; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course

subject: CAAM
title: Introduction to Integrative Medicine
description: Overview of integrative (complementary) medicine covering Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurvedic medicine, naturapathy, traditional healing practices, homeopathy, nutrition and diet, herbs and dietary supplements, environmental health, mind-body, energy, spiritual, and positive psychology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: CAAM
title: Nutrition for Clinicians
description: Provides in-depth lectures and case studies reviewing the role of nutritional therapy in health and illness.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD majors only.

subject: CALL
title: Exploring Expression: Foundations in Arts, Languages & Letters
description: First-year seminar for majors in the College of Arts, Languages & Letters that includes emphasis on the introduction to studies in a liberal arts curriculum and emphasizes the importance of writing in this discipline.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CALL majors only, or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen only.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer I
description: Face to face course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Introductory Khmer II
description: Continuation of CAM 101 . Face to face course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking, listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the introductory level, with structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer I
description: Online course aims to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Conversing in Khmer II
description: Continuation of CAM 103 . Online course continues to develop students’ proficiency in speaking and listening to Khmer at the introductory level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

subject: CAM
title: Reading/Writing in Khmer I
description: Online course aims to develop proficiency in reading and writing Khmer at the introductory level. Uses interactive multimedia web-based content and textbook to complement online instruction.

subject: CAM

subject: CAM
title: Khmer Language in the Media
description: Focus on advanced reading, writing, aural comprehension and speaking skills through the study of Khmer newspaper, radio, TV, audio/video clips and film.

subject: CEE
title: Surveying/Geodesy/Geomatics
description: Plane surveying for cadastral, engineering, and construction applications including taping, leveling, traverses, bearings and azimuths, areas and volumes, EDM. Geodesy, map projections, satellite geodesy (GPS), geodetic surveying and photogrammetry. Field lab in notes and procedures.
prereq_raw: MATH 252A (with a minimum grade of C) or MATH 242 (with a minimum grade of C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, and PREN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or MATH 242 ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: CEE
title: CAD/BIM/3D Visualization
description: Computer-aided drafting (CAD) tools using AutoCAD and Revit. AutoCAD interface, titleblocks, model/paper space, viewports, texts and annotation, dimensioning. Basics of BIM, toolbox, modeling techniques, annotating, dimensioning. CAD drafting to real-world engineering applications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, and PREN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics I
description: Forces, resultants, and equilibrium; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; centroids, moments of inertia; friction.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: PHYS 170 ; MATH 242 or MATH 252A ; and either MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

children.text: better in all of the following: PHYS 170

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Probability and Statistics
description: Description of sample data; correlation and regression; probability and statistical distributions; estimations of population parameters; fitting distributions to histograms; hypothesis testing.

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics Fundamentals
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Compressible and incompressible fluid properties; fluid statics; kinematics, energy and momentum considerations in steady flows; application of steady flow concepts to various fluid processes; with an emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Engineering
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Parameters and indices of environmental quality; materials balances; chemical kinetics; ideal reactor models; water and air pollution control; solid and hazardous waste management; emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to geotechnical engineering: soil characterization, index properties, seepage and flow in soil, stresses in soils, compressibility, consolidation, shear strength. Substantial emphasis on writing lab reports.
prereq_raw: CEE 320 and CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Fundamentals of Transportation
description: Transportation modes: land, air, water, pipelines. Tourist, urban transportation. Geometric design, human factors, vehicular flow models, capacity analysis. Overview: traffic impact, air quality, parking studies.

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Solids
description: Introduction to analysis and design of deformable bodies subject to loading. Stress, strain, constitutive relation, axially loading, torsion, statically indeterminate systems, Mohr’s circle, failure criteria, buckling, defection due to axial, shear, torsional, and flexural loading.
prereq_raw: C or better in all of the following: CEE 270 ; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).

children.text: better in all of the following: CEE 270

subject: CEE
title: Mechanics of Solids Lab
description: Tension, compression, and torsion of bars, and bending of beams. Emphasis on writing lab reports.
prereq_raw: CEE 370 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE and CNST majors only.

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- )

subject: CEE
title: Construction Materials
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Concrete properties, role of aggregates, concrete mix design, supplementary cementitious materials, chemical admixtures, behavior of concrete, concrete testing, field practices. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Analysis
description: Analysis of statically determinate plane and space trusses and frames; deflections; introduction to matrix methods; computer applications.
prereq_raw: CEE 370 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Economics
description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 (with a minimum grade of C-) or ECON 130 (with a minimum grade of C-), and senior standing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CEM, CNST, EE, and ME majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or ECON 130 ( with a minimum grade of C- ) , and senior standing

subject: CEE
title: Computer Methods in Engineering Systems
description: Numerical solutions of engineering problems using digital computers. Regression analysis; numerical differentiation and integration; solutions of algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations; and analysis of large structural systems.

subject: CEE
title: Engineering Hydraulics
description: Hydraulics of closed conduits and open channels with emphasis on engineering applications. Topics also include pump hydraulics, bridge hydraulics, urban drainage engineering, and flood plain management.
prereq_raw: CEE 320 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
description: Introduction to basic concepts of pollutant transport phenomenon through theoretical modeling, lab and field experiments and observations. Specific topics include mass balance, jets and plumes, mixing and transport in rivers, reservoirs, groundwater and estuaries; non point course pollution.
prereq_raw: CEE 320 (with a minimum grade of D-), and MATH 244 or MATH 253A (or equivalent).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D- ) , and MATH 244 or MATH 253A ( or equivalent)

subject: CEE
title: Applied Hydrology
description: Surface water hydrology topics include hydrologic cycle, hydrographs, regression methods, urban rain-runoff process, flood frequency analysis, flood routing and hydrology for detention basin design. Groundwater hydrology topics include seawater intrusion, theory of groundwater flow and solutions to steady and unsteady aquifer flows.
prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 320 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
description: Hydrologic fundamentals of water demand and supply; water and wastewater distribution; collection systems; quality characterization; analytical methods for water quality management.

subject: CEE
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. Senior standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

subject: CEE
title: Geotechnical Engineering II
description: Continuation of CEE 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, bearing capacity theory, slope stability, use of geosynthetics.

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Engineering
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design principles of flexible and rigid pavements; HMA mixture design, equipment and construction; and application of life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) in pavement engineering. Includes laboratory sessions for aggregate testing and Superpave mix design.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-), CEE 375 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of D-), and CEE 361 (with a minimum grade of C or better).

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- ) , CEE 375 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of D- ) , and CEE 361 ( with a minimum grade of C or better )

subject: CEE
title: Traffic Engineering
description: Design/analysis of signalized, unsignalized intersections, urban networks. Traffic impact studies; analysis steps and applications. Design/redesign options. Parking studies: demand, alternative designs (lot layouts).
prereq_raw: CEE 361 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Urban and Regional Transportation Planning
description: Application of travel demand forecasting models to transportation planning. Evaluation and decision-making. Term projects.
prereq_raw: CEE 361 with a minimum grade of C or better.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Methods
description: Methods of construction, primarily buildings. Construction types: light and heavy wood; steel; plain, reinforced, and prestressed concrete; masonry. Foundations; associated details of frames, walls, roofs, floors, openings, finishes. Disasters, failures, and their causes. Industrialization of the building process.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CEM, CNST, EE, ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Project Management
description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CEM, CNST, EE, and ME majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Equipment and Methods
description: Methods and equipment used on horizontal/ heavy engineering projects. Available equipment, their production, and how they are used to excavate, move, process, and place the earth.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Estimating and Bidding
description: Estimating science; techniques of estimating quantities and pricing of work for construction contracting; classification of costs, analysis of plans and specifications for estimating; computerized estimating; cash flow, bidding strategy, preparation and submission.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, EE, ME, OE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
description: To teach the theory and the practice of planning, scheduling, and reporting a construction project through the use of bar chart and CPM. Format to include lectures, text, outside speakers, site visits, discussions, case study, and computers.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Safety
description: Safety and health concepts, laws and requirements for civilian and contractor personnel in construction, including applications in project management and construction activities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CNST, CE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Construction Law
description: In-depth exploration of the legal regimes governing construction. Construction contracts, contractors, and subcontractors. Breach of contracts, claims and litigation in construction projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: CEE
title: Undergraduate Structural Research
description: Individual research project for undergraduate students in the structures track. Topic to be determined by consultation with structural faculty advisor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Loads
description: Introduction to the minimum load requirements for buildings and other structures used in current structural design codes. Derive and apply dead, live, rain, soil, snow, wind, earthquake, flood, inundation, and other loads to structural systems.
prereq_raw: CEE 305 and CEE 381 with a minimum grade of C or better.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Reinforced Concrete Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, one-way slabs and columns. Laboratory section includes design and hands-on manufacturing and testing of reinforced concrete members.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Steel Design
description: Basic properties of steel; behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and connections; introduction to rigid frames.

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project & Professional Ethics
description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills are assessed through multiple presentations to an industry. Engineering ethics, ethical decision making and deliberation.
prereq_raw: CEE 220 (with a minimum grade of D-), CEE 250 (with a minimum grade of D-), and CEE 305 (with a minimum grade of C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE or CNST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D- ) , CEE 250 ( with a minimum grade of D- ) , and CEE 305 ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: CEE
title: Senior Design Project
description: Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution. Oral communication skills will be assessed through multiple presentations to an industry panel.
prereq_raw: senior standing in CEE or CNST and CEE 489B.

children.text: in CEE or CNST and CEE 489B

subject: CEE
title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Will reflect special interests of visiting and/or permanent faculty.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing, and consent.

subject: CEE
title: Special Problems
description: Individual investigation in civil and environmental engineering topics as approved by instructor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior standing, and minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum GPA of 3.0 in engineering.

subject: CEE
title: Operations Management
description: Linear programming, simplex method, graphical representation: dual; degeneracy; transportation problem; assignment problems; data envelopment analysis; applications; case studies; managerial reporting; LINDO software.
prereq_raw: CEE 476 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and consent

subject: CEE
title: Cost Engineering and Quality Control
description: Study and applications of cost/schedule control systems criteria, earned value analysis, probabilistic cost estimating, construction risk management, construction quality control, and operations research in construction.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 472 or CEE 474 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Machine Learning in Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Science
description: Statistical machine learning and deep learning methods. Script languages for data-driven model training, validation and test. Analysis with linear algebra and statistics. Applications to engineering and earth science problems.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of Python Programming desirable.

subject: CEE
title: Risk Analysis and Decision Making
description: Risk analysis and decision making are fundamental areas of construction and project management. Students will benefit from analyzing risks and learning various decision making techniques for real-time applications.
prereq_raw: CEE 472 (with a minimum grade of B) and CEE 474 (with a minimum grade of B), or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) and CEE 474 ( with a minimum grade of B ) , or consent

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice-negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

subject: CEE
title: Parallel Computing for Engineers
description: Concepts and techniques in high performance parallel computing. Topics include parallel language and algorithms, parallelizing pre-existing serial codes, statistical analysis, and techniques up to increase computational speed and accuracy for problems requiring large memory size.

subject: CEE
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BE, CEE, ECE, ME majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

subject: CEE
title: Fluid Mechanics
description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.
prereq_raw: CEE 627 with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: CEE
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

subject: CEE
title: Surface Water Hydrology
description: Deterministic and probabilistic methods include reliability of empirical distributions, multiple regression analysis, extreme value analysis and domain of attraction. Short-memory models for stochastic simulation of streamflows include autoregressive, Markov chain and moving average models. Time series analysis of hydrologic data is discussed.

subject: CEE
title: Groundwater Hydrology
description: Groundwater occurrence, movement, quality, and resource evaluation, development, and management. Emphasis on saltwater encroachment, well evaluation, aquifer protection, recharge with wastewater, and Hawaiʻi type hydrology.

subject: CEE
title: Physical and Chemical Treatment
description: Introduction to physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment: Review of momentum and mass transfer, chemical reactions, colloidal chemistry, coagulation and flocculation, granular filtration, sedimentation, carbon adsorption, gas transfer, disinfection and oxidation.

subject: CEE
title: Biological Treatment
description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Chemistry
description: Basic concepts of chemistry as related to the environment, with more emphasis on water. Topics include chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base, precipitation and dissolution redox reactions, sorption, organic chemicals in the environment.

subject: CEE
title: Environmental Microbiology
description: Combined lecture-discussion on major topics in environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, and a broad understanding of microbial processes in natural and engineered environments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in CEE or consent. CEE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Applied Mathematics for Engineers
description: Application of advanced mathematics to engineering phenomena; linear algebra, Eigen systems; partial differentiation and multiple integrals; vector/tensor analysis; Fourier series/transforms and Laplace transform; ordinary/partial differential equations; probability and statistics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ME, ORE, and ECE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: CEE
title: Hazardous Waste Remediation
description: Introduces the national problems dealing with the contamination of groundwater and presents remedial measures. Such measures include pump and treat (PAT) technology, in-situ bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, electrokinetics, hydraulic fracturing, reactive walls, and phytoremediation.

subject: CEE
title: Water Quality Modeling
description: Mathematical formulation of pollutant transport and mixing in the water environment. Kinetics formulation and parameter identification, model calibration and verification. Design projects.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 422 and CEE 431 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Membrane Separations
description: Applications of membrane separations to desalination, power generation, and ultrapure water systems. Discussion of reverse osmosis, osmosis-driven processes, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, electrodialysis and ion exchange technologies. Membrane fouling and concentration polarization from practical/theoretical standpoints.

subject: CEE
title: Seepage, Drainage, and Dewatering
description: Theory of seepage, field and laboratory methods of measurement; graphical and numerical methods; design of drainage structures; construction dewatering.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Deep Foundations
description: Analysis and design of deep foundations; driven piles and drilled shafts.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D ) and CEE 455 ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Numerical Methods in Geotechnical Engineering
description: Finite element and finite difference formulation and analyses to solve problems in geotechnical engineering. Also covers constitutive modelling.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of C) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) and CEE 455 ( with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
description: Soil continuum mechanics principles; elastic, plastic, and Cam clay soil behavior; critical state and strength; interpretation of laboratory test results.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Slope and Earth Structures
description: Classification of landslides and triggering mechanisms; field investigation procedures; limit equilibrium slope stability methods; numerical techniques; seepage and dynamic considerations; case studies.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Marine Geotechnics
description: Principles of geotechnical engineering applied to marine environments; marine geology; surveying and sampling methods; seabed sediment types, properties, and behavior; coastal and offshore foundations.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Earth Pressures
description: Estimation of lateral earth pressures; analysis and design of retaining walls and excavation support systems.
prereq_raw: CEE 355 (with a minimum grade of D) and CEE 455 (with a minimum grade of D).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of D ) and CEE 455 ( with a minimum grade of D )

subject: CEE
title: Systems Analysis for Engineers
description: Optimization used in design and management of systems for minimizing resources or optimizing outcomes. Evaluation of alternatives, economic efficiency and effectiveness analysis. Logistics. Open to engineering students. Computer applications and labs.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 462 or CEE 464 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
description: Definition, technologies and their attributes. Analysis and implementation based on FHWA’s User Services. Automated incident detection algorithms. Machine vision applications to traffic engineering.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 462 or CEE 464 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Transportation Modeling and Statistics
description: Demand modeling, discrete choice and activity-based modeling. Demand forecasting by simulation. Transportation surveys and sampling methods. Application of cluster, factor, regression, logistic and ARIMA analyses to transportation.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 305 and CEE 464 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Pavement Design and Rehabilitation
description: Pavement engineering with emphasis given to understanding fundamental issues such as historical development of pavement design, approaches used for design of new pavements and overlays, understanding of construction issues and their effects on pavement performance, and various design factors: environmental, loading and materials characterization. Introduction of pavement management systems.

subject: CEE
title: Continuum Mechanics
description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics; coordinate transformations; analysis of stress and strain; principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations; constitutive relations; field equations. Problems in elasticity.
prereq_raw: Recommended: CEE 370 or ME 371 , or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Project Management Systems
description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding.

subject: CEE
title: Negotiation
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

subject: CEE
title: Working with Entrepreneurs and Startups
description: Project-oriented course in which a team of students will work with a real local startup and entrepreneur to develop a business idea and/or viable business plan.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics I
description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity.

subject: CEE
title: Structural Dynamics II
description: Elastic and inelastic response of structures due to earthquakes. Seismic design criteria. Code design procedures. Advanced topics in time- and frequency-domain dynamic analysis of structures.

subject: CEE
title: Smart Structures Technology
description: Fundamentals of sensor technologies for structural engineering applications. Control devices and strategies for protection of structures against extreme events, i.e. earthquakes, strong winds, etc. Structural health monitoring and smart sensor networks. Smart materials for civil structures.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE majors only.

subject: CEE
title: Modern Structural Analysis
description: Fundamentals of modern structural analysis theory, with emphasis on frame structures. Virtual work. Member stiffness/flexibility. Matrix formulation of stiffness and flexibility methods. Computer modeling issues.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
description: Slender columns; biaxial bending; combined shear and torsion. Building lateral load resisting frame analysis and design-shearwalls, rigid frames. Floor system analysis and design-flat slabs, joist systems. Computer applications.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
description: Load and resistance factored design (LRFD); steel building modeling and analysis; moment-resisting frames; bracing systems; beam-columns; moment connections; composite construction; and plate girders.

subject: CEE
title: Finite Elements in Structures
description: Finite element method in structural engineering. Extension of structural theory. Virtual work. One- two-, and three-dimensional elements; axisymmetric elements; plate bending. Application to linear problems.

subject: CEE
title: Prestressed Concrete
description: Behavior of prestressed concrete members, including prestress losses. Analysis and design of prestressed beams, slabs, and composite sections. Anchorage zone design; continuous systems.

subject: CEE
title: Advanced Concrete Technology
description: Composition and hydration of concrete, chemical, and mineral admixtures, fresh and hardened properties, mix proportions, high performance concretes, durability and retrofitting technology, non-destructive testing, and advanced material characterization techniques.
prereq_raw: CEE 375 (with a minimum grade of C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: CEE
title: Seminar in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Discussions and reports on literature, research, developments and activities in civil engineering. One unit of all graduate students for each graduate degree. Student presentations are required.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in CEE or consent.

subject: CEE
title: Selected Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
description: Highly specialized topics in structures, soils, hydraulics, sanitary, water resources, applied mechanics, transportation.

subject: CEE
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: CEE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Candidacy for PhD in civil engineering.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Introduction to Chamorro, emphasis on listening and speaking, language structure. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Elementary Chamorro
description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills; emphasis on oral and reading proficiency. Meets five hours weekly.

subject: CHAM
title: Intermediate Chamorro

subject: CHEM
