title: Overseas Internship in China
description: Supervised internships in a Chinese-speaking institution in China. Students must pass CHN 486 with a B- or higher and be accepted to the Flagship Capstone Year in China to take this.
prereq_raw: CHN 461 and CHN 485 and CHN 486 (with a minimum grade of B- or better) and proficiency assessment and acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- or better ) and proficiency assessment and acceptance to Flagship Capstone year in China

subject: CHN
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

subject: CHN
title: Introduction to Study of Contemporary Chinese Linguistics
description: Panoramic overview of major perspectives in contemporary Chinese linguistics. Readings on recent developments of fields. Report on selected research papers and present analysis of linguistic phenomena of interest.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Chinese Poetry
description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th-10th century).
prereq_raw: CHN 461 or consent for (B), CHN 610B or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Poetry: ancient (to 5th century)
description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th-10th century).
prereq_raw: CHN 461 or consent for (B), 610B or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Poetry: medieval (5th-10th century)
description: Critical study of major traditional Chinese poetic forms. (B) ancient (to 5th century); (C) medieval (5th-10th century).
prereq_raw: CHN 461 or consent for (B), CHN 610B or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction
description: Formal and thematic analysis of short stories, historical romances, and novels.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) History of Chinese Language
description: (B) phonology; (C) syntax.
prereq_raw: CHN 451 , LING 421 , or consent for (B); CHN 452 or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: History of Chinese Language: phonology
description: (B) phonology; (C) syntax.
prereq_raw: CHN 451 , LING 421 , or consent for (B); CHN 452 or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: History of Chinese Language: syntax
description: (B) phonology; (C) syntax.
prereq_raw: CHN 451 , LING 421 , or consent for (B); CHN 452 or consent for (C).

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Dialects
description: Synchronic description of a Chinese dialect other than Cantonese and Mandarin; contrastive and comparative studies with Mandarin.

subject: CHN
title: Chinese Syntax and Semantics
description: Verbal categories, aspects, focus devices, resultative and directional compounds, coverbial constructions. Interaction between syntax and semantics.

subject: CHN
title: Contrastive Analysis of Mandarin and English

subject: CHN
title: Methods in Teaching Chinese as Second Language
description: Problems in language learning and teaching. Practice in preparing and presenting lessons with materials based on comparative linguistic analysis. Materials, teaching aids, test construction.

subject: CHN
title: Practicum: Teaching Chinese Language
description: For graduate students pursuing teaching Chinese language. Students gain practical skills and hands-on experiences in creating instructional and assessment materials and teaching an actual Chinese language class using the self-developed materials effectively.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Topics in Chinese Language
description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar.

subject: CHN
title: Topics in Chinese Language: teaching and testing
description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar.

subject: CHN
title: Topics in Chinese Language: cognitive grammar
description: Extensive studies of selected topics (B) teaching and testing: specific problems in teaching Chinese including characters and cultural elements; proficiency and communicative ability; (C) cognitive grammar.

subject: CHN
title: Current Topics in Chinese Grammar
description: Current approaches to Chinese grammar and related issues and debates, focusing on the papers published by leading Chinese linguists employing these approaches.
prereq_raw: CHN 452 , CHN 455 , or CHN 456 ; or consent.

subject: CHN
title: Second Semester Classical Chinese
description: Builds on the foundation laid in CHN 461 ; introduces complex syntactic patterns, advanced vocabulary; teaches sophisticated reading strategies and cultural literary contexts; exposes students to a wide range of intermediate level texts.

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar in Chinese Language
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: teaching methods
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: structure
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: classical grammar
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Language: sociolinguistics
description: (B) teaching methods; (C) structure; (D) classical grammar; (E) sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: CHN 643 for (B) and (E); CHN 452 for (C) and (D).

subject: CHN
title: (Alpha) Research Seminar in Chinese Literature
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: EALL 611 , WGSS 613 , WGSS 615 , or WGSS 650 ; or consent for (M); CHN 612 , or consent for (T).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature: modern
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: EALL 611 , WGSS 613 , WGSS 615 , or WGSS 650 ; or consent for (M); CHN 612 , or consent for (T).

subject: CHN
title: Research Seminar in Chinese Literature: traditional
description: Study of authors, a genre, a period, or a problem. (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: EALL 611 , WGSS 613 , WGSS 615 , or WGSS 650 ; or consent for (M); CHN 612 , or consent for (T).

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinematic Digital Production
description: Introduction to the basic techniques of cinematic digital production and allows students to explore their personal voice in this process.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to 3D Animation
description: A basic overview of the 3D animation production process, including modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, and rendering.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to 2D Animation
description: Introduction to traditional styles and methods of hand drawn 2D, digital, and stop motion animation through theory and practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Introduction to Cinema and Digital Media
description: Introduction to the study of cinema: history, aesthetics, and cultural impact.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Narrative Production
description: Production-intensive course with collaborative as well as individual projects. Theories and application of basic digital cinema productions, including camera, lighting, sound, and editing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematography
description: Comprehensive course in visual styles supporting screen narratives through a study of principles of camera elements, operations, lighting, color and composition. Professional role and responsibilities of cinematographer. Project-oriented.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Experimental Art and Animation
description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
prereq_raw: CINE 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE 353 / DNCE 353 / THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE 356 / DNCE 356 / THEA 356 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Modeling
description: Essential principles of 3D modeling in order to create both organic character models and hard surface models. Students will create high-quality, animation-ready 3D models with textures and poses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life through the principles of 3D animation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: 3D Lighting, Camera, and Rendering
description: Students develop the ability to manipulate light, shadow, and color within a virtual 3D space. Rendering and cinematography for 3D animation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Storyboarding and Animatics
description: Exposes students to the history, application, format, styles, and methods of creating storyboards and animatics. Visual storytelling will be analyzed by examining the foundational components of the visual language of a film.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Visual Development for Animation
description: Visual design and development for animated characters and environments. Students will create concept art, character and prop designs, movement styles, backgrounds, and layouts for animation pre-production.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Movement Study for Animation
description: Creating the illusion of life and expressive movement through the principles of 2D animation: timing, spacing, physics, staging, anatomy, attitude, and acting.

subject: CINE
title: Motion Graphics
description: A project-based introduction to motion graphics using Adobe After Effects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Producing
description: Fundamentals of producing for independent filmmaking, focusing on business acumen and role of the producer through various stages of production. Topics include proposal writing, script breakdowns, budgeting, scheduling, legal issues, festival strategy, and distribution.
prereq_raw: CINE 255 ; and one of CINE 215 , CINE 216 , or CINE 310 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting
description: Introduction to the basics of writing a short narrative screenplay for film or animation. Students learn the fundamentals and format of screenwriting as well as basic elements of storytelling and character development.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Screening Asian Americans
description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: CINE
title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process.
prereq_raw: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent. (Consent required for production experience option).

children.text: ( Consent required for production experience option)

subject: CINE
title: Oral Tradition to Screenplay
description: Adapting the stories, styles, and cultural values of oral tradition storytelling to cinematic narratives.

subject: CINE
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices.

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Aesthetics
description: Aesthetic theories and practices of indigenous cultures of the Pacific and their adaptation to the screen in cinematic storytelling.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Actor on Screen
description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances with actors from the Theatre program.
prereq_raw: CINE 215 , CINE 216 , or CINE 310 ; and CINE 350 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Editing for Cinema
description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Post-Production Sound
description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on projects involving dialogue and sound effects in post-production.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Camera for the Screen
description: Detailed analysis of cinematic grammar, placement, movement, focus, and effects of the camera to create the mise-en-scene. Practical exercises to apply theory to individual creative work and in collaboration with actors from the Theatre program.
prereq_raw: ( CINE 310 , or CINE 215 and CINE 216 ), and CINE 350 , and CINE 370 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Dialogue Replacement and Foley
description: This project-based, collaboration-oriented course examines the procedures and practices of recording and editing dialogue replacement tracks (ADR or looping) and sound effects tracks (Foley) in film, video, or animation productions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Environmental Filmmaking
description: Analysis and community co-production of environmental films covering story development and structure, production, post-production, distribution, and outreach.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Genre and Narrative Theory in Cinematic Arts
description: Focus on the concept of genre, genre films, genre film criticism, and popular genres such as the Western, film noir, and Chinese martial arts.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Studies
description: In-depth study of the nature, history, and impact of documentary filmmaking traditions around the world, focusing on the interplay between filmmaker, subject, and audience.

subject: CINE
title: Authors in Cinematic Arts
description: In-depth study of the auteur theory and specific application to the authors in cinematic arts, such as film directors, animators, or screenwriters.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics.

subject: CINE
title: (Alpha) Study Abroad
description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or cinematic production in the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. (B) cinematic studies; (C) cinematic practice.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable once for up to 6 credits combined for B and C alphas.

subject: CINE
title: Study Abroad: Cinematic Studies
description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or cinematic production in the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. (B) cinematic studies; (C) cinematic practice.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable once for up to 6 credits combined for B and C alphas.

subject: CINE
title: Study Abroad: Cinematic Practice
description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or cinematic production in the host country in a UH Mānoa-approved study abroad location. (B) cinematic studies; (C) cinematic practice.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable once for up to 6 credits combined for B and C alphas.

subject: CINE
title: Topics in Cinematic Arts
description: Topics of study and critical inquiry in a variety of areas in the cinematic arts. Taught by regular and visiting faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Techniques in Cinematic Arts
description: Specialized techniques in the creation of digital media: taught by regular and visiting faculty.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Workshop in Cinematic Arts
description: Intensive workshop in focused area of cinematic arts production.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Independent Group Project
description: Participation in a group research or creative project under supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of CINE 399/ CINE 499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.
prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent; and one of the following: CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , or CINE 330 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Documentary Production
description: Analysis and practical knowledge of the documentary process including, but not limited to, research, organization and story structure, shooting, camera coverage, and editing.
prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of the following: CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , or CINE 374 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematic Production
description: Production of a major cinematic/digital narrative project. Working in groups, each student takes on creative and technical role and responsibilities of a principal crew position. Emphasis on artistic form in narrative development; timely execution from pre- to post-production.
prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , or CINE 374 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Cinematography
description: Applies the basic foundations, techniques, and theory of cinematography (covered in CINE 312 ) to a more informed and crafted practice with Camera and Lighting Scene study workshops, and research exercises and film projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production I
description: Students work independently to produce a short, animated film. Emphasis on visual storytelling and character animation.
prereq_raw: CINE 317 or ( CINE 321 , CINE 322 , and CINE 323 ); and CINE 350 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.
prereq_raw: any CINE 215 or ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 .

subject: CINE
title: Animation Production II
description: Student teams produce a short, animated film. Prior knowledge of 2D and 3D media authoring tools and animation techniques is necessary.
prereq_raw: CINE 317 or ( CINE 321 , CINE 322 , and CINE 323 ); and CINE 350 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Advanced Screenwriting
description: Application of narrative principles of character development, story structure, and thematic spine to screenplays for live action and animated short films, television, or transmedia projects. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Indigenous Filmmaking
description: Theories and studies of indigenous films and creation of a cinematic project based in indigenous cultural and value systems.
prereq_raw: CINE 310 , CINE 350 , and one of CINE 312 , CINE 330 , CINE 370 , CINE 372 , CINE 374 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Ethics and Film
description: Ethical theory and dilemmas as reflected in film and filmmaking. Social responsibility for filmmakers.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Directing the Motion Picture
description: Students direct a narrative live-action short film from pre- through post-production, learning how to develop a directorial vision and how to implement it through storyboarding, scheduling, and collaborative skill sets.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Screenwriting Capstone
description: Culmination of beginning and advanced screenwriting classes. Students will write a treatment and first act for a feature-length project or pilot script and series bible for a television project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Oceanic Media and Culture
description: Involves close textual analysis of film, TV and multimedia content. The course includes cinematic and television screenings. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CINE
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CINE
title: Seminar in Cinematic Arts
description: Intellectual issues in cinematic arts. Conducted by regular and visiting faculty with extensive student participation and scholarly presentation.
prereq_raw: CINE 255 and junior standing, or consent.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time on different topics.

subject: CINE
title: Capstone Cinematic Production
description: Emphasis on advanced production skills in creating a capstone project in live-action fiction film, animation, documentary, or new media. Screenwriting students may also develop a feature screenplay or television pilot and series bible.
prereq_raw: CINE 405 or CINE 410 or CINE 420 or CINE 455 or CINE 475 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any CINE 215 or ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 .

subject: CINE
title: Global Media
description: Close textual analysis and strategic analysis of global media dynamics with an emphasis on transnational media corporations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Cinematic Arts Internship
description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision.
prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent; and one of the following: CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , or CINE 330 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CINE
title: Directed Study
description: Independent research or creative project under the supervision of a faculty member. Only six credits of CINE 399 /499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.
prereq_raw: CINE 350 and consent, and one of CINE 310 , CINE 315 , CINE 316 , CINE 317 , CINE 321 , CINE 322 , CINE 323 , CINE 330 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA majors only.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Theories of Society
description: A critical review of major theoretical and empirical traditions in communication and information sciences. Focus on European, American, Third World, and applied research.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Technologies
description: Technological concepts underlying data communications; information processing and computers; communication channels and networks, information storage and retrieval, and computer hardware and software.

subject: CIS
title: Communication/Information Research Methods
description: Current research methodologies in decision sciences, computer science, library science, and communication. Emphasis on methodologies suitable for interdisciplinary analysis.

subject: CIS
title: Special Topics in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Seminar reflecting research interests of faculty and current interdisciplinary topics in communication and information sciences.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Data Science Foundations
description: All aspects of data science: the methodology and processes; ethics and regulatory issues; programming tools; data acquisition, cleaning, analysis and mining; visualization, publication, curation, and preservation; applications in various fields.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: CIS
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Communication and Information Sciences
description: Exploration of relationships between disciplines in social sciences, science and technology, and humanities. Faculty and student presentations.

subject: CIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses.
prereq_raw: consent. Plan must include goals and rationale.

children.text: Plan must include goals and rationale

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egypt: Mummies, Pharaohs, and Gods
description: An overview of ancient Egyptian civilization through lectures and class discussion on Egyptian literature, archaeology, history, religion and society.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek, Roman, and Ancient Mythology
description: Combines readings and analyses of myths from the ancient world including Europe, Asia, Africa, and Hawaiʻi, with an emphasis on comparative analysis of cultures and religions.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Latin Elements in English
description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a literary vocabulary.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Latin Elements in Scientific Terminology
description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a scientific vocabulary.

subject: CLAS
title: Introduction to World Mythology
description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

subject: CLAS
title: Understanding Ancient Religions
description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome.

subject: CLAS
title: Myth, Religion, and Society
description: Survey of major theories and methods for analyzing myth, ritual, and religious practice, drawing on anthropology, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology. Emphasis on developing core analytical skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Biblical Hebrew I
description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: Biblical Hebrew II
description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions.
prereq_raw: CLAS 301 / REL 301 with C- or better.

subject: CLAS
title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics I
description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics II
description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts, including Tale of Sinuhe.

subject: CLAS
title: History of the Written Word
description: A hands-on history of writing beginning in Ancient Greece and Rome. Content includes the development of the alphabet, scripts, books, libraries, and writing in ancient culture. Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: Classics Ancient and Modern
description: Provides an in-depth introduction to a major work of classical literature and its impact on both ancient and modern poetry, prose, art, and intellectual history. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Drama
description: Survey of Greek and Roman drama, both tragedies and comedies, tracing the history of a genre that contains some of the wittiest and most agonizing moments in ancient literature.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Nature in the Ancient World
description: Study of the relationship between the Greeks and Romans and the natural environment. Particular attention will be given to the place of nature in ancient science, philosophy, literature, and “real life.” Assignments are essay-based.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman War Literature
description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: The Greek and Roman Novel
description: Survey of Greek and Roman novels, a collection of highly entertaining texts that offer windows into various aspects of life in the ancient world.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Homer, drama, and philosophy. Assignments are essay-based and attention is given to developing academic writing skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: Ancient Roman Literature in Translation
description: Major writers: emphasis on Vergil, satire, and novel.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: Greek and Roman Epic
description: A survey of Greek and Roman epic literature, beginning with Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey and proceeding through the Hellenistic Greek and Roman periods.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: CLAS
title: Topics in Ancient Greek Thought
description: Explore ancient Greek philosophy and literature through themes, thinkers, and monumental texts. Course instruction will emphasize the development of writing skills through regular writing, feedback, and such techniques as peer editing and revision.

subject: CLAS
title: Archaeology of Ancient Greece
description: Introduction to the field of Greek archaeology and methods of archaeological research in the Mediterranean.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Archaeology of Ancient Rome
description: Examines the archaeology of the Roman world from the Etruscan period to the reign of the emperor Constantine.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. Junior standing or higher.

subject: CLAS
title: Literatures of Ancient India
description: Survey of South Asia literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation. Emphasis on written communication.

subject: CLAS
title: Art of Greece and Rome
description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome.

subject: CLAS
title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age

subject: COA
title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
description: Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging.

subject: COA
title: Ethics, Aging & Society
description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging.

subject: COA
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences.

subject: COA
title: Adult Development and Aging
description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death.

subject: COA

description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level sociology course, or consent.

subject: COA
title: On Death and Dying
description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves.

subject: COA
title: Directed Reading and Research for Freshmen and Sophomores

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen and sophomores only.

subject: COA
title: Aging and Disability Policy: Intersections in Health
description: Examines health programs and policies that help kupuna and persons with disabilities stay healthy and independent, including Medicare. Will engage with local community partners for meaningful intergenerational activities and project-based learning.

subject: COA
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.

subject: COA

subject: COA
title: Directed Reading and Research for Juniors and Seniors

subject: COM

description: Adapting communication theory to forensic strategies for social action. Practice in formal argument.

subject: COMG
title: Leadership and Organizational Communication
description: Principles and practices of organizational communication and its relationship to networks, leadership, power, conflict, cultures, and other contemporary views of organizational work, change, and development.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion
description: Theories, concepts, strategies, and processes of persuasion and social influence in contemporary society. Focus on analyzing, developing, and resisting persuasive messages.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Introduction to theory and research on human communication, comprehension, creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories. Topics include prediction, inference-making, communication systems, and deception.

subject: COMG
title: Family Communication
description: Focuses on the role of interaction patterns (both constructive and destructive) in the evolution of family communications. The impact of family dynamics upon these interaction patterns is given equal attention.

subject: COMG
title: Interpersonal Relations
description: Theory and research on the development, maintenance, and termination of interpersonal relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Culture and Communication
description: Survey of major factors affecting interpersonal communication between members of different cultures. Emphasis upon interaction between U.S. and Asian-Pacific peoples.

subject: COMG
title: Special Topics in Culture and Communication
description: Contemporary research and theory on intercultural communication.

subject: COMG
title: Interrogation and Interviewing
description: Survey of theory and research on the communicative demands of obtaining reliable information from others.

subject: COMG
title: Evolution and Human Communication
description: Analysis of the role of human communication in mate attraction, intrasexual competition, cooperation, family dynamics, and coalition formation; discussion on the biological function of language, laughter, yawning, and emotion expressions.

subject: COMG
title: Research on Communication Behavior
description: Survey of research on communication behavior. Verbal and nonverbal data collection; analysis of research data. Students design and implement a research project.

subject: COMG
title: Internship
description: Analysis and application of communication knowledge and behaviors in organizational settings.

subject: COMG
title: Social Identity and Intergroup Communication
description: Surveys theory and research on communication between members of different social groups, highlighting how communication influences and is influenced by social identity. Applies concepts to intergenerational, health, family, educational, multilingual, and computer-mediated contexts.

subject: COMG
title: Political Communication
description: Survey of interpersonal and mass communication theories in the political context. Topics may include communication in public opinion processes, elections, debates, political campaigning and advertising.

subject: COMG
title: Conflict Management
description: Examination of the theories, assumptions, practices, models, and techniques of managing interpersonal conflicts.

subject: COMG
title: Science Communication
description: Introduction to principles for communicating science information effectively to a variety of audiences including the general public, policymakers, and professional peers. Application of these principles to create written and oral science communication products.

subject: COMG
title: Human Communication and Technology
description: Analysis of evolving communicative exchanges in the Internet age including how people communicate with computer technology: focus on personal, interpersonal, and cultural effects associated with technology use.

subject: COMG
title: Theories and Research in Strategic Communication
description: An in-depth overview of theories related to strategic communication and scientific approaches to attitude formation and changes. Junior standing or higher.

subject: COMG
title: Nonverbal Communication
description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance.

subject: COMG
title: Verbal Communication
description: Roles of language in human communication and social relationships; language variation, change, and social consequences.

subject: COMG
title: Deceptive Communication
description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/ discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Management
description: Survey and critical discussion of current theory and research in relational management. Focus on written analysis of the role of communication in the initiation, maintenance, decline, and dissolution of different types of relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships and professional relationships.

subject: COMG
title: Teaching Speech
description: For communicology majors who lead, under supervision, a freshman seminar section of communicology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

subject: COMG
title: Health Communication
description: Develop understanding of the process through which communication influences health outcomes, and learn how to design effective health communication programs using theory and research.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Reading
description: Pre: consent of department chair and instructor.

subject: COMG
title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
description: Enrollment for degree completion.
prereq_raw: master’s Plan B candidate and consent.

subject: COMG
title: Theories in Communicology
description: Survey and examination of theories addressing human communication. Social scientific theoretical foundations of creating understanding, interpersonal communication, and persuasion. Emphasis on scholarly writing.

subject: COMG
title: Research Methods in Communicology
description: Design and analysis of quantitative research in communicology. Focus on measurement issues, research design, descriptive and inferential statistics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COMG majors only.

subject: COMG
title: Advanced Research Methods in Communicology
description: Advanced focus on survey, laboratory, and field study design, data collection, and data analysis. Emphasis on control of variance through design and statistical analysis. Appropriate preparation for graduate theses and dissertations.

subject: COMG
title: Practicum for Instructional Communication
description: Combined seminar and lecture/ discussion format on techniques and procedures for teaching communication skills and their related components in a laboratory setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COMG majors only.

subject: COMG
title: Business Communication
description: Analysis of communication issues in business through discussion of verbal/nonverbal messages, interpersonal relationships, conflict, and persuasion. Focus on interviewing, group communication, and public speaking skills.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Persuasion and Social Influence
description: Theories of persuasion and resistance to persuasion; assessment of attitudes and measurement of change.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Creating Understanding
description: Theory and research on human communication, social cognition, comprehension, and creation of understanding. Discussion of information and message processing theories, metacognition, prediction, inference-making, and communication systems.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Relational Communication
description: Major models and theories of interpersonal communication; research on interpersonal relationships; interaction and functions of human communication.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Foundations of Intercultural Communication
description: Major models, theories, and concepts of intercultural communication; basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to intercultural communication; research on intercultural communication. Graduate standing only.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Directed Research
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times. Only 3 credits can count toward degree.

subject: COMG
title: Approaches to Instructional Communication
description: Seminar on communication theories and models in instructional environment; emphasis on message processing, classroom dynamics, cognitive and metacognitive processes associated with learning, and learning assessment.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Research in Intergroup Communication
description: Theory, concepts, research, and application of communication processes between members of different social groups.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Special Topics in Communicology
description: Substantive areas in communication that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other COMG courses. Topics vary each semester. Content to be announced.
prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B), or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Persuasion and Influence
description: Contemporary research in persuasion and influence.
prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Issues in Creating Understanding
description: Contemporary research in verbal and nonverbal message processing.
prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Relational Communication
description: Contemporary research in interpersonal relations.
prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Research on Intercultural Communication
description: Functional approach to the study of communication in intercultural settings. Examination of culture-based variables and their impact on social influence, relational management, and message processing.
prereq_raw: ( COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: COMG
title: Artificial Intelligence and Communication
description: Comprehensive understanding of the role and function of computer technology (including. A.I.) within the field of communication. Basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to semi-intelligent artifacts as information source or receiver. COMG majors or consent.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: COMG
title: Seminar in Health Communication Research
description: Contemporary interpersonal and/or public communication issues in health communication research. Topics include communication functions such as information management, interpersonal influence, relational management, emotional management, social influence.
prereq_raw: COMG 601 (or concurrent) or COMG 602 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: CSD
title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing.

subject: CSD
title: Phonetics
description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and models; cultural variations; analysis interpretation and other considerations related to speech sound development and production.

subject: CSD
title: Speech and Language Development
description: Will develop an understanding of children’s acquisition of speech, language, and normal communication development from birth through adolescence.

subject: CSD
title: Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Speech and Hearing
description: Provides an understanding of the fundamental processes underlying the production and perception of speech. Students gain an understanding of the physical and psychological aspects of sound and their measurement.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Clinical Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Provides observation and discussion of the clinical management of individuals with communication disorders, and practical experience related to clinical procedures and requirements.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Information and theoretical foundations serve as an introduction to the field of communication disorders. Will provide an overview of the normal processes and disorders of speech, language, hearing, and swallowing.

subject: CSD
title: Introduction to Audiometry and Auditory Disorders
description: Covers anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, acoustic, basic knowledge of auditory disorders and testing procedures, and introduction to rehabilitative audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Basic Statistics for Health-Related Professionals
description: Provides students from behavioral sciences and health-related professions with an overview of normal distribution, central tendency, variability, sampling, hypothesis testing, frequency distribution, correlation, regression, and t-test.

subject: CSD
title: Research Methods
description: Research methods applicable to the field of speech-language pathology and audiology; analysis and reporting of data. Required of all CSD graduate students.
prereq_raw: previous coursework in inferential statistics and consent.

subject: CSD
title: Neuroscience in Communication Sciences and Disorders
description: Explores the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the human nervous system as it relates to communication and swallowing and how neurological pathologies lead to behavioral deficits in those areas.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CSD majors only.

subject: CSD
title: Audiological Foundations for Speech- Language Pathology
description: Instrumentation; special tests of hearing.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Motor Speech Disorders
description: Provides in-depth examination of various motor speech disorders, including apraxia of speech and dysarthria. Emphasis is on assessment/treatment of these diagnoses. Review of current treatment literature, anatomy/physiology, practical exercises in treatment planning.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Phonology and Articulation
description: Study of the etiology, assessment, and remediation of disorders and articulation.

subject: CSD
title: Child Language Disorders
description: Study of the etiology, behavioral characteristics and treatment methods for child language disorders. Examination of methods, test, and instruments employed in diagnosis of child language disorders. Includes identification of language deficits and writing intervention goals.

subject: CSD
title: Language Development for Children with Hearing Deficiencies
description: Language acquisition by hard-of-hearing and deaf children; methods of stimulating growth.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology I
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, credit earned for 6 credits only.

subject: CSD
title: Audiology Practicum for Speech-Language Pathology
description: Clinical practice in administering tests, interpreting results; counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: CSD
title: Voice Disorders
description: Contemporary development and theoretical issues in the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of vocal system disorders in children and adults; current literature and clinical practice issues are addressed.

subject: CSD
title: Adult Neurogenic Language and Cognitive-Communication Disorders
description: Study of acquired adult language and cognitive-communication disorders associated with stroke, traumatic brain injury, and dementia. Application of evidence-based procedures and strategies for assessment and intervention, review of current literature, and discussion of professional issues.

subject: CSD
title: Research-Speech Pathology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing speech-language pathology.

subject: CSD
title: Research-Audiology
description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing audiology.

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Directed Study
description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area.

subject: CSD
title: Directed Study: language pathology
description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area.

subject: CSD
title: Directed Study: audiology
description: To allow student and faculty advisor to design research/study units outside existing academic structure in specialized area.

subject: CSD
title: Amplification: Assessment and Applications
description: Comprehensive study of amplification. Assessment, fitting, evaluation, electroacoustic evaluation, dispensing. Personal instruments and instructional-educational systems.

subject: CSD
title: Disorders of Fluency
description: Contemporary developments and theoretical issues in diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of disorders of fluency such as stuttering in both children and adults.

subject: CSD
title: Electrophysiologic Audiometry
description: Study of early, middle, and late auditory evoked potentials with emphasis on the auditory brainstem response.

subject: CSD
title: Dysphagia: Disorders of Swallowing
description: Explores the dynamics of normal and disordered swallowing across the life span with emphasis on the adult population.
prereq_raw: CSD 601 (with a minimum grade of B-).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CSD majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- )

subject: CSD
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology
description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology: study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology
description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Special Topics in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology: study of contemporary developments in audiology
description: (B) study of contemporary developments in speech/language pathology; (C) study of contemporary developments in audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology II
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, credit earned for 12 credits only.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology II
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results; counseling individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology-Diagnostic Procedures
description: Study of diagnostic procedures as reflected in current literature.

subject: CSD
title: Seminar in Audiology-Rehabilitative Procedures
description: Procedures and philosophies presented in recent literature dealing with rehabilitative phases of audiology.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology III
description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedure with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

subject: CSD
title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

subject: CUL
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Seminar consists of a series of presentations by certificate faculty on topics of ongoing research. Presentations will open current debates about theory and method in cultural studies.

subject: CUL
title: International Cultural Studies: History and Theory
description: Seminar on the history and theory of interdisciplinary cultural studies. The politics of culture are examined in comparative perspective, focusing on their significance for identity formation, intercultural relations, and global flows of images, people and capital. Approaches to the study of media and popular culture are taken up in terms of their relevance for contemporary issues, especially in Hawaiʻi and the Asia/ Pacific/U.S. region.

subject: CUL
title: International Cultural Studies: Research Project
description: Directed reading and research culminating in a project that engages issues in international cultural studies. Types of projects include scholarly essays, community-based projects, performances or exhibitions. Written statement of purpose and self-evaluation required.

subject: DATA
title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

subject: DATA
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Computer Programming
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; ((P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: DATA
title: Introduction to Computer Programming: Python
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: DATA
title: Machine Learning Methods
description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

subject: DATA
title: Network Science Methodology
description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

subject: DATA
title: Data Science Fundamentals
description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

subject: DATA
title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.

subject: DATA
title: Big Data Analytics
description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

subject: DATA
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
description: The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology.
prereq_raw: PHYL 141 , PHYL 141 , and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161 ; or equivalent.

subject: DH
title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities and practices.
prereq_raw: PHYL 141 , PHYL 141L , PHYL 142 , PHYL 142L , and either BIOC 141 or CHEM 161 .

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I
description: Relationship to dentistry, problems, trends, issues; role and functions of dental hygienists to prevent and control chronic oral diseases; preliminary dental hygiene clinical, includes team concepts in dentistry. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene I Lab
description: Application of preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including instrumentation, vital signs, and team concepts in dentistry.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II
description: Basic dental hygiene theory and skills including competencies in health history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, plaque control and support procedures.

subject: DH
title: Basic Dental Hygiene II Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical experiences in basic dental hygiene skills and competencies including history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, and clinic procedures.

subject: DH
title: General Histology
description: Cells, tissues, the organs they make up, and their embryologic origin.

subject: DH
title: Oral Histology and Embryology
description: Cells and tissues as they relate to the oral cavity and the embryological development of the head, neck, and related oral structures.

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography
description: Basic principles of radiation and fundamental information to understand and safely use radiation in dental radiography.

subject: DH
title: Dental Radiography Lab/Clinic
description: (1 3-hr Lab/Clinic) Preparation and evaluation of radiographic survey of patients with varying dentition; methods, and indications of safety considerations in clinical application of roentgen rays.

subject: DH
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups and the larger public.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: DH
title: General Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases and tissue alterations associated with the human body organ systems.

subject: DH
title: Oral Pathology
description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases affecting the teeth and the structures of the oral cavity.

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials
description: Science of dental materials and its application to dentistry and dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Dental Materials Lab/Clinic
description: Laboratory and clinical application of concepts in the science of dental materials.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene
description: Basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene Lab/Clinic
description: (2 1.5-hr Lab/Clinic) Application of basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: Development of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.
prereq_raw: DH 240 , DH 240L , DH 281 , DH 281L , and DH 389 .

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Clinical instruction and application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing, and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.
prereq_raw: DH 240 , DH 240L , DH 281 , DH 281L , and DH 389 .

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: Continued development of dental hygiene concepts, skills, emergency procedures, team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating oral hygiene care of patients. Review and analyze dental periodicals and conduct a case study. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Continuation of DH 375 . Clinical application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care to patients.

subject: DH
title: Pain Control and Local Anesthesia in Dentistry
description: Basic concepts of pain control and local anesthesia in dentistry with appropriate emphasis on psychological preparation, pharmacological preparation, and safe and effective administration of anesthesia in the practice of dental hygiene.

subject: DH
title: Periodontology I
description: Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Periodontology II
description: Continuation of DH 390 . Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Community Health
description: Introduction and application of principles of health education and dental public health (assess, plan, implement and evaluate) into practice in schools, community agencies, and private dental offices; epidemiology and biostatistics. Emphasis on writing.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene I
description: An in-depth knowledge and clinical application of expanded function in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Dental Hygiene I Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II
description: In-depth knowledge, communicated via oral delivery, on development of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modifications in behavior.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

subject: DH
title: Pediatric Growth and Development
description: Focus on the normal growth and development of children based on current clinical practice guidelines and evidence in pediatric research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care. DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
description: Field experience. Clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Management of Pediatric Dental Emergencies
description: Focus on the management of dental emergencies in children.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Dental Hygiene Care of Vulnerable and Special Needs Children
description: Emphasizes community-based oral health promotion, dental disease risk reduction and management in children 0-5 years of age with a focus on vulnerable and special needs populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Community-Based Practice Capstone
description: Provides an opportunity to synthesize, analyze, and develop solutions to an oral health care problem affecting children ages 0-5 years. Requires one credit to be spent in fieldwork to meet course requirements.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical II
description: Advanced clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: DH majors only.

subject: DH
title: Directed Reading, Field Work, or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading, field work, or research for major under supervision in related areas of dentistry and dental hygiene.

subject: DIS
title: Foundations in Disability and Diversity
description: Focuses on disability as a category of diversity and identity, as well as diversity within disability. Different strategies used to increase the freedom or liberty of people with disabilities are critically examined.

subject: DIS
title: Accessible Learning Technology
description: Focuses on creating accessible technology and instructional media, developing long-term resources, advancing accessible social interaction between students and students with instructors, and using case studies as examples of good practices.

subject: DIS
title: Disability History and Culture: From Homer to Hip Hop
description: How have people over many centuries, and from broad geographical perspectives perceived and treated individuals with disabilities? An overview of the history of the conditions in which people with disabilities lived.

subject: DIS
title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, Action Research, mixed methods, and Curriculum Based Assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal.

subject: DIS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

subject: DIS
title: Sexuality & Health
description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

subject: DIS
title: Supporting Multilingual Learners
description: Strategies for identifying and adopting best practices that support all students in inclusive learning environments with an emphasis on STEM curriculum for English Language Learners; (B) science; (C) technology; (D) math.

subject: DIS
title: Applied Disability Service Practicum
description: Supervised field experience in applied disability service. The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

subject: DIS
title: Disability History Through the Ages
description: A historical overview of disability that visits diverse perspectives, attitudes, and treatment toward individuals with disabilities through many centuries, societies, and cultures throughout the world; and how people with disabilities perceived themselves.

subject: DIS
title: Multicultural Issues in Disabilities
description: Provides background and understanding of various Pacific Rim cultural issues in the conceptualization and treatment of individuals with disabilities and their families.

subject: DIS
title: Special Topics in Disability and Diversity Studies
description: Explores disability and diversity across time to gain an understanding and context of issues such as difference, culture, identity, community, privilege, and oppression and how the past affects the present and future.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Disability and Diversity Issues
description: Develop understanding of current issues faced by individuals with disabilities and their families within the disability paradigm and across cultures.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Team Development
description: Develop knowledge and skills to participate effectively on interdisciplinary teams for the common goal of promoting service integration and coordination of education, social, health, mental health, and other services with individuals with disabilities and their families.

subject: DIS
title: Interdisciplinary Assessment
