subject: EALL
title: Chinese Literature: Ancient
description: Survey of all major genres from antiquity until the ninth century. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Chinese Literature: Pre-modern
description: Survey of all major genres from the ninth century till the end of the Qing.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: (Alpha) 20th-Century Chinese Literature and Culture
description: Survey of 20th-century Chinese literature in translation. Includes a variety of genres from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong: (B) 1919-1949; (C) 1949-present; emphases on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: (Alpha) Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation
description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation: short story
description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Traditional Chinese Fiction in Translation: novel
description: Survey of pre-modern Chinese fiction in translation. (B) short story; (C) novel.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: The City in Modern Chinese Literature and Visual Arts
description: Study of the fictional and visual representations of the city in the changing contexts of Chinese modernization from the late imperial age to the beginning of the 21st century.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Traditional Japanese Literature
description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in the classical tradition. No knowledge of Japanese required.
repeatable_raw: 2 times in different topics with consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Modern Japanese Literature
description: Reading and analysis of English translations of selected important works in modern Japanese literature. No knowledge of Japanese required.
repeatable_raw: 2 times in different topics with consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Japanese Cultural Studies
description: Multi-disciplinary and historically located study of Japanese culture through the examination of literary and visual texts. Specific topics will depend upon the term.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Modern Korean Women Writers and Culture
description: Study of fiction by modern Korean women writers in the changing context of Korean culture.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher.

subject: EALL
title: East-West Cultural Encounters
description: Critical examination of encounters between Western and East Asian cultures across time. In addition to literary texts, the course may use sources from other media, and focus on a specific era, region, or genre.
prereq_raw: an EALL course at 200 level or above; or a DH or DL course at 200 level or above; or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture-Chinese Diaspora
description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course.

subject: EALL
title: Perspectives on Chinese Cinema
description: Introduction to Chinese cinema studies, with emphasis on the theoretical and critical approaches to Chinese film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Senior Colloquium in East Asian Literature
description: Comparative perspectives; some works studied in the original.

subject: EALL
title: Current Issues in East Asian Language Pedagogy
description: Survey on East Asian language pedagogy designed to develop students’ familiarity with and facility in addressing the major issues, initiatives, and innovations in the field.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: EALL
title: Introduction to East Asian Linguistics
description: Introduction to cross-linguistic comparison of the writing systems, dialects, history, phonology, morphology, and syntax of Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
prereq_raw: CHN 451 and CHN 452 , or JPN 451 , or KOR 451 and KOR 452 ; or consent.

subject: EALL
title: (Alpha) Bibliographical and Research Methods
description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

subject: EALL
title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Chinese
description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

subject: EALL
title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Japanese
description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

subject: EALL
title: Bibliographical and Research Methods: Korean
description: Traditional and modern references and other library materials basic to research in all areas of East Asian studies: (C) Chinese; (J) Japanese; (K) Korean.
prereq_raw: CHN 402 for (C); JPN 407 (alpha) for (J); KOR 402 for (K).

subject: EALL
title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

subject: EALL
title: Contemporary Chinese Documentary: Record, Expression, Cultural Space
description: Introduction to contemporary Chinese independent documentary with these goals: to achieve in-depth understanding of Chinese society through documentary; be familiar with theoretical debates on documentary form; and understand documentary as a cultural discourse.

subject: EALL
title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.
repeatable_raw: 2 times in different topics, but need consent for second repeat.

subject: EALL
title: Seminar in Comparative East Asian Literature
description: Comparison of authors, modes, topics, and genres in poetry and prose; theoretical and practical criticism.

subject: EALL
title: Seminar in Comparison of East Asian Languages
description: Comparison of lexicon, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, etc., of two or more East Asian languages, contact influence on them.
prereq_raw: CHN 451 , CHN 452 , or JPN 451 ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Electrical Engineering Skills
description: Electrical engineering subjects in a skill acquisition context at the freshman level. Learning, creative problem solving, brainstorming, technical information assimilation, and presentation skills development.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
description: Engineering problem solving using MATLAB. Basic programming concepts include input/output, branching, looping, functions, file input/output, and data structures such as arrays and structures. Matrix operations for solving linear equations. Engineering computations and visualization.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE and CENG majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Programming for Engineers
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to computer programming and modern computing environments with an emphasis on algorithm and program design, implementation, and debugging. Includes a hands-on laboratory to develop and practice programming skills.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN, CNST, and ENGS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Freshman Project
description: Freshman level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. This project provides early student entry into ECE hands-on project activity providing practical skills, ECE subject exposure and experience. Second semester freshman standing required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Second programming for computer engineers. System programming language, such as C. Object-oriented programming paradigm, definition and use of classes, fundamentals of object-oriented design, such as C++. Common data structures. Common searching and sorting algorithms.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CEE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Linear passive circuits, time domain analysis, transient and steady-state responses, phasors, impedance and admittance; power and energy, frequency responses, resonance.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), and PHYS 272 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BENG, CE, CENG, EE, ME, PREN, and ENGS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Basic Circuit Analysis II
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Laplace transforms and their application to circuits, Fourier transforms and their applications to circuits, frequency selective circuits, introduction to and design of active filters, convolution, and state space analysis of circuits.
prereq_raw: ECE 211 , and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of digital systems with an emphasis on design methods and the implementation and use of fundamental digital components.
prereq_raw: ECE 160 or ECE 110 or ICS 111 or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Sophomore Project
description: Sophomore level individual or team project under ECE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ECE
title: Signal and Systems Analysis
description: Discrete-time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
prereq_raw: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I
description: Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and integrated circuit subsystems.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits I Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments on linear and logic properties of diodes and transistor networks.

subject: ECE
title: Physical Electronics
description: Review of quantum mechanics fundamentals, H-atom, and chemical bonding. Introduction to band structure models and materials. Semiconductor doping, charge carrier statistics and charge transport, including ambipolar transport. Metal-semiconductor and PN junctions.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and PHYS 274 ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II
description: Principles and design of linear electronic circuits including differential, operational, feedback, and tuned amplifiers; integrated circuits, current mirrors, signal generators, filters, and stability.

subject: ECE
title: Microelectronic Circuits II Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 326 , experiments on linear and analog electronics. Includes an emphasis on writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Theory and Design of IC Devices
description: Band structure models and carrier transport physics review. Theory and design of semiconductor IC devices: Schottky diodes, bipolar devices (PN junction diodes, BJTs), FETs (MOSFETs, JFETs, and MESFETs).
prereq_raw: ECE 324 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication
description: Technology principles, materials, and methods for the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and microelectromechanical systems.

subject: ECE
title: Microcircuit Fabrication Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on laboratory where students make various electronic and electromechanical micro-devices using IC technology. Devices are also tested and analyzed.

subject: ECE
title: Probability and Statistics
description: Probability, statistics, random variables, distributions, densities, expectations, limit theorems, and applications to electrical engineering.
prereq_raw: ECE 315 (or concurrent) and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Communication Systems
description: Signal representation, Fourier analysis; amplitude and angle modulated systems; sampling theorems, pulse and digital modulation systems; carrier modulation by digital signals.

subject: ECE
title: Communication Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of communication systems. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Networking I
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Covers 4 semesters from the Cisco Networking Academy plus supplementary material; hands-on experience with routers and switches; prepares students for the CCNA. Topics include TCP/IP, LANs, WANs, routing protocols, network security; PPP; ISDN, frame relay.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Algebra and Machine Learning
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Mathematical and algorithmic fundamentals of linear algebra and their applications and illustrations to machine learning. Lab introduces programming with data and uses machine learning libraries for an introduction to commonly used technologies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MATH, CENG, EE, CE, ME, ICS majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems
description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

subject: ECE
title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Provides experience in applying theoretical tools to analyze linear systems. Extensive use is made of computer-aided analysis and design packages study system performance.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design
description: Design methodology, processor design, control design, memory organization, system organization.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Systems and Computer Design Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 361 , experiments on digital systems and interfacing. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Discrete Math for Engineers
description: Logic, sets, number theory, properties of functions, properties of relations, methods of proofs, recursion, counting, probability, trees, graphs, analysis of algorithms, finite state autonoma.

subject: ECE
title: CMOS VLSI Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the design of very large scale integrated (VLSI) systems and use of CAD tools and design languages. Lab includes hands-on use of CAD tools and experiments with field programmable logic devices.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of data structures and algorithms, including correctness and performance. Topics include time complexity, hash tables, sorting, search trees, self-balancing trees, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.
prereq_raw: ( ECE 205 or ICS 212 ) and ( ECE 362 or ICS 241 ).

subject: ECE
title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 367 . Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing laboratory reports.

subject: ECE
title: Cyber-Physical Systems and the Internet of Things
description: Topics include General Purpose Input/Output (GPIO), serial communications, sensors, actuators, low-power wireless communications. TCP/IP networking, dynamic service discovery, distributed network messaging, machine-to-machine communication and cloud-computing interaction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
prereq_raw: ECE 160 or any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or instructor approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
description: Transient and steady-state waves on transmission lines. Plane wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Application of Maxwell’s equations under static and time-varying conditions.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
description: Solution of Maxwell’s equations under various boundary conditions. Introduction to radiation, guided waves, and principles of optics.
prereq_raw: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Engineering Electromagnetics Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of electromagnetics and optics.
prereq_raw: ECE 371 and PHYS 274 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Junior Project
description: Junior level individual or team project under EE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. It may be a continuation of ECE 296 or a new project.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Large-Scale Artificial Intelligence Systems
description: Introduces large language models, focusing on practical aspects of building engineering systems with AI capabilities. Provides hands-on experience with the necessary tools for model development, deployment and integration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, ICS, math, business, and economics majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Computer and Network Security
description: Review basic network mechanisms, introduce basic cryptography concepts, and study algorithms and protocols used in computer and network security. Discuss practical security mechanisms.
prereq_raw: ECE 361 or ICS 312 or ICS 331 or instructor consent.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Signal Processing
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, Z-transform, transform, transform analysis of linear time-invariant systems, filter design, discrete Fourier transform, and computation of discrete Fourier transform.
prereq_raw: ECE 315 and ECE 342 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Optimization
description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CENG, EE, ME, or CBA majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
prereq_raw: ( ECE 160 , ECE 211 , and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or ECE 326 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Instrumentation Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for ECE 422 .

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Analysis and Design
description: Algorithms and techniques used in computer-aided analysis and design of electronic circuits. Circuit simulation with interactive computers.

subject: ECE
title: Electronic Instrumentation II
description: Instrumentation systems and circuits for measurement, control, signal processing, transmission, and detection. Noise and interference, ADC/DAC, modulation demodulation, high-frequency and high-speed techniques, IC applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Si IC and Solid State Devices
description: State of the art Si-based devices including advanced bipolar and MOS devices, heterojunction devices, new device trends. Topics from the most current literature included.
prereq_raw: ECE 327 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A , or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Computer-Aided Circuit Design
description: Application of the computer to the analysis, design, simulation, and construction of analog and digital circuits.

subject: ECE
title: Electric Power Systems
description: Design/operation of “the grid.” History of electric power systems, three-phrase power, real and reactive power, transformers, transmission, distribution, circuit analysis, protection, load flow, load frequency control, optimal power flow, and renewable energy integration.

subject: ECE
title: Renewable Energy
description: Fundamentals of power, electric power grid and conventional electricity generation. Wind and solar power systems. Photovoltaic materials and systems. Distributed generation and energy storage.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Communications
description: Baseband transmission, intersymbol interference and pulse shaping, partial response signaling, equalization, bandpass modulation and demodulation, channel coding, synchronization, multiplexing and multiple access, spread spectrum techniques.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Foundation for algorithms, practice, and theory behind common machine-learning applications. Includes projects, statistical programming, and an introduction to the unique challenges of high-dimensional problems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, CEE, ME, MATH, ICS majors only.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and MATH 307 ( or equivalent)

subject: ECE
title: Information Theory and Coding
description: Models of communication systems. Channel noise, measurement, and coding of information. Intrinsic limits of performance of communication systems.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: ISO Reference Model. Physical Layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer and Transport Layer protocols. Wired and wireless local-area networks. Structure and operation of the Internet including routing, congestion control and flow control.
prereq_raw: ECE 315 and one of ECE 342 , or MATH 371 or MATH 471 ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Control Systems
description: Sampling/reconstruction, Z-transform, DT transfer function. Reachability/observability. State and output feedback, observer design, input-output models, diophantine equations. Implementation procedures.

subject: ECE
title: Modern Control Theory
description: Analysis and synthesis of nonlinear control systems by means of Lagrange’s equation, state space techniques, maximum principle. Lyapunov’s theorems, the phase plane, and Z-transform techniques. Optimization and adaptation by means of gradient methods, calculus of variations, dynamic programming.

subject: ECE
title: Design of Intelligent Robots
description: Study of the design principles of computer-controlled, intelligent robots such as roving vehicles, hand-eye systems.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture
description: Structure of stored program machines, data flow machines, pipelining, fault-tolerant computing, instruction set design, effects of compilation on architecture, RISC vs. CISC architecture, uses of parallelism.

subject: ECE
title: Object-oriented Software Engineering
description: Introduction to advanced techniques for designing, implementing, and testing computer software with a particular focus on using object-oriented design, analysis, and programming to produce high-quality computer programs that solve non-trivial problems.

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Operating Systems
description: Computer system organization; multiprocessor systems, memory hierarchies, assemblers, compilers, operating systems, virtual machine, memory management, processor management; information management. Emphasis on written communication through written assignments on relevant topics.
prereq_raw: ECE 361 (or concurrent) and ECE 367 or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Wireless Data Networks
description: Mobile agent’s platforms and systems, mobile agent-based service implementation, middleware, and configuration, wireless local area networks, wireless protocols, network architecture supporting wireless applications, routing protocols in mobile and wireless networks, handoff in mobile and wireless networks.

subject: ECE
title: Physical Optics
description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
prereq_raw: ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-) or PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) or PHYS 450 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

subject: ECE
title: Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Introduction to computational methods used to simulate/solve engineering design problems focusing on electromagnetics. Finite difference, method of moments, and finite elements methods will be described; students will write computer programs in each.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BE, CENG, EE, ENGR majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Microwave Engineering
description: Passive and active microwave devices and circuits for RF and wireless applications. Scattering parameters, signal-flow graphs, and computer-aided design.

subject: ECE
title: Antennas
description: Electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and ionized media. Geomagnetic and solar effects on the ionosphere. Absorption and dispersion. Antenna arrays, apertures, horns, impedance. Design of antenna systems.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Communications
description: Principles and applications of optical fibers and waveguides. Fundamentals of optical communication systems (optical links, high-speed systems, wavelength-division-multiplexing networks, and network elements) and optical components (guided-wave circuits, lasers, detectors, and optical amplifiers). System and network integration issues.

subject: ECE
title: Fundamentals of Radar, Sonar, and Navigation Systems
description: Discussion of basic radar detection and position- and velocity-measurement principles. Applications to various types of radar and sonar systems. Modern navigation aids.
prereq_raw: ECE 371 (or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory.

children.text: ( or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

subject: ECE
title: Introduction to Biomedical and Clinical Engineering
description: Application of engineering principles and technology to biological and medical problems. Introduction to human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical measurements. Systems modeling, physiological control systems, computer applications, health-related problems.
prereq_raw: ECE 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A .

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: Bioelectric Phenomena
description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Instrumentation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.

subject: ECE
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty; to be oriented toward juniors and seniors. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (G) computer vision; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

subject: ECE
title: Provisional Topics
description: Upper division course with subject matter to be announced.

subject: ECE
title: Ethics in Electrical Engineering
description: Equip electrical engineers with the necessary background for ethical reasoning, as it pertains to technology, society, workplace issues, and the environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CENG and EE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Capstone Design Project
description: Significant project integrating multiple aspects of the design process: reliability, safety, economics, environment, social, ethics, teamwork. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral and written communication.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Reading
description: Investigation of advanced engineering problems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

subject: ECE
title: Graph Theory and Its Applications
description: Graphs and subgraphs, trees and treelike graphs, planar graphs, connectivity and edge-connectivity, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Algorithm I
description: Design and evaluation of machine representations, techniques and algorithms for sorting, pattern processing, computational geometry, mathematical computations, and engineering applications. Introduction to computational issues of time, space, communication, and program correctness.

subject: ECE
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: LISP for machine intelligence applications, or related constraint object and logic-oriented languages.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Large-Scale Artificial Intelligence Systems
description: Explains the technical challenges of developing, deploying, and using large language models. Equips students with the skills to conduct AI research in academia or industry, emphasizing advanced techniques, rigorous evaluation, and ethical considerations in applications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, ICS, math, business, and economics majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: ECE 467 or ICS 313 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Network Algorithms
description: Network algorithms, protocols, and packet switching systems for the internet including TCP/IP, routing algorithms, transmission scheduling, link management, buffer management, and simple network management.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Networks
description: Propagation of signals in fibers, components, modulation and demodulation, transmission system engineering, network systems and architectures, network design, control and management and packet switching.
prereq_raw: ECE 342 , ECE 367 , and ECE 371 ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Computer and Network Security
description: Basic security theory, current practices, and emerging research issues. First covering the fundamentals of computer and network security, then will work on research projects on computer and network security.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
description: An advanced course in digital processing. Topics include fast DFT algorithms, multirate systems and filter banks, power spectrum estimation, linear prediction, optimum linear filters, and adaptive filtering.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Open to nonmajors for CR/NC only.

subject: ECE
title: Digital Image Processing
description: Human visual perception, image formation, sampling and quantization, enhancement and restoration, color image processing, wavelets and multiresolution representations, image and video compression.

subject: ECE
title: Linear and Convex Optimization
description: Algorithms for linear, nonlinear, and convex optimization. Emphasis is on methodology and the underlying mathematical structures. Topics include simplex method, network flow methods, optimality conditions, duality, Newton’s method and interior point methods.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ME, MIS and MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control
description: Sequential decision-making via dynamic programming. Optimal control of stochastic dynamic systems. Applications in linear-quadratic control, inventory control, resource allocation, scheduling, and control of queues. Rollout and other suboptimal methods. Value and policy iteration.
prereq_raw: ECE 342 or MATH 371 or MATH 471 , or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
description: Electronic circuits for precision measurement, computation, and signal processing. Low noise and interference reduction techniques. High-frequency and high-speed techniques. Micro-processor and biomedical applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Solid-State Devices
description: Advanced physical principles and design of modern solid-state electronic devices. Heterostructures, photodetectors, LED, junction lasers, and other devices of current importance identified from the current literature.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics I
description: Fundamentals of optical radiation, including stimulated and spontaneous processes. Optical electronics including optical resonators, lasers, optical detectors, light-guiding, and applications.

subject: ECE
title: Optical Electronics II
description: Electro-optics, noise detection, light and sound dielectric waveguide phenomena, lasers, optics, phase conjugation.

subject: ECE
title: Microsensors and Microactuators I
description: Technology methods and physical principles of microsensors and microactuators. Vacuum technology, thin film deposition and characterization techniques, solid mechanics, micromachining, acoustics, piezoelectricity and principles of current microtransducers.

subject: ECE
title: Rapid Prototyping of Electrophysical Devices
description: Hands on experience in designing, fabricating, testing, and iterating according to rapid-prototyping principles. Students learn state-of-the-art equipment for making their designs, software for simulating designs, and working in design teams.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Topics in Physical Electronics
description: Recent developments in phenomena and devices of physical electronics.

subject: ECE
title: Analysis and Design of Integrated Circuits
description: Fabrication constraints and design guidelines for integrated circuits. Nonlinear model of integrated circuit transistor. Design and analysis of integrated logic circuits and linear circuits.

subject: ECE
title: Smart Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
description: Challenges and solutions for integrating intermittent renewable energy sources into the power system, with a focus on “smart grid” approaches and demand-response. Using linear programming and other modeling techniques to answer policy-relevant questions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ECE
title: Applied Random Processes
description: Random variables, multivariate distributions, random sequences, stochastic convergence, stationary and nonstationary processes, spectral analysis, Karhunen-Loeve expansion, Markov processes, mean square estimation, Kalman filters.

subject: ECE
title: Queueing Theory
description: Poisson, Markov, and renewal processes, M/G/1 queue, G/M/1 queue, queueing networks, simulation, and performance evaluation of computer systems and communication networks.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ICS, MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Detection and Estimation Theory
description: Fundamentals of signal detection and estimation theory. Hypothesis testing, parametric and nonparametric detection, sequential detection, parametric estimation, linear estimation, robust detection and estimation, and applications to communication systems.

subject: ECE
title: Communication System Performance
description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Communication Networks
description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

subject: ECE
title: Machine Learning
description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, ME, ICS, MATH majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Information Theory
description: Measure of information, coding for discrete sources, discrete memoryless channels and capacity, the noisy channel coding theorem, source coding with fidelity criterion, rate-distortion theory, multiuser channels.

subject: ECE
title: Source Coding
description: Theory and applications of source coding, rate-distortion theory, companding, lattice coding, tree coding, trellis coding, entropy-constrained coding, asymptotic theory, predictive and differential encoding, combined source/channel coding, vector quantization.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding I
description: Linear block codes, soft and hard decision decodings, correction of random errors, cyclic codes, BCH codes, Reed-Solomon codes, majority logic decodable codes, burst-error correcting codes, concatenated codes.

subject: ECE
title: Error-Control Coding II
description: Convolutional codes, Viterbi algorithm, coded modulation, multistage decoding, concatenated coded modulation, probabilistic decoding, turbo codes, low density parity check codes and iterative decoding.

subject: ECE
title: Linear System Theory
description: State space theory of linear systems, controllability, observability, stability, irreducible realizations.

subject: ECE
title: Nonlinear Control Systems
description: Digital simulations, phase-plane analysis, limit cycles and amplitude bounds, Lyapunov’s theorem, circle criterion of stability, lure systems, Popov’s stability theorem.

subject: ECE
title: Optimal Control Systems
description: Optimal controls introduced through parametric optimization, calculus of variations, Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Pontryagin’s maximum principle, minimum-time and minimum-fuel problems, dynamic programming, applications.

subject: ECE
title: Robust Control
description: Multivariable frequency response design, signals and systems, linear fractional transformations, LQG Control, Full Information H-infinity Controller Synthesis, H-infinity filtering, model reduction, the four-block problem.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CECE, ECE, and ME majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Computer Systems
description: Modern operating system software, process communication, distributed systems, device drivers. Software development and maintenance, integration of software packages. Projects reflecting special interests of faculty.

subject: ECE
title: Telecommunication Networks
description: Telecommunication-network architecture; switching, broadcast, and wireless networks; protocols, interfaces, routing, flow- and congestion-control techniques; intelligent network architecture; service creation capabilities; multimedia, voice, data, and video networks and services.

subject: ECE
title: Wireless and Mobile Security
description: Security and privacy design principles and application in wireless and mobile devices, networks, and services, as well as research methodology in wireless and mobile security.

subject: ECE
title: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
description: Solutions of Maxwell’s equations and applications to radiation and propagation of electromagnetic waves.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Microwave Engineering
description: Advanced RF and microwave circuit design for wireless applications.

subject: ECE
title: Advanced Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
description: Develop comprehensive understanding of computations techniques for solving engineering electromagnetic problems formulated in terms of integral or differential equations. Eigenvalue problems, radiation, and electromagnetics scattering problems will be discussed and computer programming is required.
prereq_raw: ECE 471 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ECE, BE, and CENG majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Engineering Systems
description: Systems analysis and electronic instrumentation methods in biomedicine. Network and control-loop modeling, computer simulation, biological transducers, and analysis of electronic and physiological systems.
prereq_raw: ECE 326 , ECE 326L , and ECE 371 ; or consent.

subject: ECE
title: Biosensors and Bioelectronics
description: Advanced topics in the design of biological detection technologies. Topics include fundamentals of electrochemistry, electrochemical biosensors, DNA and protein biochips, and bioelectronics for bio-signal conditioning and processing.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Microdevices
description: Design and fabrication of micro- and nanodevices for biomedical applications. Topics include micro- and nanoscale physics, microfluidic physics and microfluidic devices, and micro- and nanoscale fabrication techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENG majors only.

subject: ECE
title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Analysis
description: Biomedical signals, digital filters and filter banks, spike train analysis, time-scale and time-frequency representations, nonlinear techniques, Lomb’s algorithm and the Hilbert transform, modeling, Volterra series, Wiener series, Poisson-Wiener series, multichannel data, causality.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ECE, ME, ICS majors only and any graduate student in JABSOM who has a suitable technical background.

subject: ECE
title: (Alpha) Special Topics in Electrical Engineering
description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting/permanent faculty. (B) artificial intelligence; (C) circuits; (D) communications; (E) computer hardware; (F) computer software; (H) control; (I) devices; (J) fields; (K) power.

title: Directed Reading or Research

title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for MS in electrical and computer engineering.

subject: ECE
title: Directed Instruction
description: Student assists in classroom instruction under direction and close supervision of faculty member.

subject: ECE
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
