subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Economics
description: One-semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Microeconomics
description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: An introduction to macroeconomics-the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

subject: ECON
title: Principles of Macroeconomics
description: An introduction to macroeconomics-the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

subject: ECON
title: Data Analysis and Visualization
description: Develops basic techniques of data analysis and visualization. Introduces sources of economic data; methods of preparing data from various file/data formats for analysis; methods of visualization: bubble plots, scatterplot matrices, heatmaps, hexbins, rug plots, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

subject: ECON
title: Intermediate Microeconomics
description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

subject: ECON
title: The Economy of Hawaiʻi
description: Descriptive understanding of the history of development of Hawaiʻi’s economy; current economic problems; future prospects. Emphasizes the written communication of the intuition behind economic concepts in practice in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: The Japanese Economy
description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 ; consent.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Statistics
description: Basic elements; descriptive statistics, probability, inference, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and correlation analysis.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 , or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

subject: ECON
title: Financial Markets and Institutions
description: The determination of asset prices; the risk and term structure of interest rates; efficient markets hypothesis; risk management and financial derivatives, asymmetric information models of financial market structure, innovation, regulation and deregulation; and financial crises.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

subject: ECON
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Sustainable Development
description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawaiʻi. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 , or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Network Economics
description: Fundamental questions about the connections in the social, economic, and technological worlds. Topics include: matching markets, traffic, financial and social networks; and the political and economic consequences of the internet and other large networks.

subject: ECON
title: Games and Economic Behavior
description: Introduces students to the study of strategic behavior with applications to economics, business, and public policy. Simple economic models of strategic decision making are used to analyze provision of public goods; competition, cooperation, and coordination among firms; bargaining between employers and labor unions; international trade negotiations; reputation as a competitive advantage, and others.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Economics
description: Nature and causes of environmental degradation/economic solutions, with emphasis on relevant ethical issues and decision-making. Topics include air and water pollution, toxic waste, deforestation, soil erosion, biodiversity, global warming, and sustainable development.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Seminar: Women and International Development
description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment; ethical considerations of economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty.
prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: ECON
title: Trade Policy and Globalization
description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Internship for Economics
description: Economics majors and minors work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. Students combine academic work with practical experience.

subject: ECON
title: Cooperative Education
description: Economics majors and minors, under the supervision of faculty members, work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. The Econ
coreq_raw: Co-op integrates academics with practical work experience.

coreq_tree.text: Co-op integrates academics with practical work experience

subject: ECON
title: Contemporary Topics in Economics
description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester.

subject: ECON
title: Directed Reading
description: Economics majors and minors participate in faculty supervised reading of economic literature. Enables students to self-study topics not covered in the department’s scheduled course offerings.

subject: ECON
title: The Ocean Economy
description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

subject: ECON
title: Economic History of the United States
description: U.S. economy from colonial times: government policies, institutions, industries, financial markets, economic growth, economic crises.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Global Economic Crisis and Recovery
description: Causes and consequences of financial and economic crises: crisis origins and global transmission; macroeconomic and regulatory policy responses; recovery challenges.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Asian Economic Development
description: History and economic development. Resources, population, and income, saving, investment, and consumption patterns. Role of government and private enterprise.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: The Chinese Economy
description: The Chinese economy during the imperial and republican periods, under Mao, and into the present reform era, with a brief comparison to Taiwan and Hong Kong.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Pacific Island Economies
description: Historical and current economic development of the Pacific islands (excluding Hawaiʻi). Analysis of selected economic issues such as tourism, population growth, etc.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 , ECON 130 , or ECON 131 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematical Economics
description: Mathematical techniques applied to theories of the consumer, the firm, markets. Linear programming, inputoutput analysis.
prereq_raw: ECON 300 , ECON 301 ; MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , or MATH 251A .

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Econometrics I: Data Exploration and Regression Analysis
description: Types of data, exploratory data analysis, generalizing from random samples, simple and multivariate regression, non-linear relationships, measurement error, extreme values, weights, correlated and heteroskedastic errors, instrumental variables, models for binary or discrete dependent variables.
prereq_raw: ECON 321 or MATH 241 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or ( MATH 251A and NREM 203 ) or ( MATH 371 and MATH 373 ) or ( MATH 471 and MATH 472 ); or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Introduction to Econometrics II: Prediction and Causal Inference
description: Prediction types, error measures, training and test data, cross validation, machine learning, regression trees, random forests, boosting, classification, forecasting time series, modelbased versus design-based causality, potential outcomes framework, matching, difference-in-differences, panel data, synthetic controls.
prereq_raw: ECON 425 (with a minimum grade of B- or better).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- or better )

subject: ECON
title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and ECON 321 or NREM 310 ; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics
description: Economic analysis of labor market. Investment in human capital, education, health, migration, etc.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: Determinants and consequences of growth and structure of human populations. Relationships between economic factors and fertility, population growth and economic growth.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics
description: Private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; efficient production and utilization of services; models of hospital and physician behavior; optimal public policy.

subject: ECON
title: Monetary Theory and Policy
description: Microfoundations and critical analysis of monetary and macroeconomic theory and policy. Topics include the causes and consequences of inflation, optimal monetary policy and international monetary systems, bank risk and insurance, and national debt and taxation.

subject: ECON
title: Development Economics
description: Theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for analyzing key issues facing today’s developing world. Topics include characteristics of underdeveloped economies, economic growth, structural change, poverty, inequality, education, population growth, foreign aid and financial sector.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Happiness
description: Topics covered include: measuring happiness, what individual and country characteristics contribute to individual well-being, what are the consequences of happiness on behavior, and whether happiness is a cause or an effect.

subject: ECON
title: Health in Developing Economies
description: Theoretical and analytical tools from economics to study (1) the relationship between health and economic development and (2) the determinants of health improvement in developing economies.
prereq_raw: ECON 321 (or concurrent) and ECON 301 , or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: Welfare economics, public expenditure and policy evaluation, public finance by debt and taxes.

subject: ECON
title: State and Local Finance
description: Fiscal institutions, operations, and policy questions within state and local governments in U.S. grant programs and other links with central government.

subject: ECON
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Theory of international specialization and exchange; general equilibrium, tariffs, quotas, common markets.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: The determination of output, price levels, exchange rates and the balance of payments for economies that are integrated with the global economy; theory and application to historical and/or contemporary policy issues.

subject: ECON
title: Industrial Organization
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of contemporary topics in industrial organization. Uses economic theory to analyze important issues facing firms, and examines the practical challenges of empirical applications of theory.

subject: ECON
title: Law and Economics
description: Legal issues of property rights, contracts, torts, and crime. Efficiency of U.S. legal process. Economics of law enforcement, juries, prosecutors; evolution of legal rules.

subject: ECON
title: Land and Housing Economics
description: Microeconomics explains urban land and housing phenomena, and analyzes selected land and housing issues relevant to Honolulu.

subject: ECON
title: Contemporary Economic Issues
description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester, e.g., environmental pollution, crime control, racial discrimination, traffic congestion.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced Directed Research
description: Economics majors and minors conduct research, under faculty supervision, on a topic of their choice.
prereq_raw: minimum GPA of 3.0 in economics and consent.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
description: Theory of the consumer, firm, and market. Perfect competition and efficiency. Market power and firm strategy. Market efficiencies. Role of the government.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomics for Business and Policy Analysis
description: Topics on production, consumption, labor market, asset market, economic growth, and business cycles are discussed with emphasis on real-economy applications and policy analysis. Implications of monetary, fiscal, and international finance and economic policies are explored.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory I
description: Theory of the firm: production, costs, duality; theory of the market: competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition; theory of the consumer: preferences, expenditures, duality; expected utility theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory I
description: Neoclassical theory of real and monetary equilibrium, economics of J. M. Keynes, standard IS/LM models and aggregate demand/supply analysis in the closed and open economy, theory of rational expectations.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory II
description: General equilibrium analysis: production, consumption and Walrasian equilibria; Pareto efficiency, fundamental theorems of welfare economics; externalities; public goods; game theory; information theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory II
description: Models of economic growth and fluctuations; stochastic and dynamic macroeconomic models; econometric testing of rational expectations models; theory of public debt; current topics in macroeconomic theory.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development
description: Nature and causes of economic growth and structural change. Roles of macroeconomic policy and foreign trade.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development Policy
description: Analysis of policies for the promotion of industrial and agricultural development. Project evaluation, industrial regulation, public administration, investment and capital market policies, land-use policies, trade policies, pricing, and stabilization.

subject: ECON
title: Economic Development of Japan
description: Analysis of growth from Meiji period to present. Problems of population change, capital formation, income distribution, industrial structure.

subject: ECON
title: Microeconomic Theory III
description: Game theory and strategic behavior. Economics of information and incentives principal-agent theory. Economic design. Applications include: theory of contracts; incentive compatible mechanism for provision of public goods; auction theory.

subject: ECON
title: Macroeconomic Theory III
description: Will equip students with the ability to understand, undertake, and critically evaluate theoretical and quantitative research in modern macroeconomics with a focus on the application of the search and matching methodology.

subject: ECON
title: Mathematics for Economics
description: Sets, functions, limits, convexity, continuity; constrained and unconstrained optimization; difference and differential equations; matrix algebra; simultaneous equations; comparative statics; Kuhn-Tucker theory; game theory; mathematical programming.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics I
description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics II
description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference and forecasting of econometric models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

subject: ECON
title: Econometrics III
description: Will equip students with the ability to undertake, understand, and critically assess empirical research using state-of-the-at econometric methods.

subject: ECON
title: Disasters and Economic Policy
description: Economic analysis of disasters. The economics of prevention and mitigation, as well as post-disaster economic consequences and policy, will be examined.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ECON
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

subject: ECON
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

subject: ECON
title: Marine Resource Economics
description: Seminar on the economics of the marine environment. Topics include fisheries management, ocean recreation, shipping, and coral reef protection.

subject: ECON
title: Foundations of Public Policy
description: Microeconomic principles for expenditure and tax policies. Externalities, public goods, non-convexities, regulation; cost-benefit analysis, general equilibrium, shadow-pricing; rent-seeking, corruption; optimal taxation, incidence, excess burden; dynamic public finance, national debt, social security.

subject: ECON
title: Public Economics
description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of public-sector allocation. Adverse selection, moral hazard, networks, auctions, public choice and political mechanisms; tax and mandate incidence; economics of education and local public goods; social insurance programs.

subject: ECON
title: International Trade and Welfare
description: Classical and new theories of international trade: why nations trade, gains from trade, patterns of trade, and trade policy effects under perfect and imperfect competition. Empirical trade and other special topics.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
description: Surveys theoretical and empirical research on topics such as regionalism and multilateralism, trade and wages, foreign direct investment and multinational firms, trade and the environment, and trade and economic growth.

subject: ECON
title: International Macroeconomics
description: Advanced international monetary and macroeconomic theory: balance of payments, output, price and exchange rate determination, international aspects of growth and economic fluctuations, alternative exchange rate regimes, international capital flows.

subject: ECON
title: Applied International Finance
description: Surveys empirical research in international macroeconomics, finance and econometric methods: including balance of payments adjustment, international equilibrium, international prices, interest rates and exchange rates, models of exchange rate determination, capital flows, balance of payments crises.
prereq_raw: ECON 607 and ECON 629 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Labor Economics and Policy
description: Supply of and demand for labor; implications for labor markets and unemployment level.

subject: ECON
title: Economics of Population
description: Economic determinants and consequences of population change.

subject: ECON
title: Health Economics and Policy
description: Economic analysis of health-care policy; efficient design of health-care financing schemes; private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; provider behavior.
prereq_raw: ECON 604 (or concurrent) or ECON 606 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ECON
title: Strategic Behavior and Experimental Economics
description: Experimental economics: methodology. Experimental game theory. Market experiments. Applications include: topics in industrial organization, provision of public goods, asset markets, auctions.

subject: ECON
title: Advanced Topics in Economics
description: Reflects interests of visiting and permanent faculty, focusing on specialized methods or topics in economics.

subject: ECON
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: ECON
title: Research Seminar
description: Selected issues emphasizing research techniques. Required for students who have passed the two theory qualifying exams and have not passed the comprehensive exam.

subject: ECON
title: MA Capstone Research
description: Student applies theoretical and quantitative techniques, critical thinking, and communicative skills to prepare a written and oral presentation of original research on a topic of his or her choice.
prereq_raw: ECON 606 , ECON 607 , ECON 627 , ECON 628 , and consent of graduate chair.

subject: ECON
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings.

subject: EDCS
title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply concepts from EDCS 415 and gain perspective on the role of the practitioner in ECE settings.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
description: Continuation of STE 415 : focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
description: Continuation of EDCS 415L .

subject: EDCS
title: STEM Pedagogy
description: Introduction to STEM education pedagogy with emphasis on ethical issues and effective oral communication. Designed to integrate educational theory, pedagogy, content, and practical concerns into teaching practices in the STEM fields.

subject: EDCS
title: Collaborative Language and Learning
description: Examination of language (talking, reading, and writing) processes within a collaborative teaching framework in the secondary curriculum. Field experience may be required.

subject: EDCS
title: Adolescent Literature and Literacy
description: Selection and interpretation of young adult literature, including multicultural literature for middle level and high school students. Theory and teaching strategies for integrating literacy instruction in the literature program for diverse student populations.

subject: EDCS
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

subject: EDCS
title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawaiʻi as our place of learning and teaching.

subject: EDCS
title: Methods and Materials in Science
description: Selecting and using methods and materials, demonstrations and simulations, open-ended experimentation, inquiry and discovery, task analysis measurement tools and techniques, activities from various curricula, opportunity for individualized goals and projects.
prereq_raw: STE 323 , STE 404H , teaching experience; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers, including criteria for evaluation and planning.
prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 (or concurrent), HDFS 331 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

subject: EDCS
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

subject: EDCS
title: Problem Solving in Mathematics Education
description: Experiencing and learning to teach heuristics of solving mathematical problems; designing curricula, classroom organization, evaluative measures for problem solving.

subject: EDCS
title: Difficulties in Learning Mathematics
description: Identification, analysis, and remediation of difficulties in learning mathematics.

subject: EDCS
title: Language, Learning and Teaching
description: Examines the role that language plays in the social construction of knowledge within various disciplines, K-adult. Collaborative group learning strategies will be modeled.
prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Advanced Topics in Reading
description: Current theories and teaching strategies of reading throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Topics include psychological, sociological, and cultural foundations of reading; 21st century literacies; emergent literacy; diversity; multilingual learners, formative assessment; state/national initiatives.
prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Advanced Topics in Writing and Oral Language
description: Current theories and teaching strategies of writing and oral language throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Focus on teaching writing and oral language as tools for learning and to demonstrate learning.
prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Children’s Literature in the Elementary Curriculum
description: In-depth examination of traditional and current books/media, birth through young adult, with emphasis on applications in schools or other educational contexts. Focus on use of narrative, exposition, and other genres across the curriculum.
prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Effective Writing Practices
description: Analysis and practical application of principles and strategies of effective writing and informed writing instruction in K-12 classrooms.

subject: EDCS
title: Literacy Coaching and Leadership
description: Exploration and application of literacy specialist roles. Includes teaching, coaching, providing resources, advocating for all students, and collaborating with other professionals.

subject: EDCS
title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, action research, mixed methods, and curriculum based assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/ Thesis proposal.

subject: EDCS
title: New Literacies Leadership
description: New approaches to analyzing 21st century literacies K-12, including visual, media, digital, and critical literacies as well as developing leadership practices in multi-literacies pedagogy.

subject: EDCS
title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: EDCS
title: Early Career Teaching, K-12
description: Focuses on research and practice related to the first five years of teaching. Especially recommended for beginning teachers and graduate students interested in this stage of teaching development.

subject: EDCS
title: Early Literacy and Language Development
description: Theory and practice for PK-3 early literacy and language development. Focus is on content knowledge and pedagogical strategies that support the optimal development of oral language, reading, and writing skills in PK-3 classrooms.

subject: EDCS
title: Early Childhood Education: Advanced Topics
description: Analysis and practical application of selected early childhood education program and/or instructional materials. Restricted to majors.

subject: EDCS
title: Social and Cultural Constructions of Childhood
description: Seminar examines the interrelated socially constructed concepts of children and childhood and places them in the larger contexts informed by sociological, anthropological, historical, critical, and technological perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: EDCS
title: (Alpha) Curriculum Leadership
description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Leadership: early childhood
description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Leadership: middle school
description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

subject: EDCS
title: Curriculum Leadership: K-14
description: Foundation for critical study of curriculum development and improvement from the perspective of teacher leaders. Online/hybrid sections available; (B) early childhood; (D) middle school; (G) K-14.

subject: EDCS
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

subject: EDCS
title: School Mathematics Curriculum
description: Analysis of research related to teaching and learning school mathematics, application of research to classroom practices. Appraisal of recent curriculum trends; critical examination of assumptions underlying proposed curriculum changes.

subject: EDCS
title: Social Studies Curriculum
description: Examination and evaluation of social science content, societal values and research findings as basis for development and revision of social studies materials, texts, curriculum guides, methodology.
prereq_raw: STE 322 or equivalent, social studies teaching experience, or consent.

subject: EDCS
title: Art Education K-12
description: Principles, goals, and objectives in teaching and learning art K-12; curriculum, instruction, and assessment in art education; laboratory experiences in art media.

subject: EDCS
title: Teaching and Learning with Art Objects, Museums, Collections, and Site Visits
description: Interdisciplinary inquiry and examination of the role of physical objects and site visits in schools and other educational contexts, through visits to local art museums and related sites.

subject: EDCS
title: Function of Play in Early Childhood Education
description: Review of research and theory illuminating the nature, purposes, and meaning of play as a critical aspect of early childhood education.

subject: EDCS
title: Cultural Diversity and Education
description: Examines issues, theories, perspectives and practices in multicultural education and promotes awareness, encourages knowledgeable reflection and develops skills necessary for multicultural practitioners.

subject: EDCS
title: Qualitative Research Methods
description: Methods of qualitative research in education or related social science from an interdisciplinary framework.

subject: EDCS
title: Autoethnography in Education
description: Exploration and application of autoethnography as a self-reflexive research method that utilizes the retelling of lived experience and emotion to examine historical, critical, and social topics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: EDCS
title: (Alpha) Curriculum and Instruction in Studio Art
description: Understanding art methods and materials related to art education for teachers grades K-12. Writing curricula, integrating visual arts across the curriculum, developing evaluation methods observing stages of artistic growth among students of multiple ages/abilities. (B) painting, drawing, printing; (C) fiber arts, ceramics, sculpture; (D) photography, technology, collage; (E) Combination of any three of B, C, and/or D. Previous BA, BS, BEd, and BFA only.

description: Application of formative assessments to better monitor/guide struggling readers and writers. Topics include diversity and state/national initiatives.

description: Advanced use of formative and summative assessments to monitor/lead classroom and school literacy programs. title: Reading for English Language Learners
description: Presents key concepts and theories in teaching reading to K-12 English language learners. Topics include instructional decisions in teaching reading to ELLs, the interrelationship of language skills, strategies, and teaching academic content.

title: Theory/Practice in Cooperative Occupational Education
description: Theory and practices of coordinating cooperative education in high school and community college.

description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

title: Education in American Society

description: Explores the intellectual, political, and socio-cultural histories of educational practices and institutions from pre-contact Hawaiʻi through statehood with emphasis on writing instruction. Themes include white-settler colonialism, multiculturalism, assimilation, resistance, Indigenous, and immigrant experiences.

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Comparative/ International Education
description: Introduction to basic methods of comparative studies, focusing on schooling, but also treating broader educational issues.

subject: EDEF
title: Topics in Comparative Education

subject: EDEF
title: Introduction to Educational Policy Studies
description: Examines theories and models of educational policy and policy-making and the contribution of policy analysis to the policy-making and change processes.

subject: EDEF
title: The Politics of Education
description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments.

subject: EDEF
title: Approaches to Educational Inquiry
description: Overview of different research methods in educational inquiry with an opportunity to explore through practice one or more methods (ex: case study, interviewing, narrative construction, practitioner inquiry.) Preparation for MEd or PhD proposals.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on Race, Law, and Education
description: Introduction to educational law and the way it relates to issues of race and ethnicity. Particular focus on how the U.S. courts have dealt with the question of educational inequality in a multiracial/multiethnic society.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: EDEF
title: Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
description: Focuses on the interplay of class, race, gender and ethnicity in school and community settings. Social praxis, educational reform and policy are considered.

subject: EDEF
title: Education and World Order
description: Focuses on the challenges educators face in identifying appropriate pedagogical frameworks and practices in global education that address the impact of globalization in our society today.

subject: EDEF
title: International Development Education
description: Introduction to international development education in Asian and Pacific nations. Students explore links between education and development. Emphasis is on cross-cultural perception of development.

subject: EDEF
title: Environmental Education
description: Focuses on the development of an ecological consciousness through a cultural and environmental approach to teaching and learning in schooling and everyday life.

subject: EDEF
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.

subject: EDEF
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: EDEF
title: Education and Social Change
description: Study of classical and contemporary theories of social change as these relate to school, the profession of teaching, planning of change, and social stability.

subject: EDEF
title: Recent History of American Education
description: Contemporary American education in recent historical perspective; focuses on the educational changes brought about by WW II, the Cold War, civil rights and other social movements.

subject: EDEF
title: History of American Higher Education
description: Genesis and evolution of college and university from colonial America to present.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on the Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
description: Examination of social, political, and cultural issues affecting educational policy with special emphasis on methods of inquiry and theoretical constructs.

subject: EDEF
title: Advanced Seminar in Philosophy of Education
description: Advanced studies in philosophical inquiry. Examination of philosophically based methods of analysis and interpretation and their influence in educational research and practice.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in History of Education
description: Aspects of the history of education. Application of historiography to educational problems and policy.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar on the Educational System
description: Examination of the structure and dynamics of educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior.

subject: EDEF
title: Seminar in Comparative/International Education
description: Advanced reading, research and writing in selected topics dealing with comparative and international education, including such themes as policy studies, minority education and educational reform.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Teaching as a Career
description: An experience-based introduction to teaching as a career.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through an introduction to classroom assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing.

subject: EDEP
title: Self-Regulated Learning
description: Theory and use of self-regulated learning strategies in academic contexts.

subject: EDEP
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual reading or research.

subject: EDEP
title: Fundamentals of Research in Education
description: Introduction to the methodology of systematic study of problems in education: principles of research design, data processing, technical writing, and evaluation of research proposals and reports.

subject: EDEP
title: Seminar in Contemporary Perspectives in Educational Psychology
description: In-depth analysis of contemporary issues in education from the theoretical and methodological perspectives of the faculty in educational psychology. Focuses on oral communication and intensive writing skills.

subject: EDEP
title: Student Assessment
description: Introduction to basic concepts and issues in assessment and measurement, development of formative and summative assessment procedures, descriptive statistics, scales of measurement, and standardizing testing.

subject: EDEP
title: Introductory Statistics
description: Introduction to concepts and logics of statistical reasoning and statistical literacy. Topics include descriptive statistics, sampling distribution, and inferential statistics such as z-test, t-tests, correlation, and one-way ANOVA.

subject: EDEP
title: Human Motivation and Education
description: Application of motivation theory and research to understanding and increasing human motivation for education.

subject: EDEP
title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods
description: Introductory graduate-level statistics in education and social sciences. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: EDEP
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

subject: EDEP
title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
description: Analysis of variance and other models of assessing results of experiments. Relation of analysis to design.

subject: EDEP
title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.
prereq_raw: EDEP 601 or EDEA 629 (with a grade of B), or consent.

subject: EDEP
title: Multivariate Methods
description: Builds on prior knowledge of multiple regression and will include applications of MANOVA, canonical correlation, logistic regression, discriminant function analysis, cluster analysis, multidimensional scaling, and mixture models.

subject: EDEP
title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

subject: EDEP
title: Introduction to Educational Research
description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
prereq_raw: EDEP 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B or higher ) or consent

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

description: Theories and applications of multilevel model to analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Topics include two-level and three-level models, growth models, and multilevel logistic regression.

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

description: Measurement and psychometric theories and applications using psychometric programs. Topics include classical test theory, reliability, validity, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, item bias, and item response theory.

subject: EDEP
title: Categorical Data Analysis
description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables; analysis of contingency tables, loglinear models, introduction to generalized linear models for binary, nominal, ordinal, and count outcomes in cross-sectional and longitudinal data sets.

subject: EDEP
title: Structural Equation Modeling
description: Theories and applications to test models with manifest and latent variables. Topics include path analysis, factor analysis, latent variable model, multi-group analysis, latent means model, and other advanced topics in SEM.

subject: EDEP
title: Psychometric Methods
description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, and current issues in psychometrics.

subject: EDEP
title: Adolescence and Education

subject: EDEP
title: Foundations of School Counseling
description: Explores school counseling history, philosophy, and ASCA Model. Covers delivery systems, interventions, roles, and ethics. Examines contemporary challenges and resources in supporting student development. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

subject: EDEP

description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.

subject: EDEP

description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in counseling and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.

subject: EDEP
title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP
title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues.

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

subject: EDEP

description: Intensive study of critical and theoretical issues raised by various forms of life writing (biography, autobiography, oral history, diaries, etc.) and of their history and methodology.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Cultural Studies in Asia/ Pacific
description: Intensive study of selected issues in cultural studies in Asia and the Pacific; topics to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Pacific Literatures
description: Intensive study of selected issues in the literatures of the Pacific in English, or translated into English. Topics to be announced.

title: Seminar in Literatures of Hawaiʻi
description: Introduction to comparative literature; relationship of Hawaiian to other literatures; sources and influences.

subject: ENG
title: Seminar in Hawaiian Literature
