title: Seminar in Special Topics
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ENG
title: Dissertation Research
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Freshman Seminar
description: Overview of the engineering field, the different disciplines, and opportunities. Success strategies for studying engineering.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering majors only.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Engineering
description: Topics include the engineering disciplines, the development of problem solving and technical communication skills, the design process and analysis methods using a team design project, and introduction to programming in Matlab for engineering applications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshman standing only.

subject: ENGR
title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR and BUS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Freshmen only.

subject: ENGR
title: Freshman Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for freshman-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a sophomore ( ENGR 296 ).

subject: ENGR
title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders.

subject: ENGR
title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior ( ENGR 396 ). Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ENGR
title: Career Development Seminar
description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction.

subject: ENGR
title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a senior.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ENGR
title: Engineering Management
description: Introduction to engineering management of projects and its outcomes. Development of professional skills for the systematic formulation of problems and solutions to efficiently deduce project viability. Emphasis on collaborative teamwork and performance evaluations and improvements. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ENGR
title: Field Experience
description: Supervised internship in engineering practice under professional and faculty direction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: junior standing in engineering and consent.

subject: EPET
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

subject: EPET
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. Significant oral and written communication is required.
prereq_raw: EPET 201 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107 ; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272 .

subject: EPET
title: Introduction to Human Spaceflight
description: Effects of spaceflight conditions on human physiology and psychology. Astronaut selection, training, crew composition. Ethics of space exploration. Politics & sociology of public and private human space flight. Selection of capstone project. Significant written communication.

subject: EPET
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

subject: EPET
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

subject: EPET
title: Human Spaceflight Mission Elements
description: Engineering aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, and budgets for human spaceflight missions. Design of environmental control and life support systems. Capstone project design. Significant oral and written communication.

subject: EPET
title: Capstone Project - Human Spaceflight Analog Mission
description: Science experiments in space and human space flight engineering. Human spaceflight capstone project with a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, and social scientists. Concurrent disciplinary and multidisciplinary methodologies. Human spaceflight analog mission. Significant written communication.

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Dynamic Earth Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on study of minerals, rocks, and topographic maps. Examine volcanism, hydrology, coastal processes and hazards, geologic time and earthquakes. Field trips to investigate landslides, beaches and Oʻahu geology.

subject: ERTH
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

subject: ERTH
title: Geology of the Hawaiian Islands
description: Hawaiian geology and geologic processes: origin of Hawaiian islands, volcanism, rocks and minerals, landforms, stream and coastal processes, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis, groundwater, geologic and environmental hazards. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Volcanoes in the Sea
description: Lecture with field trips covering the manner in which geological conditions, resources, and events have affected past and present circum-Pacific societies.

subject: ERTH
title: Voyage through the Solar System
description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

subject: ERTH
title: Solar System Studio
description: Explore the wonders of the Solar System through hands-on experience of science. Will study satellite images, evaluate planetary surface observations, analyze data of objects in our Solar System, conduct experiments, and communicate their findings.

subject: ERTH
title: Voyage of the Vicariance: Earth and Life through Time
description: Exploration of Earth history via an imaginary sailing voyage around the world and back in time to Earth’s formation and the origin of life. Introduces fundamental concepts in geology, paleontology, living systems, and evolutionary biology.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Volcanoes
description: Examines the origin and classification of volcanoes, volcanic eruptions, and volcanic deposits. Includes the history of volcanic studies, myths, and legends. Emphasis on volcanic eruptions, eruptive products, volcanic hazards, and risk management.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Hazards
description: Introductory course covering the causes of, and effects from, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, landslides, rockfalls, and other natural geologic phenomena. Field trips.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters and Human History
description: Examines how natural hazards have affected the course of human culture and societies from pre-history to the present in Hawaiʻi/Oceania, Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Geology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Structure, composition and evolution of Earth; processes responsible for formation, deformation and transformation of rocks; plate tectonics. Emphasis on quantitative methods, problem solving and critical thinking to geology. Laboratory and field trips required.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Lower division reading and research in any area of ERTH under the direction of a faculty member.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Inquiry
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Origin and age of the solar system and earth: interior of the earth; plate tectonics and records of biological evolution and past environments. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101L and one of ERTH 101 , ERTH 103 , ERTH 104 , ERTH 106 , or ERTH 130 ; or consent. ERTH 101L may be taken concurrently.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors.

subject: ERTH
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102 , or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Scientific Programming
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to solving scientific problems by computer programming. Overview of the MatLab programming language and environment. Emphasis placed on good style, logical reasoning, and applied mathematics.

subject: ERTH
title: Physical Volcanology
description: Volcanic eruptions and their consequences. Includes models for volcanic eruptions including explosive eruptions and lava flows, monitoring of active volcanoes, evaluation and impacts of volcanic hazards, and mitigation of volcanic risk. Field trips. Normally fall. ERTH and GEOL majors or consent.
prereq_raw: ( ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 ) with a minimum grade of B or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Mineralogy
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the chemistry, crystalline structure, geologic occurrence, and physical properties of minerals. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 and ( CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or CHEM 171 / CHEM 171L ). or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Igneous Petrology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Hazards & Geomechanics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Dynamic behavior of Earth’s surface, physical processes driving geohazards, and the risks posed to society. Theory, practical techniques, and data visualization to measure, analyze, and interpret hazards and implications.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 130 , MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A , and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Field Methods
description: Methods used in geological investigations in the field. Eight hours on Saturday in the field.

subject: ERTH
title: Work of Water
description: Physical properties of water, geological aspects of surface water and ground water occurrence, surface water and groundwater resources, use, and problems.

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentology Processes and Environments
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern and past terrestrial and oceanic processes and environments that form sediments and sedimentary rocks, and their interpretation in Earth history. Incorporates properties, principles and applications of sedimentology, sedimentary petrology, geochemistry and stratigraphy.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 , ERTH 201 or consent, and ERTH 333 or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics and Geodynamics
description: Mechanics of lithosphere deformation related to plate convergence, rifting and strike-slip faulting, and the evolution of mountain belts. Use of theory and skill-building techniques to measure, describe, analyze, and interpret structures on Earth.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 ; and ERTH 250 ; and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; and PHYS 170 .

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of Earth and Planets
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Essentials of geophysics: application of physics understanding Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Topics include heat flow, gravity, geodesy, electromagnetism, seismology. Applications to core and mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, volcanoes, hydrology, environmental concerns, and archaeology.
prereq_raw: ERTH 250 , ERTH 303 , ERTH 313 (or concurrent), MATH 242 , and PHYS 272 , PHYS 272L ; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of chemical principles and chemical analysis to Earth, ocean and environmental sciences; chemistry of hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere system, origin/ differentiation of Earth/Solar system, volcanic processes, natural radioactivity, organic/inorganic chemistry.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A , and CHEM 162 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth Materials and Structures
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lecture and lab that covers formation, occurrence, and identification of common minerals, rocks, and geologic structures. Lab work will include study of hand-samples, thin-sections, and field experiences.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior/ senior standing and consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Research in Earth Sciences
description: Research experience for Earth Science undergraduates. Under the guidance of a mentor, the student will conduct research and write a report on the background, methods, data, interpretations, and conclusions of the work.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Earth Sciences majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ERTH
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth sciences.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior/ Senior standing only.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Mineral Physics
description: Scientific study of the materials that make up the Earth. Properties of minerals on micro- and macro-scales; their properties and behavior.

subject: ERTH
title: Hawaiian Geology
description: Consists of lectures, discussions, and field trips on the geologic processes and geologic history of the Hawaiian islands, with emphasis on writing communication.

subject: ERTH
title: Remote Compositional Analysis: Spectroscopy, Mineralogy, and Geochemistry of Planetary Surfaces
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces. Comparative studies of fundamental planetary science phenomena. Planetary surface science discoveries. Sustainability of planetary environments.
prereq_raw: ( ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L , or ERTH 105 or ERTH 107 or ASTR 150 ; and CHEM 161 ; and PHYS 272 ) with a minimum grade of C+; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Natural Disasters: Geoethics and the Layman
description: Evaluates ethical practice of geoscience as it relates to studies of natural disasters that result from geological and meteorological phenomena and the means that earth scientists interact with the laymen.

subject: ERTH
title: Energy and Mineral Resources
description: Lecture and discussion on the origin, distribution and exploitation of fossil fuels, renewable energy resources and ore deposits. Coverage and detail will depend partly on student interest and background.

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Seminar
description: Gain professional training and practical experience giving scientific presentations emphasizing Earth and planetary sciences, including analysis of associated ethical issues. Grading is distributed 60/40 between three oral communication assignments and related ethics content.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth: A Model Planet
description: Integrative course that explores the interactions between the solid earth, oceans, atmosphere, and space environment, and introduces methodology and tools for computer modeling of the Earth as a system and its long-term climate and habitability.
prereq_raw: ( ERTH 101 and ERTH 250 , and at least one of ERTH 302 , ERTH 309 , ERTH 313 , ERTH 323 , ERTH 325 , or ERTH 333 ) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data.
prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Marine Geology
description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

subject: ERTH
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Covers aqueous geochemistry at the land-ocean interface, including the distribution of major and minor ions, trace metals, organic chemicals, and nutrients.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , CHEM 162 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Plate Tectonics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

subject: ERTH
title: Earthquakes and Crustal Deformation
description: Earthquakes and crustal deformation through modern seismological and geodetic observations; elastic properties of rocks, seismic waves, causes, detection, and location of earthquakes; crustal motions of the earthquake cycle; tsunami generation, liquefaction, and planetary observations.

subject: ERTH
title: Engineering Geology
description: Solutions of geotechnical problems by geologists and engineers through recognition, characterization, evaluation, and assessment of geologic processes that impact people, engineering structures, and engineering operations. Group format.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH, GEOL, and CEE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing and higher.

subject: ERTH
title: Hydrogeology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.
prereq_raw: ERTH 200 or ERTH 201 , and MATH 215 or MATH 241

subject: ERTH
title: Geological Remote Sensing
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to nonmajors.

subject: ERTH
title: Geospatial Information
description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data.

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Geology
description: Comparative geology of the terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, tectonism, geomorphology, weathering; manned and unmanned space exploration.

subject: ERTH
title: Lunar Geology
description: Introduction to the basics of the geology and spectroscopy of our Moon.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of the Solar System
description: Exploration of the origin and evolution of our solar system. Understanding the composition of the universe and its constituents (planets, asteroids, stars, comets, and meteorites).
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 130 and CHEM 161 and PHYS 170 .

subject: ERTH
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Workshops
description: Designed for in-service school professionals to learn new approaches and concepts in the fields of earth and planetary sciences.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable for credit. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: ERTH
title: Equations of Geophysics
description: Least-square approximation of functions by orthogonal series; potential, wave heat flow equations; boundary value problems; Bessel Hankel functions, spherical harmonics, potential theory, plane waves, spherical waves; emphasis on geophysics application.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , PHYS 400 , or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Explosive Volcanism
description: Explosive volcanic eruptions: from causes to consequences. Review of current physical volcanology including ascent and fragmentation of magma, transport and deposition processes in pyroclastic eruptions, volcanic crisis management and volcanic eruption scenarios. Seven-day field trip.

subject: ERTH
title: Theoretical Petrology
description: Derivation of phase diagrams from basic thermodynamics principles. Equilibria of natural silicate systems. Crystal chemistry, kinetics, diffusion, etc., applied to igneous and metamorphic petrology.
prereq_raw: ERTH 302 , ERTH 325 , and CHEM 351 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Petrology of Ocean Lithosphere
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Petrogenesis of the oceanic lithosphere, including mantle processes and rocks from mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, oceanic hotspots, back-arc basins, and intra-oceanic arcs.

subject: ERTH
title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
description: Combined lecture/discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning.

subject: ERTH
title: Lava Flow Rheology and Morphology
description: Effusion eruptions: from eruption to final flow form. Includes: rheology, effusion rate, heat loss, and field measurements, followed by inflation, flow forms, lava lakes, domes, flow hazard and modeling. Field trips to Kilauea and Makapuu.

subject: ERTH
title: Current Events in Volcanology
description: Discussion of active areas of volcanism and new publications on volcanology.

subject: ERTH
title: Submarine Volcanoes
description: Seminar exploring different aspects of submarine effusive and explosive volcanism, hydrothermal activity, and volcano-hosted ecosystems.

subject: ERTH
title: Isotopes and Trace Elements
description: Principles of radiogenic and stable isotope, and trace element geochemistry as applied to igneous petrology, mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, and terrestrial evolution.

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Teaching Geology
description: For ERTH graduate students who lead, under faculty supervision, a scheduled class in Geology and Geophysics. The instructor will define the student’s responsibilities when offering ERTH 609, and these responsibilities must be met for a passing grade. As the consent to take the class must also be granted by the department chair, the chair will also review the responsibilities required by the instructor.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH graduate students only.

subject: ERTH
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Seminar in which students present a 15- to 20-minute talk on their research or a related topic. Meets once a week with two to three talks per meeting. Graduate students are required to register for this course once per year.

subject: ERTH
title: Accelerated Introduction to Earth Sciences I
description: Lecture presenting a rapid-paced survey of earth sciences for graduate students. Includes origin of the Solar System, tectonics, volcanology, whole-earth composition, phase transformations, petrology (igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary), historical geology, and hydrology. Saturday field trips.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data. Credit earned only one time for either ERTH 413 or 613.
prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Field Study
description: Shipboard and land-based projects.

subject: ERTH
title: Literate Programming With R and RStudio
description: Literate programming with R, RStudio, and R Markdown for data analysis and research. Introduction to Matlab for rapid modeling. Emphasis on the preparation of research papers for scholarly publication in the Earth and environmental sciences.
prereq_raw: competence in basic differential and integral calculus.

subject: ERTH
title: How to Write a Scientific Paper
description: Designed for students who have collected data and want to know how to publish their work in a scientific journal. Covers the essential parts of paper preparation and submission.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH students only.

subject: ERTH
title: Summer Fieldschool Program: Hydrogeophysics in Volcanic Environments
description: Will cover the full hydrogeophysical workflow including theory, acquisition design, field data acquisition, data processing, data inversion, and hydrogeological interpretation. Methods include ambient seismic, 3D electrical resistivity tomography and induced polarization, and self-potential.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.

subject: ERTH
title: Electron Microprobe Analysis
description: Combined lecture-lab on principles and procedures for textural and geochemical analysis by the SOEST electron microprobe. Hands-on experience with the microprobe operation. Each student will complete one individual research project using the microprobe.

subject: ERTH
title: Introduction to Earth and Planetary Geophysics
description: Introductory geophysics course integrating theory, data analysis, and field methods to study Earth, planetary, and solar dynamics. Methods of seismology, gravity, geodesy, and electromagnetism, with field applications in tectonics, geomorphology, archeology, volcanism, and hydrology.
prereq_raw: ERTH 250 and MATH 242 and PHYS 272 ; or equivalents.

subject: ERTH
title: Advanced Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system and remediation methods. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase and isotope chemistry of environmental contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Numerical Modeling of Physical Systems
description: Finite difference, finite element, and other modeling techniques applied to geological and geophysical problems. Physical modeling of heat flow, molecular diffusion, solidification and melting, deformation, fluid flow, wave propagation, and other phenomena.

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics-Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation).
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

children.text: with a minimum grade of B-
for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

subject: ERTH
title: Geophysics-Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure.
prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent).

children.text: with a minimum grade of B-
for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

subject: ERTH
title: Seismology
description: Elasticity, wave equations, body waves, surface waves, free oscillations, seismometry, seismogram interpretation, tectonics, inversion, source theory, and waveform modeling.

subject: ERTH
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmospheric-sediment system and coevolution of the biota.
prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Stable Isotope Biogeochemistry
description: Stable isotope geochemistry applied to questions of biogeochemical cycling in the oceans, sediment diagenesis, paleoceanography, environmental geochemistry and ecology.

subject: ERTH
title: Coastal Geochemistry
description: Geochemistry at the land-ocean interface: coastal hydrology, subterranean estuaries and coastal mixing and their importance in governing the distribution of selected radiotracers, trace metals and nutrients. Combined lecture-lab with field trips and group projects.
prereq_raw: CHEM 162 , and MATH 241 or MATH 251A ; or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

subject: ERTH
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

subject: ERTH
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.
prereq_raw: CHEM 171 , or CHEM 161 and CHEM 162 ; PHYS 152 ; and MATH 242 or MATH 252A ; and consent.

subject: ERTH
title: Geomagnetism and Cosmic Magnetism
description: Magnetic fields of Earth, planets, stars, and galaxies; dynamo theories; paleomagnetism; terrestrial and lunar rock magnetism; planetary, regional, and local geomagnetic sounding.

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Contamination
description: Principles of groundwater chemistry; chemical evolution in natural groundwater flow systems; sources of contamination; mass transport processes; hydrochemical behavior of contaminants.

subject: ERTH
title: Groundwater Modeling
description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

subject: ERTH
title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

subject: ERTH
title: Planetary Surfaces
description: Comparative geology of terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, geomorphology; remote sensing; manned and unmanned space exploration.

subject: ERTH
title: Cosmochemistry
description: Formation and evolution of planets as astrophysical objects, geologic bodies, and abodes of life; current understanding from studies of the Solar System, star formation, meteorites, exoplanets; theory of formation and dynamics; atmospheres, oceans, habitability, biosignatures.
prereq_raw: ERTH 325 or CHEM 351 (or equivalent); or consent.

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Remote Sensing
description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

subject: ERTH
title: Remote Sensing: planets
description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

subject: ERTH
title: Remote Sensing: volcanoes
description: Spectroscopic, radar, thermal, and other methods for remote sensing applied to geologic problems; instrumental design and data analysis. (B) planets; (C) volcanoes.

subject: ERTH
title: Seminar in Tectonics
description: Evolution of ocean basins, margins, foldbelts, and platforms, from plate tectonics and regional syntheses of structure, petrology, geophysics, and stratigraphy.

subject: ERTH
title: (Alpha) Extraterrestrial Material
description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

subject: ERTH
title: Extraterrestrial Material: meteorites
description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

subject: ERTH
title: Extraterrestrial Material: petrology of the Moon and Mars
description: Mineralogical and compositional characteristics of extraterrestrial matter and the implications for the origin and history of the solar system. The subject is treated in two full-semester courses: (B) meteorites; (C) petrology of the Moon and Mars.

subject: ERTH
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paleoceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere and biosphere.

subject: ERTH
title: The Generic Mapping Tools
description: Introduction to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT). Processing of scientific data and the automated preparation of maps and illustrations using GMT on UNIX workstations, with introduction to UNIX and the C shell environment.

subject: ERTH
title: Data Analysis in the Earth and Space Sciences
description: Advanced data analysis in Earth and Space sciences, including time-series and frequency-domain methods, Bayesian statistics, Monte Carlo simulations, clustering and machine learning. Term project required.
prereq_raw: ERTH 613 , OCN 760 , or ASTR 633 or equivalent is highly recommended.

subject: ERTH
title: Bayesian Data Analysis
description: Linear and nonlinear techniques for model selection, parameter estimation, simulation and forecasting, from Bayesian principles with particular attention to large data sets and sparse noisy data.

subject: ERTH
title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
description: Interpretation of geophysical and laboratory data to understand elastic and anelastic properties, composition, phase relationships, temperature distribution in the Earth.

subject: ERTH
title: Fractures and Faults
description: Lecture on elasticity theory, fracture mechanics and boundary element modeling, with application to faults and fractures in the Earth.

subject: ERTH
title: Exoplanet Astronomy
description: Accelerated survey of exoplanet astronomy and planetary systems using data from the field’s leading edge, introduction to key theoretical concepts, application of analytic and numerical tools, and development of teamwork, presentation, and publishing skills.
prereq_raw: ASTR 633 with a minimum grade of B, or instructor permission.

subject: ERTH
title: Selected Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ERTH
title: Special Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
description: Content to be announced.

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Seminar
description: Seminar to improve student awareness of trends and practices in geoscience professions, and develop ability to prepare, deliver, and evaluate a professional scientific presentation. Targets abstract writing, oral presentation, and technical criticism.

subject: ERTH
title: MGeo Professional Project
description: Practical hands-on professional experience, typically with a local company or agency, and involving a final written report and an oral presentation. A grade of credit is assigned when the internship presentations are satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MGEO majors only.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
description: Concepts and theories analyzing ethnic group experiences in relation to colonization, immigration, racism, and social class. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values rooted in the experiences of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
description: Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popular culture (film, television, music, social media, sports, etc.). Introduction to critical media analysis and social science theories and methods. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ES
title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

subject: ES
title: Hawaiians
description: The social system, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians in a Pacific context. Transformation of the Hawaiian system by a capitalist economy. Native Hawaiian regeneration and quest for sovereign governance as an Oceanic society.

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Diaspora
description: Introduction to Filipinos in diaspora. Topics include: race, empire, migration, representation, cultural production, identity formation, and decolonization.

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Identity
description: Individual and group problems of identity, identity conflict, culture conflict, inter-ethnic relations. Critical review of available material on Hawaiʻi.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience I
description: Afrocentric perspective. Analysis of the black political/cultural diaspora, including ancient African kingdoms, the slavery experience, organized resistance, emancipation struggles, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: ES
title: African American Experience II
description: Black sociopolitical perspectives of the Reconstruction period, Jim Crow, intellectual and cultural awakenings, civil rights movements, and contemporary issues as examined through students’ written analysis and creative projects.

subject: ES
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Ethnicity and Community: Hawaiʻi
description: Site visits to museums, social welfare units, etc., as well as guest lecturers from the community including police, health, education.

subject: ES
title: Asian America
description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation. Emphasis on ethics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Hawaiʻi and the Pacific
description: Hawaiʻi as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

subject: ES
title: Japanese and Okinawans in Hawaiʻi
description: Transoceanic context of Japanese and Okinawan migration; their history in labor, politics, and business; politics of gender, race, ethnicity, and class; contemporary ethical issues in light of changing economic, social, and political conditions in Hawaiʻi.

subject: ES
title: Power and Place: Chinatowns
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of Chinese in Hawaiʻi and the U.S. continent with a focus on Chinatowns; urbanization; economic development, community organizing; comparative racialization.

subject: ES
title: Filipinos in Hawaiʻi
description: Historical and contemporary experiences; immigration; traditional culture and values; plantation experience; labor organizing; development of Filipino community; racism; discrimination; and ethnic identity. This course develops oral communication skills.

subject: ES
title: American Indian Experience
description: Provides a comprehensive look at the indigenous foundation of life and society in the Americas and elaborates on historical and contemporary importance of American Indian rights issues. Emphasis on teaching ethical issues and writing.

subject: ES
title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation.
prereq_raw: one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent.

subject: ES
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawaiʻi
description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

subject: ES
title: The Sounds of Race and Inequality
description: Explore inequality as manifested and contested in silence, music, dialect, nature, voice, and acoustic space by listening through a matrix of race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexualities. Combination of hands-on work and current scholarship.

subject: ES
title: Economic Change and Hawaiʻi’s People
description: Hawaiʻi’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

subject: ES
title: Immigration to Hawaiʻi and U.S.
description: Historical and current immigration discourses and policies in Hawai’i and the US; oceanic concepts of migration; experiences of various ethnic groups; immigrant-led movements for justice. Course develops written communication ranging from storytelling to research papers.

subject: ES
title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawaiʻi
description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawaiʻi; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
prereq_raw: one ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course.

subject: ES
title: Literatures of Hawaiʻi
description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawaiʻi, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Asian American Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing.

subject: ES
title: Issues of Diversity in Higher Education
description: Examines issues of diversity within higher education. Examines different dimensions of diversity including ethnicity, gender, national origin, age, and sexual orientation. Will utilize national and local case studies.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior class standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Fieldwork in Ethnic Studies
description: Supervision of individual student research projects pertinent to ethnic studies, including service learning, civic engagement, internship, oral history, or supervised practicum experience in teaching select ethnic studies courses.

subject: ES
title: Social Movements in Hawaiʻi
description: Examines, through writing and collaboration, interethnic movement building among Native Hawaiian, other Pacific Islander, and Asian peoples of Hawai’i through intersectional theories of social change to evaluate strategies to create just and sustainable futures.

subject: ES
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Intersecting processes of racial and gender oppression and privilege; institutional contexts and lived experiences; ethical issues in past and present anti-racist feminist thought and activism in the United States and in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: ES 101 or WGSS 151 or junior standing.

subject: ES
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Change in the Pacific-Polynesia
description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

subject: ES
title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere in Oceania with special attention to cultural interactions and connections. This course develops oral communication skills.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Ethnic Studies in the Digital World
description: The digitally networked world mediates race and ethnicity-and vice-versa. We will challenge racism and discrimination manifested in social media, changing notions of identity and group belonging, ewaste, gaming, big data, and more.

subject: ES
title: Race, Class, and the Law
description: Historical context and implications of landmark court decisions and legal issues affecting social change in ethnic communities in Hawaiʻi and the continental U.S.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Gender and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
prereq_raw: one 300-level ES or WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: -level ES or WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: ES
title: American Ethnic and Race Relations
description: Surveys ethnic and race relations in the U.S. Focus on historical conflicts and critical issues such as racism, immigration, affirmative action, economy, government, and systemic change. Develops written communication skills.

subject: ES
title: Mixed Race Identities, Multiracial Experiences
description: Critically examines historical and contemporary issues surrounding mixed race identities and experiences through themes that resonate in localized contexts within the continental U.S. and Oceania.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Filming Social Change
description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Contemporary Diasporas in Comparative Perspective
description: Compares the circumstances under which contemporary Asian, Pacific Islander, or African migrants form diasporas across the globe; focus on a particular ethnic group to examine its site-specific experiences.

subject: ES
title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ES
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: ES
title: Raciolinguistics
description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere.

subject: ES
title: (Alpha) Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

subject: ES
title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Middle East
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

subject: ES
title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C).

subject: ES
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawaiʻi
description: Historical and contemporary social processes involved in race, racism, and inter-ethnic relations in Hawaiʻi. Focus on intersection of Asian and/or Pacific Island cultures with Native Hawaiian culture.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or WGSS 202 ; or consent.

subject: ES
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ES
title: Latinx Experience in Hawaiʻi
description: Examines historical, socio-cultural, and contemporary Latinx presence; relations among Latinx, other immigrant, and Indigenous communities; causes and patterns of immigration; racism and discrimination; ethnicity and identity issues; struggles for justice.
prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Qualitative Research Methods in Oceanic Ethnic Studies
description: Engagement with theoretical elements and qualitative research methods of Oceanic Ethnic Studies.
prereq_raw: one upper division ES or SOCS course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Peoples of Hawaiʻi
description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawaiʻi using anthropological and ethnic studies approaches. Emphasis on cultural perspectives and values of peoples indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: ES
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent.

subject: ES
title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
description: Literature, methodology, ethics and project design of oral history research. Students develop and execute an oral history project.

subject: ES
title: Hawaiʻi’s Labor History
description: Conditions of work under varying political, social, and economic transformations in Hawaiʻi; anthropological, sociological, and historic data.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: ES
title: Special Topics in Ethnic Studies
description: Selected themes in ethnic studies exploring current issues and new topics; taught by regular and visiting faculty.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment I: Social and Cultural Contexts for Learning
description: Knowledge and skills related to the context of teaching. Teacher candidates will examine the impact of culture, family, school, classroom, and individual characteristics on learning, and orally present, in varied formats, acquired knowledge and competencies.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment II: Classroom and Behavior Management
description: Teacher candidates explore the ethical implications for establishing, maintaining, and restoring the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning.

subject: ESEE
title: Learner in the Environment III: Behavior Project Implementation
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate the ability to establish, maintain, and (when necessary) restore the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. Candidates demonstrate ability to identify maladaptive student behaviors and implement effective, research-based interventions.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment I: Foundations of Assessment
description: Introduction to foundational aspects of assessment and emphasizes the importance of linking assessment with planning and instruction. Candidates develop knowledge, skills, and dispositions important for designing, implementing, and analyzing effective assessments for diverse learners.

subject: ESEE
title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Science
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, using evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Mathematics in Inclusive Settings
description: Prepares beginning elementary school teachers of mathematics, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: STEM
description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to teaching and learning of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) content for inclusive elementary classrooms, K-6. Teacher candidates focus on planning, teaching, and assessing STEM.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction: Integrating Social Studies and the Performing Arts
description: Social Studies and Performing Arts integrated content in diverse K-6 classrooms. Teacher candidates engage with social issues through collaborative, expressive, aesthetic, creative, and critical pedagogy. Candidates perform, present, and teach to develop oral communication skills.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy I: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, K-3
description: Overview of principles and practices for teaching reading (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) to diverse students, grades K-3; including planning, instruction, and assessment. Writing assignments include lesson reflections, case studies, modules, and reading responses.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy II: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, Grades 4-6
description: Teacher candidates demonstrate essential reading comprehension strategies, engaging students in complex text by planning, instructing, and assessing elementary students in grades 4-6, in inclusive settings. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ESEE
title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy III: Writing and Visual Arts in Inclusive Settings, K-6
description: Methods, programs, and strategies for planning, teaching, and assessing writing for elementary students in inclusive settings, grades K-6. Visual arts methods are integrated to develop visual literacy.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience I: Response to Intervention in Reading
description: Teacher candidates in this field based course will use an evidence-based practice in reading within a response to intervention (Rtl) framework. Supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Rounds
description: Field-based course engages teacher candidates in a variety of purposeful observation and reflection activities aligned with course work. Field settings are appropriate to concurrent classes; supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience II: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

subject: ESEE
title: Field Experience III: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

subject: ESEE
title: Student Teaching in Elementary and Special Education Classrooms
description: Full-time student teaching in grades K-6 in an elementary school inclusion classroom, or a combination of general education and special education settings. The experience is directed by a qualified mentor teacher and has university-provided supervision.

subject: ESEE
title: Seminar for Student Teaching
description: Seminar to support student teaching experiences and prepare teacher candidates to transition into a full time teacher, examine ethical issues in the field, prepare for employment, and demonstrate ability to meet professional standards.

subject: ESL
title: Composition I for Second Language Writers
description: Extensive practice in writing expository essays; linguistic devices that make an essay effective. (Fulfills composition requirement for nonnative speakers of English only.)

subject: FDM
title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
description: Introduction to the fields of apparel design and merchandising including theories of fashion change, apparel industry operations, current industry issues, literature of the field, professional competencies, careers in apparel and related businesses.

subject: FDM
title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: FDM
title: Basic Apparel Construction
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles, concepts, and procedures for quality construction and custom fitting of clothing.

subject: FDM
title: Fashion History
description: Historic study of dress as related to customs and cultures in the Western world, in sociohistorical and contemporary contexts. Emphasis on 19th and 20th centuries.

subject: FDM
title: Block Pattern Design
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of pattern making for women’s apparel through manipulation of pattern blocks.

subject: FDM
title: Textiles I
description: Introduction to fibers, fabric structure, and finishes related to selection and care. Interrelationship between textile characteristics, properties, and end uses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: FDM
title: Costumes/Cultures of East Asia
description: Development of ethnic dress of China, Japan, and Korea as a visual manifestation of culture. Students will be trained in written communication skills to describe and report important designs of these ethnic dresses related to culture.

subject: FDM
title: Fashion Forecasting/Marketing
description: Principles and practices in fashion trend forecasting, including environment analysis, consumer research, competitive analysis, color and textile forecasting, style directions, and digital marketing trends. Adapting fashion trend forecasts to apparel lines.
prereq_raw: one FW or FG course, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Draping
description: Principles of pattern making through draping muslin models on standard garment forms.

subject: FDM
title: Group Collection Development
description: Advanced study in the specialty market design, pattern making, and construction for fashion design majors. Different specialty designs, such as swimwear, menswear, or others, will be offered each semester.
prereq_raw: FDM 215 , FDM 221 , and FDM 301 . Recommended: FDM 315 , FDM 330 .

subject: FDM
title: Advanced Construction
description: Principles of advanced techniques for pattern development and garment construction with emphasis on difficult-to-handle fabrics and custom fits.

subject: FDM
title: 2D/3D Computer Aided Design
description: Exploration of CAD applications from the design to the pattern-making process. Use of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop for fashion illustration. Use of OptiTex PDS pattern design software featuring 2D and 3D CAD.

subject: FDM
title: 3D Retail Store Design
description: Visual merchandising concepts and planning; use of a virtual 3D store modeling software package. Visual Retailing/Mockshop, to design store interiors, fixtures, lighting, signage, window displays, and planograms.

subject: FDM
title: Writing for the Fashion Industry
description: Analysis and creation of different types of writing in the fashion industry, with emphasis on creating a professional writing style.
prereq_raw: FDM 101 , FDM 200 or FDM 210 , and FDM 221 .

subject: FDM
title: Branding
description: Study of principles and practices in brand architecture and effective brand-building strategies; analysis of a case study and application of the concepts of brand management.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Retail Buying and Merchandising
description: Theories and procedures in selecting, buying and selling apparel and textiles. Types of merchandising organizations, analysis of consumer demand, brick-and-click opportunities and challenges, development of an image, operation location, store and floor layout.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors only.

subject: FDM
title: Merchandise Planning and Control
description: Theories, problems, and procedures of financial and assortment planning and control of merchandise inventories.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors and merchandising minors only.

subject: FDM
title: Product Lifecycle Management
description: Application of principles of apparel production management, including methods engineering (detail construction for ordering), story boards and color tables, production measurements, costing, and PLM computer applications.

subject: FDM
title: Apparel Manufacturing
description: Application of principles and procedures related to the promotion of fashion apparel. Preparation and presentation of fashion information through shows, displays, media, and written communications.

subject: FDM
title: Entrepreneurship in Retail
description: Application of principles, procedures and techniques of organizing a small retail business in a brick-and-click world. Students develop, write, and evaluate business plans creatively using low and high tech resources and oral communication skills.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors only Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Fashion Museum Management
description: Investigation of skills and techniques needed for handling textile and apparel artifacts in museums and other collections. Active involvement in documenting, researching, interpreting, and exhibiting costumes and textiles. Involves written work and oral presentations.

subject: FDM
title: Global Trade and Sourcing
description: Theories, concepts, problems of international trade of textile and apparel products. Issues of importing and exporting apparel products globally. Social, economic, and ethical factors affecting textile and apparel trade.

subject: FDM
title: Topics in Fashion
description: Study and discussion of special topics, problems. Offered by staff and visiting faculty.

subject: FDM
title: Internship and Capstone Portfolio
description: Examination of issues and opportunities associated with careers in fashion and related businesses and industries. Topics include interpersonal skills development, job search and interview strategies, and ethical issues in the workplace.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: FDM
title: Field Study in the Fashion Industry
description: Study tours to various centers of the world to examine historical and modern apparel and textiles. Merchandising and design methods and operations examined.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Beginning Filipino
description: Continuation of FIL 101 .

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: Continuation of FIL 102 . Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Intermediate Filipino
description: Continuation of FIL 201 .

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: Continuation of FIL 102 . Lessons focus on various aspects of Philippine culture and specialized topics that cater to the needs of teachers intending to teach Filipino immigrant students or teach Filipino as a second language. Meets five hours a week; daily lab work.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino for Education
description: Continuation of FIL 202 or FIL 224 .

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino I
description: Conversation, advanced reading and composition on traditional culture and indigenous knowledge. Includes emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Third-Level Filipino II
description: Conversation, advanced reading, and composition on contemporary issues. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: Training in comprehension of spoken authentic/simulated authentic materials presented in news broadcasts, songs, documentary narration, formal lectures, radio and television soap operas, etc.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Film: Art and History
description: Study and analysis of Filipino films: its history, forms, development and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic context.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino I
description: Advanced reading in traditional literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced oral communication and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Fourth-Level Filipino II
description: Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: FIL
title: Advanced Filipino Aural Comprehension
description: Continuation of FIL 315 . Training in comprehension and analysis/criticism of spoken authentic materials through films.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Translation Techniques
description: Techniques of bilingual translation: Filipino to English and English to Filipino.

subject: FIL
title: Structure of Filipino
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, syntax.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature
description: Selected readings in poetry, short stories, and plays from early 1900s to present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: FIL
title: Filipino Contemporary Literature: 1980s-Present
description: Survey of literature from the 80s (1986) to the present. Co-curricular cultural activities included.

subject: FIN
title: Personal Financial Planning
description: Focuses on principles and techniques for handling personal financial decisions, including: personal budgeting, obtaining credit, life and casualty insurance, buying a home, buying an automobile, savings and investments, and retirement planning.

subject: FIN
title: Problems of Business Finance
description: Application of financial principles to cases involving important financial decisions; emphasis on writing.

subject: FIN
title: Corporate Financial Management
description: Development and analysis of modern financial theory and its implications for management decisions: market efficiency, capital asset pricing, firm investment decisions, capital structure, dividend policy, and cost of capital.

subject: FIN
title: Investments
description: Introduction to various investment media and capital markets. Topics include the analysis of security returns using techniques such as beta, filter rules, and portfolio theory.

subject: FIN
title: International Business Finance
description: Financial management of foreign and international business operations: the regulatory environment of international finance, financing international transactions, international capital markets, taxation. Financial decision-making in the firm.

subject: FIN
title: International Banking
description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking. Includes theory and practical applications. Topics include international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and global risk management.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Aspects of New Ventures
description: Examination of underlying business models for new ventures, how to determine corresponding financial requirements, and approaches to resource acquisition. Students explore a range of financing sources and related issues of valuation and deal structure. College restriction: Shidler students only.
prereq_raw: junior standing and BUS 314 , or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

subject: FIN
title: Options and Other Derivatives
description: Options and other derivatives. Equity options, index options and options on futures. Black-Scholos Model. Trading strategies and tactics. Contemporary developments in financial engineering.

subject: FIN
title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management
description: Security analysis and portfolio management from standpoint of the professional analyst and institutional investor. Recent advances in security valuation models, portfolio selection, and techniques for appraising portfolio performance. College restriction: Shidler students only.

subject: FIN
title: Bank Financial Management
description: Analysis of financial institution management within the domestic economy and regulatory environment. Topics include federal reserve activities, interest rates, regulation, lending, investments, and asset/liability management.

subject: FIN
title: Banking and Capital Markets
description: Covers the analytical skills necessary to work in the financial services industry, in particular in the bank treasury department or the fixed income capital market sector.

subject: FIN
title: Asian Finance
description: Financial systems, regulatory structure over financial institutions in the Asia-Pacific region. Major financial policy issues for financial sector reforms in the region. Seminar format.

subject: FIN
title: Enterprise Risk Management
description: Overview analyzing various primary risks faced by corporations and developing important risk management techniques with an emphasis on enterprise risk management. Combined lectures, case studies, and discussions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BUS majors only.

subject: FIN
title: Sustainable Finance
description: Explores criticism and defense of the traditional profit maximization business model. Economic theory, recent trends, and case studies will refine students’ understanding of this cutting-edge field.

subject: FIN
title: Special Topics in Finance, Real Estate or Insurance
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of finance and finance-related fields.

title: International Monetary Systems and Global Financial Markets
description: Supply and demand for capital in national and international markets. Nature of capital movements and role of capital in industrialization of regions and nations.

subject: FIN
title: Problems in Business Finance
description: Application of financial principles and analytical techniques to financial problems. Case method.

subject: FIN
title: Investment Analysis and Management
description: Techniques of security analysis, theories of investment, and the analysis of investment decisions related to portfolio planning.
