title: Financial Analysis and Valuation
description: Introduces the standard financial analysis framework and develops skills in analysis of financial information, evaluation of firms’ business risks and earnings prospects, and related applications in valuation.

subject: FIN
title: International Financial Management
description: Financial decision-making in an international setting: analysis of direct foreign investment; economic, accounting, and regulatory environments, including taxation; international money and capital markets; import and export financing; multinational working capital management; and risk aspects of international finance.

subject: FIN
title: International Banking
description: Commercial, investment, and merchant banking in the international arena. Includes international lending, Euromarkets, global gap management, Forex activities, and international risk management.

subject: FIN
title: Entrepreneurial Finance
description: Assessment of financial needs, arranging venture financing, assessing value to the entrepreneur and the investor(s), financial aspects of strategic planning, analyzing the tradeoffs between alternative financing choices and flexibility and control, harvesting the investment.

subject: FIN
title: Advanced Capital Markets
description: Regulatory structure over capital market institutions, market developmental issues, market microstructure issues, and corporate governance, and creation of capital market infrastructure. Seminar format.

subject: FIN
title: PDEs and Stochastic Calculus
description: Covers PDEs (Partial Differential Equations) and calculus in a stochastic environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Programming in Finance
description: Addresses programming principles, and programming languages used in financial modeling.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Portfolio Optimization
description: Introduces students to principles of capital markets, classical portfolio theory, and focus on portfolio optimization.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Financial Derivatives
description: Will familiarize the students with the mathematical foundation and the application of Futures, Swaps, and Options.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Quantitative Methods in Finance
description: Focus on financial forecasting and financial econometrics as volatility and correlation modeling.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Insurance and Risk Management
description: Introduces students to topics in the actuarial science and latest developments in risk management.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Interest Rate/Credit Models
description: Addresses specific properties of interest rate modelling as mean reversion as well as latest developments in credit risk modelling.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN

description: Addresses advanced techniques in financial modelling and related fields.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in the MSF program, or consent.

subject: FIN
title: Seminar in Finance
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and issues in finance.
repeatable_raw: May be repeated with change in topic.

subject: FIN

description: Students either program a model or write a paper with high practical or scientific merit. Outcome enhances the chances for employment. Represents the culminating experience for students in this program.

description: Focus on important accounting and financial management principles relevant to management of health services organizations. Designed around a series of cases that examine the issues that confront healthcare managers.

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students only.

subject: FIN
title: Seminar in Investments
description: Covers research issues in investments. Topics include empirical asset pricing tests, characteristics of asset returns, behavioral finance, and investment issues that overlaps with corporate finance, accounting, and economics, etc.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration, or consent.

subject: FIN

subject: FISH

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FISH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: FISH

description: Students will be exposed to fisheries topics related to marine policy, economics, law, governance, and human health and well-being. Students will build on the material from FISH 601 - Fish and Fisheries .
prereq_raw: FISH 601 with a minimum grade of B.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: FISH

description: Explores Pacific communities’ fisheries management, cultural practices, and reciprocal relationships, highlighting their beliefs, traditions, and innovations in sustaining marine resources for present and future generations.

description: Provides an introduction to statistical modeling in a Bayesian framework using computation tools with applications to fisheries sciences.
prereq_raw: B or better in BIOL 220 or ECON 321 or MATH 372 , or their equivalent, or instructor approval.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: FISH

subject: FISH

description: Introduces the scientific and policy basis for federal fisheries management in the Western Pacific region. Students learn about the management process and attend a Council meeting to interact with stakeholders.

subject: FISH

description: Introduces the complexities of tropical marine fisheries through an intensive field study experience. Students learn foundational concepts in fish biology and fisheries ecology, fishery stock assessment and management, and social-ecological methods in an immersive environment.

subject: FISH
title: Fisheries Oceanography: From Physics to Landings
description: Overview of how oceanographic processes influence the distribution, life history, and abundance of fishery-relevant species. Topics will largely center on applications to Hawaiʻi, tropical/sub-tropical ecosystems, and the broader Pacific.
prereq_raw: C or better in OCN 620 or OCN 621 , and a background in biological oceanography and/or physical oceanography required.

subject: FISH

subject: FSHN
title: Food Service Safety and Sanitation
description: Principles and procedures of sanitation and safety in the food service industry, including the study of foodborne illnesses, biological, chemical, physical hazards and cross-contamination as they may occur during the flow of food.

subject: FSHN
title: Culture and Cuisine: The Global Diversity of Food
description: A timeline of the world history of food and how it relates to culture, diversity, ethnicity, and religion. International food demonstrations and tastings included.

subject: FSHN
title: Introduction to Food Preparation
description: Lectures, discussions, and demonstrations on how food components contribute to the functional, sensory, and safety characteristics of foods, and what changes occur in foods due to preparation, processing, and storage.

subject: FSHN
title: Food Preparation Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments in foods emphasizing ingredient function and standard preparation methods for food groups.

subject: FSHN
title: The Science of Human Nutrition
description: Integration of natural science concepts basic to the study of human nutrition. Emphasis on nutrient requirements of healthy individuals, food sources, functions of nutrients through a Pacific context.

subject: FSHN
title: Comparative Nutrition
description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

prereq_raw: ( FSHN 181 and FSHN 181L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: FSHN

subject: GEO

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO

subject: GEO

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: GEO

subject: GEO

subject: GEO
title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Japan
description: Regional synthesis of physical and cultural features; economic, social, political geography; origins and development of cities.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of China
description: Topics: environmental parameters and resource base, ecological control and resource management, institutional and technological transformation of agriculture, industrial potential and industrial location, settlement patterns and rural urban symbiosis.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of South Asia
description: An interdisciplinary course on South Asia covering contemporary debates and social movements pertaining to caste, gender, class, religion, region, labor, law, and development. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Southeast Asia
description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of the Pacific
description: Physical character of the Pacific; cultural, political, economic geography of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia (except Hawaiʻi).

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Honolulu
description: Development of Honolulu and Oʻahu from 1778. Evolution of function, land use, and social patterns. Contemporary planning and environmental issues arising from urban growth.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Hawaiʻi
description: Regional, physical, cultural geography. Detailed study of people and resources.

subject: GEO
title: UAV and Aerial Photography
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle systems) and the measurement, interpretation, analysis, and use of photography acquired by UAV and other aerial systems.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to Cartography and Air Photo
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of cartography: compilation and measurement from aerial photographs, alternate forms of data presentation, symbolism, design, and map projection.

subject: GEO
title: Map Design and Production
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Compilation, design and production of maps for presentations, research, and illustration using artists and mapping software.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Statistical Methods in Geography
description: Quantitative statistical methods will be explored for describing and interpreting geographic/environmental phenomena. Topics will include data display, measurement, sampling, spatial statistics, dimensional analysis, nonparametric and parametric models.
prereq_raw: ( GEO 101 or GEO 102 or GEO 151 ) or concurrent or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Introduction to GIS
description: Design, implementation, and use. Database construction and documentation. Techniques for spatial data manipulation and display. Evaluation of existing systems. Student research projects.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Reading
description: Limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in geography.

subject: GEO
title: Vegetation and the Climate System
description: Role of vegetation in the climate system; links to hydrology and biogeochemical cycling; vegetation and climate history; evolution of terrestrial ecosystems; effects of global warming.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Climate Change
description: Approaches to the study of past and future climate change.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Agricultural Climatology
description: Analyzing climatic data; relation to photosynthesis, phenological development, and crop yields. Crop-weather models as guides to improved land-use planning and agronomic practices.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Fluvial Geomorphology
description: Introduction to the single most important geomorphic agent shaping the terrestrial environment. Focus on fluvial process, fluvial dynamics, fluvial landforms, and sediment transport.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 / GEO 101L or GEO 303 or ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L .

subject: GEO
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Water in the Environment
description: Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawaiʻi and the Pacific region.
prereq_raw: either GEO 309 , BIOL 265 or BIOL 487 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Biogeography
description: Coevolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Human Role in Environmental Change
description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of GEO 101 , BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 and either GEO 322 or BIOL 310 ; or consent.

children.text: with a minimum grade of B

subject: GEO
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Resource Management in Southeast Asia
description: Challenges associated with the management of land, water resources, fisheries, forests and agriculture in modern Southeast Asia. Case studies are used to illustrate current problems and evaluate potential management solutions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Urban Geography
description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.
prereq_raw: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to nonmajors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Marine Policy
description: Introduction to the law and policies concerning the marine environment, commerce and security. Role of science, law and politics in historical and current policies for maritime trades, navigation safety, marine resources, and marine exploration.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Regional Analysis
description: Spatial dynamics and environmental implications of urban and rural development. Concepts of regions, process of regional development, patterns of spatial interaction, and theoretical bases for development strategies; emphasis on Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geographies of Popular Culture
description: Examines contemporary geographical debates related to concepts of discourse, identity, space/place, power, representation, and popular culture. Considers various landscapes of popular culture and how popular culture mediate a sense of place, geopolitics, and identity formation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

subject: GEO
title: Tea and Culture
description: Examines cultural practices of tea in different parts of the world, focusing on history and culture of tea in China, Japan, and England. Also includes changing technologies and economies of tea worldwide. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Political Geography of Oceans
description: The geopolitics of oceans and the law of the sea as applied to regions of conflict and cooperation historically and in the present. Emphasis on teaching written communication.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Geography of Peace and War
description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Topics in Geography
description: Selected topics in geography not offered in the regular geography curriculum.
prereq_raw: GEO 101 or GEO 102 or GEO 151 , or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Remote Sensing
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the principles of remote sensing and image processing skills. Topics include electromagnetic spectrum, sensors, aerial photo and satellite imagery interpretation, geometric and radiometric correction, digital image processing. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: 3D Mapping and Analysis
description: Environmental mapping and analysis using 3-dimensional geographical data acquired from high resolution remote sensing systems. Junior standing or higher.

subject: GEO
title: Field Mapping
description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Web Mapping
description: (3 2-hr Lab) Introduction to interactive web mapping techniques for sharing and visualizing various forms of geospatial data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS and Spatial Analysis for Social Sciences
description: Introduction to spacial analysis and GIS for social science studies, using open-source GIS tools to collect, visualize, and analyze social data; public health, socio-economic and social media data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

subject: GEO
title: GIS for Environmental Sciences
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr lab) Applications of GIS technologies to solve real-world problems in natural and environmental sciences. Research project, lab.

subject: GEO
title: Senior Thesis
description: Preparation of research paper under individual faculty supervision. Recommended for admission to graduate program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior GEO major and consent.

subject: GEO
title: Practicum in Geography
description: Internship in applied geography under professional and faculty supervision. Field placement integrated with academic study.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior major and consent.

subject: GEO
title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior GEO major.

subject: GEO
title: Directed Research
description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GEO majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Climatology
description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
prereq_raw: GEO 300 or GEO 400 or GEO 401 or GEO 402 or GEO 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320 ; or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawaiʻi, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

subject: GEO
title: Human Environment Systems
description: Role and potential of systems science in analysis of human environment interaction, especially resource management. Framework and methodology for problem structuring; overview of techniques.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing with consent.

subject: GEO
title: Theories and Policies of Development
description: Will critically examine what constitutes progress, advancement, or betterment in this highly uneven world, where inter-regional, inter-class, inter-group, and inter-gender differences in development are expanding. Graduate standing only.

subject: GEO
title: Coastal Planning and Management
description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture.

subject: GEO
title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

subject: GEO
title: Environment and Development
description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

subject: GEO
title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of Southeast Asia

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geography of the Pacific
description: Investigation of geographic problems of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia.

subject: GEO
title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

subject: GEO
title: Human Geography Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods in human geography. Explores and provides guided practical experience with research methods and analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Graduate seminar required of all department MA students and PhD students. Single credit course in which faculty present ongoing research in their fields.

subject: GEO
title: Concepts and Theories in Geography
description: Concepts, theory, models. Geographic approaches to spatial and environmental problems. Required of entering graduate students unless waived by department.

subject: GEO
title: Research Design/Methods in Geography
description: Elements of research design, practical field experience, exposure to research and ideologies, broad exposure to heritage and ethos of the discipline.

subject: GEO
title: Geomorphology
description: Current understanding of geomorphological concepts, processes, and the dynamic relationship between human landscape modification and system response.

subject: GEO
title: (Alpha) Special Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Special Topics: regional and locational analysis
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Special Topics: geography, environment, and culture
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Special Topics: Multi-objective decision analysis
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. (B) regional and locational analysis; (C) geography, environment, and culture; (H) Multi-objective decision analysis.

subject: GEO
title: Political Ecology
description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Resource Management in Asia-Pacific
description: Examination of resource management problems in Asia and the Pacific. Problems of resource use-agriculture, forestry, energy, minerals, ocean, air quality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate status.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Political Geography
description: Topics vary; may include borders, boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, identity politics, nations and nationalism, social categorization, the sovereign state system, territoriality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar: Geographies of Migration
description: Topics vary; may include immigration, borders, refugees, asylum, climate change, and displacement.

subject: GEO
title: Society and Space
description: Advanced seminar on social production of space. Topics include spatial metaphor in social theory; western spatiality from the renaissance through the enlightenment, modernity and post modernity; and geography of the body, home, landscape, and nation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: GEO
title: Seminar in Geographical Information Science
description: Graduate-level seminar in Geographic Information Science.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Elementary German
description: Conversation, grammar and reading.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Elementary German
description: Combined content of GER 101 and GER 102 covered in one intensive course.

subject: GER
title: Intermediate German
description: Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intermediate German
description: Conversation, grammar, reading and writing.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Intermediate German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

subject: GER
title: Phonetics and Pronunciation Practice
description: Analysis of the German phonological system and practice in pronunciation.
prereq_raw: GER 202 (or concurrent with consent) or GER 260 .

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) or GER 260

subject: GER
title: Structure of Modern German
description: Study of syntactic and morphological structures and basic pragmatic principles. Focuses on spoken and written Modern German.

subject: GER
title: Reading and Writing
description: Further development of reading and writing skills through the study of short texts, focusing on modern German short stories, fairy tales, poems and song lyrics.

subject: GER
title: Business German
description: Advanced German conversation, reading, and writing with a special emphasis on the vocabulary and cultural context of the German business world.

subject: GER
title: Contemporary Topics in Media
description: Development of listening and speaking, reading and writing skills through analysis and discussion of media: newspaper articles, radio, and television programs and online sources.

subject: GER
title: Conversation
description: Intensive practice in spoken German designed to increase vocabulary and improve oral proficiency.
prereq_raw: GER 202 (or concurrent with consent) or GER 260 .

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) or GER 260

subject: GER
title: Modern Readings: Wanderlust, Love, and Desire
description: Development of reading skills through the study of authentic modern texts (short stories; articles from newspapers, magazines, and the internet) with topics relating to culture, society, and history.

subject: GER
title: Modern Readings: Freedom, Happiness and Free Body Culture
description: Further expansion and improvement of reading skills through the study of authentic modern texts (short stories; newspaper articles, and internet) with topics relating to culture, society, and history, e.g., FKK Freikörperkultur, or free body culture.

subject: GER
title: Introduction to German Literature 1750-1914:
description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1750 to 1914.

subject: GER
title: Introduction to German Literature 1914-Present
description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1914 to present.

subject: GER
title: German Cinema
description: Study of German film history, film analysis, film theory, and film study. Lecture/discussion.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, or take LLEA 320 one time, for different topics. 6 cr. limit on GER 320/ LLEA 320 courses.

subject: GER
title: Intensive Third-Level German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the third-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

subject: GER
title: Germanic Civilization to World War II
description: German cultural heritage and history in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland until World War II.

subject: GER
title: Modern German Culture
description: Modern culture in post-World War II Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

subject: GER
title: Practical German for use in Hawaiʻi
description: Use of German in practical situations in Hawaiʻi, e.g., in travel industry.

subject: GER
title: Enlightenment-Sturm und Drang
description: Lessing and his contemporaries; early dramas of Goethe and Schiller; Goethe’s early lyrics.

subject: GER
title: Classicism
description: Classical writings of Goethe and Schiller; some reference to other writers.

subject: GER
title: Romanticism
description: Novalis, Tieck, E. T. A. Hoffmann, Eichendorff, etc.

subject: GER
title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both GER 416 and LLEA 416 .

subject: GER
title: Intensive Fourth-Level German Abroad
description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-level in German language and culture in a German-speaking country.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric & Palliative Medicine
description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric Medicine Research
description: Medical students will have the opportunity to complete a research project in the field of epidemiology of aging, and present an abstract at a local meeting. Basic principles of epidemiology and statistics will be taught.

subject: GERI
title: Geriatric and Palliative Medicine Elective
description: Provides an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in the outpatient, inpatient, homecare, and long-term care settings. Various instructional methods are utilized, including clinical experiences, workshops, and case discussions using a range of interdisciplinary teachers.

subject: GERI
title: Medical Student Training in Aging Program
description: Introduces medical students to clinical, research, and academic experiences in geriatrics, under the mentorship of faculty members.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD majors only.

subject: GERI
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: One-on-one independent study for students interested in geriatrics and/or palliative medicine. Students will work with a faculty mentor to define an area of interest and meet regularly for guidance and feedback.

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Restricted to GES majors.

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

subject: GES
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent) or SUST 112 (or concurrent).

subject: GES
title: GES Thesis Proposal
description: Supports GES majors in producing a thesis proposal that outlines and describes the timeline, required resources, etc. of the degree-required project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: GES
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

subject: GES
title: The Changing Earth and Climate System
description: Covers the Earth system, including mass and energy transfers, biogeochemical cycles, natural and anthropogenic changes on regional and global scale.
prereq_raw: MATH 241 , GES 302 (or concurrent), and OCN 201 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311 . Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
prereq_raw: GES 311 , MATH 242 , PHYS 170 / PHYS 170L , and CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. This course develops written communication skills.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Environmental Data Science
description: Provides an introduction to environmental data science by applying python-based programming techniques to Earth science datasets.
prereq_raw: MATH 242 , and ICS 110P or ICS 110C or ERTH 250 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 , GES 311 , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L , ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES 499 / OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 or BOT 305 / BIOL 305 or BOT 201 or BIOL 275 or MICR 351 or consent.

subject: GES
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305 , or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 .

subject: GES
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: GES
title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, make predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only

subject: GES
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only in their final semester.

subject: GES
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

description: Study of an author or phase in Greek studies.
