subject: HAW
title: Language in Hawaiʻi: A Microcosm of Global Language Issues
description: Survival kit for life in Hawaiʻi: Introduction to Hawaiian and language related issues enhancing communicative experience in Hawaiʻi. Examination of social, cultural, political, and linguistic cross-cultural interaction locally and globally. Taught in English/Hawaiʻi Creole English.

subject: HAW
title: Elementary Hawaiian I
description: Introductory course in Hawaiian language focused on the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding.

subject: HAW
title: Elementary Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of HAW 101 .

subject: HAW
title: Intensive Elementary Hawaiian
description: Content of HAW 101 - Elementary Hawaiian I and HAW 102 - Elementary Hawaiian II covered in one semester.

subject: HAW
title: I Ka ʻŌlelo Nō Ke Ola
description: Accelerated lecture/lab to bridge fluent speakers mainly from Kula Kaiapuni into Kawaihuelani’s system of Hawaiian that reflects a Hawaiian worldview, including HAW 101 - HAW 201 content, grammar, writing, and spelling conventions. Students matriculate into HAW 202 .

subject: HAW
title: Intermediate Hawaiian I
description: Continuation of HAW 102 with continued development in the foundational skills of language acquisition: speaking, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Increased emphasis on reading of traditional texts.
prereq_raw: HAW 102 or HAW 105 or exam or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Intermediate Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of HAW 201 .

subject: HAW
title: Intensive Intermediate Hawaiian
description: Content of HAW 201 - Intermediate Hawaiian I and HAW 202 - Intermediate Hawaiian II covered in one semester.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Literature in Translation
description: Survey of Hawaiian literature, including prose narration and poetry with reference to Polynesian and Western themes and forms.

subject: HAW
title: Papa Mele I (Mele in the Hawaiian Language Classroom)
description: The incorporation of mele and the performance thereof for the enhancement of second language acquisition in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Third-Level Hawaiian I
description: Continuation of HAW 202 with emphasis on increasing proficiency in speaking/ conversation, listening, comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian.
prereq_raw: HAW 202 or HAW 206 or exam, or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Third-Level Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of HAW 301 .

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Conversation
description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Moʻolelo Pōkole
description: Development of reading comprehension, pronunciation, vocabulary, and Hawaiian cultural knowledge through reading of Hawaiian language short stories. Short stories are from primary and secondary sources written by a variety of authors across different time periods.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Composition
description: Intensive work in the grammatical, semantic, and pragmatic dimensions of composition writing in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Listening Comprehension and Transcription
description: Development of listening comprehension through transcription and discussion of tape recordings.

subject: HAW
title: Ulu ka Hoi
description: Lecture offering focused study and creation of Hawaiian language newspapers with a concentration on the characteristics of writing in this genre. Students will produce a monthly newsletter in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Moʻomeheu Hawaiʻi
description: A survey course on the study of traditional Hawaiian culture including origins, the socioeconomic system, land tenure, religion, values, and the arts. The course will be taught in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Hana ʻOe a Kani Pono-Hawaiian Radio Broadcasting
description: Combined lecture/lab involving students in the planning and production of a weekly Hawaiian language radio broadcast. Includes research, writing, and voicing of mele and their stories on live radio.
prereq_raw: HAW 302 or HAW 384 (or concurrent with consent), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) , or consent

subject: HAW
title: Ka Haku Mele
description: Composers and Their Compositions. Provides a venue which will allow students to analyze, dissect and discuss mele (song, poetry and chant), paying close attention to the style of composition by identifying reoccurring nuances found in mele composed by the same as well as various authors.

subject: HAW
title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian I
description: Advanced speaking/conversation, discussion, listening comprehension, reading, writing, and cultural understanding. Conducted in Hawaiian. Transcribing and translating recordings of native speakers in Hawaiian.

subject: HAW
title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian II
description: Continuation of HAW 401 .

subject: HAW
title: Moʻolelo Hawaiʻi
description: Survey of the major works by Hawaiian scholars writing about the history and culture of Hawaiʻi including David Malo, Kamakau, Kepelino, and John Papa Īʻī.

subject: HAW
title: Kaʻao Hawaiʻi
description: Survey of the core literature written by Hawaiian scholars, including both historical and mythological epics and folk tales.

subject: HAW
title: I Leʻa Ka Hula I Ka Hoʻopaʻa (Moʻolelo, Kaʻao, Mele and Hula)
description: The incorporation of mele and hula performance with moʻolelo and kaʻao.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Manaʻo Politika Hawaiʻi-Political Thought in Hawaiian
description: Intensive study of Hawaiian political thought in writing and speech.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Hōʻike Honua
description: Study of Hawaiian land tenure practices through readings and discussions of audiotapes, written primary sources, maps, wind names, rain names, ʻŌlelo noʻeau (wise sayings), and mele (poetry). Readings are drawn from 19th and 20th century Hawaiian newspapers and other primary sources.

subject: HAW
title: Ma Ka Hana Ka ʻIke
description: Study of traditional Hawaiian language and cultural practices through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Moʻolelo-Creative Writing in Hawaiian
description: Study and composition of written works in various creative genres of Hawaiian storytelling, with a focus on the adaptation and maintenance of a Hawaiian voice and worldview in writing.

subject: HAW
title: I Paʻa Ke Kahua
description: An experiential approach to the acquisition of vocabulary, which will allow students to broaden and deepen their knowledge of language and the range of domains to perpetuate Hawaiian as a living language.

subject: HAW
title: E Pū Paʻakai Kākou: A Study of Traditional Hawaiian and Contemporary Food Culture
description: A study of traditional Hawaiian and contemporary food culture through hands-on applications and lectures.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Problems in Translation
description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

subject: HAW
title: Problems in Translation: legal documents
description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

subject: HAW
title: Problems in Translation: newspapers
description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

subject: HAW
title: Problems in Translation: religious writings
description: Problems in translation of: (B) legal documents; (C) newspapers; (D) religious writings.

subject: HAW
title: Nā Politika ma ka Nūhou Hawaiʻi- Politics in Hawaiian Language Media
description: Study of Hawaiian news media with emphasis on political content. Includes field trips to various archives.

subject: HAW
title: Structure of Hawaiian
description: Descriptive linguistic analysis. Intensive exercises in advanced grammar.

subject: HAW
title: ʻŌlelo Niʻihau I
description: Basic study of ʻŌlelo Niʻihau. Speaking and listening comprehension will be developed through listening to audio recordings, watching video recordings, and participating in face-to-face conversations with Niʻihau native speakers.

subject: HAW
title: History of the Hawaiian Language
description: Development from proto-Polynesian. Phonology, morphology, and grammar; history of research.
prereq_raw: HAW 302 (or concurrent) and HAW 452 , or consent.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

subject: HAW
title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: basketball
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

subject: HAW
title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: volleyball
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

subject: HAW
title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: football
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

subject: HAW
title: Haʻuki: Sports Education Through the Medium of Hawaiian: baseball
description: Provide Hawaiian language students with linguistic tools necessary to provide sports education to Hawaiian immersion schools and for basic intergenerational use of Hawaiian in the linguistic domain of sports. (B) basketball; (C) volleyball; (D) football; (E) baseball.

subject: HAW
title: Language for the Classroom
description: Examination of language needs in various classroom settings and introduction to new vocabulary in school content areas.

subject: HAW
title: Kuleana Kula Kaiapuni
description: Examination of the political struggles of the Kula Kaiapuni (Hawaiian Immersion Program)—past and present. Special attention given to federal and state governments, Department of Education, and internal political struggles.

subject: HAW
title: Hoʻomōhala Haʻawina Kaiapuni Curriculum Development
description: Examination of curricular issues of indigenous language programs; weekly participation in an immersion classroom; development of materials.

subject: HAW
title: Teaching in Hawaiian Language Immersion Program
description: Explore the knowledge base needed for teaching in the Hawaiian Language Immersion Program and initiate inquiry into the nature and social context of teaching, learning and schooling.

subject: HAW
title: Teaching Residency
description: Full-time student teaching in a Hawaiian language classroom.

subject: HAW
title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
description: Analysis and resolution of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning, professional growth and development.

subject: HAW
title: Papa Mele Wahi Pana
description: Will provide students with the opportunity to learn mele, mainly poetry and song, composed specifically for a certain area of Hawaiʻi.

subject: HAW
title: Hawaiian Poetry
description: Historical survey and analysis of poetry found in traditional chants, folk songs, modern poetry written in Hawaiian. Interpreting and composing Hawaiian poetry.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Hanakeaka-Hawaiian Language Playwriting
description: The creation and authoring of Hawaiian language play scripts based on traditional motifs.

subject: HAW
title: Kahua Hanakeaka (Hawaiian Medium Stage Production)
description: From design to performance, students mount an original production based on traditional motifs.

subject: HAW
title: ʻŌlelo Noʻeau
description: Survey and analysis of traditional proverbs and their kaona or symbolic meanings.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Mākau ʻŌlelo Aʻo Kula Kaiapuni Hawaiʻi
description: Assess the linguistic competence of prospective Hawaiian language immersion teachers to assure that all teachers entering the state DOE Hawaiian Immersion Program meet the requirements of the program with respect to Hawaiian language proficiency.
prereq_raw: HAW 402 (or concurrent), and HAW 463 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Analyzing Immersion Hawaiian
description: Analysis and acquisition of features in Hawaiian spoken by Hawaiian speaking children in Hawaiian immersion education.

subject: HAW
title: Learning Hawaiian Through Immersion
description: Learning Hawaiian in the immersion setting: cultural context, behavioral patterns, and learning concerns.
prereq_raw: HAW 302 , and either HAW 435 or HAW 484 ; or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Directed Studies
description: Study of Hawaiian language through vernacular readings in various academic fields.

subject: HAW
title: Kālaimanaʻo
description: Seminar analyzing various genres of Hawaiian language literature published in the 19th and 20th centuries, with an emphasis on understanding Hawaiian models of theory and debate employed by authors of this era.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HAW, HWST, and HSHK majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Kākāʻōlelo Oratory
description: A survey of oral performance styles to build increased oral skills.
prereq_raw: graduate standing and HAW 601 , or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Haku Palapala Noi Laeoʻo/Writing a Hawaiian Master’s Proposal
description: Seminar to select and develop students’ research topic, proposal, and organizational plan for Plan A or B completion. Majors are encouraged not to take this course in their first semester of the program.

subject: HAW
title: Ka Hana Noiʻi (Research Methods)
description: Research methodology course utilizing active research in the major repositories of Hawaiian language materials and Hawaiian-related knowledge.

subject: HAW
title: Nā Manaʻo Politika Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian Political Thought)
description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods.
prereq_raw: HAW 402 , HAW 428 , and POLS 303 ; or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Kuanaʻike
description: The examination of Hawaiian ways of speaking, as contrasted with English focusing on those features that are uniquely Hawaiian and can be said to constitute a Hawaiian worldview. Section 1 taught in Hawaiian; Section 2 taught in English.

subject: HAW
title: Moʻolelo Hawaiʻi
description: Intensive study, research, and analysis of Hawaiian history.

subject: HAW
title: (Alpha) Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Moʻolelo
description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepuʻu; (I) S. M. Kamakau.

subject: HAW
title: Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Moʻolelo: J. H. Kanepuʻu
description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepuʻu; (I) S. M. Kamakau.

subject: HAW
title: Nā Mea Kākau/Nā Haku Moʻolelo: S. M. Kamakau
description: Intensive study of an individual author, his/her works and nuances of his/her works. (E) J. H. Kanepuʻu; (I) S. M. Kamakau.

subject: HAW
title: Ke Aʻo ʻŌlelo Hou ʻAna (Teaching Hawaiian As a Second Language)
description: Survey of existing texts and teaching resources; analysis of student clientele and needs; review of pedagogical approaches for heritage and non-heritage learners; syllabus and materials development; observation of beginning Hawaiian language or Hawaiian immersion classroom.

subject: HAW
title: Pilina ʻŌlelo
description: In-depth examination and research into the grammar of Hawaiian including discussion of theories of language and incorporation of meta-language.

subject: HAW
title: ʻŌlelo Niʻihau
description: Intensive, advanced study and analysis of traditional Hawaiian Niʻihau dialect through face-to-face conversations with Niʻihau native speakers, listening to audio recordings and watching video recordings of Niʻihau native speakers.
prereq_raw: ( HAW 402 and HAW 453 ) with a minimum grade of B- or consent.

subject: HAW
title: Noiʻi Mele
description: Intensive study focusing on original compositions of Hawaiian poetry and song.

subject: HAW
title: Papahana Laeoʻo
description: Research for Plan B project/non-thesis. May include but not limited to internship with cultural practitioner.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HAW majors only.

subject: HAW
title: Directed Research
prereq_raw: consent of instructor and graduate chair.

subject: HAW
title: Noiʻi Pepa Laeoʻo (Thesis)
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: HDFS
title: Human Development
description: Concepts, issues, theories of human growth and development from conception to death; systems approaches to inquiry into factors affecting growth and development.

subject: HDFS
title: Mindfulness & Ethical Mindset
description: Lecture and experiential mindfulness practices to facilitate ethical engagement in daily life, fostering well-being and peaceful state of mind with others and within oneself. Develop skills to navigate everyday challenges through evidence-informed approaches of mindfulness.

subject: HDFS
title: Infancy and Early Childhood
description: Growth and development from prenatal period to age 5. Historical and current issues and research based on ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Childhood
description: Intensive investigation into developmental aspects of 6-12 year old children. Historical and current issues, research, and examination of the role of schools and other community resources. Focus on optimal development.

subject: HDFS
title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
description: Problems, concepts, and research related to development from puberty through early adulthood. Examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural factors affecting the individual.

subject: HDFS
title: Middle Age and Aging
description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Written assignments communicate information about physical and psychological age-related events, as well as social attitudes, values, to scholarly and community audiences.

subject: HDFS
title: Intimacy, Marriages and Families
description: Study of intimate relationships, marriages and families, their dynamics, strengths, growth and development, challenges, choices and opportunities, in the context of social change and cultural diversity.
prereq_raw: HDFS 230 or PSY 100 or SOC 100 ; or consent.

subject: HDFS
title: Parenting
description: Parenting theories, methods, skills, issues, and resources; parent-child relations in various cultural contexts.

subject: HDFS
title: Leadership and Group Process
description: Exploration of leadership research and theories and their application to leadership development; designed to enhance personal and interactive leadership.

subject: HDFS
title: Community Needs and Resources
description: Theory and practice in determining community needs and resources; community resources development based on needs identification.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Resource Management
description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Financial Planning
description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Economics
description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

subject: HDFS
title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
description: Employers regard soft skills as key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology
description: Fundamental scientific methodology, design and data collection; introduction to statistics and program evaluations, analysis of ethical issues.
prereq_raw: HDFS 230 or FDM 200 or TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

subject: HDFS
title: Research Methodology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Test design, computer use, data analysis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

subject: HDFS
title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, prepares students for direct, educational work with parents and children and for continued graduate work in child and family studies, counseling, psychology, social work and/or family life education.

subject: HDFS
title: Mindfulness and Skillful Living
description: Lecture, discussion, and experiential activities of principles and practice of an evidence-based contemplative science discipline. Focuses on development of writing skills and ethical applications to daily life, with implications for youth, families, and society.
prereq_raw: completed DS course (with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: completed DS course ( with a minimum grade of C

subject: HDFS
title: Marriage Development
description: Marital interaction and development; divorce and remarriage; resources and techniques for marital adjustment, enrichment, and growth.

subject: HDFS
title: Contemporary Family Issues
description: Investigation of current issues with impact upon family quality of life, with emphasis on the interdependent nature of families and their environments.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Life Education Methodology
description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, with service learning on Family Life Education Methodology.

subject: HDFS
title: Marriage and Family Therapy
description: Overview of the field of marriage and family therapy, including history, theory, and practice. Explores professional roles, family systems perspectives, and approaches to helping couples and families across diverse contexts.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: HDFS
title: Community Program Development
description: Concepts and theories of community program development; principles, practices, and procedures in administration and supervision of volunteer services surveyed and analyzed.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Public Policy
description: Cross-national survey of family public policy; analysis, revision, and development of family public policy; impacts of policy on consumers and families.

subject: HDFS
title: Consumer Communications
description: Development, production, analysis, and evaluation of consumer materials for print media. Use of desktop publishing computer programs.
prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

subject: HDFS
title: Family Economics
description: Study of personal family resources and its interaction with the economy. Focuses on contemporary economic problems that affect the welfare of families.
prereq_raw: HDFS 360 or an ECON course, or consent.

subject: HDFS
title: Topics in Family Resources
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: HDFS
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills in supervised work at an approved internship site and through analytical writing assignments and class discussions.
prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 , HDFS 340 , HDFS 360 , HDFS 380 , and HDFS 380L ) with a minimum grade of C.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HDFS majors only.

subject: HDFS
title: Capstone Portfolio
description: Preparation of a senior portfolio to be used as assessment of competence relative to national FCS standards. Includes extensive instruction on writing.
prereq_raw: ( HDFS 230 , HDFS 340 , HDFS 360 , HDFS 380 , HDFS 380L , and HDFS 492 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HDFS majors only.

subject: HDFS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent reading and research on a topic, done under supervision of a faculty member; outcomes contracted in writing with faculty member at beginning of semester.

subject: HIST
title: World History to 1500
description: Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from prehistory to 1500; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: World History since 1500
description: Continuation of HIST 151 . Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from 1500 to present; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: Issues in World History
description: In examining aspects of the histories of Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Oceania, this course highlights the myriad ways in which global contact has transformed our world and narratives of the past.

subject: HIST
title: World History of Human Disease
description: Examines how disease has affected humans in terms of society, culture, politics, religion, and economics. Explores the impact over a broad range of time periods, from pre-history to the present/future.

subject: HIST
title: Global Environmental History
description: Explores the influence of nature-climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms-on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Food
description: Exploration of food and eating from historical, cultural, economic, and geopolitical perspectives. Includes both historical and contemporary issues.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: Development of civilizations from prehistoric origins to 1500. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for HIST 151 and HIST 152 ; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: World Cultures in Perspective
description: Continuation of HIST 161A . Development of civilization from 1500 to the present. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for HIST 151 and HIST 152 ; students in Honors program only.

subject: HIST
title: Early European Civilization
description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states before 1500, including classical and medieval eras.

subject: HIST
title: European Civilization 1500-1800
description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states. 1500-1800.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Europe, 1789-Present
description: Major political, social, economic, and cultural trends from the revolutionary era to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: Survey of major civilizations of Asia from earliest times to 1500; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Civilizations of Asia
description: Continuation of HIST 241 . Survey of major civilizations of Asia from 1500 to the present; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: A survey of North American history from the Columbian Encounter to the U.S. Civil War.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to American History
description: Interpretive survey from 1865 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Hawaiian Islands
description: Survey of state and local history from Polynesian chiefdoms to Hawaiian Kingdom to American territory and state.

subject: HIST
title: Oceania Survey
description: Survey of major events, themes, and issues that make up the diverse histories of Oceania, including Hawaiʻi, from ancestral origins to the present, with an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Philippines
description: Traces developments in Philippine history and society from precolonial to contemporary times and explores ways in which the peoples of the Philippines embraced, resisted or negotiated new modes of thought, behavior and social organization influenced by the Spanish, American, and Japanese regimes as well as the post-colonial global order.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in History
description: Introduction to methods of historical inquiry; current issues in World, American, European, or Pacific history. Emphasis on teaching writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of Early India
description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of Modern India
description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from the Mughal Empire to the new millennium, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from the 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Early Modern Southeast Asia
description: Traces the development of Southeast Asia from early beginnings to the 19th century. Ethical issues and effective writing based on essays and ethical responses will form an important part of the course.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Southeast Asia
description: Continuation of HIST 305 , from 18th century to the present.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: Characteristics of East Asian civilizations as they developed in premodern China; variant patterns in Japan and Korea; the modernization process to 1500.

subject: HIST
title: East Asian Civilizations
description: Continuation of HIST 309 . Period after 1500.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: Chinese civilization to the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of China
description: Continuation of HIST 311 . Period since the 17th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: Survey of culture, government, economics, and institutions, to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japan
description: Continuation of HIST 321 . Period from 1700.

subject: HIST
title: Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics. Includes an emphasis on Oral Communication skills.

subject: HIST
title: The Samurai of Japan
description: A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class. Emphasis on teaching oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Beyond Palaces: Origins of Korea
description: Survey of Korea’s political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1800s. Ethical issues in nationhood, central hegemony, myth-making, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

subject: HIST
title: Beyond Kpop: Formation of Modern Korea
description: Survey of Modern Korea’s political, economic, social, and cultural developments from 1800s to the present. Ethical issues in nationhood, state power, uprisings, warfare, and memory politics are discussed.

subject: HIST
title: Beyond War: History of North Korea
description: History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, architecture, militarism, nationalism, culture, and art from 1945 to today. Context of global history is very important. Writing emphasis.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece I
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Greece II
description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Republic
description: Political, social, cultural history from the Etruscans to Augustus. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials.

subject: HIST
title: Ancient Rome: The Empire
description: Political, social, and cultural history from Augustus to 476 A.D. Emphasis on literary and archaeological materials.

subject: HIST
title: Early Medieval Europe 300-1050
description: Formation of European societies in relation to Byzantine and Islamic cultures. Writing exercises develop historical thinking and the analysis of primary sources through workshops with peer and instructor feedback.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Europe 1050-1350
description: Main trends in European economy, society, religion, politics, thought, and the arts circa 1050-1350, including interactions with Byzantine and Islamic worlds; oral presentations develop historical empathy for understanding primary sources.

subject: HIST
title: European Intellectual History
description: Undergraduate seminar on great debates in Western thought. Discussion and written analysis of primary source materials; the Scientific Revolution and Enlightenment. Significant attention paid to developing writing and textual analysis skills.

subject: HIST
title: Renaissance and Reformation
description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual developments in Europe from 1300 to 1600. Emphasis on cultural and intellectual history and its impact on social and political developments; humanism and its influence on thought and reforming movements, Protestant and Catholic Reformations.

subject: HIST
title: Comparative Economic History
description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

subject: HIST
title: The History of Economic Thought
description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.

subject: HIST
title: France in the Old Regime
description: Major social, political, and intellectual developments: Renaissance, Reformation, religious wars, Richelieu, Louis XIV, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Modern France
description: Political, social, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments in France from Revolution and Napoleon to the present. Assignments emphasize engagement with course concepts through oral communication and individual and group presentation.

subject: HIST
title: Tudor-Stuart Britain
description: Traces major developments in British politics, society, and culture between the late Medieval and Modern Eras.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Britain 1688-1945
description: Interaction of 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century intellectual, political, economic, and social changes, which together produced the British Empire and modern Britain.

subject: HIST
title: British Empire
description: Origins and expansion of the British empire between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Includes imperial policies affecting Britain, Australia, India, Ireland, and Southern Africa. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: Iberia in Asia and the Pacific
description: Comparative exploration of the Iberian empires-Spain and Portugal-and their political, economic, and cultural interactions with indigenous societies in Asia and the Pacific.

subject: HIST
title: France and Empire
description: Lecture/discussion exploring the history of France’s relationship with imperialism from the Renaissance to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Introduction to Islamic History
description: Muhammad, the Arab conquests, the Caliphate; fundamentals of Islam; classical Islamic civilization; development of Islam into modern times with emphasis on the Middle Eastern heartland.

subject: HIST
title: The Making of the Modern Middle East
description: Survey of developments that created the system of nation-states in the Middle East. History of the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Turkey; Egypt; the Arab world; Israel and Iran. Recommended: HIST 354 .

subject: HIST
title: Survey of African History
description: The history of Africa from earliest times to the present: the rise of indigenous civilizations, European and Muslim impact, colonialism and nationalism, and current issues.

subject: HIST
title: The World of Mekong
description: Historical survey, from BC period to present, of the peoples of the Mekong region, an area covering southwestern China, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HIST
title: Women in Oceania
description: Uses research and writing to explore historical processes that have impacted the lives of Indigenous women in Oceania and women’s engagements with those processes over time, with a focus on women’s voices, agency, and empowerment.

subject: HIST
title: Global History of Sport
description: Explores the relationship between sport and society in historical perspective. Analyzes global processes of imperialism, nationalism, globalization, and international relations, and studies themes such as the politics of race, class, and gender.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations to 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from initial encounters between Europeans and Native Americans through the 1890s.

subject: HIST
title: U.S. Foreign Relations From 1898
description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from the wars of 1898 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship within the total society. pre- Colonial to end of the 19th century.

subject: HIST
title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
description: Continuation of HIST 373 : the 20th century.

subject: HIST
title: History of American Business
description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

subject: HIST
title: American Empire
description: Examines an “American culture of empire” in the context of Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific, exploring ethical issues of settler colonialism and decolonial movements. Emphasis on teaching writing/oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Caribbean History
description: Survey of the history of the Caribbean region from 1500 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: The Asia-Pacific War
description: Explores WWII in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on the intersection of the grand strategy, military operations, and war crimes. Involves source analyses and discussions.

subject: HIST
title: History of Warfare to 1850
description: Classical and guerrilla warfare, revolution, and military systems and institutions.

subject: HIST
title: War and Peace Since 1850
description: Continuation of HIST 391 , from 1850 to present.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science to 1700
description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

subject: HIST
title: History of Science Since 1700
description: Continuation of HIST 394 ; science, technology, and society since 1700.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) Historical Theories and Methods
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Historical Theories and Methods: historiography
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Historical Theories and Methods: education
description: Examination of the nature of historical understanding, research, and writing, and of recent trends in historical scholarship; preparation for senior thesis, including significant discipline-specific writing instruction and a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing. (B) historiography; (C) education.

subject: HIST
title: Digital History in the Global Village
description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology. Faculty and students will use digital media to introduce innovative approaches to doing history.

subject: HIST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants.

subject: HIST
title: Rivers, Seas, and Society in Southeast Asia
description: The rivers, seas, and extensive coastlines are a dominant environmental feature in Southeast Asia. Focuses on the dynamic interaction of water and society in shaping the history of the region.

subject: HIST
title: Themes of War in History
description: Explores cross-cutting themes of war from ancient times to the present, such as concepts of just war and unjust war, valor and heroism, and war trauma among combatants and civilian populations in conflict zones.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Philippines
description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Malaysia
description: History of Malay peninsula and northern Borneo, emphasizing developments since 18th century: trade, commerce, foreign migrations, pluralism, nationalism, and Islam.

subject: HIST
title: Modern Indonesia
description: Indonesia from 14th century to present. Emphasis on period from late 18th-century Western colonial impact to struggle for independence and problems of nationhood.

subject: HIST
title: History of Islamic Southeast Asia
description: History of the coming of Islam to Southeast Asia, the spread of its ideas, and its role in the lives of Muslim communities living in the region.

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth-Century China
description: Political, economic, social, and cultural transformations of China from 1900 to the present. This lecture/discussion course examines critical events and explores important issues in the modernization of Chinese life since 1900.

subject: HIST
title: Society and Culture in Traditional China
description: Ch’ing government and Chinese society from local and regional perspectives; modes of control and disorder during the 19th century.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: An interpretive survey of Chinese ideas and values in their cultural, social and political settings from classical age to 1600.

subject: HIST
title: Chinese Intellectual History
description: Interpretive survey of Chinese thought from 1600 to the contemporary period, with special emphasis on the themes of cultural collision and change.

subject: HIST
title: China’s Foreign Relations
description: Systematic review from traditional times, with emphasis on modern and contemporary history, analyses of foreign policy formulation, objectives, and implementation. Recommended: HIST 312 .

subject: HIST
title: The Search for Modern China
description: Origins, development, and meaning of modern revolution in China, 19th century to People’s Republic. Recommended: HIST 311 and HIST 312 .

subject: HIST
title: People’s Republic of China
description: Salient developments from 1949 to the present. Topics include: social revolution and modernization, critically relevant foreign relations. Develops rhetoric and logic skills through practice with oral communications and the written word. Recommended: HIST 312 or HIST 419 .

subject: HIST
title: China in World History
description: Interpretative survey of China’s changing position, significance, and function in the evolution of world history as a way to provide a better understanding of its past and present.

subject: HIST
title: Tokugawa Japan
description: This course covers the major historical aspects of Japan’s Edo/Tokugawa period (1603-1867). Students will learn course content via lectures, discussions, and 2 written assignments of 10 pages each.

subject: HIST
title: Okinawa
description: Survey of social, cultural, economic, and political history from earliest times to present.

subject: HIST
title: Twentieth Century Japan
description: Problems of Japan’s political, economic, and social development since institutional consolidation of Meiji state (c.1890).

subject: HIST
title: Women in East Asian History
description: Survey of the changing political, social, economic, and cultural positions of women in China, Japan, and Korea from ancient times to the present.

subject: HIST
title: History of Japanese Cuisine and Foodways
description: Explores the history of Japanese cuisine and investigates the cultural, economic, and geopolitical aspects of foodways in Japanese domestic and international identity.

subject: HIST
title: Topics on Transitional Justice
description: Explores how societies in the wake of armed conflict, repression, or mass human rights abuses build institutional capacities for promoting justice, human rights, and the rule of law.

subject: HIST
title: War Crimes Trials in History
description: Explores war crimes trials in history since the end of WWII to the present. Involves extensive source analysis, discussion, research, and writing.

subject: HIST
title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
description: Writing and oral presentation-based historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states and the Roman Empire.

subject: HIST
title: Medieval Cultures
description: Topical study of medieval period (circa 300-1500) cross-cultural issues. Class discussion and written work emphasize analysis of primary source documents using an ethics historiography and world history theories. Regional focus and readings vary by semester.

subject: HIST
title: History of Christianity to 1500
description: Historical analysis of the main traditions of Christianity and elements of diversity within Europe and in relation to other parts of the world. Focus on the interpretation of primary sources and discussion of cultural issues.

subject: HIST
title: World Environmental History, 1500 to Present
description: Explores interactions between humans and the natural world from early modern era to the present. Topics include invader species and biotic exchange; environmental politics; and the ecological impact of industrialization, urbanization, science, technology, war, etc.

subject: HIST
title: WWII and the Making of Modern Asia/Pacific
description: A research seminar that builds knowledge of the transformation of Asia and the Pacific following the end of World War II and that guides students to produce substantial research papers.

subject: HIST
title: 20th-Century Europe
description: Contemporary problems and their historical background.

subject: HIST
title: Expansion of Europe
description: Historical processes in modern European colonization from 16th to 20th century; impact on non-Europeans in Asia and Africa.

subject: HIST
title: War and Violence in Early Modern Europe
description: History of the intellectual, social, and cultural causes and consequences of violence, including military conflicts.

subject: HIST
title: French Revolution and Napoleon
description: Causes and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies in the Revolutionary process; discussion and written analysis of primary sources; significant attention to developing writing and textual analysis skills.

subject: HIST
title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

subject: HIST
title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

subject: HIST
title: Topics in African History
description: Selected themes important in African history, including, for example, the politics, economics, societies, and cultures of pre-colonial, colonial, or modern Africa. Topics to be pre-announced.

subject: HIST
title: (Alpha) History and Literature
description: Explores the many relationships between history and literature, including how literature has reflected and shaped society in the past and our relationship to the past; (B) United States; (C) Europe; (D) Asia/Pacific; (E) World/Comparative; (F) Provisional topics.

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Medicine
description: Evolution of Western medical traditions; challenges created by European expansion and colonial interactions; development of modern racial and gender theories. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HIST
title: The American Revolution
description: Lecture/discussion on the origins, development, and consequences of the American Revolution, explored within the context of the broader revolutionary Atlantic world. Emphasis on learning history through writing.

subject: HIST
title: African American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins of racial slavery, slave and free black culture, slave resistance and antislavery, post-emancipation black life, the rise of Jim Crow, the Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights Movement.

subject: HIST
title: Native American History
description: Lecture/ discussion on the history of North American Indians from the seventeenth century to the present. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: Early America
description: Lecture/discussion on Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in North America from contact to independence. Social, cultural, and economic themes and intersections of race, class, and gender explored.

subject: HIST
title: The Early American Republic
description: Lecture/ discussion on the Constitution, the growth of partisan politics, the market revolution, religious revivalism, abolitionism and the expansion of slavery in the U.S. during the age of Jefferson and Jackson.

subject: HIST
title: American Civil War Era 1841—1877
description: The crisis of the Union: antebellum society and culture, slavery, reform, sectionalism, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

subject: HIST
title: Transformation of America 1877—1920
description: Selected themes that explain major changes in American life during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including the westward movement, consolidation of capitalism, world power diplomacy, popular culture, progressivism, and World War I.

subject: HIST
title: The United States 1920—1948
description: The Roaring Twenties, the Depression, New Deal, coming of World War II, America during the war, origins of the Cold War.

subject: HIST
title: The U.S.: 1948 to the Present
description: The atomic age and the Cold War, the age of anxiety, the 1960s, the Vietnam War, the Reagan-Bush era, and beyond.

subject: HIST
title: American Television History
description: Lecture/ discussion examining the impact of television on American society, culture and politics. Analyzed in depth are family sitcoms, presidential politics, Vietnam and the presentation of gender and ethnicity. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: Viva Las Vegas!
description: Upper-division lecture on the historical and cultural significance of Las Vegas in twentieth-century America. Open to nonmajors.

subject: HIST
title: The Cold War
description: Cold War as a global struggle. Topics will include U.S.-Soviet economic and political rivalry, Capitalism vs. Communism as practical policy and ideology, and the force of Third World anti-colonial nationalism. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: HIST
title: Music, Industry, and Society
description: History of U.S. music and recording industry. How industry relates to economy as a whole, and how it reflects broad patterns and trends in American culture and society.

subject: HIST
title: Slavery and Freedom
description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

subject: HIST
title: The American West
description: Lecture/discussion surveying North American settler colonialism, indigenous resistance, and the consolidation of a US West in the context of a growing transcontinental and Pacific empire. Emphasis on teaching writing.

subject: HIST
title: Constitutional History of the U.S.
description: Origins, development of Constitution, Colonial to modern times.

subject: HIST
title: Race and Racism in America
description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

subject: HIST
title: History of American Workers
description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

subject: HIST
title: Colonial Latin America
description: Pre-Columbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social, and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

subject: HIST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania I
description: Explores the diverse, interconnected histories of Oceania from ancestral origins through the early colonial period. Topics include voyaging, orality, land, gender, power, exchange, cross-cultural encounter, disease, colonization, resistance, and historiography. Additional focus on oral communication.

subject: HIST
title: Histories of Oceania II
description: Examines Oceania’s histories of protest during the colonial and post-colonial eras as responses to empire expansion. Explores ethical issues concerning these movements, emphasizing Hawaiʻi experiences and their intersection with those across Oceania.

subject: HIST
title: United States in the Pacific
description: Growth of economic and political interests and policies.

subject: HIST
title: The Hawaiian Kingdom 1819-1893
description: Transformation of Hawaiʻi into a state influenced by American and European ideas and institutions and Asian peoples, with an emphasis on instruction on writing.

subject: HIST
title: History of 20th-Century Hawaiʻi
description: Formation of an American Hawaiʻi with its unique local culture from 1898 to the present.

subject: HIST
title: World Maritime History
description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

subject: HIST
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

subject: HIST
title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
description: Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond.

subject: HIST
title: Senior Tutorial in History
description: Analysis of sources and evaluation of methods of historical writing. Students undertake a major research and writing project in field of special interest. Capstone course requires a 20-25 page minimum final research paper.

subject: HIST
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual projects in various fields. History majors with consent. Maximum 5 credit hours. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Historiography
description: History of history and historians; philosophies of history.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in Digital History
description: Examines the various ways that the production, presentation, and learning of history through digital media is changing the way people access and process information about the past. Graduate standing only.

subject: HIST
title: Advanced Topics in Environmental History
description: Introduction to leading themes, methodologies, and topics in world environmental history. Drawing on new and influential scholarship, readings explore the diverse forces that shape humans’ adaptation to and impact on the natural world.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

subject: HIST
title: Seminar in World History
description: Analysis, research, and discussion of themes and issues in study of history of humankind.

description: Selected themes- feudalism, economic and industrial development, etc.- important in global history. Topics pre-announced.

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi I

subject: HNDI
title: Elementary Hindi II
description: Build on your HNDI 101 skills. Content includes Bollywood Film Festival at Honolulu Museum of Art. Create your own audio-visual projects-make movie trailers, write children’s books, or perform at South Asian events.

subject: HNDI
title: Intermediate Hindi I
description: Improve your communicative and cultural proficiency. Make Bollywood your language coach. Talk about cross-cultural values and practices of food, family, and friendship. Project-based course that builds bridges to your majors, minors, and other interests.

subject: HNDI
title: Intermediate Hindi II
description: Prepare your proficiency for traveling to India. Create audio-visual presentations, documentaries, movie parodies, poetry, plays, dance, or projects from your majors/minors. Develop critical, cross-cultural, and creative skills. Bollywood built into course content.

subject: HNDI
title: Third-Level Hindi: Culture

subject: HNDI
title: Third-Level Hindi: Film
description: Continuation of HNDI 202 . Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected Hindi-Urdu films.
