subject: HON
title: Transformational Research Experiences for Early Undergraduates
description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus.

subject: HON
title: Public Policy-Making
description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/discussion and fieldtrips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence.
prereq_raw: HON 101 or HON 291 (Alpha), or departmental approval.

subject: HON
title: Civic Engagement and Social Justice
description: Seminar on history, theory, and practice of civic engagement in the U.S. and abroad. Involves comparative study of social justice movements, historically and today. Focus on role of university students in social justice movements.
prereq_raw: HON 101 or HON 291 , or departmental approval.

subject: HON
title: Off Campus Study Project
description: Honors students participating in off campus study (via Study Abroad Center, MIX, or NSE) enhance their experience through a project at the host site, designed with and approved with consultation with Honors advisor.
prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and Study Abroad director.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Honors students only.

children.text: of Honors director and Study Abroad director

subject: HON
title: Experiential Learning and Scholarly Engagement
description: Students develop an understanding of theory and practice of experiential learning through direct engagement and focused scholarly reflection while assimilating and synthesizing new knowledge and developing critical thinking skills.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Honors Program approval only.

subject: HON
title: From Ideas to Page: Learn The Publication Process
description: Learn the publication process through a “hands on” experiential learning, emphasizing diverse knowledge systems, writing, and ethics. Learn how to solicit contributions, review, and edit articles as a part of the Horizons Undergraduate Journal publication cycle.
prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and instructor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Honors students only.

subject: HON
title: Peer Mentoring
description: Students develop understanding of dynamics of leadership skills within the contexts of paired to large groups. Significant portion is dedicated to writing and oral communication instruction. Honors Program students only. pre-semester training sessions, on-going training and supervision.

subject: HON
title: Research Mentoring
description: Mentors help others and themselves improve research methods, practice effective project management, and build research support networks. Students will learn the skills of mentoring and develop a mentoring and teaching philosophy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: HON
title: Honors Seminar
description: Project-based experiential learning involving community-based research or creative work. Focus on project design, practical skills, and teamwork. Significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Multi-disciplinary topics vary each semester. Honors Program students only.

subject: HON
title: Honors Thesis Proposal
description: Library research skills; scholarship of research and creative work; methodological and ethical issues; development of individual proposal or prospectus for Senior Honors Project. Limited to candidates for the Honors degree.

subject: HON
title: Honors Workshop
description: Supplemental workshop for students beginning independent work on their senior honors thesis. HON students only. Junior or senior standing only.

subject: HON
title: Honors Senior Project I
description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. First semester of project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

subject: HON
title: Honors Senior Project II
description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. Second semester of project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

subject: HON
title: Honors Colloquium
description: Weekly meetings for discussion of enduring issues and problems of an interdisciplinary nature. Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

subject: HON
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Directed reading and/or research.
repeatable_raw: 3 times per alpha, up to 12 credits

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management
description: Survey of the field covering recruitment, selection, training, appraisals, grievance handling, communications, discipline, safety, compensation, and benefits.

subject: HRM
title: Leadership and Group Dynamics
description: Explore frameworks leaders can use to get things done in their teams. Examine how leaders can engage employees, improve decision-making, manage interpersonal dynamics, and adapt to changing internal and external contexts. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: HRM
title: Organizational Change and Effectiveness
description: Identify and evaluate methods to promote an effective change transition through efficient integration of corporate goals with the organizational culture.

subject: HRM
title: Labor Problems
description: Problems and economics of labor; history, structure, government, activities of trade unions.

subject: HRM
title: Labor and Social Legislation
description: Evolution, interpretation, and application of labor and social welfare legislation with special emphasis on impact of labor-management relations.

subject: HRM
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: HRM
title: Personnel Compensation
description: Selected topics. Emphasis on trends, recent issues, job evaluation, incentive systems, salary administration, executive compensation, profit sharing, benefit programs, retirement plans.

subject: HRM
title: The Staffing Process
description: Contemporary practices and trends in personnel planning for a competent work force; legal constraints, recruitment and selection, differential placement, training, career programming.

subject: HRM
title: Negotiation and Workplace Dispute Resolution
description: Theory and practice in negotiating; design and operation of different kinds of workplace dispute resolution (such as mediation, arbitration, and various alternatives); features exercises on bargaining and negotiation and advocacy and decision skills.

subject: HRM
title: Labor Management Relations
description: Review and analysis of basic factors that distinguish employment relations; examination of the development of recent legislation and programs at federal, state, and municipal levels. Specific consideration given to current problems on the mainland and Hawaiʻi.

subject: HRM
title: Training and Development
description: Analysis of the current concepts and practices in the design, delivery, and assessment of training.

subject: HRM
title: Seminar in HRM
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in HRM.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management
description: Analysis and critical evaluation of basic issues, policies, and trends in personnel administration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Training and Development
description: Covers issues in design, delivery, and assessment of training, theoretical background of training and development process, types of training process, cross cultural and other types of diversity training and development of training modules.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Advanced Organizational Behavior
description: Organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MHRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Finance for Human Resource Management
description: Intends to give HR professionals a basic overview of the vocabulary and concepts of financial decision-making. Topics include: understanding financial information, budgeting, the finance of retirement and employee benefit and business valuation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MHRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Compensation
description: Survey of compensation methods and procedures including job evaluations, incentive systems, salary administration, fringe benefits, appropriate legislation, policies and strategy issues of compensation systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: The Staffing Process
description: Recruiting and selection to optimize organizations including job design, job analysis, recruitment and selection methods, such as types of interviews and assessment centers, within legislative environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Negotiations and Labor Relations
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations. MHRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: International Human Resources
description: Exploring global trends in human resources with focus on the Asia Pacific region.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management-Topics
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in human resources.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MHRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resource Management Capstone
description: The final course in the MHRM curriculum. It provides students opportunity to integrate and apply previous course content to their professional organization offering a value-added opportunity to enhance organizational performance.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MHRM majors only.

subject: HRM
title: Human Resources Leadership in Healthcare Organizations
description: Builds on previous leadership and management courses, focus on development of individual leadership skills emphasizing ethical and critical decision making, effective working relationships, and a systems-perspective relevant to healthcare organizations.

subject: HSSW
title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.

subject: HSSW
title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiʻi: Center of the Pacific
description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawaiʻi and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiʻi: Center of the Pacific
description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawaiʻi and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupuaʻa
description: Examination of the ahupuaʻa system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the mālama ʻāina track designed to build critical writing skills.

subject: HWST
title: ʻAʻa Ka Hula: Introduction to Hula
description: Introductory-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).

subject: HWST
title: Kūnihi Ka Mauna: Introduction to Oli
description: (2 1-hr Lec, 1 2-hr Lab/practice) Introductory-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Visual Culture Studio
description: Introduction to a variety of material (fiber, bone, wood, and stone) and skills in the media used in the Hawaiian culture. Research and explore basic techniques within the media with emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses, and conservation.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana Noʻeau Maʻawe
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to a variety of fibers used in the Hawaiian culture. Emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses and conservation of the fibers. Areas explored are kapa, plaiting, netting and twining.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
description: Research and express personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through Hawaiian visual culture. Introduction to painting and drawing media and exploration of various materials and techniques as applied to individual student styles.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to Native Hawaiian perspective and world view in images used in print and the basic material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery through the indigenous eyes.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to the Literature of Native Hawaiians and Other Indigenous People Written in English
description: Surveys literature of Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous Peoples, especially to focus on the situational impetus from which these texts were created.

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Composition
description: Focus on studying and applying Native Hawaiian composition practices from the nineteenth century into the present day.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Mythology
description: Survey of gods, ʻaumākua, kupua, mythical heroes, heroines, and their kinolau as the basis of traditional Hawaiian metaphor.

subject: HWST
title: Papahulilani Hawaiian Astronomy I
description: Introduction to Hawaiian ancestral understandings of the movements of the sun, moon and stars, and their use in ordering the Hawaiian year in planting, fishing, and ceremony.
prereq_raw: ( HWST 107 and HWST 270 ) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: HWST
title: Hoʻokele I: Hawaiian Astronomy
description: Introduction to Hawaiian views of astronomy and the stars used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators. Introduction and comparison to various Pacific island non-instrument navigation systems and star names.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Restricted to majors.

subject: HWST
title: Hoʻokele I Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Stargazing laboratory to accompany HWST 281 .

subject: HWST
title: Hoʻokele II: Hawaiian Navigation
description: Hawaiian and other Oceanic canoe design, navigation, Pacific weather, sailing dynamics for canoes, and sail planning strategies used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators for long voyages.

subject: HWST
title: Hoʻokele II Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands on experience on voyaging skills and sailing canoes to accompany HWST 282 .

subject: HWST
title: Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hawaiian Medicinal Herbs
description: Presentation of Hawaiian medicinal herbs including basic philosophy, identification, utilization, and preparation of such herbs for human ailments.

subject: HWST
title: Perspectives in Hawaiian Studies
description: Interdisciplinary lectures and discussions examining traditional and contemporary experiences in Hawaiian society and setting; resources, methods, and techniques.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama ʻĀina Resource Management Visual Technologies
description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

subject: HWST
title: Ke Haʻa Lā: Intermediate Hula
description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Hula (Dance) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).
prereq_raw: HWST 212 , and HAW 201 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kū Ka Pūnohu: Intermediate Oli
description: Intermediate-level, performance-based Oli (Chant) course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in Mele (Song, Poetry) and Moʻolelo (History and Literatures).
prereq_raw: HWST 214 , and HAW 201 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Art Media
description: Examine and explore advance techniques within the media and the customary and contemporary uses of a variety of material and skills used in traditional Hawaiian everyday life.

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio- Hana Noʻeau Maʻawe
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Examine the customary and contemporary use of fiber materials and the skills used in Hawaiian culture. Research and explore advanced techniques within the media used in traditional Hawaiʻi.

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
description: Advanced research and expression of personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through visual culture and language. Students will further their definitions, analysis skills, research, and understandings through painting and drawing media.

subject: HWST
title: Advanced Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Advanced Native Hawaiian perspective in imagery in print and the material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery. Lecture-lab with studio work time.

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Traditions in Literature
description: Discusses theoretical frameworks, main features, and cultural contexts of Hawaiian literature, with significant attention paid to developing writing skills.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , and HAW 202 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian and Indigenous Digital Media
description: Focus on studying, analyzing, and creating various forms of Hawaiian and Indigenous digital storytelling.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Genealogies
description: Survey of major Hawaiian chiefly lineages from the four main islands: Hawaiʻi, Maui, Oʻahu and Kauaʻi. Political history from the Kumulipo to Western contact.

subject: HWST
title: Chiefs of Post-Contact Hawaiʻi
description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

subject: HWST
title: Myths of Hawaiian History
description: Thematic exploration of some common myths of Hawaiian history, including infanticide, slavery, feudalism, constant warfare, human sacrifice, and a limited pre-contact population, to determine the role of myth making in perceptions of Hawaiian history. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Mahiʻai Kalo I: Taro Cultivation
description: Historical, cultural and philosophical foundations of the cultivation and uses of taro.

subject: HWST
title: Mahiʻai Kalo II: Advanced Taro
description: In depth-study of taro cultivation techniques and systems.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama Loko Iʻa
description: Study of traditional Hawaiian fishpond management with hands-on experience at Heʻeia fishpond near Kāneʻohe, merging traditional Native knowledge and ways of seeing with Western science.

subject: HWST
title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Pana Oʻahu: Famous Place Names
description: A survey of the famous place names in each ahupuaʻa of Oʻahu, including accounts of mythical heroes, heiau, fishponds, wind, rain names, and their metaphoric value in Hawaiian literature.

subject: HWST
title: Pana Paemoku o Kanaloa: The Northwestern Hawaiian Islands
description: Will look at the use of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands during precontact times, the historical period of the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi, after the islands were ceded to the U.S., and the contemporary politics that surround the region today.

subject: HWST
title: Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hoʻi Ka Mana i Loko
description: Advanced study and preparation of Hawaiian medicinal herb combinations.

subject: HWST
title: Issues in Modern Hawaiʻi
description: Cultural and political aspects of the current Hawaiian movement; historical colonization; conflicts over tourism, the military, and agriculture; forms of native self-determination. Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Native Hawaiian Rights and Practices
description: Students will strengthen their cultural, political, and legal foundations by: (1) reviewing Hawaiʻi’s historical traditions and customs, (2) learning legal analysis techniques, and (3) applying those techniques to issues that govern native Hawaiian “rights” today. Sophomore or higher standing.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , and HWST 341 (or concurrent) and HAW 102 .

subject: HWST
title: Visiting Artist Seminar
description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Explore indigenous concepts through the media of a visiting indigenous master artist by looking at traditional media in indigenous cultures, and the possibilities for contemporary expression in other media.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , one course in 220 level ( HWST 222 , HWST 224 , HWST 225 ), one course in 320 level ( HWST 322 , HWST 324 , HWST 325 ); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only.

children.text: ) , one course in 320 level ( HWST 322 , HWST 324 , HWST 325 ) ; or consent

subject: HWST
title: Ka Mana Moʻolelo: Topics in Hawaiian and Indigenous Moʻolelo
description: Advanced course of study focusing on pressing topics connected with Hawaiian and Indigenous literatures, such as land struggle, climate change, or issues of governance and sovereignty.

subject: HWST
title: Māhele Land Awards
description: Practical guide to the researching of land awards and change in title for a single ahupuaʻa, 1848 to present. Focus on field trips.

subject: HWST
title: Ceded Lands: Focus on Crown and Government Lands (1848 to Present)
description: Inventorying “Ceded Lands” in Hawaiʻi with emphasis on historical, legal, and cultural changes from the Kingdom through statehood.

subject: HWST
title: Introduction to Indigenous Research
description: Survey course introduces students to a range of methods by beginning with a critical analysis of dominant research methodologies from the perspective of Indigenous scholars.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior/senior standing only.

subject: HWST
title: Territorial Land Law Changes & Their Effects on Kānaka
description: Advanced course of study focusing on Hawaiʻi’s post-overthrow (Territorial Era) land law changes and their current day effects.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Institutions
description: Comprehensive analysis of institutions like Bishop Estate/Kamehameha Schools, OHA, Liliʻuokalani Trust, Department of Hawaiian Home Lands and The Queen’s Hospital.

subject: HWST
title: Wehe Ka ʻĀina: Cultivating a Sovereign Land Base
description: A Mālama ʻĀina and Kūkulu Aupuni course that identifies modern options in land access for reestablishing or resuming Hawaiian traditional and customary practices relating to food sovereignty and self-sustainability.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 and HWST 343 and HWST 351 ; HAW 202 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: Ola I Ka Wai; Water and Sovereignty in Hawaiʻi
description: Focus on Hawaiian relationships with Ka Wai Ola a Kāne (water), traditional and contemporary water management practices, as well as contemporary resource management issues and native Hawaiian community advocacy for water.
prereq_raw: HWST 307 and HAW 202 (or concurrent) or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kiaʻi Kanaloa-Guarding Our Ocean Resources
description: Students will actively monitor and practice coastal and ocean stewardship in support of local communities and practitioners while also exploring how the Hawaiian worldview can plan a role in aloha ʻāina conservation movements.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: HWST
title: ʻĀina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

subject: HWST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356

subject: HWST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of Oʻahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

subject: HWST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawaiʻi. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 .

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiʻi & Indigenous Economies
description: Students will map out indigenous economies by articulating cultural similarity and diversity between academic experience and professional experiences.

subject: HWST
title: Mālama ʻĀina Field Methods Course
description: Intensive field methods program to research Mālama ʻĀina strategies. Introduces students to a variety of field techniques including land research, historical documents, ecological surveys, and Papakū Makawalu.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 , or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: HWST
title: ʻIke Akua Papakū Makawalu: Ancestral Understanding of Elements
description: Uses Dr. Pualani Kanahele’s Papakū Makawalu methodology to analyze akua as elements and as a paradigm for understanding ancestral knowledge. Senior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: HWST 270 , HWST 372 (or concurrent), and HAW 301 (or concurrent).

subject: HWST
title: Mele Au Hou: Music and Native Identity
description: Presents Hawaiian music as it has been an avenue for native social, cultural and political expression in traditional and contemporary society.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 or HWST 343 or HWST 390 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Mahi Lāʻau Lapaʻau: Hawaiian Medicinal Horticulture
description: The science of planting and harvesting Hawaiian medicinal plants and exploring production and marketing strategies.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 285 and HWST 385 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health.

subject: HWST
title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration.
prereq_raw: HWST 341 , HWST 342 , [ HWST 343 or HWST 390 or HWST 490 (or concurrent)] and [ HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 285 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356 ] and [ SUST 222 or HWST 224 or HWST 225 or HWST 372 or HWST 478 ].
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Political Speech: Haʻi ʻŌlelo Kūʻē
description: Senior seminar in short, extemporaneous speeches in persuasive, passionate and dynamic styles of Native Hawaiian orators.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 , HWST 342 , or HAW 202 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Modern Pacific Women’s Poetry
description: Critical examination of modern indigenous women’s poetry from the Pacific Islands. Thematic concentration on land, family, sexual and national oppression.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kānāwai: Western Law and Hawaiʻi
description: The rise of Western law in Hawaiʻi, its contribution to nation building and colonialism.
prereq_raw: HWST 342 or HWST 343 or HWST 390 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai II: Practical Application of Rights
description: Historical analysis of land use, race and self-determination; introduced to legal case briefing, analysis of legal precedent, practical impacts of rules and regulations and the sociopolitical factors that influence law and law enforcement.

subject: HWST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individual reading/research.

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
description: Reading seminar for developing a Native Hawaiian epistemology from sources in comparative indigenous thought.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Archival Research
description: Research seminar aimed at familiarizing students with the rich historical primary sources existent in various archives in Honolulu.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Review of Hawaiian Literature
description: Seminar in review of Hawaiian literature to understand the significance of secondary sources in Hawaiian subjects. This makes up part of the Hawaiian Studies graduate core.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Writing a Hawaiian Thesis
description: Seminar to help fashion student’s research and thesis proposal. To be taken by all HWST MA students as they begin designing their capstone project. Course will be team-taught by HWST faculty.

subject: HWST
title: ʻIke Pono-Visual/Cultural Interpretations
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that examines (from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint) colonial imaging; collecting and site of contestation; resilience and resistance; and re-righting.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , and one course from HWST 220 - HWST 225 , and one course from HWST 320 - HWST 325 ; or consent.

subject: HWST
title: ʻIke Maka-Visual/Cultural Knowledge
description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that carefully examines and develops critical consciousness-from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint-visual hegemony, rhetorical tropes; and representation-imag(in)ing and re-imag(in)ing.

subject: HWST
title: Pono Science: Ethical Implications of Science in Hawaiʻi
description: Support student dialogue on the foundations of pono science. Through discussions and structured guidance, students will explore Hawaiian ethics, implications of research, and decolonizing methodology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: HWST
title: Moʻolelo ʻŌiwi: Historical Perspectives
description: Research seminar for developing interpretations of the past from Native Hawaiian and foreign world views with particular emphasis on understanding the meaning of culturally-based knowledge systems.

subject: HWST
title: Mele Hawaiʻi: Mele as Systems of Knowledge
description: Seminar on Mele Hawaiʻi (Songs, Poetry, Chants) as systems of knowledge that record, communicate, and critique historical, political, environmental, and cultural information. Will include learning and analysis of mele, culminating with a research project.
prereq_raw: HAW 302 and ( HWST 478 or HAW 384 or HAW 484 ).

subject: HWST
title: Hawaiian Geography and Resource Management
description: Seminar in geography of Hawaiʻi from a Native Hawaiian perspective that will enable the researcher to define and develop resource management methods consistent with Native Hawaiian understandings and traditions.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent).

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: ʻĀina Waiwai: Water, Food Sovereignty, and Ancestral Abundance
description: Topical graduate seminar focuses on indigenous perspectives on water, food sovereignty, Hawaiian terrestrial and marine food production systems, and ancestral abundance. Seminar perspective to change each term.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 and HAW 202 or consent.

subject: HWST
title: Kānāwai Lawaiʻa: Hawaiʻi’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance.

subject: HWST
title: Historic Preservation Law
description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws.

subject: HWST
title: He Aliʻi Ka ʻĀina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ʻĀina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ʻĀina future.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Comparative Hawaiian and Tahitian Cosmogonies
description: Seminar comparing Gods/myths from Ancient Tahiti by Teuira Henry (600 pages) with the six volumes of Hawaiian historians Kamakau and Malo.

subject: HWST
title: Kumu Kahiki: Pacific Life Narratives in Mixed Media and Literature
description: Research seminar in relevant literary traditions, histories of interaction, colonization, and literary politics in the Pacific region through the examination of life narratives in mixed media and literature.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: HWST majors only.

subject: HWST
title: Indigenous Futurisms: Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and Beyond
description: Seminar on Indigenous Futurisms as developed in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, and other Indigenous contexts, and expressed through art, literature, film, music, and scholarship.

subject: HWST
title: Huakaʻi Huli Heiau Hawaiʻinuiākea: Study Abroad on Polynesian Temples
description: Comparative study of Hawaiian/Polynesian temple design taught over a 3-week period in Hawaiʻi and Polynesia. Travel costs to be paid by student.
prereq_raw: HWST 670 (with a minimum grade of B) and HAW 302 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) and HAW 302 ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Envisioning the Nation
description: A research seminar designed to provide an overview of community activism and Native Hawaiian empowerment in Hawaiʻi in contexts that range from local to international, and to provide a foundation for further study and professional growth.
prereq_raw: HWST 107 , HWST 270 , HWST 341 (or concurrent), HWST 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent) or HWST 390 (or concurrent) or HWST 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: one of the following: HWST 343 (or concurrent)

subject: HWST
title: Kūkulu Aupuni: Sovereign Hawaiian State, Domestic Kingdom Law, Governance and Politics
description: Research seminar on the subject of domestic law, governance, and politics of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the historical relevance of this to the contemporary case for independent, sovereign state continuity under public international law.

subject: HWST
title: Practicum Research Plan B
description: Practicum for Plan B.

subject: HWST
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Tools for the Information World
description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc. Honors Equivalent: ICS 101A

subject: ICS
title: Digital Tools for the Information World
description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Data Science
description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Science Principles
description: General course that provides a broad overview of computer science. Will address abstraction, data and information, algorithms, programming, the Internet and the global impact of computers.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Generative AI
description: Introduces fundamentals of generative Artificial Intelligence (Al). Through hands-on projects, students will learn prompt engineering, model customization, ethical considerations, and practical uses of generative Al in writing, design, and education.

subject: ICS
title: (Alpha) Introduction to Computer Programming
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Programming: C
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Programming: through animations
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Programming: Python
description: Basic concepts needed to write computer programs. Simple program design and implementation using a specific programming language; (C) C; (D) through animations; (P) Python.
repeatable_raw: Each alpha repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Science I
description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.
prereq_raw: Recommended: computer experience. Honors Equivalent: ICS 111A

prereq_tree.text: Recommended: computer experience. Honors Equivalent: ICS 111A

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Science I
description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.

subject: ICS
title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science I
description: Includes logic, sets, functions, matrices, algorithmic concepts, mathematical reasoning, recursion, counting techniques, and probability theory.

subject: ICS
title: Information Systems in Society
description: Lecture/ discussion critically explores sociopolitical dimensions of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), and the information professions.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Science II
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.
prereq_raw: ICS 111 or consent. Honors Equivalent: ICS 211A

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Science II
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr. Lab) Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.

subject: ICS
title: Program Structure
description: Program organization paradigms, programming environments, implementation of a module from specifications, the C and C programming languages.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Scripting
description: Introduction to scripting languages for the integration of applications and systems. Scripting in operating systems, web pages, server-side application integration, regular expressions, and event handling for languages such as Perl, JavaScript, PHP, Python, shell scripting.

subject: ICS
title: Basic Concepts of Computer Science
description: What is the subject of computer science? What is a computer? Understand the basic models of computation and the concepts of computability, complexity, and network computation, and learn to use them in practice.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Methods
description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

subject: ICS
title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science II
description: Includes program correctness, recurrence relations and their solutions, relations and their properties, divide and conquer relations, graph theory, trees and their applications, Boolean algebra, introduction to formal languages and automata theory.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Science Careers: An Exploration of the Specialties of Computer Science
description: Exploration of the specialties of computer science. Meets every two week for 2.5 hours to explore specific areas in computer science.

subject: ICS
title: Sophomore Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in a beginner-level design of a software project expected to be continued in ICS 396 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Algorithms
description: (4 1-hr Lec) Design and correctness of algorithms, including divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming methods. Complexity analyses using recurrence relations, probabilistic methods, and NP-completeness. Applications to order statistics, disjoint sets, B-trees and balanced trees, graphs, network flows, and string matching.
prereq_raw: ICS 211 , and [( ICS 241 or ECE 362 ) and ( MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A )] or ( MATH 301 and MATH 372 ); or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Machine-Level and Systems Programming
description: Machine organization, machine instructions, addressing modes, assembler language, subroutine linkage, linking to higher-level languages, interface to operating systems, introduction to assemblers, loaders and compilers.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) (or concurrent), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Programming Language Theory
description: Syntax, semantics, control structures, variable binding and scopes, data and control abstractions. Programming in functional (LISP) and logic (Prolog) programming styles.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering I
description: Problem analysis and design, team-oriented development, quality assurance, configuration management, project planning. These topics are covered in the sequence 314-414.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 211 or ECE 205 ) and [ ICS 241 or ECE 362 or ( MATH 301 and MATH 372 )]; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems I
description: Introduction to relational database systems, data modeling, query processing, transaction processing, storage, and indexing.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Logic Design and Microprocessors
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Basic machine architecture, microprocessors, bus organization, circuit elements, logic circuit analysis and design, microcomputer system design.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ), ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ), and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Operating Systems
description: Operating system concepts and structure, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, scheduling, file systems, inter-process communication, virtualization, popular operating systems.

subject: ICS
title: Network Design and Management
description: Overview of the internet and its capabilities; introduction to HTTP, TCP/IP, ethernet, and wireless 802.11; routers, switches, and NAT; network and wireless security; practical experience in designing and implementing networks.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.

subject: ICS
title: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 215 or ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Computational Media Systems
description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.
prereq_raw: Any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or ECE 160 or instructor approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE, CENG, ICS, CM, CSCI, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Computing Ethics for Lab Assistants
description: Lecture/discussion/internship on ethical issues and instructional techniques for students assisting computer sciences classes in various settings. The class uses multiple significant writing and oral presentation activities to help students learn course content.

subject: ICS
title: Junior Project
description: Part of a multi-year project-based courses sequence where students will work in teams on acquiring experience in intermediate-level design, implementation and presentation of a software project that may have been initiated in ICS 296 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Software Engineering II
description: Continuation of ICS 314 . Project management, quality, and productivity control, testing and validation, team management. Team-oriented software-implementation project.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Programming for the Web
description: Introduction to emerging technologies for construction of World Wide Web (WWW)-based software. Covers programming and scripting languages used for the creation of WWW sites and client-server programming. Students will complete a medium-sized software project that uses languages and concepts discussed in class.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: The Science, Psychology and Philosophy of Systems Design
description: Scientific, psychological and philosophical bases of systems design, including a survey of human-factors and ergonomic standards; the nature of innovation and creativity as it relates to systems design. Web-enhanced course.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Database Systems II
description: Very large database systems, data integration, data warehousing, designing big data systems, parallel query processing, distributed transactions.

subject: ICS
title: Network Science Methodology
description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

subject: ICS
title: Data Security and Cryptography I
description: Secret communication and confidentiality data storage. Elements of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Classical ciphers. Symmetric key cryptography. Public key cryptography. Data security in cyber space.

subject: ICS
title: Application Frameworks
description: Experience producing applications with at least two different applications frameworks.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Security and Ethics
description: Theoretical results, security policy, encryption, key management, digital signatures, certificates, passwords. Ethics: privacy, computer crime, professional ethics. Effects of the computer revolution on society.

subject: ICS
title: Computer System Security
description: Information flow, confinement, information assurance, malicious programs, vulnerability analysis, network security, writing secure programs.

subject: ICS
title: Programming Approaches to Software Quality Assurance
description: Examination of best practices associated with developing and supporting software applications with respect to potential security risks. Will augment software engineering practices learned in other courses with the basic principles of cybersecurity.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Forensics
description: Provides students with the knowledge of underlying principles and skills to identify, preserve, and extract electronic evidence for further analysis.

subject: ICS
title: Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies
description: Studies the fundamentals and reviews the latest developments in the field of Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies, including programming of introductory Smart Contracts. Knowledge of programming or finance recommended.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture
description: Memory management, control flow, interrupt mechanisms, multiprocessor systems, special-purpose devices.

subject: ICS
title: Concurrent and High-Performance Programming
description: Principles of concurrent and high performance programming. Multi-threading in C and Java for shared-memory programming. Distributed memory programming with Java. Introduction to cluster computing.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ICS 332 and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Data Science Fundamentals
description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.

subject: ICS
title: Big Data Analytics
description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Computation
description: Grammars, sequential machines, equivalence, minimalization, analysis and synthesis, regular expressions, computability, unsolvability, Gödel’s theorem, Turing machines.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Analytical Models and Methods
description: Applications of mathematical methods in computer science with emphasis on discrete mathematics, numerical computation, algebraic models, operations research.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Parallel Algorithms
description: Introduction to parallel models of computation and design and analysis of parallel algorithms.

subject: ICS
title: Security Science of Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
description: Safety is a central concern in applications of machine learning and natural language processing. The course presents a framework for applying dependability models and methodologies to intelligent software.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

subject: ICS
title: Data Networks
description: Network analysis, architecture, digital signal analysis and design; circuit switching, packet switching, packet broadcasting; protocols and standards; local area networks; satellite networks; ALOHA channels; examples.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Software Design for Robotics
description: Sensors, actuators, signal processing, paradigms of robotic software design, introduction to machine learning, introduction to computer vision, and robot-to-human interaction.
prereq_raw: two ICS 300-level courses or consent. Recommended: ICS 312 and ICS 313 .

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust II: Information Assurance
description: Channel security. Trojan and noninterference. Basic concepts of cryptology. Cryptographic primitives. Protocols for authentication and key establishment.

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence
description: Survey of artificial intelligence: natural language processing, vision and robotics, expert systems. Emphasis on fundamental concepts: search, planning, and problem solving, logic, knowledge representation.

subject: ICS
title: Artificial Intelligence for Games
description: Techniques to stimulate intelligence in video games: movement, pathfinding with A* search, decision/ behavior trees, state machines, machine learning, tactics. Extend games with your own AI implementations; experience “shootout” contests for the best AI algorithm/implementation.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 and ( PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 ).

subject: ICS
title: Human Computer Interaction I
description: Application of concepts and methodologies of human factors, psychology and software engineering to address ergonomic, cognitive, and social factors in the design and evaluation of human-computer systems.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Hypermedia
description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.

subject: ICS
title: Design for Mobile Devices
description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Cognitive Science
description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and neuroscience.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Probability, Statistics, and Queuing
description: A hands-on introduction to probability, statistical inference, regression, Markov chains, queuing theory. Use of an interactive statistical graphics environment such as R.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Sequences and Genomes Analysis
description: Introduction to bioinformatics to computer sciences students by focusing on how computer sciences techniques can be used for the storage, analysis, prediction and simulation of biological sequences (DNA, RNA and proteins).
prereq_raw: ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 , or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics Algorithms and Tool Development
description: Study of commonly used bioinformatic algorithms, with an emphasis on string, tree, and graph algorithms. Presentation of probabilistic and clustering methods. Implementation of the studied algorithms and design of applications.

subject: ICS
title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
description: Fundamentals of computer graphics including graphics hardware, representation, manipulation, and display of two- and three-dimensional objects, use of commercial software.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 369 or ECE 369 ) and ( MATH 307 or MATH 311 ); or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Graphics
description: Review of selected graphics literature, with a software development project based on a topic of interest.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Vision
description: Introductory course in computer vision. Topics include image formation, image processing and filtering, edge detection, texture analysis and synthesis, binocular stereo, segmentation, tracking, object recognition and applications.
prereq_raw: ( ICS 212 or ECE 205 ) and ( ICS 311 or ECE 367 ) and ICS 314 and ( MATH 307 or MATH 311 or ECE 345 ); or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Video Game Design and Development
description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments.
prereq_raw: any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or CINE 215 .
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.
prereq_raw: any ICS 110 (Alpha) or ICS 111 or CINE 215 .

subject: ICS
title: 3D Modeling and Animation Techniques
description: Principles, techniques, and history of 3D computer graphics. Modeling and animation techniques will be covered, as well as basic lighting and rendering.

subject: ICS
title: 3D Rendering Techniques
description: Software development within a commercial 3D application with a focus on scripting and plugin development for procedural modeling, animation, and shading.

subject: ICS
title: Software Techniques for Computer Visual Effects
description: Principles, techniques, and history of visual effects and underlying software techniques for computer visual effects. Project-based course involving the merging of computer generated imagery with live action footage.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics
description: Reflects special interests of faculty. Oriented toward juniors and seniors.
prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS classes or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics in Security
description: Special topics in security oriented toward juniors and seniors.
prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS courses or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Capstone Project
description: Project-based course where students work in teams on a software project. Knowledge acquired in the computer science curriculum will be applied to design and implement a software product with potential real-world applicability.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Project
description: Individual or small-group projects in system design or application under faculty supervision.

subject: ICS
title: Applied Computing Industry Seminar
description: Introduction to the importance of building and utilizing AI systems and an exploration of the current industry landscape.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Practical Problem Solving with Algorithms
description: Effectively identify and solve problems using various algorithmic approaches. Through hands-on projects and real-world examples, students will learn to analyze, design, and implement foundational algorithms.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Applied Computing Fundamentals
description: Provides necessary programming skills in Python for data science and AI, and introduces language models as programming copilots. Students also learn AI-assisted programming through validation, testing, documentation, optimization, and software design.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Applied Data Science
description: Introduces foundational principles of data science, emphasizing elementary concepts and essential tools integral to the data scientist’s role from data wrangling to foundational tools for modeling data, without requiring knowledge of linear algebra or calculus.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
description: Covers fundamentals of artificial intelligence, and especially machine learning, for students and industry professionals who aim to immediately implement AI and data science solutions in their career.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
prereq_raw: ICS 313 or ECE 467 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent

subject: ICS
title: Practicum / Internship
description: Designed to provide students with real-world experience in the field of computer science. Aims to bridge the gap between academic theories and practical applications in a professional environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Compiler Theory and Construction
description: Design and implementation of compilers, syntactic and semantic descriptions of programming languages, algorithms for syntactic analysis and object code generation.

subject: ICS
title: Theory of Operating Systems
description: Advanced study in operating systems theory and design with emphasis on case studies and distributed systems.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Software Engineering
description: Fundamental software engineering procedures, including planning, estimation, design, testing, process definition and improvement, and software quality assurance. Measurement techniques are used to support empirically-driven software process improvement throughout the course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Medical Informatics I
description: Introduction to the field of medical informatics, which is found at the intersection of clinical science, public health, information science, computer technology and communications technology. Concentration on current issues.

subject: ICS
title: Software Quality and Maintenance
description: Introduction to software quality concepts and the major activities involved in software maintenance.

subject: ICS
title: Information Architecture and Web Design
description: User-centered design of websites; survey Information Architecture (IA) systems (organization, navigation, labeling, searching); gain experience in methodologies for creating IA, tools for IA, web standards and usability tests.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in ICS or LIS or related field or consent. ICS and LIS majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Analysis of Algorithms
description: Analysis and design of algorithms: modeling, comparison, measures, applications.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Network Science
description: Modeling human-made and natural systems as networks to understand their structure and dynamics. Computational and statistical methods and research results they enabled. Use of network analysis software. Applications to topics of interest to students.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Cryptography
description: Taxonomy of security properties: methods for defining and proving security. Randomness, pseudorandomness, and indistinguishability. Functional encryption and obfuscation. Zero knowledge.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Management
description: Exploration of information retrieval and object-relational tools and methods for the management of distributed multimedia database systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Principles of High Performance Computing
description: Principles of high performance computing for single-processor and parallel architectures. Detailed coverage of parallel architectures and exposure to shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallelism. Hands-on experience with message-passing and multi-threaded programming.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in computer science or closely related field, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Machine Learning
description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification.

subject: ICS
title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. Includes instruction in the latest software frameworks.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
description: Covers the latest developments in human-centered artificial intelligence, including ethics, bias, explainability, privacy, fairness, and usability. Involves discussion, writing assignments, and a final project.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Theory of Computation
description: Advanced topics in formal languages, automata, computability, computational complexity.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Parallel Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of parallel algorithms, with emphasis on advanced techniques and latest advances in parallel algorithms.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Security Science of Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
description: The advances in machine learning and natural language processing open a gamut of new security challenges and opportunities. Updating security concepts and methods requires a scientific approach.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Networks
description: Elementary principles of modern computer networking. Detailed coverage of overall architecture and the physical, data link, and network layers, with emphasis on the network layer.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in ICS, or consent. ICS majors only.

subject: ICS
title: Security and Trust III: Cyber Security and Commerce
description: Tools and methods for security managers. Tools and methods to secure and monetize services and applications. Network as a computer and as a market. Problems of cyber war, cyber crime, cyber bullying.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Architecture I
description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
description: Current issues in artificial intelligence, including expert systems, knowledge representation, logic programming, learning, natural language processing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Pattern Recognition
description: Nature of the problem in pattern recognition and clustering; explanation of various algorithms.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Human-Computer Interaction II
description: Studies of human performance in designing and using information systems. Emphasizes concepts and methodologies from human factors, psychology, and software engineering relating to human performance.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: User Interfaces and Hypermedia
description: Advanced concepts in construction of interfaces between computers and their users. Hypermedia information structures, guidelines, problems, and tradeoffs. Discussion of selected readings, implementation of prototypes.

subject: ICS
title: HCI Design Methods
description: Advanced analytical and empirical methods for the design and evaluation of usable, useful, and robust human-computer interfaces. Students will apply selected methodologies to a major system design project.

subject: ICS
title: Social Informatics
description: An advanced introduction to the design of human-computer systems and other technological artifacts for supporting human collaboration in learning, work and social contexts, and to theoretical perspectives and empirical studies of collaboration that inform such design.
prereq_raw: ICS 464 or ICS 465 or ICS 664 or ICS 665 or ICS 667 or LIS 677 ; or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Social Computing
description: Participative analysis of online communities and user-generated content collections. Theoretical and practical aspects of online interaction, identity, trust, and virtual social capital.

subject: ICS
title: Evolutionary Computation I: Survey of Methods
description: Evolutionary computation surveys in the field to prepare students for research. Topics include diverse engineering applications, theory, and concepts including search spaces, representation, objective functions, variation operators, selection, and population based search.
prereq_raw: ICS 211 (B or better) and ICS 241 (C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent.

children.text: ( B or better) and ICS 241 ( C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Sequences Analysis
description: To expose students to bioinformatics at the biological sequences analysis level (DNA, RNA, proteins). Several bioinformatics methods and algorithms are introduced. Students are required to present one paper and to participate in a small group project.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Bioinformatics: Microarrays
description: Introduction to the basic principles of biology relevant for microarray gene expression data and to Bioconductor. Collaborative open-source project to develop a modular general framework for the analysis of cDNA arrays and gene chips.
prereq_raw: ICS 311 or background in biology, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Computer Graphics
description: Selected advanced topics in computer graphics. Substantial project required.

subject: ICS
title: Numerical Computation
description: Selected topics in numerical analysis, mathematical software, and scientific computation; examples include sparse matrix methods, finite element methods, mathematical programming.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Computer Vision
description: Fundamental problems and core concepts and techniques in computer vision, covering both theoretical and practical issues in the field.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Data Visualization
description: Explores advanced techniques in data visualization by surveying visualization techniques from the past 5-10 years, and designing and developing data visualizations leveraging those techniques.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
description: Students will learn the science, engineering, art, and applications of virtual reality and augmented reality, with an emphasis on the construction of working virtual environments.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ICS
title: Digital Video Information
description: Principles and techniques of technical and context analysis of digital video information. Video capture and editing tools, compression and analysis algorithms, visual culture, narrative structure, juxtaposition of multimedia elements and their effects on information transmission.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ICS
title: Seminar in ICS
description: Series of talks on advanced research topics.

subject: ICS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Computer Science
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Science: area 1
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Science: area 2
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.
