description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Science: area 4
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Topics in Computer Science: general
description: Reflects special interests of faculty in various areas of computer science. (B) area 1; (C) area 2; (D) area 3; (E) area 4; (G) general.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times in different topics and different areas.

subject: ICS
title: Special Topics Seminar
description: Seminar discussing special topics in information and computer science. Topics and number of credits vary.

subject: ICS
title: Advanced Special Topics in Security
description: Current topics and upcoming issues relevant to the field of information assurance and cyber security.

subject: ICS
title: Directed Reading/Research
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: ICS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: ICS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD in computer science.

subject: ILO
title: Beginning Ilokano I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

subject: ILO
title: Beginning Ilokano II
description: Continuation of ILO 101 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano for Health Sciences
description: Development of listening, speaking, reading, writing and other communication skills designed specifically for Nursing, Dentistry, Dental Hygiene, Public Health and Social Work students. Culture integrated with language study.

subject: ILO
title: Intermediate Ilokano I
description: Continuation of ILO 102 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

subject: ILO
title: Intermediate Ilokano II
description: Continuation of ILO 201 . Course meets three hours weekly, with an additional sixteen course hours dedicated to out-of-class field experience (co-curricular cultural activities).

subject: ILO
title: Third-Level Ilokano
description: To further acquire and develop Ilokano language skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing, utilizes ethnographic and sociolinguistic approaches in order to further examine and interrogate the relationship of language and culture.

subject: ILO
title: Third-Level Ilokano
description: Continuation of ILO 301 .

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano Aural Comprehension
description: Training in listening comprehension of different authentic and simulated materials as presented in documentaries, soap operas, radio and television news and other broadcasts, formal lectures, plays, natural conversations, songs, and student-created sitcoms and dramas.

subject: ILO
title: Contemporary Ilokano Literature
description: Conducted in Ilokano, this course explores the literary landscape of Ilokano literature from the perspective of Ilokano writers based in the Philippines as well as those outside of the country.

subject: ILO
title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
description: Taught in Ilokano; explores the language’s applications in social services, communication, education, and healthcare. Students perform tasks such as writing reports, conducting interviews, and documenting the life stories of immigrant Ilokanos in Hawai’i.

subject: ILO
title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
description: Continuation of ILO 401 .

subject: ILO
title: Introduction to Ilokano for Interpreters
description: Techniques for interpreting Ilokano into English and vice versa.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano Interpretation Field Practicum
description: Provide extensive practical training in consecutive, simultaneous, sight and telephonic interpreting. It requires observation and study of interpretation strategies and techniques in relevant situations.

subject: ILO
title: Structure of Ilokano
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and syntax.

subject: ILO
title: Ilokano for the Mass Media
description: Ilokano as the medium for print journalism, for radio show programming, and for television production.

subject: IND
title: Elementary Indonesian I
description: First semester of elementary Indonesian. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Indonesia.

subject: IND
title: Elementary Indonesian II
description: Second semester of elementary Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of communicative competence in both oral and written language.

subject: IND
title: Intermediate Indonesian I
description: The first semester of intermediate Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advance communication and travel.

subject: IND
title: Intermediate Indonesian II
description: Second semester of intermediate Indonesian. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advanced communication, travel, and further study.

subject: IND
title: Third-Level Indonesian
description: Continuation of IND 202 . Conducted in Indonesian. Meets three hours a week. Reading, discussion, composition, and projects.

subject: IND
title: Third-Level Indonesian
description: Continuation of IND 301 .

subject: IND
title: Third Level Indonesian
description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring the language of the contemporary Indonesian media with an emphasis on reading, writing, and listening comprehension. Not open to students who have taken IND 301 .

subject: IND
title: Third Level Indonesian

description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Written communication emphasis.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Classical Hindu Mythology
description: Study of myths and narratives of classical Hinduism through the Sanskrit epics Rāmāyana and Mahābhārata; exploring major concepts such as dharma, karma, and yoga. Intensive, interpretive writing, and peer-review exercises, will hone students’ writing skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Games, Sports and Martial Arts
description: Introduces an experiential approach in the study of Philippine traditional games, sports, and martial arts. It also focuses on the historical and socio-cultural aspects of games, sports, and martial arts. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Diasporic Literatures
description: Appreciation, reexamination, and analysis of Philippine literature of exile; a reevaluation of Philippine writing from the diaspora. Sophomore standing or higher or consent.

subject: IP
title: Critical Discourses in IPLL Studies: Philippines
description: Revaluation and analysis of critical discourses in Philippine languages and literatures and an examination of alternative perspectives to the prevailing studies on Philippine culture; an appreciation of emerging knowledge on the Philippines.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
description: Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: IP
title: Theories in Ilokano Studies
description: Examines the various theories employed in the study of Ilokano society, language, and culture from a variety of historical periods.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Literary Cultural Relations (Philippines and Southeast Asia)
description: An appreciation, a re-examination, and an analysis of the literary and cultural relations among the various nation states of Southeast Asia. Various texts are examined to establish the connections of these nation states. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: IP
title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in various communities. Explores how language policies, discourses, and ideologies shape people’s use of language. Emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: IP

description: Traditional Polynesian genres (legends, myths, folktales, fables, proverbs, songs, riddles, jokes) examined in translation and culturally and structurally interpreted.

subject: IS
title: Ethics, Aging & Society
description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging.

subject: IS
title: Independent Study Tutorial
description: Independent study tutorial.

subject: IS
title: Native Americans and Native Hawaiians
description: Comparative-contrastive examination of similarities and differences between Native Americans and Native Hawaiians as the only indigenous peoples of the U.S. with special attention to sociohistorical parallels and mutual contacts since contact with Europeans. Perspective is explicitly interdisciplinary by drawing not only on sociology and history, but also on archaeology, ethnology, linguistics and still other disciplines.
prereq_raw: HIST 152 and an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science or sociology; or consent.

children.text: an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science

subject: IS
title: Ethnohistory
description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e. the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

subject: IS
title: Information Technology and Culture
description: Investigation of the impact of information technologies on contemporary culture from a variety of perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Science and Culture
description: Cultural studies of science from historical, philosophical, sociological and literary perspectives. Examination of intersections of science, race, gender and environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Human Values and the Environment
description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts-literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics-in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent.

subject: IS
title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles.

subject: IS

prereq_raw: ANSC 200 , BIOL 101 , MICR 130 , PH 201 , or consent of instructor.

description: People’s impact on quality of coastal and ocean environments, especially Hawaiian; scientific, legal, socioeconomic aspects. Ocean pollution, ocean technology.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 , ORE 202 , or ZOOL 200 ; or consent.

subject: IS
title: British Life and Culture
description: For Study Abroad Program students participating in the UH Mānoa Semester in London. Emphasis is placed on understanding within historical contexts important issues for contemporary British society-particularly those of class, power, gender, and race.

subject: IS
title: One Health Journal Club
description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics.

subject: IS
title: Directed Reading and Research

subject: IS
title: The Humboldt Brothers’ Legacy
description: Life and thought of the two Humboldt brothers. Alexander (1769-1859) helped to lay the foundations of modern science, including geology, geography, botany, zoology, physiology and anthropology. Older, less well-known Wilhelm (1767—1835) was an influential statesman, classical scholar, man of letters, humanist, political philosopher, anthropologist and linguist, and founded the University of Berlin. Review of the two polymaths’ impact on modern science in the Americas, the Pacific and Asia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper-division or consent.

subject: IS
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

subject: IS
title: Becoming an Inclusive Leader
description: Emphasis on the knowledge and skills to become effective and inclusive leaders who can foster diverse, equitable, and inclusive communities. Interdisciplinary exploration of the theoretical foundations of inclusivity.

description: Training in advanced business writing for bilingual and other advanced learners. Japanese writing intensive.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Proficiency Through Multimedia
description: Training in oral communication, comprehension, and vocabulary expansion presented through multimedia.

subject: JPN
title: Structure of Japanese
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics of modern colloquial Japanese.
prereq_raw: JPN 302 or JPN 305 ; and JPN 350 or LING 320 ; or consent.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Pedagogical Grammar
description: Introduction to teaching of basic Japanese grammatical patterns.
prereq_raw: JPN 350 or LING 320 , and JPN 401 , JPN 403 , JPN 404 , or JPN 405 ; or consent.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Teaching Japanese as a Foreign Language
description: Introduction to instructional approaches for Japanese language classroom teaching that focus on everyday language use. Students develop instructional materials, pedagogical practices, and assessment tools for engaged and effective teaching and learning of Japanese.
prereq_raw: JPN 350 (or concurrent) and JPN 401 , JPN 403 , JPN 404 , or JPN 405 (or concurrent); or instructor’s consent. .

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Level Japanese Abroad
description: Intensive course of full time instruction on the fourth-year level in Japanese language and culture in Japan.

subject: JPN
title: Fourth-Level Japanese Abroad
description: Continuation of JPN 458 .

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Classical Japanese
description: Basic classical Japanese grammar to develop reading skills.

subject: JPN
title: Readings in Classical Japanese
description: Introduction to major genres of prose and poetry.

subject: JPN
title: Okinawan Language and Culture
description: Focuses on the language, heritage, and folk culture of Okinawa.

subject: JPN
title: Okinawan Language and Literature
description: Focuses on Okinawan literature across various genres and periods. Will require weekly reaction papers, the midterm reading/writing project, and a final research project report.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Sociolinguistics
description: Application of general linguistics to social phenomena such as group identity, language and gender, dialects and intercultural communication.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Readings in Modern Japanese Literature
description: Advanced course to foster speed, accuracy and attention to stylistic issues in modern Japanese literature.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Readings in Modern Japanese Contemporary Topics
description: Advanced course to foster speed, accuracy, and attention to content in reading modern discursive texts.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Japanese Language Study
description: Advanced course in spoken and written Japanese stressing intensive research using the Internet, electronic mail in Japanese and conventional media. Oral presentations, written reports and journal writing.

subject: JPN
title: Project Work in Japanese
description: Enhances Japanese language skills through a field-based research project on a topic of the individual student’s choice. Interviews, surveys, observations, written materials and A/V-assisted oral presentations.

subject: JPN
title: Career Foundations in Japanese
description: Preparation for internship in Japan, with a primary focus on effective workplace communication, Japanese work culture & professional competencies, and research projects.

subject: JPN
title: Internship Program
description: Participation in an internship program in Japan, Hawaiʻi, or elsewhere under faculty supervision.

subject: JPN
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Phonology and Morphology
description: Introduction to the phonology and morphology of modern colloquial Japanese.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Syntax and Semantics
description: Introduction to theories of syntax, sentence structure, parts of speech, constituency, grammatical relations and case marking, word order, passives, causatives, tense, aspect, and embeddings.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Language Pedagogy
description: Training in the identification and analysis of general problems in Japanese language learning, teaching, and testing by examining theoretical issues and conducting classroom research.
prereq_raw: JPN 407 or equivalent, and JPN 451 ; or consent.

subject: JPN
title: Research Methodology in Japanese Linguistics and Language Teaching
description: Japanese-specific training in the formulation of testable hypotheses, in basic statistical and other evaluation techniques, and in the organization and presentation of ideas and data in paper, abstracts, etc.

subject: JPN
title: Japanese Sociolinguistics
description: Introduces theories of language use and provides training in the methodology and analysis of Japanese sociolinguistics.
prereq_raw: JPN 407 and JPN 475 or equivalent, or consent.

subject: JPN
title: (Alpha) Japanese Poetry
description: Historical survey of major poetic types.
prereq_raw: JPN 466 or consent for (B) and (C); JPN 485 or consent for (D).
repeatable_raw: 1 time with consent (B) classical; (C) medieval and Edo; (D) modern.

subject: JPN
title: (Alpha) Modern Japanese Literature
description: Representative literary works, emphasis on fiction; (B) Meiji-Taisho (1868-1926); (C) Showa-Heisei (1926- present).

subject: JPN
title: Modern Japanese Literature: Meiji-Taisho (1868-1926)
description: Representative literary works, emphasis on fiction; (B) Meiji-Taisho (1868-1926); (C) Showa-Heisei (1926- present).

subject: JPN
title: Modern Japanese Literature: Showa-Heisei (1926-present)
description: Representative literary works, emphasis on fiction; (B) Meiji-Taisho (1868-1926); (C) Showa-Heisei (1926- present).

subject: JPN
title: Edo Literature
description: Critical reading and analysis; emphasis on prose.

subject: JPN
title: Medieval Japanese Literature
description: Critical reading and analysis of Kamakura and Muromachi literature, emphasis on prose.

subject: JPN
title: Classical Japanese Literature
description: Critical reading and analysis of Heian literature; emphasis on prose.

subject: JPN
title: (Alpha) Practicum: Teaching Japanese Language
description: For graduate students who are planning to teach Japanese as a foreign language. Through lectures and discussions on language learning and teaching, and through observation and teaching of a Japanese language class, students will learn to make informed decisions about curriculum and instruction, and will develop instructional skills and practices for analyzing their teaching experiences. (B) beginning level Japanese instruction; (C) advanced level Japanese instruction. Each alpha may be taken one time.

subject: JPN
title: Practicum: Teaching Japanese Language: Beginning Level Japanese Instruction
description: For graduate students who are planning to teach Japanese as a foreign language. Through lectures and discussions on language learning and teaching, and through observation and teaching of a Japanese language class, students will learn to make informed decisions about curriculum and instruction, and will develop instructional skills and practices for analyzing their teaching experiences. (B) beginning level Japanese instruction; (C) advanced level Japanese instruction. Each alpha may be taken one time.

subject: JPN
title: Practicum: Teaching Japanese Language: Advanced Level Japanese Instruction
description: For graduate students who are planning to teach Japanese as a foreign language. Through lectures and discussions on language learning and teaching, and through observation and teaching of a Japanese language class, students will learn to make informed decisions about curriculum and instruction, and will develop instructional skills and practices for analyzing their teaching experiences. (B) beginning level Japanese instruction; (C) advanced level Japanese instruction. Each alpha may be taken one time.

subject: JPN
title: Introduction to Japanese Manuscripts and Xylographs
description: Introduction to Classical Japanese writing system as found in the xylographs and manuscripts of the Heian and Kamakura periods; reading and analysis of the texts in original script.

subject: JPN
title: History of the Japanese Language
description: Survey, theories of origin; related topics in linguistic methodology.

subject: JPN
title: Teaching Japanese as a Second Language
description: Practical overview of major problems; motivation; adult second language learning; communicative and linguistic competence; practical classroom techniques of teaching and testing.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Japanese Sociolinguistics
description: Variations in language form and use depending on social factors.
prereq_raw: JPN 601 or JPN 602 (or concurrent), and JPN 606 ; or consent.

subject: JPN
title: Advanced Japanese Syntax and Semantics
description: Theoretical problems in description of Japanese; contributions of Japanese linguistic study to syntactic theory.

subject: JPN
title: Topics in Japanese Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics in Japanese literature, primarily of the modern period. English translations of original texts will be provided whenever available.

subject: JPN
title: Traditional Literary Theory
description: Reading and analysis of major works of literary theory and criticism from the classical, medieval, and Edo periods.

subject: JPN
title: Kambun
description: Introduction to kambun [the Japanese manner of reading and writing classical Chinese], with critical reading of kambun by Japanese authors.

subject: JPN
title: (Alpha) Topics in Japanese Linguistics
description: (C) Japanese/English contrastive analysis; (G) structure; (H) historical change; (K) history of Japanese language studies (Kokugo-gaku-shi); (M) morphophonemics; (P) pedagogy; (S) sociolinguistics.

subject: KOR
title: Elementary Korean I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.

subject: KOR
title: Elementary Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 101 .

subject: KOR
title: Accelerated Elementary Korean
description: Content of KOR 101 and KOR 102 covered in one intensive course. Four 2-hour sessions per week, Monday-Thursday, plus daily lab work.

subject: KOR
title: Elementary Conversational Korean I
description: Development of basic skills (listening, speaking and grammar) of spoken Korean, with application to some familiar everyday topics.

subject: KOR
title: Elementary Conversational Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 111 .

subject: KOR
title: Intermediate Korean I
description: Continuation of KOR 101 and KOR 102 . Meets one hour, four times a week, plus lab work.
prereq_raw: KOR 102 or placement test; or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Intermediate Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 201 .
prereq_raw: KOR 201 or placement test; or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Accelerated Intermediate Korean
description: Content of KOR 201 and KOR 202 covered in one intensive course. Four 2-hour sessions per week, Monday- Thursday, plus daily lab work.
prereq_raw: KOR 102 , KOR 105 , KOR 112 , placement test; or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Intermediate Conversational Korean I
description: Further development of listening and speaking skills. The student is expected to be able to comprehend and produce speech at the paragraph level.

subject: KOR
title: Intermediate Conversational Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 211 .

subject: KOR
title: Third-Level Korean I
description: Continuation of KOR 201 and KOR 202 . Major emphasis on comprehension of modern written Korean. Chinese characters.

subject: KOR
title: Third-Level Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 301 .

subject: KOR
title: Accelerated Third-Level Korean
description: Content of KOR 301 and KOR 302 covered in one intensive summer course. Five 3-hour sessions per week, Monday- Friday.
prereq_raw: KOR 202 , KOR 205 , placement test, or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Readings in Chinese Characters I
description: Training intermediate and advanced learners of Korean to master the reading, writing and usage of some 250 basic Chinese characters as they are used in a wide variety of Korean reading texts.

subject: KOR
title: Readings in Chinese Characters II
description: Continuation of KOR 307 , covering an additional 250 basic Chinese characters.

subject: KOR
title: Reading and Translating Korean Poetry
description: Introduction to modern Korean poetry and translation for students with third-year level Korean abilities. Students will learn how to interpret poems and translate them from Korean to English.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Proficiency Through TV Drama
description: Increasing Korean proficiency to advanced level through TV drama, which provides culturally and situationally rich contexts. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: KOR
title: Directed Third-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Offered if staff available.

subject: KOR
title: Fourth-Level Korean I
description: Continuation of KOR 302 .

subject: KOR
title: Fourth-Level Korean II
description: Continuation of KOR 401 .

subject: KOR
title: High-Advanced Korean: Korean Society
description: Emphasis on the highest level of listening, speaking, reading, and writing, with application to Korean society, using authentic materials.

subject: KOR
title: High-Advanced Korean: Korean Culture
description: Continuation of KOR 402 . Emphasis on the highest level of listening, speaking, reading and writing, with application to Korean culture using authentic materials and focusing on training in oral presentation skills.

subject: KOR
title: Advanced Oral Communication in Korean
description: Fourth-year advanced Korean course to increase learners’ oral fluency and accuracy; with an emphasis on formal speaking. Covers linguistic proficiency as well as social and cultural proficiencies.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Composition
description: Training in modern structural and stylistic techniques; writing on designated themes.

subject: KOR
title: Media Analysis in Korean: Contemporary Korean Culture
description: Focus on analyzing, comparing, and evaluating current media materials in South Korea to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of contemporary Korean society.

subject: KOR
title: Media Analysis in Korean: Culture in South and North Korea
description: Focus on comparing and analyzing cultural or historical issues in South and North Korea using media materials to develop professional language skills and to deepen knowledge and understanding of the two Koreas.

subject: KOR
title: Selected Readings in Korean
description: Selected readings in various disciplines. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: KOR
title: Structure of Korean: Phonology/Morphology
description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and history.

subject: KOR
title: Structure of Korean: Syntax
description: Introduction to syntax and semantics.

subject: KOR
title: Language and Culture of Korea
description: Relation of Korean language to literature, history, philosophy, social structure, values, and interpersonal relationships; social and regional varieties. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Proficiency Through Film
description: Study of Korean culture through films to elevate students’ Korean proficiency level and improve their knowledge of Korea. Emphasis on writing instruction. Requires a minimum of 16 pages of graded writing.

subject: KOR
title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Humanities
description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in various Humanities disciplines, including history, religion, language, education, and literature. Taught entirely in Korean.

subject: KOR
title: Korean for Academic Purposes: Social Sciences & Others
description: Focus on expanding students’ Korean literacy and cultural knowledge in social Science and other disciplines, including politics, economy, society, and writing in Korean.

subject: KOR
title: Introduction to Traditional Korean Literature
description: Critical readings from earliest times and presentations that emphasize genre, style, and context.

subject: KOR
title: Introduction to Modern Korean Literature
description: Critical Korean-language readings of 20th-century literature that emphasize context and the development of style. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: KOR
title: Internship Program
description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts on Oʻahu or in Korea. Students will also attend an on-campus preparatory and follow-up language class.
prereq_raw: KOR 486 , diagnostic assessment procedures; or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Abroad
description: Supervised internship with Korean professional hosts in Korea. Students also undergo a one-week training module designed to prepare them to maximize the benefits of the overseas internship.
prereq_raw: KOR 495 , diagnostic assessment procedures; or consent.

subject: KOR
title: Directed Fourth-Level Reading
description: For those who need special assistance, e.g., in reading texts in area of specialization or at a pace more rapid than those of standard courses. Primarily for graduate students from other departments.

subject: KOR
title: (Alpha) Korean Verse
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga , changga , hanshi , sijo , kasa , free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Verse: modern
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga , changga , hanshi , sijo , kasa , free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Verse: traditional
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean lyric and didactic verse (e.g., hyangga , changga , hanshi , sijo , kasa , free form): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: (Alpha) Korean Narrative
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori , shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Narrative: modern
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori , shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Narrative: traditional
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected works of Korean narrative (e.g., myth, p’ansori , shaman song, essay, biography, fiction): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: (Alpha) Korean Drama
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Drama: modern
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Korean Drama: traditional
description: Intensive and analytical reading of selected materials in Korean performing arts (e.g., spectacle, farce play, mask dance, staged narratives, theatrical drama): (M) modern; (T) traditional.
prereq_raw: KOR 494 or consent for (M), KOR 493 or consent for (T).

subject: KOR
title: Media Research in Korean
description: Focuses on searching, analyzing, and evaluating media data for research in areas of student specializations. Students are required to write short analysis papers and a final research paper.
prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

subject: KOR
title: Comparative Studies of Contemporary South and North Korean Language
description: Comparing and analyzing language data to investigate language heterogeneity problems, its causes, and importance of comparative studies in NK/SK language differences; differences in language policy, grammar, and vocabulary, pronunciation, and discourse style.
prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

subject: KOR
title: Interdisciplinary Research in Korean
description: Combined lecture-discussion on preparing students to be able to conduct interdisciplinary research in Korean. Require advanced-level Korean proficiency.
prereq_raw: diagnostic assessment (equivalent to ILR Level 2) or consent.

children.text: diagnostic assessment ( equivalent to ILR Level 2)

subject: KOR
title: (Alpha) Analysis of Korean Academic Discourse
description: Co-taught by Korean faculty of professional schools and Korean instruction in domain of (B) economics; (C) political science; (D) computer science; (E) travel industry management; (G) business; (H) law; (I) medicine; (J) nursing and public health; and (K) others. Exclusively in Korean.

subject: KOR
title: History and Dialects of Korean Language
description: Survey of various hypotheses on the genetic relationship of Korean; evolution of Korean from the 15th century to the present; Korean dialects.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Phonology and Morphology
description: Review of Korean vocalic and consonantal phonology. Phonological and morphological analysis of Korean derivation and inflection.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Syntax and Semantics
description: Review of theoretical problems in Korean syntax and semantics; different approaches; and contributions of Korean linguistic study to syntactic and semantic theory.

subject: KOR
title: Topics in Korean Sociolinguistics
description: Korean language in social context, honorifics and politeness, regional and social variation, gendered language, multilingualism, social media discourse, diaspora and globalized Korean, AI and language technology, offered with different focus.

subject: KOR
title: Pedagogy of Teaching Korean as a Foreign Language
description: Identification and analysis of major problems in Korean language learning, teaching, testing, and materials development by examining theoretical issues and conducting classroom research; practical techniques of teaching and testing skills in listening, reading, speaking, writing and culture.

subject: KOR
title: Topics in Korean Conversation Analysis
description: Theoretical framework and methodology of Korean conversation analysis; training for data collection, transcription, and data analysis; offered with different focuses, covering grammar and interaction, second language teaching, as well as language and body.

subject: KOR
title: Literary Translation of Korean
description: The art and craft of translating traditional and modern Korean literary works into English.

subject: KOR
title: Korean Language Acquisition
description: Examining human language acquisition by comparing first (L1) and second language (L2) learning, focusing on unique cognitive and linguistic challenges of acquiring Korean through scientific and statistical analysis of language behavior patterns.

subject: KOR
title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature.

subject: KOR
title: Practicum: Teaching Korean as a Foreign Language
description: Designed for graduate students pursuing Korean language teaching, while developing practical teaching skills through class observation, action research and discussion under supervision.

subject: KOR
title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical socio-cultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

subject: KOR
title: Research Seminar in Korean Literature
description: Advanced study of an author, school, period, genre, or problem leading to a research paper.

subject: KOR
title: Research Seminar in Korean Language
description: Advanced study in history and dialects, phonology and morphology, syntax and semantics, sociolinguistics, or pedagogy, leading to a research paper.

subject: KRS
title: Physical Fitness
description: Conditioning exercises and activities to develop and maintain physical efficiency. Motor fitness tests administered to measure status and progress.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aerobic Fitness
description: Aerobic fitness improvement upon completion of course by regularly attending and practicing safe workout routines. Learn fitness components, names of muscles and exercises associated with each one.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Beginning
description: Adjusting to and immersing in water, floating, sculling; correct arm stroke, leg kick, breathing techniques and their coordination. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Intermediate
description: Perfecting and integrating basic strokes with added emphasis for speed and distance. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Swimming: Advanced
description: Correct techniques used in competitive swimming, racing starts, correct turning techniques, long-distance swimming. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: SCUBA Diving: Beginning
description: Learning watermanship, equipment handling skills, and the knowledge to become safe divers. Additional costs for equipment, diver manual, dive tables, and certification fee.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aqua-Aerobic Fitness
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on aerobic fitness improvement through total body aquatic workouts with music, and development of individualized aquatics fitness program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, stance, drive, normal iron shots, approach shots, putting.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Intermediate
description: Corrective work on basic swing mechanics and rhythm; adjustments for bunker play, uphill lies, downhill lies, short game around and on the green; handicapping and match play competition.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Golf: Advanced
description: Improving drive, fairway wood shots, long iron shots, control shots, trouble shots, putting, course management, competitive strategy, problems in rules. Greens fees paid by students for play on courses.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of those interested in pursuing health-related careers. Structure and function of major systems examined (gross anatomy, micro-anatomy, physiology, and pathology).

subject: KRS
title: Bowling
description: Rules, etiquette, arm swing, approach, execution, scoring, spare pickups. Students pay charge for use of alley.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Badminton
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, smash, drive, net play, offensive and defensive strategy; singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Folk and National Dances
description: Popular dances of various national groups, including square dances.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawaiʻi
description: Background and fundamentals of hula. Selected dances with and without instruments.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Dances of Hawaiʻi: Advanced
description: Advanced techniques in hula movements. Selected dances taught will be more complex, including work with instruments. Individual choreography will be emphasized.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Ballroom
description: Social dances including fox trot, waltz, swing, and other popular dances. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Social Dance: Latin
description: Social dances of a Latin flavor including rhumba, cha-cha, tango, samba, and others. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, volleying; singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Intermediate
description: Corrective work in three basic strokes and in net play; the lob, drop shot, overhead smash, and half-volley; applying spin in basic strokes; basic strategy in singles and doubles play.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tennis: Advanced
description: Improving upon the strokes introduced in KRS 130 and KRS 131 ; advanced competitive strategy; problems in rules; officiating; elements of tournament play.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Beginning
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on beginner skills and knowledge relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Volleyball: Intermediate
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on improving skills and knowledge through practice and cognitive activities relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Basketball
description: Rules, passing, shooting, dribbling, rebounding, individual defensive and offensive maneuvers; team offense and defense.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Adapted and Prescribed Exercises
description: Small group and individual guidance and instruction for students recommended by student health service.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Weight Training
description: Kinesiology of lifting and weight training, various types of exercises and methods of training with resistance.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Olympic and Power Lifting
description: Exercise technique and prescription with an emphasis on anaerobic exercise. Explores advanced periodization models and their utilization, mastery of Olympic lifts, and plyometric programs.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Heavy Apparatus
description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Judo
description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Aikido
description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
description: Classic forms of t’ai chi ch’uan.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Beginning
description: Rules, etiquette, basic stances, blocks, thrusts, kicks, ippon kumite, and selected kata. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Karate: Intermediate
description: Emphasis on improving the basic techniques (stances, punches, kicks, forms, and sparring); introduction to combination techniques. (Student to provide own gi.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Wrestling: Beginning
description: Rules: fundamental defensive and offensive maneuvers and competitive strategy, i.e., takedowns, reversals, escapes, and pinning combinations; conditioning exercises.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Beginning
description: Experiencing yoga and its effects on body, mind and consciousness of individual. Encompasses exercise, breathing techniques, deep relaxation, meditation, practice in concentration, and yogic postures.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Yoga: Intermediate
description: Corrective work and improvement of basic techniques. Exercise sets and combinations designed to develop endurance, flexibility, muscle and nerve strength, meditation, and deep relaxation technique.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Water Polo
description: Fundamentals of basic water polo skills, namely, ball handling, passing, shooting, dribbling plus a brief introduction into beginning techniques of individual offense and defense.
prereq_raw: KRS 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

children.text: ( Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency I: Invasion
description: Knowledge, skill development, and strategy of various invasion type games and sports. Sports like basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee and/or others are introduced within a tactical framework.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Sport Proficiency II: Net, Field, and Target
description: Knowledge, skill development, position, and strategy of net, field and target sports. Sports like volleyball, tennis, softball, and golf are introduced within a tactical framework.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Floor Exercise Gymnastics
description: An entry-level course designed to develop students’ knowledge of men’s and women’s gymnastics floor exercise routines, including injury prevention, skill progression, spotting techniques, and routine choreography. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Track and Field for Physical Education
description: Knowledge, skills, and rules of various track and field events. Organization of track meets and strategy in competition. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: Softball
description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on basic skills, rules, etiquette, offensive and defensive strategies, position play, and game situations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all students.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, but credit earned 1 time only.

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Elementary
description: Responsibilities of elementary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing teacher’s role in health instruction, health services, school health policies.

subject: KRS
title: School Health Problems: Secondary
description: Responsibilities of secondary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing health instruction, health services, healthful school living, school health policies.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Kinesiology
description: Kinesiology as a professional field. Overview of history, philosophy, and current trends in kinesiology. Survey of psychological and sociological foundations of kinesiology, exercise, fitness and sport.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors or approval.

subject: KRS
title: Recreation Services in Contemporary Society
description: Theories and philosophies in recreation: history; contemporary issues; roles in modern society; relationship to health, physical education, and exercise science.

subject: KRS
title: Human Development
description: Developmental processes across the life span. Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Human growth and development from conception to death with major theories and related research on maintaining healthy lifestyles.

subject: KRS
title: Safety and Risk Management
description: Understanding the fundamental principles and techniques of safety and accident-prevention programming emphasizing school, home, public places, on the job, and motor vehicle situations.

subject: KRS
title: Outdoor Recreation Management
description: Objectives and values of outdoor recreation; characteristics and determinants of programs; planning, organization, leadership, and facilities for recreational uses of natural environments.

subject: KRS
title: Health Education Curriculum
description: Objectives of school health program, emphasizing scope and sequence of health instruction; critical examination of health curriculum guides from various states.

subject: KRS
title: Programming and Leadership
description: Factors in planning and leading recreation programs; characteristics and responsibilities of leadership in relation to nature, scope, and resources of a variety of programs.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Health and Physical Education
description: Introduction to foundational knowledge for effective teaching, history, philosophy, and current practices in health and physical education. Provides the basis for later coursework in K-12 health and physical education. Required field experience.

subject: KRS
title: Performance Based Assessment in Health and Physical Education
description: Assessment and evaluative techniques applied to health and physical education, including test construction, performance-based assessment, measurement criteria and instruments, interpretation of data and content, as well as program evaluation.

subject: KRS
title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Understanding standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment in health with a focus on advocacy, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and prevention of disease within sub-topics of health (mental, social, emotional, environmental, financial, etc.).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Principles of Sports Medicine
description: Examines with some depth, principles of risk management and pathology of athletic injuries, major musculoskeletal structures, and concepts of evaluative skills, treatment, and rehabilitation for common athletic injuries.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Football
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive football coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Basketball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive basketball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Baseball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive baseball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Volleyball
description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive volleyball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

subject: KRS
title: Music and Rhythm in Physical Education
description: Use of music in physical education programming (K-12), emphasizing selection of appropriate music for specific activities as expressive or creative movement, movement exploration, rhythmic gymnastics, and dancing. A variety of strategies for teaching dance will be shared.

subject: KRS
title: Managing Recreation Services
description: Administrative framework and procedures pertinent to the operation of agencies providing recreational services to the various publics.

subject: KRS
title: Water Safety Training
description: Theory and methods of advanced lifesaving and water safety leading to American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor (WSI) certification.
prereq_raw: KRS 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

subject: KRS
title: Emergency Care and First Aid Training
description: Practicum in training of persons to become qualified in emergency care knowledge, basic life support, and first aid skills. First Aid and CPR certificates may be earned.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Movement Education I
description: A movement-based approach to teaching basic motor skills in preschool/elementary physical education. Students actively participate and learn about developmentally appropriate content and pedagogy for children in grades P-5/6. Peer bit teaching is included.

subject: KRS
title: Movement Education II
description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Content and pedadogy for teaching Pre/K-5 physical education. Students will learn to plan and teach physical education for children. Peer bit and field teaching included.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Track and Field
description: Techniques and rules of sprints, distance runs, relays, hurdles, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus, and javelin throws; conduct of track and field meets; specific conditioning and training problems.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching of Swimming
description: Theory and methods of coaching competitive swimming. Technical, organizational, and administrative aspects. Emphasis on stroke mechanics and training methods.

subject: KRS
title: Fieldwork in Recreation I
description: Initial supervised leadership experience in recreational agencies. One hour per week in class discussion sessions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: For recreation majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Special Recreation
description: Special recreation as a professional field. Overview of special recreation services. Emphasis on recreation services for special populations.

subject: KRS
title: Structural Kinesiology
description: Gross human anatomy, emphasizing identification and description of parts of the musculoskeletal system; selected applications to motor activity. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent.
prereq_raw: KRS 113 or BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 / PHYL 141L or PHYL 301 / PHYL 301L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Exercise and Sport Physiology
description: Emphasis on physiological responses to exercises and physical training as related to strength, muscular endurance, cardio-respiratory endurance. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent.
prereq_raw: KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Exercise and Sport Physiology Lab
description: Laboratory section to accompany KRS 354 . Emphasis will be hands-on data collection and analysis of the physiological responses to exercise and physical training. Lab report development and scientific writing will also be emphasized.
prereq_raw: KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Techniques I: Elementary
description: Teaching techniques and methods of elementary physical education. Content to include basic skills and games in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Techniques II: Secondary
description: Teaching techniques and methods of secondary physical education. Content to include invasion, net, field, and target activities. Emphasizes the tactical approach in a school-based experience, as well as writing through lesson planning. Primarily for Health & Physical Education majors.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for Health & Physical Education majors.

subject: KRS
title: Drugs and Society
description: Introduction to psychoactive drugs and their effects; drug regulations; education and rehabilitation programs; psycho-social variables related to the decisions to use/abuse drugs.

subject: KRS
title: Physical Fitness for Physical Education Teachers
description: Diagnosis and prescription for basic health and fitness problems, scientific principles of training, guidelines for exercise; essentials of scientifically based individualized physical fitness program.

subject: KRS
title: Field Work in Strength and Conditioning I
description: Supervised practicum in strength training and conditioning. Students will be exposed to the theory and practice of designing and implementing both strength/ power, and general conditioning programs.

subject: KRS
title: Personal Health and Wellness
description: Core concepts in health allow students to take responsibility for their own health-related behaviors by developing basic competencies in identifying, analyzing, and responsibly deliberating contemporary ethical issues related to health and wellness.

subject: KRS
title: Directed Reading
description: Individual problems. Limited to senior majors in health education, physical education, athletic training, or recreation with a minimum GPA of 2.75 in major field.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Health Concepts
description: Understanding health issues for individuals, families, schools, and communities, in regards to Hawaii K-12 schools. Focusing on the acquisition of functional health content and proficiency in health-related skills to enhance healthy behaviors in learners.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: (Alpha) Teaching Practicum in Physical Education
description: Field experience in teaching physical education activities in schools, K-12; techniques in leadership; selection of activities and program evaluation for K-12 licensure. (E) elementary; (S) secondary.
prereq_raw: admittance to licensure track; pass basic skills tests specified by the Hawaiʻi Teacher Standards Board ( www.htsb.org ) or bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Guidance and Classroom Management
description: Guidance principles applied to classroom management for teachers.

subject: KRS
title: K-12 Teaching Methods in Physical Education
description: Methods and materials in teaching physical education, including techniques, leadership skills, program evaluation, and designing course content using written communication skills.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: KRS
title: (Alpha) Teaching Residency
description: Full-time supervised experience in elementary and secondary school level. School level corresponds to level of licensure desired. (E) elementary; (S) secondary. Each alpha can be taken one time.
prereq_raw: KRS 402 E (with a minimum grade of B-), KRS 402 S (with a minimum grade of B-), and KRS 404 (with a minimum grade of B-); admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.

title: Teaching Residency: elementary
description: Full-time supervised experience in elementary and secondary school level. School level corresponds to level of licensure desired. (E) elementary; (S) secondary. Each alpha can be taken one time.
prereq_raw: KRS 402 E (with a minimum grade of B-), KRS 402 S (with a minimum grade of B-), and KRS 404 (with a minimum grade of B-); admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Residency: secondary
description: Full-time supervised experience in elementary and secondary school level. School level corresponds to level of licensure desired. (E) elementary; (S) secondary. Each alpha can be taken one time.
prereq_raw: KRS 402 E (with a minimum grade of B-), KRS 402 S (with a minimum grade of B-), and KRS 404 (with a minimum grade of B-); admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Physical Education, and Secondary Education-Physical Education majors only.

children.text: E ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , KRS 402 S ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and KRS 404 ( with a minimum grade of B- ) ; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
description: Analysis and resolutions of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning; professional growth and development.
prereq_raw: KRS 402 E, KRS 402 S, and KRS 404 or consent; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests.
