subject: KRS
title: Psychosocial Aspects of Sport
description: Examination and application of sociological and psychological theories and ethical reasoning to the sociocultural and psychological aspects of sport through the medium of writing.

subject: KRS
title: Prevent/Care of Athletic Injuries
description: An examination of the most recent practices and procedures in the prevention and care of athletic and sports injuries. Observational field experiences in athletic training will be required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Fundamentals of Ergonomics
description: Introduction to ergonomics principles and their application in understanding and prevention of Muscular Skeletal Disorders encountered in the working environment including introduction to legal aspects of ergonomics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Post-Master’s Certificate in Nursing majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Allied Health
description: An examination of organization and administration in Athletic Training, Allied Health and Exercise Science. Content includes leadership and motivation models, legal liability, ethical considerations and management strategies for all aspects of Health Care Administration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Lower Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the lower extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Upper Extremity Assessment
description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the upper extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Curriculum and Supervision
description: Effective program development, planning, and supervision, including issues in legal liability and administration of all aspects of physical education programming in grades K-12.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Current Issues in Leisure Services
description: Philosophical foundations and current and emerging issues in leisure services management and programming. Coverage of leisure research and its implications to practice.
prereq_raw: KRS 238 , KRS 249 , and KRS 329 ; or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Evaluating and Marketing Leisure Services
description: Basic methods in marketing, planning, evaluating programs and problem-solving methods, survey research, research design, data analysis, and report generation for park, recreation, and tourism systems.

subject: KRS
title: Emergency Care for the Professional Rescuer
description: Combined lecture-lab on advanced emergency care for injuries and illnesses and includes certifications for CPR/First Aid/AED. Class size of approximately 20 students.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all majors.

subject: KRS
title: Coaching Athletics
description: Combined lecture-lab with emphasis on scientific principles, theory and practice, and professional qualities of the coach. Writing is integrated with the intent that students will enhance their communication skills through writing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Camp Resources and Planning
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Combined lecture-lab for camp counselors and camp leadership. Plan and evaluate camp experiences for children and youth, including those with disabilities. Includes field trips.

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Camping
description: Supervised leadership at a camp setting with children and youth, including those with disabilities. Day or residential camps. One full week camping for each credit hour. Maximum of four credit hours.

subject: KRS
title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr. Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Sport Biomechanics
description: Concepts and scientific principles essential to efficient human movement; proper application of biomechanical principles to fundamental movements and selected complex motor skills.
prereq_raw: KRS 353 , and either PHYS 100 , PHYS 151 , or PHYS 170 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Fitness for Life
description: Students will gain knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to plan, implement, and evaluate Fitness for Life curriculum. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Teaching Methods in Health Education
description: Experiences in developing standards-based, interactive learning opportunities to teach quality health education in schools. Focus on creating curriculum and assessments aligned with the National and State Standards for Health Education.

subject: KRS
title: Learning Communities
description: Theory, basic research, interactive process, and methodology of the cooperative learning process known as Tribes. Will develop participants’ abilities to foster and facilitate learning communities in a variety of settings.

subject: KRS
title: Sociocultural Issues in Physical Activity
description: Contemporary and historical perspective on socio-cultural issues that influence health and physical activity settings. Understanding ethics and culturally responsive practice around race, gender, sexuality, class, etc. Emphasis on ethics and teaching writing for the profession.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Statistics
description: Basic elements for: descriptive statistics, probability, inference, regression, and correlation analysis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Motor Learning and Performance
description: Basic consideration is kinesthesis, motor ability, fatigue, developmental factors, practice, motivation in relation to motor learning and human performance.

subject: KRS
title: Motor Development and Learning
description: Motor learning and development through the lifespan with an emphasis on fundamental principles and patterns. Areas such as memory, knowledge of performance, and motivation are incorporated and demonstrated through activities and assignments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Primarily for KRS majors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Adapted Physical Activity in Early Childhood
description: Concepts of developmentally appropriate practice, importance of movement in overall development, and design of physical activity sessions and environments for young children with and without disabilities are covered.

subject: KRS
title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
prereq_raw: ( FSHN 185 , and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or ( PHYL 141 / PHYL 141L and PHYL 142 / PHYL 142L ) or PHYL 301 ) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Research in KRS
description: Research methods in the study of physical activity, types of research, statistical concepts and techniques, and reporting research results.

subject: KRS
title: Commercial Recreation
description: Overview of leisure services and trends in commercial, private and employee recreation, and resort and recreational tourism. The social, economic, and environmental significance is examined.

subject: KRS
title: Recreation Planning and Maintenance
description: Examination of social, economic, and environmental factors of recreation and tourism development. Emphasis on methods, processes, citizen participation, design issues/regulations, and land use.

subject: KRS
title: Drug Abuse, Violence, and Injury Prevention
description: Standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment on the scientific, socio-cultural, and attitudinal aspects of drug abuse, violence, and injury prevention. Focus on incidence and prevalence, roles, prevention, and high-risk populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: KRS
title: Sexual Health Education
description: Program planning, curriculum development and classroom teaching strategies in the areas of human sexuality, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Focus on research-based curriculum and strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

subject: KRS
title: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning Lab
description: Designed to provide knowledge of laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of aerobic and anaerobic testing results, and individual exercise program/prescription.

subject: KRS
title: Practicum in Health and Exercise Science
description: Requires 160 hours of supervised practicum experience in health, wellness, fitness, lifestyle-management (contingent upon instructor’s approval in the registered semester). Emphasis will be on experimental learning, writing and self-directed research related to students’ internship experiences.
prereq_raw: current CPR and First Aid Certification, KRS 152 , KRS 332 , KRS 353 , KRS 354 , and KRS 463 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Health and Exercise Science majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Program Design in Strength Training and Conditioning
description: Designed to provide theoretical and practical experience in supervision of a strength training center. Content includes program design, exercise techniques, organization, testing, evaluation, methods of strength development, facility design and special populations.
prereq_raw: KRS 152 , KRS 153 , KRS 353 , KRS 354L , KRS 354 , and KRS 463 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Athletic Training Clinic
description: Introduction to the Professional Athletic Training Education Program and the Clinical Education Plan. Students are required to document all requirements and demonstrate proficiency in basic clinical skills.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. ATEP Program students only.

subject: KRS
title: AT Practicum I
description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

subject: KRS
title: AT Practicum II
description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Practicum III
description: Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Practicum IV
description: (5 2-hr Practicum) Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

subject: KRS
title: Foundations of School Counseling
description: Explores school counseling history, philosophy, and ASCA Model. Covers delivery systems, interventions, roles, and ethics. Examines contemporary challenges and resources in supporting student development. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

subject: KRS
title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen with emphasis on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Human Development Across the Lifespan
description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

subject: KRS
title: Counseling: Theory and Practice
description: Overview of major counseling theories, techniques, and evidence-based practices as preparation for practicum and internship. Explores integrative approaches and theoretical concepts. Application to diverse populations in school, rehabilitation, and community settings.

subject: KRS
title: Scientific Principles of Physical Conditioning
description: Application of physiological principles to physical conditioning and athletic performance.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Muscular Strength and Power Development
description: Interpretation of scientific principles of muscular strength and power development. Examination of muscular adaptations to increased and decreased use.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience I
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Must be completed during first semester post admission into program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience II
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum includes duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Practicum must be completed during second semester post admission to the program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience III
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience IV
description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Clinical Practicum
description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced clinical practicum in which the BOC certified or certification-eligible graduate student experiences an enhancement of athletic training knowledge and refinement of athletic training skills.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Research Practicum
description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced research practicum in which the BOC certified or certification-eligible graduate student deepens their understanding and enhances their critical thinking abilities in order to contribute to the advancement of the discipline and the athletic training profession.

subject: KRS
title: (Alpha) Clinical Examination of Pathology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: lower body
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: head, neck, and spine
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Clinical Examination of Pathology: upper body
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Examination, care and treatment of musculoskeletal, neurological, and neuromuscular conditions and pathology; (B) lower body; (H) head, neck and spine; (U) upper body.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Orthopedic Assessment
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Advanced knowledge and skills of athletic training as they are specifically applied to the understanding, treatment, and rehabilitation of sport-related injuries. (e.g. epidemiology, legal, ethical concerns, sports psychology, pharm, drug abuse, health issues)

subject: KRS
title: Therapeutic Interventions: Modalities
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physiology principles and operational procedures of contemporary therapeutic modalities as they relate to the care and treatment of athletic injuries.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Therapeutic Interventions: Rehabilitative Exercise
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Concepts and principles of comprehensive rehabilitation programs (therapeutic goals and objectives, exercise selection, methods of evaluation and recording progress, progression and return to competition criteria, and physiological effects of tissue trauma and inactivity).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: General Medical Conditions in Sports Medicine
description: An examination/evaluation of general medical conditions associated with sports medicine including pathology, care and treatment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Athletic Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Athletic Training
description: Designed to provide the student with analytical skills and practical experience relative to research as it applies to sports related injuries.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Therapeutic Exercise
description: Advanced concepts and evidence-based principles of rehabilitation programs. Enhancement of previously learned therapeutic exercise techniques and integration of therapeutic modalities and therapeutic exercise, including objective and functional goal setting and evaluation for appropriate progression and expedited return to activity.
prereq_raw: KRS 617 and KRS 618 or basic therapeutic exercise and therapeutic modalities courses, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Athletic Training Capstone Experience
description: Capstone culminating experience preparing the student for the computer-based BOC Exam and for a career in athletic training. Follows the students’ didactic and clinical preparation in the 12 competency areas of athletic training.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Administration in Kinesiology
description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Community Counseling
description: Philosophy, organization, and function of community service agencies, programs, and institutions as related to professional work in counseling.

subject: KRS
title: Introduction to Practicum
description: Theory and techniques of counseling as preparation for practicum and internship. Emphasis on counseling relationships and basic skill development. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

subject: KRS
title: Career Development and Vocational Counseling
description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.

subject: KRS
title: Research and Evaluation in Counseling
description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in counseling and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.

subject: KRS
title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.
prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and KRS 606 / EDEP 635 , and consent.

subject: KRS
title: Assessment and Appraisals in Counseling
description: Assessment methods and tools for evaluating aptitudes, achievements, and interests. Applications to educational, instructional, and career counseling.

subject: KRS
title: School Counseling Approaches to Transition and Adjustment
description: Principles of behavior affecting interpersonal relationships in school with emphasis on application to actual situations.

subject: KRS
title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.

subject: KRS
title: Trauma and Crisis Counseling
description: Crisis intervention strategies and counseling skills for schools. Trauma-informed approaches for crises like suicide and violence. Focus on age-appropriate interventions, resilience, and school collaboration.

subject: KRS
title: Inclusive Physical Activity
description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

subject: KRS
title: Elementary Physical Education
description: Content and pedagogy for teaching preschool/elementary physical education. Students will learn appropriate content and pedagogy for learners in elementary school. Bit teaching and field experiences are included.

subject: KRS
title: Theory and Assessment of Personality
description: Personality testing; practice in administration and use of personality assessment; examination of psychometric and social issues.

subject: KRS
title: Multicultural Counseling
description: Significance of cultural factors in counseling relationships, delivery of counseling services in multicultural settings with attention to Hawaiʻi. Emphasis on process of cultural learning and implications for counselor roles and functions.

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Physical Activity
description: Trends, research, and problems related to physical activity across the lifespan. A variety of topics and contexts will be addressed. Enrolled in KRS graduate program only.

subject: KRS
title: Seminar: Health/Exercise Science
description: Review of selected current literature in exercise/sport science and leisure studies. Practice of presentation in group setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Training majors only.

subject: KRS
title: Secondary Physical Education
description: Detailed examination of effective physical education curriculum and instruction in middle and high schools.

subject: KRS
title: American College Student
description: Study of psychosocial characteristics of American college students and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work.

subject: KRS
title: Social Emotional Learning (SEL) Pedagogy and Practice
description: Introduces concepts, theories, and pedagogies of Social Emotional Learning (SEL), health and wellness, and trauma informed teaching with an emphasis on culture, social justice, and equity in Hawaiʻi and our global community.

subject: KRS
title: Sexuality & Health
description: Examines concepts, theories, and skills-based practices of sexuality and health. Topics on underserved populations, disability, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Utilizes research-based curriculum/strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

subject: KRS
title: Marriage, Family, and Child Counseling
description: Theory/practice of marriage, family, and child counseling, including major model in clinical practice; supervised counseling project by each student. Liability insurance required.

subject: KRS
title: Biomechanics of Human Motion
description: Principles of motion as applied to sport and physical rehabilitation. Introduction to the technology used in the analysis of motion.

subject: KRS
title: Physiology of Exercise
description: Physiological bases of modern physical training methods and sports science.

subject: KRS
title: Metabolic Analysis
description: Theory and practice of metabolic analysis of human performance examining each of the power systems used in energy production during exercise and how to use this information to prescribe exercise programs.

subject: KRS
title: Advanced Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription
description: Provides knowledge of field and laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of testing results and individual exercise program/prescription techniques.

subject: KRS
title: Body Composition and Weight Management
description: Analysis of the theory and practice used in the assessment of body composition and human physique. Includes strategies for implementing changes in body composition.

subject: KRS
title: Consultation: Theory and Practice
description: Consultation in educational, business, health, community, and human services agencies.

subject: KRS
title: Research Methods in KRS
description: The use of experimental designs/models in physical education research with emphasis on understanding the concepts, applications, and interpretations of statistical analysis.

subject: KRS
title: Assessment in Physical Activity
description: Overview of assessment purposes, types, practices and procedures used in physical education for those with disabilities. Frequently used motor assessments and practices in collection of data will be specifically addressed.

subject: KRS
title: Transdisciplinary Approach to Teaching the Motor Domain
description: Highlights a transdisciplinary approach for effectively teaching students with disabilities in the motor domain. Important characteristics and components of this approach will be shared. Strategies for its implementation will also be addressed.

subject: KRS
title: Principles and Practice of Rehabilitation Counseling
description: Principles, practices of rehabilitation counseling; review of history and influence of legislation on vocational rehabilitation; current issues, developments, with emphasis on local situation.

subject: KRS
title: Medical and Psychosocial Aspects of Disability
description: Functional implications of chronic illnesses and disabilities on psychological, social and vocational areas of an individuals life. Case studies and presentations will stimulate discussion and help students to apply theoretical information into practical everyday context.

subject: KRS
title: Case Management in Rehabilitation
description: Knowledge and skills required in case and case-load management in public as well as private sector rehabilitation sites. Emphasis on professional/client relationship, interviewing process, decision-making, goal-setting, recording/documentation, time management, and other tasks.

subject: KRS
title: Psychopathology in Counseling
description: Discussion-oriented course (potentially Web-based). Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues.

subject: KRS
title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Counseling
description: Developing ethical reasoning capabilities for resolution of ethical dilemmas likely to be encountered in counseling, psychology, and specialty practices (e.g., community, rehabilitation, school, mental health, alcohol and substance abuse, marriage and family counseling, and the like).

subject: KRS
title: Vocational Evaluation and Assessment in Rehabilitation
description: Theory, process, and techniques of vocational evaluation and assessment. Assessment methods and processes as they relate to vocational choice and adjustment of special groups.

subject: KRS
title: Assistive Technology in Rehabilitation Counseling
description: Study of application of assistive technologies to enhance the lives of people with disabilities. Case studies provide the vehicle in guiding students toward integration of available information into reality of actual situations. Special emphasis on the importance of using a consumer-centered approach in providing assistive technology services.

subject: KRS
title: Theory and Techniques of Job Placement
description: Theory, process, and techniques of job readiness, job development, and job placement.

subject: KRS
title: Promoting Physical Activity
description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

subject: KRS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individual reading and/or research.
prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair.

subject: KRS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: KRS
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Counseling
description: Supervised clinical or school counseling experience at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.
prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

prereq_raw: KRS 626 / EDEP 637 or KRS 683 / EDEP 650 , and consent.

subject: KRS
title: Contemporary Issues in Counseling
description: Current issues and problems. (Meets EdD common required elective.)

subject: KRS
title: (Alpha) Internship I
description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. title: Internship I: rehabilitation
description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

description: Supervised post-practicum experience in clinical rehabilitation or school counseling at an approved site, including a weekly class meeting. Provides advanced practical application of formal academic training. (C) community service; (E) elementary; (H) secondary; (R) rehabilitation; (U) college.

title: Seminar in School Counseling
description: In-depth study of professional concerns in school counseling.

description: In-depth study of professional concerns in community counseling.

subject: KRS

subject: KRS
title: Doctoral Seminar and Research I in Kinesiology
description: Will expose the PhD student to the basic nature of behavioral and somatic science research. Learning experiences will consist of journal review, laboratory/field techniques, and subject or data collector exposures as directed by faculty mentors.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits.

subject: KRS
title: Doctoral Seminar and Research II in Kinesiology
description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to be involved in research, under the direction of the faculty mentor, as the assistant project director and as the project director for pilot studies. Student will gain experience in these roles with close supervision by the faculty mentor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits.

subject: KRS
title: Doctoral Seminar and Research III in Kinesiology
description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to assume the role of director of a research project under the supervision of the faculty mentor. The research project will represent a piece of the ongoing line of research of the faculty mentor. Responsibilities will be comparable of a project director of research funded by a research grant.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: one time, up to six credits.

subject: KRS
title: Doctoral Seminar IV in Kinesiology
description: Designed to enable PhD students to gain a perspective of the discipline, both historically and philosophically, prepare them for the issues they may face in the real world, particularly higher education and help them initiate their dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: KRS majors only.
repeatable_raw: one time, up to six credits.

subject: KRS
title: Seminar in Rehabilitation Counseling
description: In-depth study of professional concerns in rehabilitation counseling.

subject: LAIS
title: Islands/Islas/Ilhas and Global Exchange
description: Cross-cultural study of global issues of navigation, commerce, and the environment, as expressed by the arts, traditions, and narratives from 1492 to the present. Connections with Europe, Africa, Americas, Asia, Oceania.

subject: LAIS
title: Vaqueros, Gauchos, Paniolo: Cowboy Legacies of the Americas and Hawaiʻi
description: Histories and traditions (literature, music, dance, poetry, food, fashion) of the Hispanic cowboy, Americas to Hawaiʻi. Examines symbolic interpretations of the vaquero concerning nation and identity, and the material consequences of ranching (colonialism, commerce, environment). Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Chocolate Tales & Culinary Cultures: Latin America to Hawaiʻi
description: Traces evolution of uses, meanings, and cultural representations of chocolate and other food native to Latin America. Emphasis on how narratives of food and food practices engage with national, ethnic, social, and gender identity constructions. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: (Alpha) Studies in Culture
description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Studies in Culture: Latin America
description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Studies in Culture: Iberian Peninsula
description: Politics of culture and representation. Will consider issues, traditions, movements, texts, and cultural icons for their significance for national and regional identity formation, intercultural relations and global flows of images, people, and capital. (B) Latin America; (C) Iberian Peninsula.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: U.S. Latino Culture and Literature
description: The culture and history of U.S. Latinos through an analysis of their literature and arts and their sociopolitical relationship to the U.S. mainstream culture.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Spanish Film
description: A chronological survey of films from Spain, from the Silent Era to the present. Conceptually, a cultural history of Spain in the 20th century, as seen through films.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Latin American Film
description: A survey of films from Latin America, the Silent Era to the present, and their representation of the cultural history of the region. Develops written communication skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Households in Cross-Cultural Perspectives: Home, Hale, Casa
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LAIS
title: (Alpha) Indigenous Peoples of Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Mesoamerica
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Indigenous Peoples of Latin America: Andean South America
description: Survey of the history and culture of the indigenous peoples of Latin America through a study of their literature, texts and practices. (B) Mesoamerica; (C) Andean South America.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Studies in Culture: Portugal and Brazil
description: Surveys the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world from pre-Lusitanian times, including connections with Africa, Asia, the U.S., and Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Asians and Pacific Islanders in Latin America
description: Survey of the history and culture of Asian, Polynesian, and Pacific Islander communities in Latin America. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LAIS
title: Colonial Latin American History
description: Pre-Columbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

subject: LAIS
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

subject: LAIS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies
description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture.
prereq_raw: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380 , and SPAN 351 , and SPAN 352 ; or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies: Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama
description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture.
prereq_raw: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380 , and SPAN 351 , and SPAN 352 ; or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Topics in Latin American and Iberian Studies: Luso-Hispanic pop culture
description: Combined lecture-discussion on political, social, cultural themes of Iberia and Latin America; (B) Aztlán, Quetzalcóatl, Pachamama; (C) Luso-Hispanic pop culture.
prereq_raw: LAIS 360 or LAIS 363 or LAIS 368 or LAIS 372 or LAIS 380 , and SPAN 351 , and SPAN 352 ; or consent.

subject: LAIS
title: Hispanic Cultural Studies
description: Critical overview of contemporary theories on Hispanic culture. Issues of identity such as mestizaje, hybridity, and pluralism will be discussed from a hemispheric perspective.

subject: LATN
title: Elementary Latin
description: Grammar and vocabulary, with reading of simple Latin.

subject: LATN
title: Elementary Latin
description: Continuation of LATN 101 .

subject: LATN
title: Intermediate Latin
description: Development of reading and translation skills. Emphasis on prose.

subject: LATN
title: Intermediate Latin
description: Continuation of LATN 201 : emphasis on poetry.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Historians
description: Selections from Caesar, Sallust, and others.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Epic
description: Selections from Virgil, Ovid, and others.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Philosophy
description: Selections from Lucretius, Cicero, and Seneca.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Drama
description: Selections from Plautus, Terence, and Seneca.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Lyric
description: Selections from Catullus, Horace, and others.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Novel
description: Selections from Petronius and Apuleius.

subject: LATN
title: Roman Satire
description: Selections from Horace and Juvenal.

subject: LATN
title: Seminar in Roman Studies
description: Study of an author or phase in Roman studies.
prereq_raw: any two 300-level LATN courses, or consent.

subject: LAW
title: Exchange Student Program
description: Designed for students accepted to participate in an exchange program while enrolled at William S. Richardson School of Law. Must obtain prior approval for the transfer credits.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Organizing for Social Change
description: Examines conditions that lead people to become active, self-governing agents. Covered are strategies and tactics of organizers, history of social change movements, anti-subordination theories of justice and organizing case studies.

subject: LAW
title: Historic Preservation Law
description: Introduction to the protection of cultural, archaeological, and historical resources with emphasis on key federal and state laws.

subject: LAW
title: Lawyering Fundamentals I
description: Comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces students to legal problem solving and writing through the types of documents lawyers prepare in practice.

subject: LAW
title: Lawyering Fundamentals II
description: A comprehensive program that teaches students the analytical and presentational skills necessary for excellent legal writing. Introduces skills and strategies for preparing written legal arguments and oral advocacy.

subject: LAW
title: Contracts
description: Law of private agreements. Focuses on common law doctrines with some attention to key Uniform Commercial Code provisions. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, defenses to enforcement, contract interpretation, breach, and remedies.

subject: LAW
title: Employment Discrimination
description: A study of the law of employment discrimination.

subject: LAW
title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice- negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

subject: LAW
title: Contracts I
description: Law of private agreements. Explores the evolution and application of common law doctrines, and, where applicable, relevant provisions of the Uniform Commercial Code. Examines the bases of promissory liability, contract formation, mutual assent, defenses to enforcement, excuses, remedies and damages, and the rights and interests of third parties. Attention will be paid throughout the course to the role of contracts in a market society and the conflicting interests of certainty, freedom of contract and fairness.

subject: LAW
title: Contracts II
description: Continuation of LAW 509 . Topics include defenses to enforcement, performance and breach, and remedies.
prereq_raw: LAW 509 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Professional Responsibility
description: Introductory consideration of selected topics relating to functions, structure, and responsibilities of the legal profession and its future role in society.

subject: LAW
title: Reparations and Reconciliation
description: Seminar addresses a legally and socially important contemporary issue-healing present-day wounds of historic injustice. Considers how to repair the continuing social damage of injustice.

subject: LAW
title: Criminal Law
description: Examination of substantive rules, enforcement procedures, and rationales of criminal law in the U.S.

subject: LAW
title: Children, Parents and the Law
description: Exploration of fundamental concepts of law relating to children, ethical issues, and the role of lawyers in assisting children, and how the child’s rights and obligations are balanced with those of parents and state.

subject: LAW
title: Business Reorganization in Bankruptcy
description: Examination of the rights and remedies available to a failing business and its creditors when the business seeks to reorganize its business and financial affairs under chapter 11 of the federal bankruptcy code. The course is structured as a “practicum,” which tracks a single business through restructuring and emphasizes the practical and strategic aspects of lawyering. Recommended: LAW 562 .

subject: LAW
title: Civil Procedure I
description: Study of pre-trial, trial, and appellate procedures in the federal and Hawaiʻi courts.

subject: LAW
title: Civil Procedure II
description: Building upon the principles of LAW 516 , continues the study of pre-trial, trial, and appellate procedures in the federal and Hawaiʻi courts.
prereq_raw: LAW 516 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Real Property I
description: Basic course in property ownership, development, regulation. Emphasis on theory.

subject: LAW
title: Real Property II
description: Contract of sale, equitable conversion, deed.
prereq_raw: LAW 518 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Law, Aging and Medicine
description: Introduction to basic legal issues at the intersection of law, aging and medicine. Addresses various issues confronting elderly; issues confronting the general population including health care financing, decision-making, and bioethics.

subject: LAW
title: Torts
description: Torts cover the statutory and common law of negligence, causation, defenses, damages, strict liability, intentional torts and tort policy and reform, with emphasis on national and Hawaiʻi law.

subject: LAW
title: Law and Psychology
description: Approaches psychology as a problem solving tool that can facilitate legal analysis. Covers a variety of areas including jury decision-making, research methodology, social cognition, culture, and behavioral economics, among others.

subject: LAW
title: Advanced Torts and Insurance Law
description: Advanced study of several areas of tort law and an introduction to insurance law and policy. This course is of considerable importance to students interested in civil litigation and personal injury law. Recent important developments in Hawaiʻi tort and insurance law will be included.
prereq_raw: LAW 522 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Legislation and Statutory Interpretation
description: The interrelationship between the legislative and judicial branches of government is explored through a review of Federal and Hawaiʻi law-making processes, direct democracy, legislative drafting, and theories of the legislative process and statutory interpretation.

subject: LAW
title: Group Directed Study
description: Designed for maximum flexibility, this course allows a professor to work with a small number of students on a reading/ discussion project of mutual interest.

subject: LAW
title: Federal Indian Law
description: Examines Federal Indian Law, including fundamental concepts and the historical evolution of legal doctrines. Considers the implications of Native Hawaiian sovereignty within the framework of Federal Indian Law.

subject: LAW
title: Second-Year Seminar
description: Seminar required for spring semester of all second-year law students. Substantial paper required. Topics announced in previous fall semester. Placement by lottery.

subject: LAW
title: Business Associations
description: After a brief survey of agency, partnerships, and other forms of business organization, the course will cover the fundamentals of corporations, and securities regulation, including disregarding the corporate entity, management and control of closely held corporations, merger, liability under the federal securities laws, takeovers, public registration, exemptions, and derivative suits.

subject: LAW
title: Health Law
description: Introduction to medical jurisprudence, medical malpractice, informed consent, health care decisions, medical ethics, the health care industry, managed care, financing health care, and the role of government in health care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only; NURS DNP majors only

subject: LAW
title: Constitutional Law I
description: Introduction to judicial function in constitutional cases, jurisdiction of the U.S. Supreme Court, and discretionary barriers to judicial review.

subject: LAW
title: Constitutional Law II
description: Advanced course in constitutional law with special emphasis on rights secured by the First, Fifth, and Fourteenth Amendments to the Constitution of the U.S.
prereq_raw: LAW 533 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Intellectual Property
description: A study of the law relating to property rights resulting from intellectual effort, including patents, copyright, trademarks, and trade secrets.

subject: LAW
title: Conflict of Laws
description: Problems respecting the law applicable in transactions or to relationships with elements in more than one state.

subject: LAW
title: Remedies
description: Examines both practice aspects and theoretical underpinnings of equitable remedies. Frequently, compensatory damages cannot adequately protect clients or provide them with the relief they need. Topics include temporary restraining orders, preliminary and permanent injunctions, restitution and unjust enrichment, specific performance, and equitable defenses such as unclean hands, laches, and estoppel. Practice issues concerning appeal, jury trials, and the relationship of equity to law are also explored.

subject: LAW
title: Contract Drafting
description: Hands-on workshop class in drafting contracts, agreement, and similar documents for commercial/business purposes.
prereq_raw: LAW 506 , or LAW 509 and LAW 510 , with a minimum grade of C-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

children.text: with a minimum grade of C-

subject: LAW
title: Criminal Procedure
description: Issues of free press and fair trial, illegal search and seizure, arrest and confession, speedy trial, double jeopardy are covered through student interactions as defense or prosecution attorneys and as judges.

subject: LAW
title: Advanced Civil Procedure
description: Addresses various aspects of complex litigation and recent criticism of the civil litigation system itself. Theoretical in emphasis.
prereq_raw: LAW 516 and LAW 517 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: Evidence
description: “Objection, your Honor!” This course examines the rules of evidence that govern trials in both federal and Hawaiʻi courts and will focus on such topics as hearsay, witness examination, impeachment, physical and demonstrative evidence, expert testimony, writings, relevance, judicial notice, and presumptions.

subject: LAW
title: Race, Culture, and Law
description: U.S. cases and legal theory emphasizing law in the social construction of racial categories, shifts in race-based anti-discrimination law, and the interaction of culture and law in judicial decision-making.

subject: LAW
title: Licensing Intellectual Property
description: Theory and practice of the law relating to the transfer of rights in information and other intangibles are examined together with end user license agreements and the structure and negotiation of upstream licensing mechanisms.

subject: LAW
title: (Alpha) Intercession-J Term
description: January term provides students the opportunity to explore contemporary legal topics with national and international experts. (B) alternative dispute resolution; (C) rule of law; (D) law practice; (E) diversity; (F) access to justice; (G) public law; (H) legal theory; (I) legal practice; (J) rights.

subject: LAW
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

subject: LAW
title: Immigration Law
description: Introduction to U.S. Immigration and Nationality Law: a brief overview of historical development of immigration law; analysis of exclusion and deportation grounds and remedies; the study of both immigrant and nonimmigrant visa applications and petitions. Current law on asylum and refugee applications and U.S. citizenship and naturalization requirements.

subject: LAW
title: Admiralty Law
description: Introduction to U.S. maritime law and admiralty jurisdiction emphasizing development of rules of maritime law and rights of seamen and maritime workers.

subject: LAW
title: Corporate and Partnership Taxation
description: Examines tax aspects of formation, operation, reorganization, and liquidation of partnerships and corporations.

subject: LAW
title: Trusts and Estates
description: Deals primarily with the disposition of family wealth including: the making of wills; the creation, enforcement, administration, and termination of trusts; and intestate succession, including probate.

subject: LAW
title: E-Discovery
description: Surveys the relevant law, theory, and practice governing the review and production of electronically stored information, focusing on the rules of civil procedure, the rules of evidence, and case law.
prereq_raw: LAW 516 and LAW 517 with a minimum grade of C-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Secured Transactions
description: Introduction to Uniform Commercial Code, particularly Article 9- reducing risk of nonpayment by obtaining an interest in borrowers’ property.

subject: LAW
title: (Alpha) Externship
description: Legal work for judges and attorney supervisors in public agencies, private law firms, and the legislature. (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) outside Hawaiʻi.

subject: LAW
title: Externship: Hawaiʻi
description: Legal work for judges and attorney supervisors in public agencies, private law firms, and the legislature. (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) outside Hawaiʻi.

subject: LAW
title: Externship: outside Hawaiʻi
description: Legal work for judges and attorney supervisors in public agencies, private law firms, and the legislature. (H) Hawaiʻi; (P) outside Hawaiʻi.

subject: LAW
title: Corporate Finance
description: Provides an understanding of the basic financial concepts and tools for lawyers with transactional practices, preferred stock, common stock and convertible securities.

subject: LAW
title: Labor Law I
description: Regulation of union-management relations under state and federal laws.

subject: LAW
title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 531 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

subject: LAW
title: Administrative Law
description: Procedure and remedies for resolving controversies between citizens and government officials exercising administrative power.

subject: LAW
title: Debtors’ and Creditors’ Rights
description: Bankruptcy laws and rules, laws of liens, receiverships.

subject: LAW
title: Trial Practice
description: Examination of sequential stages of pre-trial and trial practice in a problem setting. Topics include investigation, pleadings, motions, discovery, voir dire examination, opening statements, direct and cross examination, closing argument, selected evidentiary problems, post-trial motions, and appellate practice. Students engage in simulated exercises, and their work is critiqued.

subject: LAW
title: Pre-Trial Litigation
description: Theory and practice of civil pre-trial litigation with focus on pleading, discovery, and pre-trial motions.

subject: LAW
title: Non-Profit Organizations
description: Examines the meaning, scope, and role of non-profit organizations in contemporary society, and focuses on selected non-tax laws and primary tax issues relevant to non-profits. Recommended: LAW 531 and LAW 567 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law students only.

subject: LAW
title: Federal Income Taxation
description: Surveys the entire federal income tax system, with emphasis on those areas of greatest importance to non-tax lawyers. Students are expected to develop proficiency in the use of the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury Regulations.

subject: LAW
title: Family Law
description: Legal forms of-and responses to-formation, maintenance, and dissolution of the family. Marriage, annulment, divorce, alimony, separation agreements, child custody and adoption, parentage.

subject: LAW
title: Federal Courts
description: An examination of the jurisdiction and law-making powers of the federal courts, standing issues, appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, federal-question and diversity-of-citizenship jurisdiction of the federal district courts, immunities from suit in the federal courts possessed by governmental entities and officers, intervention by federal courts in state proceedings, and choice of law in the federal courts. Particular emphasis on relevant Federal Rules of Civil Procedure.
prereq_raw: LAW 533 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: LAW
title: International Protection of Human Rights
description: The growing body of international human rights laws, including procedural law and role of nongovernmental organizations.

subject: LAW
title: Jurisprudence
description: Relationships between the concepts of law and morality with views of legal and moral philosophers.

subject: LAW
title: State and Local Government Law and Finance
description: City, town, county, district governments: administrative organization; regulatory powers; police power; local governmental taxation; relationship between local, state, and federal government.

subject: LAW
title: Advanced Legal Analysis
description: Designed to help students enhance their legal writing and analysis skills as law students, bar examinees, and legal professionals.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Artificial Intelligence and Social Justice
description: Introduces you to and engages you directly in the study of artificial intelligence, legislation and regulation, and social justice in a variety of application contexts.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Introduction to Space Law & Policy
description: Acquaints students with the fundamental principles of space law and policy, including the pre- and post-Sputnik history of space exploration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Land Use Management and Control
description: Survey course of public land use management.

subject: LAW
title: Advanced Immigration Law & Policy
description: Current immigration policy developments as a window into the way law, both legislated and case-law driven, interacts with policy objectives to produce desirable as well as unanticipated outcomes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Real Estate Development and Financing
description: Federal and state laws in the practice of real estate development and financing law. Condominium, securities, subdivision, consumer protection, and mortgage areas.

subject: LAW
title: Civil Rights
description: Focuses on the civil rights of Americans and introduces alternative remedies and procedures for securing these rights.

subject: LAW
title: Refugees, Asylum & Forced Migration
description: Based on international agreements, implemented through domestic federal statutory law, and administered by Executive Branch agencies who are subject to judicial review, creating a rich context for legal learning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Extended Bar Review I
description: Provides students with critical skills for success on the bar exam, specifically, MBE and MEE question practice and review of highly tested topics in Civil Procedure, Criminal Law and Procedure, and Real Property.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Extended Bar Review II
description: Provides students with critical skills for success on the bar exam, specifically, MBE and MEE question practice and review of highly tested topics in Contracts, Evidence, and Torts.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Labor and Employment Law
description: Employment law, statutory rights affecting the employment relation, and alternative contract provisions to secure the parties’ intentions. Focus on the practical application of labor and employment law. Materials relating to the unionized employment relationship. Emphasis on the labor arbitration process and possibly, to issues regarding internal union affairs.

subject: LAW
title: Integrity and Ethics in the Real World
description: Interactive course addressing important topical ethical issues in areas including the corporate, entertainment, medical, legal, political, education, and sports worlds. Renowned knowledgeable guests will discuss critical issues in their respective fields through panel conversations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LAW
title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle.

subject: LAW
title: Directed Study and Research
description: Individual research and writing under the direction of faculty.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to the Study of Language
description: Non-formal introduction to language, emphasizing the everyday use of language, its relevance to contemporary issues in society, and local language issues. Content studied through lecture, readings, and writing; emphasis on writing as a grading criterion.

subject: LING
title: Language and Symbolic Reasoning
description: Introduction to language as a formal symbolic system and to the techniques of analysis and reasoning that reveal its workings.

subject: LING
title: Language Endangerment, Globalization, and Indigenous Peoples
description: Focus on language endangerment and globalization. Students are introduced to case studies on language endangerment from around the world and throughout history. Offered through the distance-learning Unit Mastery program.

subject: LING
title: Language as a Window to the Mind
description: Introduction to language-related phenomena, which gives insight into the organization of the human mind. Combines lecture, discussion and group projects.

subject: LING
title: Logic and Language
description: Introduces logic as a way of understanding the meanings of everyday words and sentences, as well as the inferences that humans draw from them. Topics include propositional logic, first-order logic, elementary set theory, and relations.

subject: LING
title: Language and AI: A Basic Introduction
description: This non-mathematical introduction to language and language models critically investigates traditional versus AI-driven editing, translation, language learning, and linguistic research, exploring major and little-studied languages, dangers, ethical issues, future advances and likely limitations.

subject: LING
title: (Alpha) Language in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific
description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawaiʻi and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion.

subject: LING
title: Language in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific: unit mastery
description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawaiʻi and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion.

subject: LING
title: Language in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific: lecture discussion
description: Introduction to the study of language and language-related issues, with a focus on Hawaiʻi and the Pacific; (B) unit mastery; (C) lecture discussion with focus on writing as a grading criterion.

subject: LING
title: The Language of Children
description: Survey of findings about the child’s acquisition of language.

subject: LING
title: Language Documentation for Non- Linguists
description: Provides training in the fundamentals of language documentation and conservation for non-linguists.
prereq_raw: proficiency in a lesser studied language and consent.

children.text: proficiency in a lesser studied language

subject: LING
title: Bad Words
description: An examination of the link between language and society through the use and perception of taboo words.

subject: LING
title: General Linguistics
description: Introduction to the formal analysis of language, focusing on phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, semantics, historical linguistics, language acquisition, and related topics.

subject: LING
title: Computer Applications
description: Background; uses for machine translation, dictionary programs, speech synthesis, grammar modeling, etc.

subject: LING
title: Languages of the World
description: Survey of major language families; typological classification and language universals; writing systems, “contact” languages. Variety of grammatical structures illustrated by selected languages.

subject: LING
title: The Philippine Language Family
description: Introduction; phonological and grammatical systems; historical developments; emphasis on Filipino, Cebuano, and Ilokano.
prereq_raw: grade of B or better in LING 102 or LING 320 and experience with a Philippine language, or consent.

subject: LING
title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles.

subject: LING
title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in various communities. Explores how language policies, discourses, and ideologies shape people’s use of language. Emphasis on developing oral communication and written skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LING
title: Articulatory Phonetics
description: Intensive training in recognition, reproduction, and recording of human speech sounds; preparation for fieldwork with unrecorded languages and for clinical work in speech pathology.

subject: LING
title: Psycholinguistics
description: The mental processes involved in producing, understanding, and acquiring language. Students will conduct a small psycholinguistic experiment.
prereq_raw: one of LING 102 , LING 320 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

subject: LING
title: Language and Gender
description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

subject: LING
title: Language as a Public Concern
description: How does language serve as a proxy for larger social questions? Focuses on four main themes: language revitalization, discrimination on the basis of accent, gender miscommunication and the English Only Movement.

subject: LING
title: Language Endangerment and Revitalization
description: An overview of language endangerment, especially in the Pacific and Asia, and a critical examination of the strategies that are being developed to combat it.
prereq_raw: one of LING 102 , LING 150B , LING 150C , LING 105 , LING 320 , SLS 150 , SLS 301 , or consent.

subject: LING
title: Raciolinguistics
description: Theory and applications of critical race studies, ethnic studies, and linguistic anthropology as they pertain to the science of language, language behavior, language attitudes, and language in the public sphere.

subject: LING
title: Morphology
description: Theory of word structure; analysis of a variety of morphological types.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Phonological Analysis
description: Phonological analysis and theory.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Grammatical Analysis
description: Syntactic analysis and grammatical theory.

subject: LING
title: Cognitive Linguistics
description: Conceptual systems and language from a cognitive science perspective. Linguistic evidence on conceptual structure, reasoning, categorization, and understanding.
prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: LING
title: Animal Communication
description: Investigates animal communication from the perspective of modern linguistics. Dispels common misconceptions about “talking animals” and shows how the cognitive, biological, and environmental needs and opportunities of animals determine what and how they communicate.

subject: LING
title: Computational Modeling
description: Hands-on introduction to modeling language. Focuses on connectionism, relations between language perception, and motor control. Requires no programming experience.
prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: LING
title: Topics in Linguistics
description: Variable topics in special areas of Linguistics, depending on instructor interest.

subject: LING
title: Meaning
description: Theories of how literal and figurative language encode meaning and processes of meaning encoding and decoding.
prereq_raw: LING 102 , LING 320 , ICS 111 , or PSY 100 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: LING
title: Polynesian Language Family
description: Introduction to the language family of Hawaiian, Samoan, Tahitian, Tongan, etc.; models of migration and settlement and linguistic evidence; subgrouping and reconstruction of Proto-Polynesian; linguistic characteristics of present-day languages; language endangerment and conservation in Polynesia.
prereq_raw: LING 320 with a grade of B or better, or consent.

subject: LING
title: Induction of Linguistic Structure
description: Phonological and grammatical structures of a previously uncodified language are determined by linguistic analysis of data obtained from speakers of the language.

subject: LING
title: Children’s Speech
description: Child language acquisition, language milestones, multilingualism. Relation of cognitive development to language development. Emphasis on developing research skills, with an emphasis on written communication.

subject: LING
title: Acoustic and Auditory Phonetics
description: Principles of acoustics and audition as they relate to speech sounds, use of computer-based analysis tools to investigate acoustic properties of speech.

subject: LING
title: The Nature of Language
description: Language as a communication system, current theories of grammar, meaning, sociolinguistics, linguistic change and comparison.

subject: LING
title: Language Acquisition and Language Revitalization
description: Provides training relevant to the study and revitalization of heritage languages and endangered languages.

subject: LING
title: Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Introduction to data science for linguistic research.

subject: LING
title: Practical Exercises in Data Science for Linguistic Research
description: Exercises in data science for linguistic research.

subject: LING
title: Phonology
description: Phonological theory and problems of analysis.

subject: LING
title: Grammar
description: Grammatical theory and problems of analysis.

subject: LING
title: Semantics and Pragmatics
description: Ways in which the interpretation of sentences in natural language depends upon the literal meaning of propositions and their logical (semantic) and conversational (pragmatic) inferences.

subject: LING
title: Discourse and Grammar
description: Usage-based examination of grammar in the context of spontaneous spoken language, including the role of discourse on synchronic and diachronic grammatical structure, discourse in interaction, and discourse in language documentation.

subject: LING
title: Language Data Processing
description: Preparation of language data for computer processing; use readymade programs; write simple language processing programs using SNOBOL4. Applications to student’s research.

subject: LING
title: Laboratory and Quantitative Research Methods
description: Laboratory and quantitative methods for research on language. Introduction to hardware, software, research designs, and basic analysis techniques commonly used in quantitative language research. Combines lecture, laboratory work ,and discussion.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: LING
title: Linguistics of Sign Languages
description: Universals and uniqueness in the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures of sign languages, taught inductively with emphasis on hands-on analysis. Opportunities exist for skills development in American or Ho Chi Minh City sign languages.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LING
title: Hawaiʻi Sign Language Linguistics: Documentation, Conservation, and Revitalization of HSL
description: Descriptive information on the phonological, morphological, and syntactic structures and lexicon of Hawaiʻi Sign Language (HSL); language skills development in HSL; and guided research related to the documentation, conservation, and revitalization of HSL.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LING
title: (Alpha) Topics in Linguistics
description: History of the discipline, schools of linguistic thought, current issues, etc.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times. (E) English linguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (H) history of the discipline; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.
