subject: LING
title: Professionalism in Linguistics
description: Topics related to career development and professional/scholarly communication in linguistics, including CVs, abstracts, grant proposals, publications, conference planning. Topics vary by instructor.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Historical Linguistics
description: Introduction to historical-comparative linguistics; attention to both Indo-European and languages with few or no written records.

subject: LING
title: Issues in Historical Linguistics
description: Continuation of LING 645 . Addresses advanced topics in historical linguistics that have generated controversy rather than consensus.

subject: LING
title: Developmental Linguistics
description: Survey of the literature in language acquisition; emphasis on relation to linguistic theory.

subject: LING
title: Introduction to Language Documentation
description: Covers history, method, and theory behind language documentation, and the role of language endangerment in the field. Discussion on skills required to undertake documentation; topics may vary depending on the emphases of the instructor.

subject: LING
title: Techniques of Language Documentation
description: Students learn to conduct best-practice digital language documentation projects, from equipment purchase to data collection to data annotation to archiving and presentation.

subject: LING
title: Field Methods
description: Work with native speakers of lesser-known languages to develop techniques for data collection and analysis.
prereq_raw: LING 421 and LING 422 and one of LING 621 or LING 622 ; or consent.

subject: LING
title: Advanced Field Methods
description: Advanced training in linguistic fieldwork and language documentation through first-hand work with a speaker of a non-dominant language.

subject: LING
title: Directed Research
description: CR/NC only.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, up to 6 credit hours.

subject: LING
title: Language Typology
description: Language typology deals with how and why the elements of language interact and function. Students acquire a broad overview of this grammatical make-up of languages in general and understanding of Functional-Typological linguistics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LING
title: Advanced Laboratory Research
description: Advanced laboratory methods for research in linguistics. Specialized and/or advanced uses of hardware, software, research designs, and analysis techniques. Specific topic varies: check with department. Combines lecture, laboratory work and discussion.

subject: LING
title: (Alpha) Seminar
description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

title: Seminar: psycholinguistics
description: Reporting and discussion of current research in linguistics. (E) ethnolinguistics; (F) phonology and phonetics; (G) general; (M) semantics; (Q) language acquisition; (R) written language; (S) sociolinguistics; (X) syntax; (Y) psycholinguistics.

subject: LING
title: Areal Linguistics
description: Structures of languages of various areas of the world; diffusion.

subject: LING
title: Apprenticeship in Teaching Linguistics
description: Experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation.
prereq_raw: admission to doctoral program and consent.

subject: LIS
title: Think Critically, Click Wisely in the Digital Era: Information, Media and News Literacy
description: Practice skills to evaluate information, media, and news critically, distinguishing between credible sources and misinformation. Develop essential competencies for navigating today’s digital landscape and fostering a well-informed, democratic society.

subject: LIS
title: The Information Environment
description: Investigates how information flows in society, providing a critical perspective on how technologies shape knowledge, experience and memory.

subject: LIS
title: Library and Information Studies Workshop
description: Designed for in-service librarians and other information specialists needing to update their professional skills, focus on a particular topic, or learn new approaches and concepts.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable for credit. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Reference and Information Services
description: Philosophy, principles, and practice of reference services in libraries, information centers and information literacy. Bibliographic control, reference research, reference interview, online searching, evaluation of bibliographic and Webliographic material. Field component. MLISc degree required course.

subject: LIS
title: Resource Discovery
description: Techniques and strategies for discovery of information resources from professional online databases and the Web. Query formulation and use of advanced functions to match retrieved resources with user needs for research and reference work.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Metadata Creation for Information Organization
description: Theory and practice of metadata creation for organization of information resources, cataloging code for resource description and access, Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal Classification schemes, use of OCLC.

subject: LIS
title: Foundations of the Information Professions
description: Lecture/discussion/survey of the information professions, development of professional identity, professional values and ethics, historical development, current issues in the information professions.

subject: LIS
title: Intellectual Freedom
description: Seminar surveying the core philosophical principles and practices of intellectual freedom with special application to librarianship and information sciences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LIS majors only.

subject: LIS
title: History of Information
description: History of the recording, preservation, and transmission of knowledge. Development of libraries and other information organizations as instruments of cultural transmission.

subject: LIS
title: Navigating Information Organizations
description: Principles of effective management of information organizations, with emphasis on organizational information flows, team skills, communication, planning, resource allocation, assessment, outreach, and advocacy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Collection Management
description: Principles and issues of collection management and care. Criteria and tools for selecting and deselecting materials. Relationships with publishers/producers.

subject: LIS
title: Preservation Management
description: Introduction to preservation management. Focus on management strategies for preservation of materials in libraries and archives. Covers preservation planning, condition surveys, disaster planning, grantsmanship, and basic issues relating to deterioration. LIS majors only.

subject: LIS
title: Community Engagement
description: Explores how information professionals in libraries and other settings collaborate with community members and organizations. Provides an overview of theory and practice emphasizing critical analysis of policies, services, and trends. Required course for CALIS.

subject: LIS
title: Introduction to Hawaiʻi and Pacific Librarianship
description: Overview of resources and issues concerning librarianship in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Islands. Reference strategies and materials to answer common research questions, collection development, and management issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Indigenous Librarianship
description: Development and delivery of information services with and for indigenous communities. Issues include cultural protocols, traditional knowledge organization and ethics of access.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Multicultural Resources for Diverse User Groups
description: Examines resources and materials targeted for diverse user populations in libraries and community organizations, locally and globally. Surveys issues and trends related to diversity initiatives affecting the publishing industry, libraries, and cultural institutions worldwide.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Traditional Literature and Oral Narration
description: Analysis of traditional literature including Asian and Pacific Island resources. Selection and evaluation of traditional literature emphasizing cultural values. Introduction to oral tradition, history and techniques of storytelling.

subject: LIS
title: Responding to Reading in Libraries
description: Research-intensive seminar that explores the reading process in library contexts and similar settings. Critical examination of ways in which library and literacy services impact reading engagement and interests of library users.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LIS majors only.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Librarianship
description: Lecture with demonstrations to introduce the essential types of digital resources and the software tools for finding high quality and relevant information efficiently from digital journal archives and reference databases.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories.

subject: LIS
title: Government Documents
description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.

subject: LIS
title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management, assessment, leadership, outreach, and advocacy.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Arrangement and Description
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope and content.

subject: LIS
title: Records, Archives and Memory
description: Introduction to records, archives, and memory including the global history and nature of records, archives, and the archival profession. Topics include cultural memory, ethics and values, tribal and indigenous records, archival theory, practice and perspectives.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Archives
description: The role of technology in archival theory and practice. Topics include digital preservation, authenticity assessment, arrangement and description, content management, and access systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Moving Image Archives
description: Principles and technologies of processing, preservation, and accessibility of archival audiovisual materials in moving image archives. Topics include moving image repositories, critical analysis of archival footage, format identification, digitization strategies, equipment, and vendor considerations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only

subject: LIS
title: Records Management
description: Management of records in all media formats. Selection of media format based on government and internal records requirements. Problems associated with electronic media such as legality and shelf life.

subject: LIS
title: Archival and Special Collections Management
description: Management of archives, manuscript collections, and special collections using approaches and best practices from archival studies. Topics include management theory, appraisal theory, facilities issues, privacy, intellectual property, records management, advocacy, fundraising, reference, and educational outreach.

subject: LIS
title: Archival Access, Representation and Use
description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope, and content. LIS majors only.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Informatics
description: Sociotechnical concepts and processes underlying information systems, services, and use.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Asian Informatics
description: Lecture/discussion on the transformative effects of information and communication technologies in East Asia. Topics include media, mobile devices, social media, publishing, e-government, and e-commerce.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Digital Instruction
description: Study and application of principles and practices that influence digital instruction related to information literacy in libraries and other information environments. Focus on application of instructional design and standards-based outcome assessment. Field research component.

subject: LIS
title: Technology for Libraries and Information Centers
description: Survey of theories, concepts, methods and practices relating to the application of information technology to support the administration and use of information resources. Includes digital, printed and audiovisual materials.

subject: LIS
title: Database Design and Creation
description: Designing and creating textual and/or directory databases from the viewpoint of information specialists and content providers. Needs analysis, file design, record content and structuring, software choice. Students implement prototype database.

subject: LIS
title: Creating Digital Libraries
description: Principles, techniques, and technologies supporting the creation of user-centered digital libraries. Selection, organization, maintenance, access, and retrieval of digital collections.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Human Dimension in Information Systems
description: Lecture/discussion on human element in information systems, including physical, cognitive and affective behavior in interaction with information systems. Information retrieval, human-computer interaction and cognitive science research, quantitative and qualitative research methods. Research component.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Children
description: History and criticism of children’s literature. Contemporary books and media. Trends in book publishing and media production. Developmental needs and interests of children. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Books and Media for Young Adults
description: History and criticism of literature for young adults. Contemporary books and media. Trends in media for young adults. Developmental needs and interests of adolescents. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

subject: LIS
title: Services in Public Libraries
description: Planning and implementing services and programming in public and school libraries. Trends, issues, networking, public relations, outreach, competencies, services for the disabled and other special groups.

subject: LIS
title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

subject: LIS
title: Internship
description: Field experience in library or information agency settings with supervision of professional librarians or information specialists. Available to classified students only. Selection based on academic advisor approval, application form, interview and possession of required competencies. Students must apply and be accepted before registration. Selection is by agency.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio and preparation for professional practice. Peer mentoring and student presentations. MLISc degree Plan B required course.

subject: LIS
title: Masters Seminar II
description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio or thesis. Peer mentoring, faculty, and student presentations. MLISc degree required course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Studies
description: Includes issues of topical interest in the information professions. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as services for specific groups and special collections. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times if course content is different.

subject: LIS
title: Special Topics in Information Technology
description: Includes issues of topical interest in information technology. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as digital archives, content management systems and informatics. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times if course content is different.

subject: LIS
title: Practicum School Librarianship
description: Skill development and application of academic study through observation and practice in a fieldwork program with accompanying seminar. Required for school library certification in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: 12 credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LIS majors only.

children.text: credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required

subject: LIS
title: Directed Reading and/or Research
description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Enrollment requires approval before end of previous semester, with specification of goals, work requirements, number of credits, rationale.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, credit earned up to 6 credits.

subject: LIS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: LIS
title: Seminar in International Librarianship
description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

subject: LLEA
title: Death and Dying in Literature and Film
description: Exploration of death and dying in literature and film as manifested across time and cultures throughout the world. Analysis of narratives from ancient times to the modern era from multiple theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

subject: LLEA
title: Directed Language Study
description: Study in European languages not taught regularly, depending on demand and staff.

subject: LLEA
title: Italian Film
description: Study of Italian film history and technique.

subject: LLEA
title: French Film
description: Study of French film history and technique.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: freshman standing.

subject: LLEA
title: Gods, Heroes, and Dragons: Germanic Myth, Legends, and Fairy Tales
description: Study of Germanic myth, legends, and fairy tales. Analysis of narratives from ancient times to the modern era from multiple theoretical perspectives.

subject: LLEA
title: French Culture for Americans
description: Study of the shared cultural and historical foundations of France and the U.S. both past and present.

subject: LLEA
title: Freaks and Monsters
description: Monsters, freaks and otherness in literature, film, history and medicine. Suitable for non-literature majors.

subject: LLEA
title: German Cinema
description: Study of German film history, film theory, film analysis, and film style.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing only.
repeatable_raw: 1 time or take GER 320 one time for different topics. 6 cr. limit on GER 320 /LLEA 320 courses.

subject: LLEA
title: Italian Literature as Film
description: Exploration of the distinction between literature and film as artistic genres as well as study of major works of literature in respect to the present, from the Middle Ages through the 20th century.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: French Literature Since 1800
description: Rapid reading in translation; lectures, discussions, reports.
prereq_raw: junior standing or one course in French language or literature.

subject: LLEA
title: French African Literature
description: Black African literature in French in 20th century. Major themes of negritude, national political unity, colonialism, traditional culture.
prereq_raw: junior standing or one course in French language or literature.

subject: LLEA
title: Topics in Italian Literature in Translation
description: Introduction to Italian literature in translation, with varying topics in different iterations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Love, Murder, and Greed in French Cinema
description: French literature and cinema from the Middle Ages through the 21st century, exploring how stories of passion, betrayal, and ambition reshape the boundaries between classical texts and films.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing.

subject: LLEA
title: Classical German Literature
description: Readings in translation from dramatic works of Lessing, Goethe, Schiller. Philosophic and aesthetic views of leading writers of the Enlightenment, Storm and Stress, and classical periods.

subject: LLEA
title: German Opera and Literature
description: Introduction to German opera, its history, and analysis. Developing critical skills through analysis of German opera music and literature. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: German Fascism and Propaganda
description: Study of German Fascism and propaganda in German literature, art, film, and associated ethical issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: Russian Short Story
description: Origin and development (19th and 20th century); periods, themes, styles, and major authors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: 19th-Century Russian Literature
description: Survey in English of major writers from Pushkin through Chekhov; lectures, discussions, short papers.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Russian Literature 1900—1950
description: Study of significant works of twentieth century Russian literature with particular focus on its relationship to Europe and Asia. Students will work intensively on their own writing and research in close collaboration with their instructor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Russia: Between Europe & Asia
description: Russian culture (literature, film, theater, music, arts, etc.) as an amalgam of European and Asian traditions and its impact on the world throughout history; develops written communication skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Russia: Faces of Asia
description: Survey in English of 19th-21st century representations of Asia in the contexts of the Russian Empire, the Soviet Union, and post-Soviet space.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Russian Film
description: A study of Russian film from the 1920’s to the present.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: The Art of Western Love
description: Chronological illustration of romantic love in European and Francophone Pacific literature and films, from its inception in 12th-century French courtly literature to our contemporary age of materialistic disenchantment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Survey of French Civilizations
description: A historical survey of the development of French and Francophone cultures. The course is interdisciplinary, dealing with politics, music, art, other forms of cultural expression, and daily life.

subject: LLEA
title: Europeans in the Pacific
description: European presence in the Pacific, in relation to literature, art, culture, and civilization. Not applicable to language requirement.

subject: LLEA
title: Teaching Practicum in Large Lecture Courses
description: Supervised undergraduate teaching practicum in large-lecture LLEA courses.
prereq_raw: completion of course in which practicum will be done and consent of instructor, no waiver.

children.text: completion of course in which practicum will be done

subject: LLEA
title: (Alpha) European and Latin American Cinema
description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: European and Latin American Cinema: Topic
description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: European and Latin American Cinema: Genre
description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: European and Latin American Cinema: Director
description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: European and Latin American Cinema: Era
description: Study of major developments in European and Latin American cinema studies focusing on a specific area. (B) Topic; (C) Genre; (D) Director; (E) Era. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: Directed Reading
description: Pre: limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major, and consent of department chair.

subject: LLEA
title: Spies, Memory, & The Cold War: Literature, Film, and Culture in Postwar Germany
description: East and West German literature, film, and culture (1945-1989), focusing on postwar recovery, espionage, and surveillance. Explores how cultural production reflects memory, private/public life, and political tensions in a divided society under geopolitical pressures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both LLEA 416 and GER 416 . Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: Learning and Teaching World Languages
description: Hybrid technology intensive course for pre- or in-service teachers of world languages. Topics: online learning, curriculum and lesson planning, assessment, language teaching approaches, technology for learning world languages. Junior standing or higher.

subject: LLEA
title: Freaks and Monsters 2: The Ethics of Otherness
description: An interdisciplinary examination of corporeal Otherness. Unusual real and fictional bodies from fairground history, art, anatomy, literature, natural history and ethnology. Discussion of the moral, medical, philosophical and aesthetic dilemmas of spectacular difference.

subject: LLEA
title: (Alpha) Fantasy and the Fantastic
description: Cross-cultural study of fantasy and the fantastic in short stories, fairy tales, films and novels from Europe and the Americas in English translation. Discussion of illusion, identity, time, the future, the bizarre and major concepts in fantasy literature. (B) fairies, devils and fantasy; (C) the fantastic, the strange and science fiction.

subject: LLEA

description: Cross-cultural study of fantasy and the fantastic in short stories, fairy tales, films and novels from Europe and the Americas in English translation. subject: LLEA

Discussion of illusion, identity, time, the future, the bizarre and major concepts in fantasy literature. (B) fairies, devils and fantasy; (C) the fantastic, the strange and science fiction.

subject: LLEA
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Independent study of approved reading and research with faculty supervision.

subject: LLEA
title: Seminar in Research Methods
description: Study of basic research methods and tools, including technology. Print and electronic source materials. Information literacy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: LLEA
title: Western Literature and Cultures in the Pacific
description: Impact of and reaction to western writings and cultural influences in the Pacific as represented in texts from the 16th century to the present.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

MA candidates in European languages read works in their major in the original.

description: Study in English of topics, periods, etc., in the languages taught in the department: (B) comparison of Romance languages; (C) interpersonal communication; (D) social perspectives.

subject: LWLW
title: Law Thesis
description: Intensive writing that satisfies the law school’s upper division writing requirement and results in advanced law paper of publishable quality, extending over two consecutive semesters of study.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LWLW
title: Law Teaching Seminar I
description: Interdisciplinary seminar used LP 1 assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of substantive law assignments and the methodology used to teach them.

subject: LWLW
title: Law Teaching Seminar II
description: Interdisciplinary seminar uses LP II assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of appellate advocacy and negotiation and the methodologies used to teach them.

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in Japan
description: An extended historical review of the foundations of Japanese law in society: Japan’s adoption and adaptation of Chinese legal doctrines, continental European legal structures and ideas, and American influences. Consideration of the structure of contemporary law in Japan: a look at the various players in the legal system, some important legal doctrines, and the real-world operation of Japan’s laws today.

subject: LWPA
title: Asian Pacific Insolvency Law
description: Comparison of corporate insolvency law of selected Asian and Pacific island countries, with a focus on recently enacted laws and pending proposals that have followed the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis. Recommended: LAW 515 , LAW 554 , LAW 562 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law students only.

subject: LWPA
title: Asian Comparative Labor Law
description: Area studies of Asian legal systems and issues, focusing on administration of Asian labor laws in a comparative context. Possible effects on foreign direct investment and foreign migrant contract workers. Comparison of Chinese, Japanese and other legal approaches in dealing with common issues.

subject: LWPA
title: International Criminal Law
description: Designed to give an understanding of international criminal law. Will review all aspects of international criminal law from substantive international crimes to criminal liability and sentencing by domestic and international tribunals.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in Korea
description: Provides students with an understanding of the law, society, and legal systems in Korea. Areas of law including constitutional, civil, criminal, and business are discussed. Emphasis on South Korea. Law majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Human Rights in Asia
description: A survey of human rights norms, institutions, and implementation mechanism of international human rights law in light of the rapid development of regional cooperation and integration in Asia.

subject: LWPA
title: International Business Transactions
description: An examination of the law, rules, and practices relating to transborder commercial transactions. Roughly half of the semester focuses on international sales transactions, the remaining portion focuses on domestic and multinational governance of the international business arena.

subject: LWPA
title: Foundations for Kānāwai
description: Examines Hawaiʻi’s cultural and legal foundations as essential context for Native Hawaiian Law. Integrating ʻike Hawaiʻi (Hawaiian knowledge), it specifically focuses on Hawaiʻi’s history, culture, and justice through an ʻŌiwi lens.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Native Hawaiian Law
description: Status and evolution of rights of Native Hawaiians to the land and its usufructs. Potential of utilizing native rights based on statute, custom, and use to develop new and expanded rights.

subject: LWPA
title: (Alpha) Topics-Native Hawaiian Law
description: Specific topic areas depend on current developments and issues in Native Hawaiian and Indigenous law in Hawaiʻi, the nation, and internationally, and expertise of faculty and visiting faculty. (B) policy and governance; (C) business and economic development; (D) law and culture; (E) Indigenous peoples, (F) Indigenous environment and sustainability.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW students only.

subject: LWPA
title: Legal History of Hawaiʻi
description: Designed to acquaint the student with the unique legal history of Hawaiʻi, emphasizing particular legal controversies that have shaped the law of our island society.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only.

subject: LWPA
title: Emerging Hawaiʻi Water Issues
description: Introduction to the legal framework for water resource management in Hawaiʻi; case studies illuminate the litigation process and evolution of the public trust, precautionary principle, and other legal, scientific, and policy areas.

subject: LWPA
title: International Law
description: Evolving process of formulating rules to govern nations and peoples of the world in their attempts to solve problems recognized as requiring global solutions.

subject: LWPA
title: Law and Society in China
description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

subject: LWPA
title: Comparative Law
description: Introduction to the civil law tradition, particularly as exemplified by the legal systems of East and Southeast Asia. After a brief review of comparative law study and the historical development of the civil law, the course will examine the structure and role of the courts, judicial process, the legal profession and constitutional law and administrative law in Western Europe and in the Asian civil law countries.

subject: LWPA
title: International Human Rights Advocacy
description: Applying international human rights law and legal skills to promote and protect human rights by way of United Nations Charter-based human rights mechanism, treaty-based mechanism, or other international human rights institutions.

subject: LWPA
title: International Economic Law
description: Problem-based course teaches theory and practice of interrelated global private regulation and public development consequences, as situated in cross-border transactions and dispute resolution in world law, international investment law, and international financial law.

subject: LWPA
title: Pacific Islands Legal Systems
description: Study of substantive rules of one or more Pacific Islands jurisdictions, development of legal systems, relationship of legal systems to culture and tradition.

subject: LWPA
title: International Intellectual Property
description: Primer on the World Intellectual Property Organization and the treaties it administers. Will explore the various international legislative and judicial developments in intellectual property as well as analyze international methods to harmonize several regional and national laws to protect rights in trademarks, patents, and copyrights. Students will be exposed to issues of territoriality and jurisdiction, international antitrust issues, and international dispute resolution, and human rights implications of international intellectual property rights protections.

subject: LWUL
title: American Legal Systems
description: Introduces foundational concepts in American legal systems. Engages students in legal analysis and techniques of legal advocacy.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Ulu Lehua Scholars only.

subject: LWUL
title: American Legal Systems II
description: Introduces conceptual and historical foundations of systems of public and private ordering in the U.S. and its territories. Subjects include federalism, constitutional democracy, separation of powers, and the common law.

subject: MAO
title: Beginning Maori I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing, grammar. Meets three hours weekly.

subject: MAO
title: Beginning Maori II
description: Continuation of MAO 101 . Meets three hours weekly.

subject: MAO
title: Intermediate Maori I
description: Continuation of MAO 102 . Meets three hours weekly.

subject: MAO
title: Intermediate Maori II
description: Continuation of MAO 201 . Meets three hours weekly.

subject: MAO
title: Maori Literature and Culture
description: Survey of literature concerning myths, traditions, poetry and song as well as contemporary literature (in English) relating to the Treaty of Waitangi, Maori prophetic sayings. Students who have previously taken this course as PACS 492 may not take this course.

subject: MAO
title: Advanced Maori Language and Culture
description: Advanced Maori language and culture.

subject: MAO
title: Advanced Maori Language and Culture
description: Advanced Maori language and culture.

subject: MAO
title: Modern Maori Literature and Culture
description: Survey of modern Maori and Hawaiian literature and culture from the mid-twentieth and early twenty-first centuries.

subject: MAO
title: Te Reo Waiata: Mâori Language in Song
description: Survey and analysis of Maori song poetry texts, traditional and contemporary, and their development and performance over time.

subject: MAO
title: Fourth-Level Maori I
description: Continuation of MAO 302 . Conducted in Maori. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Cultural contemporary and historical topics.

subject: MAO
title: Fourth-Level Maori II
description: Continuation of MAO 401 . Conducted in Maori. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Cultural contemporary and historical topics.

subject: MATH
title: Survey of Mathematics
description: Selected topics designed to acquaint non-specialists with examples of mathematical reasoning. May not be taken for credit after MATH 215 or higher.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers I
description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas, problem solving, and reasoning. Number systems, place value, fractions, and properties of operations. Prospective elementary education majors only.

subject: MATH
title: Math for Elementary Teachers II
description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas; problem solving; reasoning and proof; and using symbolism. Patterns and algebraic thinking, place value and decimals, geometry, and mathematical modeling.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions
description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational exponential and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing.
prereq_raw: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry.

prereq_tree.text: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus
description: Algebra review. Polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. Trigonometric function, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, and related topics.
prereq_raw: MATH 134 or MATH 161 or assessment exam.

subject: MATH
title: Precalculus and Elements of Calculus for Economics and the Social Sciences
description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, algebra of functions, techniques of graphing, differentiation and integration of algebraic functions, applications in economics and social sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Programming
description: (3 hr) Introduction to numerical algorithms and structured programming using Fortran, MATLAB, or other appropriate language.
prereq_raw: one semester of calculus ( MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , MATH 242 , MATH 243 , MATH 244 , MATH 251A , MATH 252A , or MATH 253A ) (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
description: Basic concepts; differentiation and integration applications to management, finance, economics, and the social sciences.
prereq_raw: MATH 134 or MATH 161 , or placement exam.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation, differential equations and integration with applications directed primarily to the life sciences.

subject: MATH
title: Applied Calculus II
description: Differential calculus for functions in several variables and curves, systems of ordinary differential equations, series approximation of functions, continuous probability, exposure to use of calculus in the literature.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration.
prereq_raw: MATH 140X or MATH 215 or placement exam.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations,
prereq_raw: MATH 241 or MATH 251A or a grade of B or better in MATH 215 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus IV
description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus I
description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth.
prereq_raw: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in MATH 140X and consent.

children.text: a grade of A in MATH 140X

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus II
description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations, introduction to vectors.
prereq_raw: MATH 251A (with a minimum grade of B) or MATH 241 (with a minimum grade of A and consent).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or MATH 241 ( with a minimum grade of A and consent )

subject: MATH
title: Accelerated Calculus III
description: Vector calculus; maxima and minima in several variables; multiple integrals; line integrals, surface integrals and their applications.
prereq_raw: MATH 252A with a grade of B or better, or consent.

subject: MATH
title: History of Mathematics
description: The historical development of mathematical thought.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
description: Symbolic logic, sets and relations, algorithms, trees and other graphs. Additional topics chosen from algebraic systems, networks, automata.
prereq_raw: one semester of calculus from mathematics department; or consent. Recommended: one semester programming.

children.text: one semester of calculus from mathematics department;

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations I
description: First order ordinary differential equations, constant coefficient linear equations, oscillations, Laplace transform, convolution, Green’s function.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Differential Equations II
description: Constant coefficient linear systems, variable coefficient ordinary differential equations, series solutions and special functions, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models
description: Deterministic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include difference equations, qualitative behavior solutions of ODEs and reaction-diffusion equations. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A , or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for MATH 304 .

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models
description: Probabilistic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include stochastic and Poisson processes, Markov models, estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A , or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models Lab
description: Optional laboratory for MATH 305 .

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
description: Introduction to linear algebra, application of eigenvalue techniques to the solution of differential equations. Students may receive credit for only one of MATH 307 or MATH 311 .

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
description: Algebra of matrices, linear equations, real vector spaces and transformations. Emphasis on concepts and abstraction and instruction of careful writing. Students may receive credit for only one of MATH 307 or MATH 311.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Advanced Mathematics
description: Formal introduction to the concepts of logic, finite and infinite sets, functions, methods of proof and axiomatic systems. Learning mathematical expressions in writing is an integral part of the course.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Real Analysis
description: A rigorous axiomatic development of one variable calculus. Completeness, topology of the line, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing.
prereq_raw: MATH 242 or MATH 252A , and MATH 321 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Foundation of Euclidean Geometry
description: Axiomatic Euclidean geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 321 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Non-Euclidean Geometries
description: Hyperbolic, other non-Euclidean geometries.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Euclidean and Non- Euclidean Geometries
description: Axiomatic geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method; Euclidean geometry; hyperbolic geometry, and other non-Euclidean geometries.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 321 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Financial Mathematics
description: Interest rate measurement, valuation of annuities, loan repayment, bond valuation, rate of return. Term structure of interest rates, cashflow duration, and immunization. Financial mathematics actuarial exam topics.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A or ( MATH 203 and BUS 250 ).

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability Theory
description: Sets, discrete sample spaces, problems in combinatorial probability, random variables, mathematical expectations, classical distributions, applications.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 , MATH 242 , or MATH 252A ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
description: Problem-oriented introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics, providing a foundation for applications and further study.
prereq_raw: MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Elementary Statistics
description: Estimation, tests of significance, the concept of power.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations I
description: Integral surfaces and characteristics of first and second order partial differential equations. Applications to the equations of mathematical physics.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , or consent. Recommended: MATH 244 and MATH 302 .

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations II
description: Laplace’s equation, Fourier transform methods for PDEs, higher dimensional PDEs, spherical harmonics, Laplace series, special functions and applications.

subject: MATH
title: Ordinary Differential Equations
description: Systems of linear ordinary differential equations, autonomous systems, and stability theory applications. Optional topics include series solutions, Sturm theory, numerical methods.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical solution of equations, interpolation, least-squares approximation, quadrature, eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 407- MATH 408 .)
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 , and one semester programming; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Continuation of MATH 407 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 407 .

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra
description: Vector spaces over arbitrary fields, minimal polynomials, invariant subspaces, canonical forms of matrices; unitary and Hermitian matrices, quadratic forms.
prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 , and MATH 321 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Introduction to basic algebraic structures. Groups, finite groups, abelian groups, rings, integral domains, fields, factorization, polynomial rings, field extensions, quotient fields. Emphasis on writing instruction. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 412- MATH 413 .)

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
description: Continuation of MATH 412 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 412. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: MATH
title: Optimization: Theory & Methods
description: Introduction to theory and methods for optimization. Topics may include least square analysis, search methods, conjugate direction methods, linear programming, integer programming, and constrained optimization.
prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
description: Congruences, quadratic residues, arithmetic functions, distribution of primes. Emphasis is on teaching theory and writing, not on computation.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: General topology, including compactness and connectedness; the Jordan Curve Theorem and the classification of surfaces; first homotopy or homology groups.

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis I
description: Topology of Rn, metric spaces, continuous functions, Riemann integration, sequences and series, uniform convergence, implicit function theorems, differentials and Jacobians. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 431-432.)
prereq_raw: MATH 311 , MATH 321 , and MATH 331 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Principles of Analysis II
description: Continuation of MATH 431 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 431 . Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

subject: MATH
title: Vector Analysis
description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 , or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Differential Geometry
description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , and MATH 311 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Complex Analysis
description: Analytic functions, complex integration, introduction to conformal mapping.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; recommended MATH 331 ; or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Topics in Undergraduate Mathematics
description: Advanced topics from various areas: algebra, number theory, analysis, and geometry.

subject: MATH
title: Axiomatic Set Theory
description: Sets, relations, ordinal arithmetic, cardinal arithmetic, axiomatic set theory, axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis.
prereq_raw: MATH 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent.

children.text: in a related field or consent

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Logic
description: A system of first order logic. Formal notions of well-formed formula, proof, and derivability. Semantic notions of model, truth, and validity. Completeness theorem.
prereq_raw: MATH 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent. Recommended: 454.

children.text: in a related field or consent . Recommended: 454

subject: MATH
title: Probability
description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectations, moment-generating and characteristic functions, limit theorems. Continuous probability emphasized.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent), or consent. Recommended: MATH 305 or MATH 371 or MATH 372 ; or consent.

children.text: Recommended: MATH 305 or MATH 371 or MATH 372 ; or consent

subject: MATH
title: Statistical Inference
description: Sampling and parameter estimation, tests of hypotheses, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, sequential analysis, rank order statistics.

subject: MATH
title: Combinatorial Mathematics
description: Finite configurations. Topics may include counting methods, generating functions, graph theory, map coloring, block design, network flows, analysis of discrete algorithms.

subject: MATH
title: Senior Seminar
description: Seminar for senior mathematics majors, including an introduction to methods of research. Significant portion of class time is dedicated to the instruction and critique of oral presentations. All students must give the equivalent of three presentations.

subject: MATH
title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher and consent.

subject: MATH
title: Directed Reading
description: Limited to advanced students who must arrange with an instructor before enrolling.

subject: MATH
title: Problem Solving for Teachers
description: Practicing teachers develop and improve their problem-solving skills by working on challenging mathematical tasks. Students improve their mathematics content knowledge by working on problems and learning to design challenge problems for their own classes. Practicing teachers in grades K-12 only.

subject: MATH
title: (Alpha) Career Skills for Graduate Students in Mathematics
description: Seminar addresses issues important in the career of a mathematician, beginning from their time in graduate school, through navigating the job market and on to their eventual work in industry or academia. (B) teaching.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MATH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MATH

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MATH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, Only one time for (B).

subject: MATH
title: Applied Dynamical Systems
description: Continuous and discrete dynamical systems; bifurcation theory; chaotic maps. Additional topics from PDEs and linear algebra.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Methods of Applied Mathematics
description: Linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and partial differential equations. Topics include spectral theory, matrix exponentiation, initial-value problems, dynamical systems, bifurcation theory, first-order PDEs, characteristics, Sturm-Liouville theory, boundary-value problems, Green’s functions.

subject: MATH
title: Partial Differential Equations
description: Classical existence and uniqueness theory for PDEs, qualitative properties, classification, boundary value and initial value problems, fundamental solutions, other topics.

subject: MATH
title: Numerical Analysis
description: Numerical linear algebra including iterative methods, SVD, and other matrix factorizations, locating eigenvalues, discrete approximation to partial differential equations. Recommended: MATH 407 , MATH 411 , or consent.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Linear Algebra
description: Key concepts of linear algebra for graduate students in mathematics. Specific topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, multilinear forms, and Jordan decomposition. May not receive credit for both MATH 411 and MATH 610. MATH majors only.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Modules, Sylow theorems, Jordan-Holder theorem, unique factorization domains, Galois theory, algebraic closures, transcendence bases. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 611- MATH 612 .)

subject: MATH
title: Modern Algebra
description: Continuation of MATH 611 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 611 .

subject: MATH
title: Group Theory
description: Sylow theorems, solvable groups, nilpotent groups, extension theory, representation theory, additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Commutative Ring Theory
description: Ideal theory, Noetherian rings, localization, domains, radicals and primes, and additional topics.

subject: MATH
title: Lattice Theory
description: Introduction with applications to general algebra. Partially ordered sets, decomposition theory, representations of lattices, varieties and free lattices, coordinatization of modular lattices.

subject: MATH
title: Universal Algebra
description: Introduction to basic techniques, including subalgebras, congruences, automorphisms and endomorphisms, varieties of algebras, Mal’cev conditions.

subject: MATH
title: Key Elements of Topology
description: Key concepts of Topology for graduate students in mathematics; topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; continuity. MATH majors only.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Properties of topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; metrizability; convergence and continuity. Additional topics from general and algebraic topology. (These topics are covered in the year sequence MATH 621- MATH 622 .)

subject: MATH
title: Topology
description: Continuation of MATH 621 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 621 .

subject: MATH
title: Geometric Group Theory
description: Geometric, topological, and dynamical methods in the study of finitely generated infinite groups.
prereq_raw: MATH 621 (with a minimum grade of B-).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MATH

subject: MATH

description: Lebesgue measure and integral, convergence of integrals, functions of bounded variation, Lebesgue- Stieltjes integral and more general theory of measure and integration. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 631-632.)

subject: MATH
title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
description: Continuation of MATH 631 . This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as MATH 631 .

subject: MATH
title: Functional Analysis
description: Linear topological spaces, normed spaces, Hilbert spaces, function algebras, operator theory.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus of Variations

subject: MATH
title: Analytic Function Theory

subject: MATH

subject: ME
title: Space Exploration
description: Introduction to science and engineering of Solar System exploration with laboratory exercises. Covers planetary science, model-based systems engineering, mission planning, constraints on payload and spacecraft design, human spaceflight technology. Research projects emphasize written communication.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Engineering Design
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Introductory experience in communication, presentation, professional ethics, social responsibility, engineering economics, quality control, and computer-aided drafting. Teamwork and project required.

subject: ME
title: Applied Mechanics II
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, CNST, ENGS, ME majors only.

subject: ME
title: Space Science and Instrumentation
description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation. Significant oral and written communication is required.
prereq_raw: EPET 201 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105 , or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107 ; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272 .

subject: ME
title: Thermodynamics
description: (3 Lec, 1 Discussion) Basic laws, closed and open systems. Work, heat, concept of entropy. Properties of pure simple substances. Ideal gases. Introduction to power and refrigeration cycles.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A ), PHYS 170 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A ).

subject: ME
title: Mechanics of Fluids and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Incompressible and compressible ideal fluids, effects of viscosity. Similitude, boundary layer flow. Measurement techniques in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermos-fluid systems. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of ME 311 and CEE 271 (or ME 271 ).

subject: ME
title: Materials Science and Engineering
description: Electronic, atomic, and crystalline structure of materials and their effect on the mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties of engineering metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A ), MATH 242 (or MATH 252A ), and PHYS 170 .

subject: ME
title: Manufacturing Processes and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Energy requirements for manufacturing methods. Manufacturing methods to obtain components with desired size/shape/properties. Conduct manufacturing experiments. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ME
title: Computer Methods in Engineering
description: Numerical solutions for algebraic and transcendental equations, simultaneous linear algebraic equations, integration and differentiation; integration of ordinary differential equations. Engineering applications.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of ECE 160 (or ECE 110 or ICS 111 ), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A ), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307 ).

prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (or ME 271 ) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307 ).

subject: ME
title: Space Mission Design
description: Covers all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, budgets, and ethical issues that are important to consider in producing a fully successful mission.

subject: ME
title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists. Will build a small spacecraft and payload and seeks to answer important science questions. Emphasizes review report and proposal writing.

subject: ME
title: Dynamics Systems Laboratory

prereq_raw: ME 422 (or concurrent ), and either ME 360 , MATH 407 or PHYS 305 ; or consent.

subject: ME
title: Orbital Mechanics

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermodynamics
description: Gas mixtures, generalized thermodynamic relationships, combustion and thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, power and refrigeration cycles.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in ME 311 .

subject: ME
title: Applied Thermal Engineering
description: Principles, design and analysis of practical thermal systems. Engineering applications. Valve, compressor, condenser and evaporator technologies. System integration and control. Thermal loads and thermal comfort.

subject: ME
title: Power and Propulsion
description: Principles, performance, and design of gas turbine power plants and propulsion systems.

subject: ME
title: Astronautics
description: The space environment (vacuum, neutral, radiation, and plasma); motion in gravitational fields; orbit transfers; Earth-satellite operations; rocketry; propulsion analysis and performance; reentry dynamics; interplanetary trajectories; attitude dynamics and stabilization.

subject: ME
title: Heat Transfer and Lab
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Steady and unsteady conduction; steady convection and radiation; heat exchangers. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: ME
title: Mass Transfer
description: Elementary mass diffusion; diffusion in a stationary medium; diffusion in a moving medium; low and high mass transfer theories; simultaneous heat and mass transfer; condensation, evaporation, and boiling; transpiration cooling; species boundary layers; engineering and design of heat and mass exchangers; current refrigerants and environmental regulations.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Gas Dynamics
description: One-dimensional compressible flow involving change of area, friction, heat transfer. Normal and oblique shocks. Prandtl-Meyer flow. Application to nozzles, diffusers, airfoils.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Management of Electronic Systems
description: To introduce concepts in the thermal management of electronics, and to develop sound technical tools to approach modern electronic packaging and cooling applications.

subject: ME
title: Scaling Methods in Engineering
description: Scaling methods and optimization under global constraints; multi-scale optimal design of mechanical, thermal, and natural systems; effectiveness of heat, fluid, and convective trees; theoretical design optimization of manmade and natural power systems; analysis of time dependent structures.

subject: ME
title: Solar Thermal Engineering
description: Fundamentals of solar energy, solar engineering material characteristics, and solar thermal and photovoltaic systems. Will learn solar thermal system components, and be able to perform simple system design.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Failures in Materials
description: Analysis of component failures due to imperfections, fatigue, brittle fracture, wear, corrosion, bending, impact, and overload. Fracture mechanics. Case studies.

subject: ME
title: Materials Selection for Design
description: Methodology for the selection of materials for mechanical applications to prevent mechanical failure and environmental degradation. Design considerations associated with the use of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.

subject: ME
title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods-theory and hands-on experience.

subject: ME
title: Corrosion Engineering
description: Basics of corrosion processes and emphasis on corrosion control. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion, metal alloys and their behavior, corrosion control techniques (cathodic protection, anodic protection, coatings, and inhibitors).

subject: ME
title: Mechatronics
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Modern mechatronics components and design principles; functionality of products, processes and systems; electrical circuits and mechanical components; programming and control; hands on technology; application case studies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME, EE, CE, ICS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or consent.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Materials Manufacturing
description: (2 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Introduction to anisotropic materials, advanced manufacturing techniques for composite and intelligent materials, joining of composites, thin film processing and stereolithography, computer aided manufacturing and rapid prototyping, manufacturing process optimization, open-ended manufacturing projects.
prereq_raw: ME 341 , and senior standing; or consent.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
description: (3 Lec) Tools and techniques of micro- and nano-technology in design, modeling, simulations, analysis, fabrication, testing and characterization; nano-materials, nanostructures, nano-composites, nano-coating, nano-optics, nano-electronics and nano-biotechnology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

subject: ME
title: Nanosystem and Microsystem Design
description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale. Microfabrication/nanofabrication, fabrication process design, electrostatistic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, measurements. Course work will focus on process and system design.
prereq_raw: ME 331 (with a minimum grade of C-), ME 375 (with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) , ME 375 ( with a minimum grade of C- ) , or consent

subject: ME
title: Research Methods in Engineering
description: Introduces the basic skills of preparing and publishing scientific research. Students will learn how to prepare, write, publish, and present a scientific paper, while working on a research project related to thermofluids.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Feedback-Control Systems
description: Analysis/ design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

subject: ME
title: Robotics
description: Principles and design methods for autonomous systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing.

subject: ME
title: Energy Conversion Systems
description: Energy conversion and its impact on the environment. Conventional, hydroelectric, nuclear fission and fusion, solar, wind, ocean, geothermal, and biomass power; energy storage, transmission and conservation.
prereq_raw: ME 322 , ME 411 , and ME 422 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Nuclear Energy & Engineering
description: Covers the fundamentals of nuclear energy and engineering principles as applied to the operation of nuclear reactors and the design of reactors for electrical power generation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME, ECE, CE majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Nuclear Power Engineering
description: Nuclear reactor principles. Reactor heat transfer, heat generation and removal. Design and analysis of reactor power systems and plants.

subject: ME
title: Flow Visualization and Measurement
description: Overview of flow visualization and measurement techniques including high speed photography of wakes, jets, shear layer, particle motion. Experimental design, statistics, image processing and data analysis. Junior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: Materials for Solar Energy Conversion
description: Atom structure, electromagnetic waves and energy, electronic and energetic properties of semi-conducting materials, junctions, solar cells operations, bulk and thin film materials synthesis, integration of solar cells into the electric grid.
prereq_raw: ( ME 331 or ECE 324 ) with a minimum grade of C-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EE and ME majors only.

subject: ME
title: Electrochemical Power Sources: Principles, Applications, and Sustainability
description: Electrochemistry, batteries, fuel cells, flow batteries, electrochemical capacitors, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage.
prereq_raw: ME 331 , CHEM 162 , CHEM 171 , or CHEM 181A (with a grade of C- or better).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ENGR majors only.

children.text: ( with a grade of C- or better )

subject: ME
title: Experimental Stress Analysis
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis: strain and deflection measurement of beams and shafts, strain to stress conversion, principal and maximum shearing stresses, failure in biaxial stress states, stress concentrations, residual stresses, buckling, creep, electrical resistance strain gages, brittle coatings, photoelastic methods, transducers.

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Vibrations
description: Response of machines and systems to transient and periodic excitation. Vibration isolation and transmissibility. Modal analysis of multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Applications to design.

subject: ME
title: Fundamentals of Acoustics
description: Plane and spherical acoustic waves. Transmission, reflection, radiation, and absorption. Near and far fields, radiation patterns. Applications to noise control. Instruments.

subject: ME
title: Thermofluid Measurements and Design
description: Measurement techniques in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Contemporary engineering ethics issues. Final report and presentation are required.

subject: ME
title: Design Project I
description: (2 1-hr Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Heuristic application of engineering design process and project planning via a significant, open-ended design project that includes realistic constraints involving economics, environmental sustainability, manufacturability, ethics, health, safety, society, and politics. Extensive written communication required.
prereq_raw: ME 322 , ME 341 , ME 372 , and ME 375 ; or consent.

subject: ME
title: Design Project II
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Continuation of design project initiated in ME 481 . Extension of conceptual design to final design. Manufacturing of prototype: material and part selection, procurement, manufacturing specifications/ drawings. Testing of complex systems. Extensive oral communication required.

subject: ME
title: Research and Experiment Design
description: Introduction to research and experimentation via pursuit and reporting of an open-ended design project. Ethical issues in research and experimentation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering, Biological Engineering, and Ocean & Resources Engineering majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: ME
title: System Engineering
description: Will cover system engineering design, analysis, and development concepts, requirements derivation/management, and program management processes, such as risk identification/ management and fiscal/schedule tools. Senior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: ME 213 (with a minimum grade of C).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME majors only.

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ME majors only.
