description: Analysis of principles of operation of renewable energy systems, and its interactions with sustainability. Fundamentals of renewable energy production, storage, and distribution.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Thermodynamics
description: Introduction to general principles of classical thermodynamics. Main topics include equilibrium conditions, thermodynamic relations, Legendre transformations, Maxwell relations, stability of thermodynamic systems, phase transitions, and critical phenomena.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics. Main topics include entropy, Boltzmann law, thermodynamic driving forces, statistical mechanics, chemical equilibria, solutions and mixtures, and applications of statistical thermodynamics in biology, chemistry, physics, and nanoscience.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Aerodynamics
description: Advanced topics in aerodynamics, two- and three-dimensional wing theory, slender-body theory, lifting surface methods, vortex and wave drag, analytical and numerical methods, for computing unsteady aerodynamic behavior and introduction to flight-dynamics.

subject: ME
title: Thermal Environmental Engineering
description: Physiological response to thermal environment, designs of passive and active cooling systems, student project.

subject: ME
title: Boiling and Two-Phase Flow
description: Two-phase flow pattern and flow pattern maps; two-phase flow models (homogeneous, separate, drift flux, annular); laminar and turbulent film condensations; boiling incipience; pool boiling heat transfer; flow boiling heat transfer; critical heat flux (CHF).

subject: ME
title: Biological Fluid Mechanics
description: Review of Newtonian fluid mechanics. Blood rheology and flow in elastic tubes. Murray’s Law and pulsatile flow propagation. Microcirculation dynamics and biological transport. Aquatic movement and comparative biological examples.

subject: ME
title: Conduction Heat Transfer
description: Steady and unsteady heat conduction with and without heat sources in solids. Analytical, numerical, graphical, analog methods for solving heat conduction problems.

subject: ME
title: Convection Heat Transfer
description: Heat transfer in laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Analogy between heat, momentum, mass transfer.

subject: ME
title: Radiation Heat Transfer
description: Radiant interchange among surfaces. Gaseous radiation. Combined conduction, convection, and radiation heat transfer.

subject: ME
title: Microfluidics and Nanofluidics
description: Introduction to fundamental understanding of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena at micro-nanoscale; electrokinetics; chemical separation; colloids and emulsions; biophysics; micro-nanofabrication.

subject: ME
title: Numerical Methods in Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer
description: Integration of ordinary differential equations. Finite difference solutions of partial differential equations with applications to conduction and convection. Introduction to finite element methods.
prereq_raw: ME 422 , and either MATH 190 or ECE 160 .

subject: ME
title: Viscous Flows
description: Formulation and properties of the Navier-Stokes equations; exact solutions; creeping flows; lubrication theory; laminar boundary layers; laminar stability, and transition to turbulence; turbulent boundary layers.

subject: ME
title: Environmental Heat, Mass, and Momentum Transfer
description: Heat and mass transfer in Earth’s interior with applications to geothermal and petroleum reservoir engineering.

subject: ME
title: Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design
description: Chemical kinetics with heat and mass transfer. Balance equations applied to selected ideal reactors. Departures from ideality.

subject: ME
title: Renewable Energy Engineering I: Biomass
description: (1 Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Experimental methods and theory of thermochemical biomass conversion: static and dynamic temperature and mass measurements, thermogravimetry, differential scanning calorimetry, GCMS and HPLC techniques.

subject: ME
title: Rheology
description: Vector and tensor operations. Constutive equations. Generalized Newtonian fluids and linear viscoelastic fluids. Rheometry and experiments. Flow of suspensions. Advanced topics and rheology of polymers, food products, biomaterials and asphalt, laboratories.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Materials Science
description: Properties of materials interpreted from the atomistic viewpoint. Crystal structure and defects. Thermodynamics of solids; phase transformations; experimental techniques.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Transport Phenomena
description: Theory of momentum, heat, and mass transfer processes. Integral and differential conservation equations, constitutive laws, and interfacial boundary conditions. Dimensional analysis, perturbation theory, asymptotics, similarity, and Green’s function methodology. Applications to problems in engineering.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in ME 322 or ECE 626 , or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Li-ion Battery Mechanistic Modeling: Principles and State of the Art
description: Electrochemistry, Li-ion batteries, electric vehicles, electrochemical grid storage.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering majors only.

subject: ME
title: Corrosion Theory
description: Application of electrochemical theory and materials science to corrosion and oxidation reactions. Effect of environment, especially marine. Cathodic protection, coatings, inhibitors, treatment of water systems.

subject: ME
title: Fundamentals of Electrochemistry
description: Thermodynamics of cells, electrode kinetics, mass transfer by migration and diffusion, microelectrode techniques, forced convection, impedance, double-layer structure, and absorbed intermediates in electrode processes.

subject: ME
title: Mechanical Behavior of Engineering Materials
description: Mechanical property tests. Stress concentrations. Fracture mechanics; applications to materials failures and to selection of materials; emphasis on mechanical engineering applications.

subject: ME
title: Clinically Driven Design and Development
description: Exploration of simple, cost-effective alternatives in medicine through different stages of concept generation, design analysis, and prototype validation and investigation of their commercialization potential.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Mechanics and Design Composites
description: Introduction to composites; anisotropic elasticity and laminate theory; hygrothermal effects; composite beams, columns, rods, plates, and shells; energy method; failure theories; joining of composites, computer-aided design in composites.

subject: ME
title: Nanoscience and Nanotechnology
description: Science and applications of nanotechnology. Synthesis of nanostructures; nanoscale structure characterization by electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy; electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of nanostructures; fabrication of nanodevices; energy, environmental, and biological applications of nanomaterials.

subject: ME
title: Nanosystems
description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale, including electrostatic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, and measurements. Course work will focus on literature review and integration of current research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Engineering majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Surface Phenomena
description: Fundamental and modern concepts of colloid and surface science. Main topics include surface thermodynamics, capillarity and wetting phenomena, surface forces, surfactants, and particles.

subject: ME
title: Automatic Control
description: Linear optimal feedback control, discrete time optimal control, fundamentals of adaptive control, application to motion and force control of robot arms and manipulators.

subject: ME
title: Guidance, Navigation and Control
description: Develop modern and advanced techniques in the design, development, and implementation of guidance, navigation, and control (GNC) systems for flight vehicles and other controllable dynamical systems.
prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of the following: ME 271 or CEE 271 ; ME 375 ; MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; MATH 302 or MATH 307 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

children.text: better in all of the following: ME 271

subject: ME
title: Autonomous Marine Systems
description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies.
prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

children.text: ( or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 ( or equivalent), or instructor consent

subject: ME
title: Introduction to Fuel Cell Technology
description: Working principles of all major fuel cell types; fundamentals of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells; state-of-the-art theoretical models and diagnostic technologies for PEM fuel cells.

subject: ME
title: Energy Transport and Conversion at the Nanoscale
description: Basics of energy transport and conversion processes and emphasis on microscopic behaviors of energy carriers. Introduction to quantum mechanics and solid state physics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or instructor consent.

subject: ME
title: Shape Memory Alloys-Constitutive Modeling, Dynamics, and Nonlinear Control
description: Shape memory alloys; Shape Memory Effect (SME) and Superelasticity; hysteresis; applications in engineering, medical devices, and robotics; modeling and characterization; nonlineal control; finite element analyses. Engineering and computer science majors only.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ME
title: Continuum Mechanics
description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics, coordinate transformations, analysis of stress and strain, principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations, constitutive relations, field equations. Problems in elasticity.
prereq_raw: Recommended: ME 371 or CEE 370 , or consent.

subject: ME
title: Finite Element Analysis
description: Introduction to finite element analysis and design in mechanical engineering. Applications to machine design, vibrations, elasticity, heat transfer.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Dynamics
description: Lecture on rigid-body dynamics. Topics include: dynamical systems; motion representation and constraints; Newtonian mechanics; Lagrangian mechanics; Hamilton’s principle; stability analysis; introduction to multibody dynamics.

subject: ME
title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 531 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

subject: ME
title: Air Pollution, Toxics, and Control
description: Chemical mechanisms of formation and destruction of major air pollutants, transport phenomena, and health and environmental impacts. Evolution of source and control technologies. Current and pending regulations and policies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: CE, ECE, ME, and OE majors only.

subject: ME
title: Seminar
description: Current problems in all branches of mechanical engineering. All graduate students are required to attend; registrants are expected to present talks.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ME
title: Advanced Topics in Mechanical Engineering
description: Highly specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, system, or design.

subject: ME
title: Directed Reading or Research
description: Directed study on subject of mutual interest to student and a staff member. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: ME
title: Thesis Research
description: Thesis for degree of MS in mechanical engineering.
prereq_raw: admission to candidacy and consent of thesis advisor.

subject: ME
title: Directed Instruction
description: Student assists in undergraduate classroom and/or project instruction under the direction and close supervision of faculty member.
prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy or consent.

subject: ME
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for PhD in mechanical engineering.

subject: MED
title: Internal Medicine Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting, and four-week hospital-based experience.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology
description: Designed to acquaint students to the field of medical technology (clinical laboratory science).

subject: MEDT
title: Introduction to Medical Technology II
description: Basic principles and lab skills in medical technology (medical lab science). Required for second bachelor’s degree students (not MLT credentialed) wishing to major in medical technology.
prereq_raw: MEDT 151 , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L , BIOL 171 / BIOL 171L (or concurrent)
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Second bachelor’s degree students only.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Theory and clinical application of medical laboratory methods and healthcare professional relationships.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: The Clinical Laboratory II
description: Theory and clinical application of medical technology methods and healthcare professional relationships. Companion course to MEDT 301 ; and required, for second bachelor’s degree students who were admitted to MEDT major.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only. Second Bachelor’s degree standing or higher.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Laboratory Management
description: Students will become familiar with fundamental administration of a clinical laboratory to include technical, personnel, and financial management areas. Ethical issues in clinical laboratory management will be discussed, with an emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Parasitology
description: (1 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Modern diagnostic practices in parasitology.

subject: MEDT
title: Hematology
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental study of blood in normal and pathological states: formation, development, and classification of blood cells.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Hematology Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany MEDT 451 . Emphasis on writing to study content.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Immunohematology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Antigen-antibody relationships in human blood, study of blood groups, clinical problems in transfusion.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Fundamentals of Clinical Parasitology
description: Covers epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections. Provides a foundation for successful MLS ASCP board certification, and benefits students pursuing careers related to medicine, public health and biomedical sciences.
prereq_raw: MICR 130 or any general microbiology course, or consent.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Biochemistry I
description: Biochemical processes in human health and disease states.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Biochemistry II
description: Continuation of MEDT 471 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses I
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Lab experiments illustrating fundamental principles and methods of clinical laboratory analyses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses II
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Continuation of MEDT 477 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Professional Issues in Medical Lab Science
description: Discussions about various professional issues through oral presentations and critiquing of peer presentations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Immunology
description: Explore immunology by studying antigen-antibody structures, biological functions, and antibody synthesis fundamentals. Understand the relationship between immunology, biology, and medical sciences, preparing for advanced study and practical applications in medical technology.

subject: MEDT
title: Diagnostic Clinical Bacteriology
description: Equips students with preanalytical, analytical and post-analytical knowledge on procedures required in the accurate diagnosis of infectious diseases in humans. Benefits students pursuing careers related to medicine, public health and biomedical sciences.
prereq_raw: MICR 130 or any general microbiology course, or consent.

subject: MEDT
title: Special Topics in Medical Technology
description: Acquaints student with role of the medical technologist and overlap of major sciences in clinical situations to help student develop qualities unique to med technology.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MEDT majors only.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Microbiology Preceptorship
description: Clinical training for students with bachelor’s degree in microbiology to be able to qualify as clinical microbiologists in a healthcare setting. Includes specimen procurement, processing, detection and identification, susceptibility testing, and other diagnostic technology.

subject: MEDT
title: Clinical Training in Medical Technology
description: Application of theory and simulated laboratory experiences in immuno-hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, parasitology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, immunology, to meet stated career entry-level competencies.

subject: MEDT
title: Seminar in Medical Technology
description: Analysis of research and recent literature pertaining to various aspects of medical technology.

subject: MGT
title: Fundamentals of Entrepreneurship
description: Covers the role of new ventures and entrepreneurship in the world economy, the formation, funding, marketing, structure and implementation of business ventures.

subject: MGT
title: Multinational Business Management
description: Introduction to the unique problems and challenges in managing multinational business enterprises. Systems approach to the management process in such multinational firms stressed.

subject: MGT
title: Comparative Management Systems: United States and Japan
description: Similarities and differences in managers, in process of management, and in relevant environmental constraints in Japan and the U.S.

subject: MGT
title: Seminar in Management
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration.
repeatable_raw: May be repeated with change in topic.

subject: MGT
title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
description: Integrative course in entrepreneurship designed around the development of an original business concept and the completion of a comprehensive business plan for a new venture. Intended as final course for students completing entrepreneurship minor.

subject: MGT
title: History of American Business
description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

subject: MGT
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: MGT
title: Behavior in Organizations
description: Contributions made by sociology, psychology, and related behavioral sciences to the understanding and prediction of human behavior in organizations.

subject: MGT
title: Family Business
description: The exploration of business, personal, and interpersonal issues associated with a family owned and managed company. Topics include: family psychology and organizational structure, life cycles in family business, strategic family and business planning, succession planning, family business conflict resolution, estate planning, the role of professional managers, and others. This is not a course about how to become an entrepreneur or how to start or manage a business. It is most appropriate for those students who are part of a family that owns and manages a business.
prereq_raw: BUS 315 or graduate status, or consent.

subject: MGT
title: Asia Pacific Business Systems
description: Business systems in Asia Pacific countries including Japan, Korea, China, Taiwan, Singapore, and Hong Kong in terms of particular organization strategies and how they relate to the industrial trade policies.
prereq_raw: BBA core excluding BUS 345 , or consent.

subject: MGT
title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
description: Exploration of the nature and role of entrepreneurship behavior inside larger, established organizations. An examination of obstacles to entrepreneurial activity and approaches to creating work environments that foster entrepreneurship.

subject: MGT
title: (Alpha) Advanced Organizational Behavior
description: (B) experiential learning (EL); (C) organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

subject: MGT
title: Advanced Organizational Behavior: experiential learning (EL)
description: (B) experiential learning (EL); (C) organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

subject: MGT
title: Advanced Organizational Behavior: organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior
description: (B) experiential learning (EL); (C) organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

subject: MGT
title: Comparative Management
description: Crosscultural analysis of the values and environmental constraints that shape management patterns and policies. Emphasis on Pacific area nations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

subject: MGT
title: New Venture Management
description: Technical aspects of entrepreneurship, components and requirements for developing a business plan.

subject: MGT
title: International Business: Environment and Enterprise
description: Survey of the environment of international business with theory and policy focusing on strategic planning, international management and operational issues confronting the multinational corporations in the global environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only.

subject: MGT
title: Management Topics
description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration.

subject: MGT
title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
description: Entrepreneurship behavior involving the founding of new business units within established companies; understanding and dealing with barriers to entrepreneurship in corporations; recognizing corporate entrepreneurship opportunities; and learning various approaches organizations can take to increase entrepreneurship.

subject: MGT
title: Working with Entrepreneurs and Startups
description: Project-oriented course in which a team of students will work with a real local startup and entrepreneur to develop a business idea and/or viable business plan.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MGT
title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses. Recommended: LAW 530 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Law, MBA, and ME students only.

subject: MGT
title: Negotiation
description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multiparty, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

subject: MGT
title: (Alpha) International Management and Industrial Relations
description: Selected topics in international management and industrial relations: (B) Chinese management systems; (C) Japanese management systems; (D) management of multinational corporations; (F) contemporary issues in international business foreign direct investment; (G) cross-cultural communication in international business; (H) interactive strategies in Asian culture; (I) international human resource management; (J) international joint ventures; (K) international management of technology; (M) Korean management systems; (N) multinational corporation and environmental issues; (O) strategy of the multinational corporation; (P) international transfer of technology.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MBA or MAcc students only (except for (D).

subject: MGT
title: International Strategic Management
description: Analysis of the strategic management of firms engaged in multinational business including specific content on Asia. Permits students to focus on specific countries such as China and Japan.

subject: MGT
title: Entrepreneurship for Science and Technology
description: Recognizing and screening technology opportunities, the commercialization process, intellectual property acquisition, business model related to high technology strategies needed for growth in high tech firms.

subject: MGT
title: Asian/Pacific Entrepreneurship
description: Innovative ventures, issues related to noticing opportunities, conceptualizing and developing a business model, starting and growing a new venture with specific emphasis on the Asian/Pacific region.

subject: MGT
title: Health Policy, Systems, and the Legal Environment
description: Covers health care policy topics including: analyzing health service needs, access, use, disparities; health professional supply; policy issues for health organizations; health care financing policy; health law/ethical issues.

subject: MGT
title: Cross-Cultural Management
description: Provides tools to compare and contrast management practices across nations and to examine the role of culture in shaping those practices.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: MGT
title: PhD Seminar-Corporate Strategy and International Business
description: Objectives include: explore research topics in corporate strategy and international business, examine conceptual and empirical literature on management of the multinational corporation, and prepare students for comprehensive examination.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: MGT
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in an area of management under the direction of faculty member(s).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: MICR
title: General Microbiology
description: Role of microorganisms; how they affect people, property, and the environment. A basic survey course covering broad aspects of biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, and physiology; host-parasite relationships, public health, bacterial, mycotic and viral diseases; epidemiology; ecology of soils and water; environmental pollution; food microbiology; industrial applications at an introductory level. Not open to those with credit in MICR 351 or equivalent.

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology Laboratory
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany MICR 130 . Microbiological techniques and cultivation of microorganisms. Instruction in lab safety. Primarily for students in nursing and dental hygiene.

subject: MICR
title: Research Ethics
description: Introduction to the ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Based on case studies, students will discuss and write about ethical issues in research. Issues include humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data, genetic technologies and record keeping. This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Biology of Microorganisms
description: Anatomy, chemistry, physiology, genetics, development, and environmental interactions of microorganisms.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 or equivalent, CHEM 272 / CHEM 272L ; or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Biology of Microorganisms Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Laboratory exercises to accompany MICR 351 .
prereq_raw: CHEM 272 / CHEM 272L , and BIOL 171 or equivalent.

subject: MICR
title: Introductory Bioinformatics
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Introductory bioinformatics will provide a basic foundation of biological information (DNA, protein, genome and proteome) by using information technology (IT).

subject: MICR
title: Marine Microbiology
description: Evolution, ecology, biochemistry, genetics and physiology of marine bacteria by examining defined systems and organisms.
prereq_raw: BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and BIOL 301 (or concurrent)/ BIOL 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; or consent.

children.text: / BIOL 301L (or concurrent) , and OCN 201 ; or MICR 351 / MICR 351L ; or consent

subject: MICR

description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany MICR 401 .

subject: MICR
title: Microbial Physiology
description: Fundamental physiological and metabolic processes of bacteria; emphasis on growth, functions of cell structures, varieties of energy metabolism, metabolic regulation, and differentiation at the prokaryote level.

subject: MICR
title: Microbial Physiology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Components and metabolism of the bacterial cell; emphasis on techniques of analysis of metabolism and molecular structure.

subject: MICR
title: Immunology
description: Structure and biological actions of antigens and antibodies; fundamentals of antibody synthesis; the relation of immunology to biology and medical sciences.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 or BIOL 171 , or consent. Recommended: BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L .

subject: MICR
title: Immunology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Basic exercises and experiments in immunology, immunochemistry, immuno-biology to illustrate principles of MICR 461 .

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology of Pathogens
description: Host-parasite relationships in microbial diseases of humans and animals with emphasis on bacterial pathogens.

subject: MICR
title: Microbiology of Pathogens Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Characterization of bacterial pathogens. Isolation, identification, and diagnosis. This course develops written communication skills.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis
description: Fundamental mechanisms of bacterial infectious diseases or pathogenesis at the molecular level. Emphasis on bacterial virulence and host-pathogen interactions.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Molecular Pathogenesis Laboratory
description: Modern techniques to study infectious diseases. Covers tissue culture and animal models to study virulence of extracellular and intracellular infecting bacteria, bacterial resistance mechanisms toward antibacterial drugs, and virulence factor assays.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics
description: Genetic analysis and molecular basis of transmission replication, mutation, and expression of heritable characteristics in prokaryotes.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of transfer and expression of prokaryotic genes: transformation, conjugation, transposon mutagenesis, preparation and analysis of plasmid and chromosomal DNA. This course develops written communication skills.

subject: MICR
title: Microbes and Their Environment
description: Distribution, diversity, and roles of microorganisms in terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems. Importance of bacteria in pesticide degradation, bioremediation of oil spills, sewage treatment, biocontrol, food fermentation.

subject: MICR
title: Microbes and Their Environment Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of interaction of microorganisms with and within their natural habitats; symbiosis between microorganisms and plants and animals; role of microorganisms in element cycling; food fermentation by bacteria.

subject: MICR
title: Virology
description: Basic principles of virus biology. Topics include methods for virus study, virus structure, replication, gene expression, pathogenesis and host response.

subject: MICR
title: Virology Lab
description: (2 3-hr Lab) General laboratory techniques and related theories in virology; including isolation, cell culture, assay, purification, and identification of viruses.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 / MICR 351L or BIOL 275 / BIOL 275L and MICR 490 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Molecular Cell Biology
description: Provide fundamental concepts and dynamic characteristics of the molecules of the prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell, their biosynthesis and regulation, and the mechanisms that regulate cellular activities.
prereq_raw: basic course in cell and molecular biology, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Molecular Biology and Genetics
description: Graduate-level basic course on molecular biology and genetics. Prepares students to understand advanced concepts in related subjects such as biochemistry, cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, plant genetics, and genomics.
prereq_raw: MBBE 402 / BIOL 402 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or with consent from instructor.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B or higher ) , or with consent from instructor

subject: MICR
title: Research Ethics
description: Introduction to ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Moral reasoning, humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data and genetic technologies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in MICR or related field, or consent. MICR graduates only.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Immunology
description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature.

subject: MICR
title: Microbial Genome
description: Advanced studies of Microbial genome: relation to functional genomics, structural genomics, and proteomics.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 and one 400-level MICR course, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Microbial Physiology
description: Selected topics.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Marine Microbiology
description: Advanced studies of marine microorganisms in diverse habitats with consideration of applications of marine microbes, interactions with higher organisms, phylogeny and diversity, and past and current methods.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Virology
description: Detailed reports and discussions on selected advanced topics and current research literature.

subject: MICR
title: Regulations of Gene Expressions in Microorganisms
description: Use of bioinformatic tools to understand comparative genomics, metabolic pathways, and protein evolution.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 and one 400 level MICR course, or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Bacterial Genetics
description: Directed study and discussion of research literature on bacterial and bacterial virus mutation, genetic recombination, evolution and control mechanisms.
prereq_raw: graduate standing; undergraduates that have taken MICR 475 may register with consent.

children.text: undergraduates that have taken MICR 475 may register with consent

subject: MICR
title: Advances in Microbial Ecology
description: One topic area will be selected for in-depth study of microbial ecology, e.g. beneficial symbioses, responses to environmental changes, or interaction of microorganisms with abiotic and biotic components. Relevant, modern techniques will be discussed.

subject: MICR
title: Host-Parasite Relationships
description: Mechanisms of pathogenicity of microorganisms and defense mechanisms of human and animal hosts. Review of contemporary literature.

subject: MICR
title: Molecular and Cellular Bacterial Pathogenesis
description: Detailed examination of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of bacterial pathogenesis. Overview of key literature, synthesis of scientific problems into research proposals.
prereq_raw: MICR 431 , MICR 463 , or MICR 470 ; or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Seminar
description: Seminar required for Microbiology graduate students to present their research progress, practice their presentation skills and receive feedback to help with their research. Outside/faculty speakers broaden students’ knowledge and provide real-life examples.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Microbiology graduate students only.

subject: MICR
title: Research Literature Review
description: Review of primary literature in a selected area of microbiology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate status or consent.

subject: MICR
title: Directed Research
description: Selected problems in microbiology.

subject: MICR
title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B or better ) or consent

subject: MICR
title: Special Topics in Microbiology
description: Selected topics in any aspect of microbiology.

subject: MKT
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Research and Data Analytics
description: Use of marketing research and marketing management and data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: the research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; and digital media analytics.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Communications
description: In-depth coverage of the major communication tools used in marketing such as advertising, sales promotion, public relations and the internet. Emphasis on integrated marketing communications.

subject: MKT
title: Integrated Communication Campaigns
description: Management of integrated marketing communications campaigns. Includes: conducting target market and competitor research, developing creative content and media strategies, production of communication materials and completion of major real world project.

subject: MKT
title: Retailing Management
description: Analysis of opportunities and challenges in physical and digital retailing management: physical layout and digital design; merchandise planning; organizational forms; expense analysis; integration of physical/digital programs.

subject: MKT
title: Sales and Sales Management
description: Delves into selling and the sales management process. Through a variety of activities, students experience applying selling techniques, sales planning, recruiting and training salespeople, methods of motivating and compensating, territory management and sales team communications.

subject: MKT
title: Professional Selling
description: Emphasis on selling technique, social-psychological principles of persuasion, and interpersonal communication. Lecture, discussion, and application of relevant principles and techniques. Includes an emphasis on instruction and feedback in oral communication.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Marketing
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of marketing.
prereq_raw: BUS 312 and usually senior standing, or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Digital Marketing
description: Provides comprehensive understanding of digital marketing’s growing role in new product development; marketing research; direct sales; and marketing communications. Students learn multiple digital tools for analysis of customer behavior. Real-world projects provide opportunities for application.

subject: MKT
title: Customer Relationship Management
description: Focuses on the evolving field of customer relationship management. Students learn how to manage marketing information and decision-making systems that maximize customer retention and build long-term relationships.

subject: MKT
title: Sustainable Marketing
description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing for New Ventures
description: Examines role of marketing in the formation and launch of entrepreneurial ventures within and outside of ongoing businesses. Emphasis on new product development and low cost, high impact marketing activities.

subject: MKT
title: International Marketing
description: Principles and topics related to international marketing, with emphasis on strategic planning and applications.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Strategies
description: Decision-making by the marketing executive; integration of all elements of the marketing program based on actual business situations.
prereq_raw: MKT 311 , MKT 321 , and BUS 312 ; or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Analytics
description: Introduces current quantitative techniques and analytical approaches to better marketing decision-making. Students learn how to solve problems in a data-driven way using software tools.

subject: MKT
title: New Product Innovation and Development
description: Innovation/development processes critical to successful new products. Emphasis on existing larger businesses. Students gain experience in bringing new products from creative idea generation to market launch.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing.

subject: MKT
title: Consumer Behavior for Managers
description: Designed to help students better understand how consumers process information, form attitudes, and make decisions. Draws on theories from social sciences to help students manage consumer needs and satisfaction.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MKT
title: Sales Leadership
description: Sales managers participate in diverse activities including hiring, designing and implementing training programs, in-field coaching and development, motivating and compensating employees, and team building. Helps students develop knowledge and skills in these areas.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: MKT
title: Advanced Marketing Management
description: A case course in the application of advanced marketing methods.

subject: MKT
title: Japanese Marketing Systems
description: Specialized study of Japanese marketing systems, considers both global and domestic marketing activities in the context of the Japanese economy.

subject: MKT
title: International Marketing Management
description: Integrated and comparative approach to international marketing management. Emphasis on the development of a competitive strategy in a global environment. Applications to both developing and industrialized markets.

subject: MKT
title: Strategic Brand Management
description: The study of branding and brand management. Explores how managers can formulate and implement integrated marketing strategies to build brand equity. Includes relevant theory and real world applications.

subject: MKT
title: Marketing Research Management
description: Examines use of marketing research/data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; digital media analytics. Real world project reinforce learning.

subject: MKT
title: Creativity in Marketing
description: Thought processes that relate to creativity. Through a series of exercises, students experience enriched creativity and enhanced communication skills.

subject: MKT
title: Services Marketing
description: Conceptual understanding of distinctive aspects of services, services management, and services research.

subject: MKT
title: Digital Marketing Management
description: Examines digital marketing’s role in new product development; direct sales; marketing communications via the internet, social media, and mobile devices; and digital tools such as online tracking and analysis. Real activities provide opportunities for application.

subject: MKT
title: Patient Centered Communication Management in Health Care Organizations
description: Provides training on managing patient communications in general and shared decision making in particular. Increases ability to use tools available to improve patient-provider decision making quality and satisfaction.

subject: MKT
title: Advanced Seminar in Marketing
description: Significant topics, problems in marketing.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Marketing Theory
description: Focuses on the building blocks of theory, their use, and evolution within a marketing context. Explores marketing theories, theory construction, and the creation of marketing knowledge.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Consumer Behavior
description: Focuses on consumer behavior theory. Provides in-depth review of important published work in traditional and cross-cultural consumer behavior fields.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Marketing Strategy
description: Focuses on theories of strategic marketing and planning. Explores the theoretical principles of marketing concepts, tools, and processes that can be used to help an organization develop a sustainable competitive advantage.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Seminar in Selected Marketing Topics
description: Selected topics in any aspect of marketing to increase exposure to the range of issues researchers commonly confront.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in business administration or consent.

subject: MKT
title: Directed Research
description: Reading and research in an area of marketing under the direction of faculty member(s).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD student status in international management or consent.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Physical Fitness
description: Hands-on participatory course following the Army’s physical fitness program. Classes conducted three days per week with Army ROTC cadets. Focus is on aerobic conditioning, muscular strength and endurance.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science I
description: Introduces cadets to personal challenges and competencies critical for effective leadership; personal development of life skills such as goal setting, time management, physical fitness, and stress management related to leadership, officership, and the Army profession. Focus on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of Army Leadership Dimensions while understanding the ROTC program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science I Lab
description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II
description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feedback and using effective writing skills. Explores leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Cadre role models and building stronger relationships among cadets through common experience and practical interaction are critical.

subject: MSL
title: Introduction to Military Science II Lab
description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

subject: MSL
title: Intermediate Military Science I
description: Explores creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles through historical case studies and engaging in interactive student exercises. Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building by planning, executing, and assessing team exercises. Focus is on continued development of leadership values and attributes through understanding of rank, uniform, customs and courtesies.

subject: MSL
title: Intermediate Military Science II
description: Challenges of leading complex, contemporary operational environments. Dimensions of cross-cultural challenges of leadership in a constantly changing world are highlighted and applied to practical Army leadership tasks and situations. Cadets develop greater self awareness as they practice communication and team building skills, and tactics in real world scenarios. Provides a smooth transition to MSL 301 .

subject: MSL
title: ROTC Basic Camp
description: Four-week summer course conducted at Ft. Knox, Kentucky. Substitutes for ROTC basic course ( MSL 101 , MSL 102 , MSL 201 , and MSL 202 ) and fulfills course requirement for admission to ROTC advanced courses. Credit will be given for MSL 203 or basic courses, but not both.

subject: MSL
title: Leading Small Organizations I
description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills with demands of the ROTC Advanced Camp. Challenging scenarios related to small unit tactical operations will develop self-awareness and critical thinking skills. Cadets will receive systematic, specific feedback on their leadership abilities, and analyze/evaluate their leadership values, attributes, skills and actions.
prereq_raw: MSL 101 , MSL 102 , MSL 201 , and MSL 202 ; or MSL 203 ; or consent.

subject: MSL
title: Leading Small Organizations II
description: (2 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Intense situational leadership challenges to build awareness and skills in leading small units. Decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members under fire are explored, evaluated, and developed. Military operations are reviewed to prepare for the ROTC Advance Camp. Cadets apply principles of Law of Land Warfare, Army training, and motivation to troop leading procedures; and are evaluated on what they know and do as leaders.

subject: MSL
title: ROTC Advanced Camp
description: Five-week summer field training exercise conducted at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Arduous and intensified leadership training is conducted throughout the five-week period. Required for U.S. Army commissioning.

subject: MSL
title: History of Military Warfare
description: Lecture/ discussion on the art and science of warfare concentrating on U.S. military history from the Colonial Period to present. Generally restricted to Army ROTC students, requiring twenty pages of graded writing assignments.

subject: MSL
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Limited to military science students who have had at least one previous military science course for which a grade of B or higher was earned and a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better.

subject: MSL
title: Fundamentals of Leadership
description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of leadership. Activities challenge students to connect theory to practice, develop positive relationships through application of effective leadership concepts with emphasis on teaching writing for personal development and team-building.

subject: MSL
title: Leadership Challenges and Goal Setting
description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Develops proficiency in planning, execution, and assessment of complex operations; students will learn to assess risk, make ethical decisions, function as a staff member, and provide leadership performance feedback to subordinates; emphasis on oral communication.

subject: MSL
title: Transition to Lieutenant
description: (3 Lec, 2-hr Lab) Explores dynamics of leading in complex situations of current military operations. Examines differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism. Interaction with non-government organizations, civilians on the battlefield, and host nation support are examined and evaluated. Case studies, scenarios, and What Now, Lieutenant? exercises prepare cadets to lead as commissioned officers in the U.S. Army.

subject: MSL
title: Advanced Military Research
description: Directs the student to conduct detailed research on a military topic and present to the department leadership plus assist MSL 400 series students on a battle analysis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Must be in Military Science and Leadership Program or Military Service member in junior or greater standing.

subject: MUS
title: Electronic Music
description: Basic techniques of electronic sound synthesis.

subject: MUS
title: Audio Recording/Mixing/Sound Design
description: Preproduction, mixing, setup and recording suitable for film. Mixing techniques in software for small systems. Sound design using original synthesis techniques to enhance film and support stories.

subject: MUS
title: Digital Audio Synthesis and Multimedia Applications
description: Sound control through graphical interfaces. Advanced digital audio synthesis techniques. Audio control of graphics and video. Introduction of alternate controllers.

subject: MUS
title: Western Music and Japan
description: Historical survey of Western music in Japan from modernization through the Meiji Restoration up to the present. Topics include: Western-style symphonic music, J-pop, and Enka by Japanese artists; develops written communication skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: MUS
title: Marching Band Design and Techniques
description: Design and techniques for the modern field marching band.

subject: MUS
title: Integrating World Music in Education
description: Application of musical concepts through an integrated approach. This includes strategies, world music, literature, materials and resources for the classroom curriculum.

subject: MUS
title: General Music Methods
description: Required for K-12 music specialists. Scope and nature of music in the lives of children and adolescents; planning, teaching, learning, and evaluating music in elementary, middle, and high school curriculum.
prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 288 , or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

subject: MUS
title: General Music Methods Lab
description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in general music classrooms. Supervised 40 hours of field experiences required.
prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 288 ; or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Music Methods
description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of instrumental music in schools.
prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Instrumental Music Methods Lab
description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in instrumental settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required.
prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Music Methods
description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of choral music in schools.
prereq_raw: MUS 122B , MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MUS ED majors only, or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Choral Music Methods Lab
description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in choral settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required.
prereq_raw: MUS 250 , MUS 286 , and MUS 326 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Piano Pedagogy
description: Concepts, materials, and procedures for class and individual instruction in piano. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

subject: MUS
title: Piano Pedagogy
description: Continuation of MUS 358 . Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

subject: MUS
title: Music in Film
description: Lecture investigating the role of music in narrative film, and developing critical skills through close study. Understanding styles, techniques and aesthetics of film music in historical contexts. Significant attention paid to developing writing skills.

subject: MUS
title: Curtain Up! Broadway Musicals, Then and Now
description: Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the “Hamilton” phenomenon, exploring their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. Course develops written communication skills.

subject: MUS
title: Superstars: A History of Musical Celebrity
description: Explores how the cultural phenomenon of celebrity has impacted musicians and composers from antiquity to the present.

subject: MUS
title: Music in Modern America
description: Varieties of music, including jazz and other popular forms; relevant antecedents.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing; freshmen with consent only.

subject: MUS
title: Counterpoint
description: Form, texture, and style in music literature from Renaissance to present. Formal analysis and writing. Contrapuntal textures and forms.

subject: MUS
title: Form and Analysis
description: Form, texture, and style in music literature from Renaissance to present. Formal analysis and writing. Larger forms with various textures; recent contemporary approaches to continuity.

subject: MUS
title: Orchestration
description: Basic principles of scoring for orchestra and band; instrumental ranges, timbres, transpositions; transcribing or composing for band, orchestra, and chorus.

subject: MUS
title: Theory and Practice of Jazz Improvisation
description: Development of an improvising technique through analysis and performance practice. For instrumentalists only.

subject: MUS
title: Directed Study
description: Limited to majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in music.

subject: MUS
title: Topics in Music
description: Topics in history, literature, theory, applied music, music education, and ethnomusicology; for music majors. Consult department for topics and specific dates.
prereq_raw: MUS 281 and appropriate lower division music courses; or consent.

subject: MUS
title: Music Cultures of the World
description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific, representative styles and regional characteristics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership Laboratory
description: Laboratory instruction will include leadership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed for students pursuing Navy and Marine Corps commissions.

subject: NAVL
title: Introduction to Naval Science
description: Overview of the Navy’s mission, customs, traditions, and the duties required of Junior Officers. Provides students with a basic knowledge of damage control, shipboard organization, and safety procedures prior to their first summer training cruise.

subject: NAVL
title: Seapower and Maritime Affairs
description: Study of the Navy and the influence of seapower upon history that incorporates both an historical and political perspective to explore major events and circumstances that have shaped a bold and proud history.

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership and Management
description: Comprehensive study of organizational behavior and management with a special emphasis on situational leadership in the Navy. Exploration of a variety of leadership and management topics, including classical theories of management, motivation, and communication.

subject: NAVL
title: Navigation
description: Designed to provide midshipmen with an in-depth study of the theory, principles, procedures, and application of plotting, piloting, and electronic navigation, as well as an introduction to maneuvering boards.

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ships System I: Engineering
description: Will learn ship design and control, hydrodynamic forces, stability, electrical theory, and damage control coupled with design of steam, gas turbine and nuclear propulsion. Case studies merging both ethical and technical challenges.

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Ship Systems II: Weapons
description: Outlines the theory and employment of naval warship weapons systems. Supplemented with review/ analysis of case studies involving the moral and ethical responsibilities of leaders in the employment of weapons.

subject: NAVL
title: Evolution of Warfare
description: Focuses on enhancing students’ writing abilities through an in-depth examination of the historical foundations of contemporary warfighting theories, encompassing philosophies, domains, tactics, and technology.

subject: NAVL
title: Fundamentals of Maneuver Warfare
description: Embark in a writing and oral-focused exploration of the USMC as the premiere Maneuver Warfighting Organization. Delve into theoretical concepts and historical examples, examining foundational principles through written analysis and oral discussion.

subject: NAVL
title: United States Pacific Fleet Internship
description: Leadership development, teamwork, and activities designed for NROTC students. Learn how to write a federal resume, be a Federal Employee, and learn the skills needed to complete and present their U.S. Pacific Fleet capstone project.
prereq_raw: NAVL 100L , NAVL 101 , NAVL 102 , NAVL 201 , NAVL 202 , NAVL 303 , NAVL 304 , or NAVL 402 .

subject: NAVL
title: Naval Operations and Seamanship
description: Study of U.S. Navy ships professional and efficient operations. Lecture series on Fleet communications, tactical employment, relative motion plotting, seamanship, Joint Warfare, and employment of naval forces as an element of National Security.

subject: NAVL
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Introduces ethical theories in discussion-based formats, fostering understanding of diverse moral, ethical, and leadership philosophies. Enhances moral character, awareness of ethical decision-making tools, and addresses contemporary dilemmas through discussion, written journaling, and a research paper.

subject: NHH
title: E Malama i Ke Ola Loko: The Practice of Self-Care and Wellness from a Kānaka Maoli Perspective
description: An examination of self-care and wellness models from a Native Hawaiian perspective, exploration of self-care as lahui care, and practical application of wellness through ʻaina-based education.

subject: NHH
title: Applied Health Disparities Research
description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

subject: NHH

subject: NREM

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program students only.

subject: NREM
title: Introduction to Natural Resources and Environmental Management
description: Introduction to NREM student learning outcomes and scholarly breadth within the department, exposure to on-campus resources, networking with current and former NREM students and external stakeholders, career skills development.

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Service Learning II
description: Experiential service learning course for students participating in the Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program as Hana Hou members. Hawaiʻi Youth Conservation Corps summer program students only.

subject: NREM
title: Applied Calculus for Management, Life Sciences, and Human Resilience
description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Applications of calculus (limits, continuity, derivatives, exponential and logarithmic functions, partials, integrals) to problems in business management, social sciences, and life sciences. Applies symbolic techniques and quantitative methods in problem solving, utilizes concept of proof as a chain of inferences, and promotes development of reasoning skills and mathematical logic in bridging theory and practice.

subject: NREM
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: NREM
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

subject: NREM
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: NREM
title: Internship Preparation
description: Exploration of internship and career opportunities for NREM majors. Development of career-building skills, including resume, interview, and professional networking.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only.

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Management
description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
prereq_raw: ( NREM 251 / TPSS 251 or NREM 210 ; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Management Lab
description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory and field methods covering biological and physical principles and concepts in natural resource management. Emphasis on basic field measurement techniques, computer skills commonly used in managing natural resources and writing scientific lab reports.
prereq_raw: NREM 192 with a minimum grade of C-.

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawaiʻi state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues.
prereq_raw: NREM 210 / PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or NREM 251 / SOCS 251 / TPSS 251 or ( BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or ( ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM 220 / SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.

subject: NREM
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science
description: Origin, development, properties, management of tropical soils; classification of Hawaiian soils.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Minimum prerequisite grade of C or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science Laboratory
description: Field and analytical methods for exploring the origin, development, properties, and management of soils, with an emphasis on tropical and Hawaiian soils.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
prereq_raw: NREM 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103 .

subject: NREM
title: Statistics in Agriculture and Human Resources
description: Theory, applications, and presentation of statistical reasoning. Descriptive, probability, and inferential reasoning for one-variable analysis with extensions to multiple variable cases.

subject: NREM
title: Current Topics in Plant Science
description: An undergraduate seminar that provides the presentation and discussion of topics of current relevance to students preparing for careers in applied plant sciences. Oral focus designation.
prereq_raw: NREM 210 or TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Managerial Accounting
description: Principles and methods of agricultural accounting. Preparing and interpreting financial statements. Sources and costs of credit, capital budgeting, tax management, estate planning.
prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Enterprise Management
description: Introduction of practical concepts and methods used in business management. Introduce broad range of business strategies. Understand the critical role each strategy plays. Facilitate student’s practice of analytical and critical thinking through case studies.

subject: NREM
title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.
prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Tropical Forestry/Agroforestry
description: Biophysical and socioeconomic description and analysis of major tropical forestry and agroforestry management systems, including Hawaiʻi and the Pacific Basin. The role of traditional land use, pressures from regional and global development, and efforts to create sustainable, diverse systems for rural communities will be discussed.
prereq_raw: CHEM 151 or higher and BIOL 171 or higher.

subject: NREM
title: Directed Study
description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students qualified to carry on advanced study.

subject: NREM
title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Biochemistry
description: Biochemical and chemical principles of occurrence, distribution, biotic and abiotic conversion, fate, and impact of synthetic and natural molecules in the environment. Important pollutants will be used as case studies to illustrate the principles.

subject: NREM
title: Community and Natural Resource Management
description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
prereq_raw: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

prereq_raw: NREM 220 / SUST 220 or ECON 130 , and SUST 310 or ECON 321 ; or consent.

subject: NREM

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: NREM

subject: NREM

subject: NREM

prereq_raw: ( TPSS 304 and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Soil and Water Conservation
description: Past and present issues in soil and water conservation will be examined. Principles of erosion, conservation tillage, irrigation, and drainage will be discussed. Land-based threats to coastal zones and watershed management will also be covered.

subject: NREM
title: Irrigation and Water Management
description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality.
prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 ( or equivalent), or consent

subject: NREM
title: Natural Resources Conservation Planning
description: Combined lecture and hands-on field course on theory and practice of natural resource conservation planning. Includes individual and group projects.
prereq_raw: Recommended: at least one upper division course in soils, natural resources, planning, physical geography, or related area; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: undergraduate junior or senior or graduate standing.

children.text: Recommended: at least one upper division course in soils, natural resources, planning, physical geography,

subject: NREM
title: Plant Nutrient Diagnosis in the Tropics
description: Designed for students to identify essential nutrients required by plants; diagnose nutrient disorders in plants; and propose environmentally sound solutions to correct disorders.

subject: NREM
title: Geographic Information Systems for Resource Managers
description: Combined lecture-lab on the basic concepts and principles of geographic information systems, remote sensing, and global positioning system. Practical skills to be developed by solving real natural resources and environmental problems.
prereq_raw: either NREM 203 (or concurrent) or NREM 310 (or concurrent), and NREM 301 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Applied Forest Ecology
description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).
prereq_raw: ( NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 380 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Hoʻokâhua: ʻāina Based Leadership Education (ABLE)
description: Hoʻokâhua: is an ʻāina based leadership course encompassing Hawaiian culture, Environmental Science, Law & Policy, Planning and Community Development to equip students to care for, guard, and govern natural resources they care about.

subject: NREM
title: Topics in Natural Resources and Environmental Management
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: NREM
title: Internship Experience
description: Internship work experience for NREM majors. Completion of writing assignments with a minimum of 4,000 words.

subject: NREM
title: Environmental Problem Solving
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Senior-level capstone for NREM. Ecosystem management within problem-solving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Directed Study
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing and consent.

subject: NREM
title: Foundations of Natural Resource and Environmental Management and Policy
description: Critical evaluation of environmental and social components of NREM and policy. Students develop research skills and integrative knowledge important for all resource managers in, e.g., ecology, applied economics, hydrology, policy/management, soils, and human dimensions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Social-Ecological Systems Analysis of Natural Resource and Environmental Management
description: Case study approach to building the structural and behavioral framework for complex, dynamic systems underlying sustainable NREM and policy, emphasizing the transdisciplinary interactions of the ecological and economic components.
prereq_raw: NREM 600 (with a minimum grade of B-), and ( ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and BIOL 171 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and ( ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and BIOL 171 ) with a minimum grade of C , or consent

subject: NREM
title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

subject: NREM
title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
prereq_raw: grade of C- or above in ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
prereq_raw: NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

subject: NREM
title: Kaiaulu: Care and Collaborative Management of Natural Resources
