description: Engagement with theory and practice of collaboration to care for natural resources. Topics include community based management, common property, Hawaiian knowledge, co-management, and access through readings, discussion, and projects with Hawaiʻi communities.

subject: NREM
title: ʻImi ʻIke: Social Science Field Methods for Environmental Research
description: Students learn and apply social science research methods tailored to natural resource management and environmental issues to a class project with Hawaiʻi community. Emphasis on qualitative and participatory approaches.

subject: NREM
title: Applied Microeconomic Analysis
description: Economic applications to the agricultural and nonagricultural industries are emphasized. Econometric techniques are used to estimate demand, supply, production and cost functions which are analyzed in terms of economic theory and market information.

subject: NREM
title: Sustainable Agriculture Seminar
description: Critical evaluation of existing and alternative cropping systems from a long-term perspective. Value conflicts and resolution.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing, and consent.

subject: NREM
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

subject: NREM
title: Land Systems Science
description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socioecological system function.
prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461 .

subject: NREM
title: Soil Plant Nutrient Relations
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Soil-plant interactions, emphasis on characteristics of tropical soils and plants influencing nutrient uptake by plants. Diagnostic methods to identify nutrient deficiencies and element toxicity.
prereq_raw: TPSS 450 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or consent

subject: NREM
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

subject: NREM
title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

subject: NREM
title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

subject: NREM
title: Watershed Hydrology
description: Theory and application of basic hydrologic processes and management occurring on small islands watersheds.
prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and PHYS 151 (or equivalent) and NREM 477 or GEO 388 (or equivalent); or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and PHYS 151 ( or equivalent) and NREM 477 or GEO 388 ( or equivalent); or consent

subject: NREM
title: Small Watershed Modeling
description: Introduction to process-based modeling of watershed with emphasis on model applications. Deals with the characterization and simulation of small watershed hydrolic and pollutant transport processes.
prereq_raw: CEE 424 (or concurrent) or ERTH 425 / SUST 425 (or concurrent) or BS degree from NREM, or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Coastal Resources Management
description: Study of coastal systems, estuaries, and coral reefs. Emphasis on interdisciplinary science and integration of coastal ecology, geoscience, and social science. Coastal and marine wildlife-human interactions, environmental pertubations, and management strategies will be discussed.
prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate course work in marine biology, oceanography, geoscience, and sustainability recommended.

children.text: advanced undergraduate course work in marine biology, oceanography, geoscience,

subject: NREM
title: People and the Sea: Exploring Multiple Perspectives for Coastal and Marine Systems
description: Through readings and discussion, this course explores how the social sciences have engaged in marine and coastal spaces and how they contribute to advancing effective and equitable resource management and conservation.

subject: NREM
title: Interdisciplinary Methods for Agrarian Systems
description: Interdisciplinary methodologies for conducting research and impact analyses on agrarian systems, sustainable development, and resource management.

subject: NREM
title: International Agricultural Systems
description: Analysis of trends and strategies in international agricultural research and development. International agricultural research centers (IARC), Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), university networks and consortia, and private voluntary organizations (PVOs).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing, and consent.

subject: NREM
title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
description: Fundamentals, techniques, and applications of remote sensing for natural resource assessments and environmental monitoring. Lab consisting of field radiometric exercises, computer modeling of energy-matter interaction, processing, and analysis of remotely sensed imagery.
prereq_raw: one physics course (e.g. PHYS 151 ), one calculus course (e.g. NREM 203 ), and one statistics course (e.g. NREM 310 ), or consent. Recommended: either GEO 470 or ERTH 460 or one introductory remote sensing course.

children.text: ) , one calculus course ( e.g. NREM 203 ) , and one statistics course ( e.g. NREM 310 ) , or consent . Recommended: either GEO 470 or ERTH 460 or one introductory remote sensing course

subject: NREM
title: Ecosystem Ecology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of ecosystem ecology with emphasis on tropical forests, human impacts, and global environmental change. Factors controlling ecosystem structure, productivity, nutrient cycling, plant-soil-atmosphere interactions, and energy balance. Field and laboratory methods in ecosystem science.
prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate coursework in ecology and soil science; graduate standing; and consent.

subject: NREM
title: Restoration Ecology
description: Graduate seminar on foundations of restoration ecology, application of ecological theory to restoration practice. Emphasis on restoration of structure and function in degraded terrestrial ecosystems using case studies from Hawaiʻi and around the world.
prereq_raw: advanced undergraduate ecology course and graduate standing, or consent. Completion of NREM 680 recommended, but not required.

children.text: Completion of NREM 680 recommended, but not required

subject: NREM
title: Landscape Ecology
description: Focuses on the history, theories, and contemporary views of landscapes; including scale, land cover, land use, landscape metrics, disturbance regimes, land management, landscape change, the relationship of landscapes to species, and modeling.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate students, or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Conservation Biology
description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.

subject: NREM
title: Advanced Topics in Natural Resources and Environmental Management
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: NREM
title: Capstone Preparation in NREM
description: Preparation for NREM Master’s Plan B capstone experience.
prereq_raw: NREM 600 and NREM 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and one graduate methods course (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and one graduate methods course (or concurrent)

subject: NREM
title: Capstone Experience in NREM
description: Capstone experience in NREM.
prereq_raw: ( NREM 695 and NREM 601 ) with a minimum grade of B-, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only.

subject: NREM
title: Directed Research
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: NREM
title: Research Seminar
description: Presentation and discussion of student research proposals, theses and dissertations, and research presentations by NREM faculty, students, and invited speakers.

subject: NSCI
title: Natural Sciences and Life-Pulling the Puzzles Apart
description: Journey through the Natural Sciences finding fun, excitement, and success in science, mathematics, engineering, medicine, and all that is the natural sciences. Focus upon challenging worldviews of belief, invention, impact, and ethics.

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar for Science Teachers
description: Seminar and discussions of current and significant topics and problems in science where teachers can exchange new and innovative teaching ideas and strategies.

subject: NSCI
title: Computers in Classroom
description: Combined lecture, laboratory and discussion on the use of computers as a teaching tool in the classroom. To be taught in a hands-on manner appropriate for the science teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Mathematics Workshop for Teachers
description: An in-depth study of topics from intermediate and high school mathematics. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

subject: NSCI
title: Seminar on Science Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods; organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audio-visual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

subject: NSEB
title: National Student Exchange
description: Study at another campus through National Student Exchange (NSE). Transfer credits earned upon successful completion of courses on exchange.
repeatable_raw: 1 time at same host campus. Unlimited times at different host campuses.
grade_option_raw: CR/NC only. Credits to be granted in transfer upon successful completion of course work at exchange institution.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing I
description: This first level course focuses on nursing practice and education. Professional responsibilities in the practice of nursing are emphasized.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Professional Nursing II
description: This second level course builds on the knowledge and skills gained in the first level and focuses on professional responsibilities in nursing practice and education.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan
description: Focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. It introduces the nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. Introduces nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing
description: Professional responsibilities of nursing practice are examined through the history of nursing, practice and education, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, and nursing roles.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology
description: Focus on pathophysiological concepts that are basic to understanding illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human responses, which serve as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nursing
description: This course will help students to gain knowledge of the mechanism of action, toxicity, adverse reactions, side effects, therapeutic uses, and nursing implications of the major categories of drugs.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I
description: Focuses on nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness.
prereq_raw: NURS 210 , NURS 210L , and NURS 212 , or departmental approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness I Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on using nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. Nursing skills are integrated into clinical experiences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Health Promotion
description: Provides an introduction to the HSNC Competencies and spiraling of concepts and is based on the assumption of student responsibility for learning. Emphasis on writing instruction, and research evidence to support nursing care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Statistics in Nursing Research
description: Focuses on the basic concepts and applications of statistics as applied to nursing research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, family-centered care. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health
description: Nursing care and health promotion for children and families. Emphasis on concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Child and Family Health Lab
description: Nursing care and health promotion lab for children and families. Application of concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Health Care
description: Explore contemporary ethical issues and their legal implications in health care. Focus on decision-making in professional practice and social policy formation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology: Its Nursing Implications
description: Explores attitudes toward the aged, biological and psychological aspects, ethnicity, sexuality, nutritional problems, community resources, other related topics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing in the Multicultural Milieu
description: Relates values, beliefs, attitudes, family organization, lifestyles, and health practices in different ethnic groups to health-care and nursing practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III
description: Focuses on complex situations requiring strong recognition skills, and rapid decision making. The evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.
prereq_raw: NURS 321 , NURS 321L , NURS 322 , and NURS 322L , or departmental approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Illness III Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on complex situations requiring application of strong recognition skills and rapid decision making. Evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Education and Promotion
description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups, and the larger public.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Nursing Research
description: Introduction to the research process and an understanding of the applicability of the scientific approach to nursing. Analysis and resolution of contemporary medical ethics issues in research and general nursing practice are primary focuses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Nursing Research and Evidence-Based Practice
description: Introduces the process for research application and evidence-based practice. Includes: EBP questions, evidence sources, literature search and synthesis, levels and quality of evidence, and determination of clinical significance. Focus on contemporary medical ethics issues.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.

subject: NURS
title: Student Ambassador Program
description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of Nursing and alumni, prospective students, and the general public.
prereq_raw: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

prereq_tree.text: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

subject: NURS
title: NCLEX Review
description: Overview of the NCLEX-RN licensure examination and regular, systematic practice in taking multiple choice examinations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Cooperative Education in Nursing
description: A two-semester course with seminar in professional role development in addition to paid work experience in nursing at a local agency. Upper division
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Internship
description: Practicum experience for students to learn the role of the professional nurse by building on previously learned knowledge and skills in the nursing program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies
description: Survey of complementary and alternative therapies used for health promotion of individuals and groups.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Open to non-nursing majors with consent.

subject: NURS
title: Veteran Healthcare, Education, and Cultural Needs
description: Provides a broad overview of the Veteran-Military population and their unique culture, educational, and health care needs. Open to non-nursing majors.

subject: NURS
title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society. Junior standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing
description: Theory course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing Lab
description: Clinical course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local, national, and international levels. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Population Health Nursing
description: Theory on population and global health nursing with emphasis on analysis of strategies to address concepts of health disparities, inequity, social justice issues, and ethics which impact health outcomes of populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: NURS
title: Population Health Nursing Lab
description: Clinic on population health nursing emphasizing application of strategies to address health disparities, inequity, social justice issues, and ethics impacting population health outcomes. Emphasis on oral and writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Cultural Aspects of Health Management in Populations Indigenous to Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia
description: Focuses on cultural aspects that influence health management in indigenous populations of Hawaiʻi, the Pacific, and Asia, with an emphasis on development of culturally sensitive strategies to promote and improve health management.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Undergraduate majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Genetics and Genomics in Nursing Practice
description: Fundamentals of genetics and genomics, including principles of inheritance in humans, cellular function, mutations, epigenetics, and implications for health and disease. Includes overview of topics involving genetics/genomics in clinical settings and health care delivery.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Complex Nursing and Leadership
description: Theory course emphasizes the judgments, knowledge, and skills necessary for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. The experience focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Complex Nursing and Leadership Lab
description: Clinical course emphasizes application of knowledge and skills for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. Focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Pathophysiology
description: Provides an advanced understanding of pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying human illness across the lifespan. Provides a foundation for formulating clinical decisions and therapeutic plans of care to promote disease prevention and health promotion.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN
description: Theory focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN Field Work
description: Field work focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
description: Examination of human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing Lab
description: Application of the nursing process involving human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing and Leadership Immersion
description: Nursing theory course designed to enhance proficiency in complex clinical judgments, interprofessional team collaboration, and leadership. Focus is on knowledge and skills needed for nursing practice, including case management and quality management.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing and Leadership Immersion Lab
description: Clinical nursing course develops proficiency in complex clinical judgments, interprofessional team collaboration, and leadership skills in nursing. Application of knowledge, incorporation of case management and quality management experiences, and writing instruction are highlighted.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Honors Research Project
description: Involves directed, mentored research study for Nursing Honors students with their honors advisor. The course grade depends on meeting objectives negotiated each course semester.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Planned individualized study or research in specialized area related to interprofessional collaborative practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Senior undergraduate NURS students only.

subject: NURS
title: Professionalism in Nursing
description: Introduction to history of nursing and leaders in the field. Will explore contemporary nursing issues and research. Strategies to foster adherence to a professional code of ethics in practice will be examined.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology
description: Web-enhanced on pathophysiologic concepts as a basis of illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human response, which serves as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nursing Practice
description: Essential principles of pharmacology using a pathophysiologic approach with emphasis on administering medications and evaluating their effects.
coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 504 , NURS 504L , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Assessment
description: Concepts/theories of health assessment, data collection, and analysis to distinguish between health/wellness, risk factors or health deviations across the lifespan. Attention to principles of communication and interviewing.
coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 503 , NURS 504L , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Assessment Lab
description: Application of assessment skills in dry lab and clinical settings, with attention to principles of communication, interviewing and physical examination skills.
coreq_raw: NURS 501 , NURS 502 , NURS 503 , NURS 504 , NURS 505 , NURS 505L .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Foundations of Nursing Science
description: Nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Foundations of Nursing Science and Practice Lab
description: Application of the nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing
description: Biopsychosocial theories of human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; reviews current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing Clinic/ Lab
description: Application of current knowledge regarding human behavior related to function, alteration, and/ or disruption of mental processes; applies current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/ psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families
description: Introduction to the theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care of the perinatal family. Women’s and men’s health issues are discussed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families Clinical/Lab
description: Application of the nursing care of the mother and family. The student will apply clinical and theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care for women experiencing customary and complicated perinatal processes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Children and Families
description: Focus on well-child care and nursing care of children with acute and chronic conditions. Pediatric concepts include family-centered, developmentally appropriate, and atraumatic care. Lab course taken concurrently.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Care of Children and Families Clinical/Lab
description: Focus on well-child care and nursing care of children with acute and chronic conditions. Pediatric concepts include family-centered, developmentally appropriate, and atraumatic care. Critical thinking, clinical judgment, and EBP are applied.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Acute Care Nursing
description: Addresses the bio/ psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatment in the acute setting will be covered.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Acute Care Nursing Lab
description: Application of the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Application of health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatments in the acute care setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice
description: Examination of continuity of care for clients with complex needs. Emphasis on application of leadership, management, and quality improvement in the clinical setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice Lab
description: Deliver comprehensive nursing care to clients with complex needs in community and/or acute care settings. Leadership, management, and quality improvement competencies are stressed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing
description: Introduces community and public health nursing with an emphasis on application to nursing practice in the community and public health settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing Lab
description: Application of health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention and detection and nursing care treatments in the community setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

subject: NURS
title: Epidemiology for Advanced Nursing
description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods, with an emphasis on its application to nursing practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and prevention of common health and illness conditions with culturally diverse individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes didactic (30 hrs) and fieldwork (45 hrs).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: classified graduate student status in SONDH.

subject: NURS
title: Applied Biostatistics and Epidemiology for Nurses in Advance Practice
description: Investigation of epidemiologic and biostatistical methods for advance practice nurses within healthcare settings and complementary roles of epi/biostatistics in shaping advance nurse practice. Application of epi/biostatistical approaches to the design and analysis of DNP projects.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or permission.

subject: NURS
title: Genetics and Health Care
description: Addresses the scientific, psycho-social, ethical, cultural, and spiritual issues surrounding genetic disease, genetic testing, and living with an inherited condition.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Health Politics & Policy
description: Review of contemporary national health policies, issues and concerns; and international comparison of health policy evolution; includes didactic and 45 hours of fieldwork experience learning.

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Assessment and Diagnosis
description: Identification and synthesis of pertinent biopsychosocial and cultural data to complete advanced psychiatric-mental health assessments and diagnoses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning
description: Provides a framework for the development of advanced skills for systematic and comprehensive data collection, organization, precise recording, accurate assessment and communication of data reflecting the biopsychophysical status of individuals across the life span.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning Lab
description: Clinical lab and practicum for advanced practice nursing. Emphasis on integration of knowledge, skills and outcome evaluation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice
description: Provides an understanding of normal physiological mechanisms and pathological processes to serve as a foundation for clinical assessment, decision making, and clinical management across the lifespan.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrollment as a classified student in a graduate program in SONDH. NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Skills and Procedures for Advanced Practice Nursing
description: Clinical laboratory that focuses on clinical skills and procedures performed by advanced practice nurses (nurse practitioners and/or clinical nurse specialists). Topics will vary by section and semester.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS and NURD majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Mental Health in Primary Care
description: Augment APRN students’ understanding, evaluation, treatment plan development, and competence to care for patients with mental health and psychiatric disorders treatment plans across the lifespan in the primary care settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-A
description: The first of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.
prereq_raw: NURS 612 , NURS 612L , and NURS 613 ; no waiver.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-B
description: Second of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.
prereq_raw: NURS 612 , NURS 612L , and NURS 613 ; no waiver.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Emerging Diseases & Implications for Advanced Nursing Practice
description: Selected emerging diseases are examined within historical context, known science (past and present) and societal factors that influence prevention, detection, treatment and containment strategies. Considerations for advanced public health nursing practice are identified and examined.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Research, Theory, and Evidence-Based Practice
description: Examination of theory, research, and evidence-based inquiry to support evidence-based practice among MS prepared nurses.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: enrollment as a classified student in the graduate degree program in SONDH.

subject: NURS
title: Acute and Episodic Care Management
description: Diagnosis and management of health and illness with emphasis on clients with common acute/episodic conditions seen in context of family and community. Advanced practice nurse-client relationship, practice roles, and culturally relevant care are included.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Issues and Roles
description: Exploration of major issues and roles in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Survey of biopsychological bases of and biotherapies for major mental disorders, including the schizophrenias, affective and personality disorders, pediatric and geriatric problems, and neurological dysfunctions with appropriate applications to health care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Adolescent and Family Psychiatric- Mental Health Care
description: Seminar on theory/research in advanced psychiatric-mental health nursing of adolescents and families representing diverse populations. Emphasis on developmental and nursing theories, evidence-based practice, therapeutic modalities and disease management of psychiatric illness.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing Roles
description: Provides students with an understanding of different roles of the advanced professional nurse; an ability to proactively manage the environment of their specialty practice; includes 45 hours of field work experience.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Population Health Nursing
description: Introduction to the core competencies, key theoretical models and concepts that guide advanced population health nursing. The student will initiate their professional portfolio, which must be completed during the last semester of the MS program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Child/Family Health Assessment
description: (2 Sem, 8-hr Lab) Opportunity to develop specialized clinical competence in assessment of children as a basis for the development of clinical specialization. Development of the individual’s potential toward health maintenance functioning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Special Health Needs
description: Provides a theoretical basis required for specialized clinical competence in adapting recent findings on child/ parent assessments, social and health risk indicators, the role of environment, and multidisciplinary settings in the care of pediatrics.
prereq_raw: NURS 612 / NURS 612L , NURS 633 and NURS 634 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Pharmacology for Nurses in Advanced Practice
description: Prepares APNs to evaluate, monitor, and prescribe pharmaceuticals to treat acute and chronic illness across lifespan. Emphasis on drug indications, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, adverse effects, interactions, monitoring, education, and cost effectiveness. Enrollment as a classified student in a SONDH graduate degree program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Information Technology in Healthcare
description: Introduction to the use of information systems in healthcare. Selected information systems and data sets are explored with application of results to various patient populations and clinical practice settings.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Psychopharmacology Across the Lifespan
description: Examines the legal, ethical and therapeutic role of the psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioner (PMHNP) in prescribing psychotropic medications for diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Diverse biopsychosocial perspectives will be considered.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Therapeutic Modalities
description: Therapeutic modalities used in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Presents normal developmental, physiological and social needs of children within the context of family; then focuses on the management of common acute and chronic illnesses of children.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Child Health: Advanced Pediatric Acute/ Chronic Care
description: Focuses on the evaluation of pediatric clients with higher acuity and more complex management issues. Emphasizes critical analysis of evidence based research in pediatric health care.
prereq_raw: Admission into the PNP and FNP program; NURS 612 / NURS 612L , and NURS 633 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Women’s Health: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Provides a foundation of concepts necessary to maintain and promote women’s health, including developmental, physiological and social needs of women of all ages and the management of common health problems and concerns specific to women.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Women’s Health: Special Problem
description: (2 Sem, 12-hr Lab) Focuses upon assessment and intervention of at-risk and high-risk women during pregnancy, interconception, and the menopausal years. Emphasizes critical analysis of research in pregnancy, family planning, and common gynecological problems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Population Health Intervention Strategies for Advanced Nurses
description: Develops advanced skills and knowledge in population health nursing by using epidemiological and system-level data to identify gaps and inequities in care and health outcomes, with a focus on management of chronic conditions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Child and Adolescent Psychiatric-Mental Health
description: Theory and research in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing of children and adolescents representing culturally diverse populations. Emphasis on growth and development, assessment and diagnosis, and therapeutic modalities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Disciplinary Knowledge I
description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and the emergence of nursing as a discipline.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Chronic Illness Management
description: Management of chronic illness using selected health care systems in culturally diverse communities. Management includes practice, consultation, education, research, and evaluation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing in the Global Health Environment
description: Exploration and analysis of key global health topics of concern for advanced nurses.

subject: NURS
title: Health Care Technology and Informatics
description: Introduction to the field of health care technology and informatics for clinicians through the application of health care information systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to students in other healthcare fields by permission.

subject: NURS
title: Health Law
description: Introduction to medical jurisprudence, medical malpractice, informed consent, health care decisions, medical ethics, the health care industry, managed care, financing health care, and the role of government in health care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAW majors only; NURS DNP majors only

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Psychiatric-Mental Health Practicum
description: Supervised application of theories, research, and skills for advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations. Includes the program’s capstone experience.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Family Systems in Health and Illness
description: Family systems approach to include selected family theories, family research and family centered culturally sensitive clinical assessment and intervention in health and illness situations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Complementary and Traditional Care
description: A review of theoretical systems and approaches to complementary and traditional care in culturally diverse populations with a focus on wellness. Appropriate for all health-care professionals.

subject: NURS
title: Tests and Measurement in Nursing Education
description: Testing and evaluation applied to nursing education.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: (Alpha) Selected Topics in Nursing
description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

subject: NURS
title: Selected Topics in Nursing: developmentally disabled children and their families
description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

subject: NURS
title: Selected Topics in Nursing: current issues in professional nursing
description: Advanced study, exploration of special topics in clinical nursing. (D) developmentally disabled children and their families; (I) current issues in professional nursing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent for (D).

subject: NURS
title: Human Resource Management in Healthcare Agencies
description: Analyze and critically evaluate basic issues, policies and trends in human resource management as it applies to health care agencies.

subject: NURS
title: Leadership, Role, Identity and Organizational/System Change
description: Seminar focused on theoretical and conceptual models of leadership and management as applied to relevant advanced nurses’ roles, their respective populations, and changing healthcare environments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Analysis of Healthcare Delivery Models
description: Analysis of various clinical management concepts and health-care delivery systems influencing outcomes, process, and costs in the delivery of care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar and Practicum in Nursing Executive Leadership
description: Supervised practicum to build mid to senior level nursing leadership competencies and facilitate change in complex healthcare organizations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical Economics and Finance
description: Economic and financial concepts and tools for use in developing and managing patient care processes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Community Based Participatory Research (CBPR) Methods
description: Focuses on use of CBPR methods to address population level issues amendable to interventions; 15 hours of didactic and 90 hours of field experience are included.

subject: NURS
title: Evaluating Research for Evidence-based Practice
description: Introduces evidence-based practice methods for improving the quality of nursing practice. Develops skills in differentiating quantitative and qualitative research, statistical methods, and searching, critiquing, and synthesizing literature, pertinent to health care issues.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Nursing During Public Health Disasters
description: The role of the advanced professional nurse in public health preparedness, planning, and response.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Biostatistics: Application in the Advanced Nursing Practice Setting
description: Includes basic bio-statistical techniques and the application of statistical findings to practice programmatic decisions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in the Department of Nursing or consent. NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Population Health Nursing Practicum
description: Student will conduct a complex service project for a public or community based agency. May be taken for 1-6 credits. (45 hours of practicum experience awarded for each one credit of the course)
prereq_raw: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

children.text: credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing or consent

subject: NURS
title: Implementation and Evaluation Strategies for Evidence-Based Practice
description: Using knowledge of translational science, designs an implementation plan for a practice guideline. Determines evaluation methods and selects outcome variables that best measure success. Discusses institutionalization of, and identifies facilitators and barriers to, practice change.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Clinical
description: Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing.
prereq_raw: NURS 612 / NURS 612L , NURS 613 , and NURS 629 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care I Seminar: Health Assessment
description: Seminar to discuss the evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management. Utilization of clinical cases and current literature on health care assessment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care I Lab (beginning level): Health Assessment
description: Beginning level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients for advanced practice nursing students in primary care settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care II Seminar: Management of the Adult
description: Intermediate level seminar where students discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care II Lab (intermediate level): Acute & Chronic Conditions (Adult)
description: Intermediate level practicum. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management, and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing focusing on adults with acute or chronic diagnoses in primary care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care III Seminar: Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
description: Intermediate level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care III Lab (intermediate level): Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
description: Intermediate level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients in a primary care setting for advanced practice nursing students focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care IV Seminar: Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
description: Advanced level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management focusing on primary care of clients across the lifespan.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Primary Care IV Lab (advanced level): Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
description: Advanced level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients across the lifespan in primary care settings for advanced practice nursing students.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Cultural Competency in Nursing Education
description: Evaluates the impact of history on the culture of nursing and nursing education. Explore strategies to provide education in a culturally sensitive manner to culturally diverse students.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Diagnosis & Management of Complex Care Across the Lifespan
description: Culminating seminar synthesizing and applying concepts from all APRN didactic course work, using case/problem-based learning via student and faculty-guided discussions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health and Healing Practices of Populations with Health Disparities in Hawaiʻi and Other Places
description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and the prevention of common conditions of disease among populations with health disparities in Hawaiʻi and other places; includes didactic and 45 hours of field experience.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Psychobiology of Mental Health Disorders
description: Focuses on the psychological and biological factors that influence mental health and illness among diverse groups of individuals across the lifespan. Relevant biopsychosocial theories and research findings are applied.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: First of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan I
description: Complements NURS 684; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits.

subject: NURS
title: Individual Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
description: Major modalities of individual psychotherapy, such as psychodynamic, cognitive-behavioral, brief solution-focused, and multicultural approaches will be examined. Critical dialogue about race, gender, culture, sexuality and socioeconomic status will be applied to case studies and reenactments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
description: The second of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan II
description: Complements NURS 686; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, up to six credits.

subject: NURS
title: Family and Group Psychotherapy for Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioners
description: Major approaches in family and group psychotherapy are examined in this course. The role of the PMHNP and issues in providing care across the lifespan, among diverse populations, in traditional and non-traditional settings are addressed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Theory: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
description: The final of three courses focused on preparing students in the Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) Program to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners (PMHNPs).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Clinical: Psychiatric-Mental Health Advanced Practice Nursing Across the Lifespan III
description: Complements NURS 688; prepares DNP students to become psychiatric-mental health nurse practitioners; and incorporates the accrual of 135 clinical hours.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable one time, or up to six credits.

subject: NURS
title: Introduction to Research Methods
description: Nursing research methods for qualitative and quantitative studies, institutional review board procedures, and how to develop a research proposal.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Practice Clinical for Clinical Nurse Specialists
description: Application of concepts and principles of education, consultation, research, and management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for adult health clinical nurse specialist students.
prereq_raw: NURS 612 (or concurrent), NURS 612L (or concurrent), NURS 613 (or concurrent), and NURS 629 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Successful Aging: Physiologic
description: Advanced study of the functional, cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic phenomena that impact the physiology of normal and abnormal aging. Emphasis is on promoting successful aging among elder residents of the Pacific Basin and applications to primary health care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only or consent.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Education Capstone
description: A culminating experience in nursing education program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Directed Study or Research
description: Directed study of problems related to nursing theory and practice.

subject: NURS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Gerontology: Promotion and Maintenance
description: Analyze biologic, psychosocial, physiologic, and health disparity aspects with conceptual application to healthcare of the aging population. Demonstrate understanding and distinguish normal changes from common disease-related changes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Philosophical Thoughts
description: Introduces the major fields of philosophy for use in research. Frameworks for the evaluation and critique of philosophical approaches to research will be explored, debated, analyzed, and applied as relevant to the PhD student’s dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Philosophical Thought and Disciplinary Knowledge for Nursing
description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and disciplinary thought.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Research Design and Methods for Nursing Science
description: Overview of scientific approaches relevant to nursing and health care research. Application of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods research approaches for answering questions and generating knowledge relevant to the discipline and practice of nursing.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar I: Nursing Science
description: Development and refinement of the student’s research area of interest. Synthesis of theory from nursing and related disciplines. Articulation of the problem, significance, purpose of inquiry, related question(s), hypotheses (as applicable) and specific aims.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar II: Literature Review
description: In-depth review, critique, evaluation, and synthesis of a body of literature. Students will use standardized approaches to systematically search, locate, and evaluate evidence in a focused area to generate an integrative review.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar III: Refining the Research Plan
description: Continued research and scholarly development in an area of nursing scientific concentration. Student refines the research plan (in terms of quantitative, qualitative, and/or mixed methods approaches).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar IV: Building a Program of Research
description: Students advance skills for development and peer critique of research proposals, honing grant and scientific writing skills. Emphasis placed on dissemination strategies relevant and affirming to culturally diverse/marginalized populations and multidisciplinary professional audiences.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Nursing majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

subject: NURS
title: Designing and Conducting Clinical Trials
description: Small group sections will guide students as they produce their own clinical trial protocol. Topics like ethics and statistical power will be addressed briefly.

subject: NURS
title: Instrument Development and Evaluation in Research
description: Theory of testing and evaluation applied to nursing research in culturally diverse populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Principles of Evidence-based Practice for Advanced Nursing
description: Evaluates conceptual models for use in evidence-based practice. Refines skills in searching and critiquing the literature for application to practice change. Synthesizes a body of literature to design interventions pertinent to a practice problem.

subject: NURS
title: Best Practices & Innovation in Teaching and Learning in Nursing Education
description: Current best practices and innovative teaching and learning strategies in nursing education.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Effective Program Evaluation for Quality Improvement
description: Integration of program evaluation and translational science for assessment and communication of programmatic health impacts to improve well-being of patients, families, and stakeholders/communities at local, regional, national/ international levels.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Nursing Science
description: Provides opportunities to know and practice the process of theory development in nursing and to test concepts, relationships, and models about health behavior in culturally diverse populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Health Policy and Economics
description: Evaluate the implications of policies on health care funding and regulations, provider payments, and other variables shaping the ability of health care systems (Western and other) on advanced practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Quantitative Methods and Measures
description: Critical analysis of quantitative research methods used to analyze problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
prereq_raw: NURS 620 or equivalent course and an advanced statistics course; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Qualitative Methods
description: Qualitative methods and approaches to research used in nursing and health sciences will be examined. Multiple paradigms and traditions will be reviewed, including culturally safe approaches and indigenous methodologies.

subject: NURS
title: Seminar on Women and Health
description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.

subject: NURS
title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
description: Analysis of forces that affect adult learners. Concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Methods of Program Evaluation & Quality Improvement
description: Principles of and frameworks for program evaluation. Students develop logic models and evaluation plans for a community program and collect and analyze evaluation data.

subject: NURS
title: Curriculum Development and Assessment Strategies in Nursing Education
description: Current theories, issues, and trends of curriculum development and assessment strategies in nursing education.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Education & Leadership Capstone Practicum
description: A culminating experience in nursing education and leadership program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.
prereq_raw: ( NURS 732 and NURS 747 ) with a minimum grade of B-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Curriculum Evaluation & Accreditation in Nursing Education
description: Current trends of planning for evaluation and critical analysis and application of curriculum evaluation in nursing curriculum.
prereq_raw: NURS 747 with a minimum grade of B-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Foundation of Health Systems and Translation Science
description: Integrate scientific findings from various fields of study to the leadership and management of healthcare systems to ensure the delivery of quality and safe care.

subject: NURS
title: Concept Development and Analysis
description: First course offering in-depth analysis of specific concepts and theoretical formulations of nursing and other disciplines pertinent to the student’s area of research interest. Addresses human responses to health in culturally diverse populations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Statistics I
description: Advanced application of general linear model theory to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
prereq_raw: NURS 741 (or equivalent) or consent. Once a year.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . Once a year

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Statistics II
description: Advanced application of multivariate statistics to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
prereq_raw: NURS 741 and NURS 752 or equivalent courses, or consent. Once a year.

subject: NURS
title: DNP Scholarly Project A: Proposal
description: Prepares students to implement a Doctor of Nursing Practice Scholarly Project Evidenced Based Practice problem by identifying a practice problem, developing a PICO(T) statement, conducting a literature review and synthesis, and developing an implementation plan.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURD majors only.

subject: NURS
title: DNP Scholarly Project B: Implementation
description: Experiential learning course where students implement their Evidence Based Practice (EBP) change in collaboration with content experts, team members, and stakeholders within SONDH and the organization where the change is occurring.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURD majors only.

subject: NURS
title: DNP Scholarly Project C: Evaluation & Dissemination
description: Prepares Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) students to evaluate the effectiveness of their evidence based practice change, synthesize findings of the project, and disseminate results and conclusions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURD majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Trends in Healthcare
description: Evaluates the historical foundations of healthcare systems and their relationship to current issues and trends in healthcare services. Analyzes the variations in healthcare delivery systems across nations and the impact on health outcomes.

subject: NURS
title: Translation Science
description: Synthesis and analysis of interventions and variables that influence the rate of adoption of innovations. Application of concepts to patient populations and systems of healthcare.

subject: NURS
title: Culturally Competent Research Methods
description: Analysis of concepts, issues, and methods in conducting culturally competent research in the health field.

subject: NURS
title: Advanced Clinical Economics and Finance
description: Theory and practice of financial management to achieve high quality and cost effectiveness in healthcare. Hybrid course which combines face-to-face with online learning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Dissertation Proposal Writing Seminar
description: Provides students with advanced study and critique from faculty leading to the development of a draft dissertation proposal. Peer exchange facilities individual scholarship, research topic mastery, and ability to conduct rigorous critique.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Best Practices in Leading Healthcare Patient Safety and Quality
description: Examination of quality of health care, the process of managing health-care outcomes and costs in the delivery of care through the interdisciplinary process.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Capstone Field Study
description: Supervised experience in executive nursing leadership to address important health issues for high-risk or under-served populations utilizing an interdisciplinary systems-based approach.
prereq_raw: NURS 664 and NURS 774 (or concurrent), or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Project
description: Under the guidance of their DNP Project Team members, students will synthesize, integrate, and translate newly acquired knowledge and skills in the implementation and evaluation of their DNP Project.

subject: NURS
title: Nursing Research Practicum
description: Faculty guided research opportunity to gain mastery of research skills and techniques through participation in mentored research.
prereq_raw: NURS 741 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 742 (with a minimum grade of B-), NURS 751 (with a minimum grade of B-) and a quantitative methods course.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , NURS 742 ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , NURS 751 ( with a minimum grade of B- ) and a quantitative methods course

subject: NURS
title: Grant Writing and Grant Management
description: Designed to introduce students to grants, grant writing, and grant management. Combined lecture discussion, seminar, and exercises on grants, grant writing, and grant management for health sciences. Open to NURS students only, others with approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: NURS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NURS majors only.

subject: OBGN
title: Directed Clinical and Translational Research in Obstetrics and Gynecology
description: Directed research within the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology at JABSOM in a clinical or translational context.

subject: OBGN
title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in outpatient setting, covering assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and/ or management of common gynecologic problems and normal and complicated pregnancies. Emphasis on prevention and health maintenance.
prereq_raw: third-year standing, and concurrent registration in OBGN 532 courses.
coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, PED, PSTY, and SURG 632.

subject: OBGN
title: (Alpha) Electives in OB/GYN
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: labor and delivery
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: Sub-internship in family planning
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: high-risk OB
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: endocrinology
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: oncology
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: topics with individual preceptor
description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OBGN
title: Electives in OB/GYN: extramural electives
