description: Opportunities for advanced study of selected topics. (B) labor and delivery; (D) sub-internship in family planning; (E) high-risk OB; (F) endocrinology; (G) oncology; (H) topics with individual preceptor; (I) extramural electives.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: OCN 102 (or concurrent) or GES 102 or (or concurrent) SUST 112 (or concurrent).

subject: OCN
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawaiʻi/Oceania. Active learning environment.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Challenges
description: Scientific approach to evaluating human-caused environmental challenges and their potential solutions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: OCN
title: Research Experiences in Marine Science
description: Inquiry-driven and experimental marine biology summer program based on the expertise of HIMB researchers whose specialties demonstrate how human impacts and global change affect coral reef ecosystems. Emphases on student team research projects.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: High school or UG freshman only.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Directed Research
description: Reading and research in any area of Oceanography under the direction of a faculty member.

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea
description: Origin and features of ocean basins and seawater; global cycles of carbon and nutrients; currents; waves; tides; characteristics of marine organisms; marine ecological principles; marine pollution; climate change causes and consequences. Online asynchronous; synchronous format.

subject: OCN
title: Science of the Sea Laboratory
description: Experiments, computer exercises, and field trips demonstrating the geological, physical, chemical, and biological principles of earth and ocean sciences.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change
description: Delve into global environmental change issues such as geometric population growth, food production, plastic waste, and global warming that are of growing interest and importance to our society.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 , ATMO 200 , or similar environmental/ natural sciences course.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Designed for non-GES majors.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

subject: OCN
title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Introduction to environmental monitoring systems for earth science students. Students will learn how to construct, program, and deploy simple environmental monitoring systems to collect in-situ environmental data.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L or ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L , and MATH 241 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES, ERTH, ATMO majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement GES 311 . Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
prereq_raw: GES 311 , MATH 242 , PHYS 170 / PHYS 170L , and CHEM 161 / CHEM 161L ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Pollution
description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives. This course develops written communication skills.

subject: OCN
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: OCN
title: Mineral and Energy Resources of the Sea
description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration, and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

subject: OCN
title: Living Resources of the Sea-Mai ke Kai Mai ke Ola
description: Marine fisheries, aquaculture, and law of the sea. Principles of management of renewable resources. Political and scientific constraints and limitations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Remote Sensing of the Environment
description: Covers principles of remote sensing technologies for land, ocean, and climate applications. Students will explore the fundamentals of electromagnetic radiation, and learn to critically interpret patterns in environmental changes over time and space.

subject: OCN
title: Undergraduate Internship
description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Undergraduate SOEST majors only. Open to GES majors. Class Standing Restrictions: junior/senior standing and consent.

subject: OCN
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Systems
description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course with an emphasis on improving student writing skills.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 , GES 311 , BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L , CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L , ERTH 101 / ERTH 101L , GES 319L (or concurrent), ATMO 200 (or concurrent), and GES 499 / OCN 499 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing only.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology.

subject: OCN
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
description: Builds upon OCN 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series environmental measurements.
prereq_raw: OCN 318 , MATH 242 , PHYS 272 / PHYS 272L , and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN, ERTH, ATMO majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Geology
description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including benthopelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Climate Change and Urbanization
description: The following topics will be addressed: How are cities impacted by, and impacting climate change? How do urbanization, alteration of atmospheric processes, and extreme weather events affect urban systems and populations?

subject: OCN
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: OCN
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: OCN
title: Plate Tectonics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

subject: OCN
title: Aquaculture Production
description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics, and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445 : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher.

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / BIOL 172L and CHEM 162 / CHEM 162L or higher

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome
description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 or BOT 305 / BIOL 305 or BOT 201 or BIOL 275 or MICR 351 or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305 , or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 .

subject: OCN
title: Ridge to Reef: Coastal Ecosystem Ecology and Connectivity
description: Watershed and coastal biogeochemistry/ecosystem science. Emphasis on field surveying and sampling of stream and reef habitats; laboratory chemical/biological analyses. Analysis of land use impacts on ecosystem health and ahupuaʻa resource management.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L ; and either OCN 310 / ATMO 310 , or GES 311 ; or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Data Analysis in Earth Science
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture and discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
prereq_raw: OCN 201 / OCN 201L , GES 311 , GES 319L , and PHYS 272 / PHYS 272L ; and consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biogeochemical and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on plankton blooms. Students learn ecosystem dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.
prereq_raw: ( GES 311 and either OCN 312 / ERTH 312 (or concurrent) or MATH 307 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Communication of Research Results
description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only in their final semester.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Global Environmental Science
description: Lecture and discussion or seminar. Current topics in environmental science explored in detail. Typically offered by faculty in their specialties, or developed in response to student interest.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES majors only.
repeatable_raw: Unlimited times, credits earned up to 6 credits.

subject: OCN
title: Undergraduate Thesis
description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

subject: OCN
title: Physical Oceanography
description: Introduction to properties of seawater, oceanographic instruments and methods, heat budget, general ocean circulation, regional oceanography, waves, tides, sea level. Formation of water masses, dynamics of circulation.

subject: OCN
title: Biological Oceanography
description: Factors governing productivity, population dynamics, distribution of organisms in major ecosystems of the ocean, emphasis on ecology of pelagic zone.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Geological Oceanography
description: Marine geological processes, ocean basin structure and tectonics, sedimentation.

subject: OCN
title: Chemical Oceanography
description: Chemical processes occurring in marine waters; why they occur and how they affect oceanic environment.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Photosynthesis
description: Biochemical and biophysical concepts of photosynthesis. Application and interpretation of ecological processes of photosynthesis in aquatic systems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Microplankton Ecology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Distribution, abundance, and ecology of marine microplankton, including bacteria, algae, and protozoans, with an emphasis on metabolic rates and processes.

subject: OCN
title: Ecology of Pelagic Marine Animals
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Ecology of pelagic animals including feeding, energetics, predation, and anti-predation tactics. Life-history strategies, vertical flux of materials, population dynamics, fisheries.

subject: OCN
title: Benthic Biological Oceanography
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Processes controlling the structure and function of benthic communities, including organism-sediment-flow interactions, sediment geochemistry, feeding strategies, recruitment, succession, and population interactions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN and MB majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Molecular Methods in Marine Ecology
description: Molecular methods for studying marine functional ecology; emphasis on hand-on tools for ecological and biogeochemical processes of microbes; developing practical skills for research project in marine microbial ecology and biological oceanography.
prereq_raw: OCN 403 , OCN 626 , OCN 627 , or OCN 628 ; or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Deep-Sea Biology
description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Minerals
description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.
prereq_raw: one of OCN 622 , OCN 623 , ERTH 407 , or ERTH 603 .

subject: OCN
title: Fisheries Oceanography: From Physics to Landings
description: Overview of how oceanographic processes influence the distribution, life history, and abundance of fishery-relevant species. Topics will largely center on applications to Hawaiʻi, tropical/sub-tropical ecosystems, and the broader Pacific.
prereq_raw: C or better in OCN 620 or OCN 621 , and a background in biological oceanography and/or physical oceanography required.

subject: OCN
title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses of the collected samples throughout the remainder of the semester.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and CHEM 161 and ERTH 101 ; or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Chemistry
description: Chemical reactions support life and stabilize Earth’s climate. We explore marine and fresh waters through chemical equilibrium and reaction kinetics. Topics include mineral stability, ocean acidification, complexation/bioavailability, pollution, and quantitative approximation of natural systems.

subject: OCN
title: Aquatic Microbial Geochemistry
description: The synergy between the biogeochemistry of element cycling and the microbial organisms involved, interfacing across disciplines from the perspective of a practical blend of aquatic chemistry, microbiology, biogeochemistry, and molecular biology.

subject: OCN
title: Earth System Science and Global Change
description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmosphere-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus.

subject: OCN
title: Observational Physical Oceanography
description: Application of the scientific method; physical regimes in the ocean; ocean processes and observational strategies; resolution, sampling, array design and observing systems; models and data assimilation; major field programs; operational oceanography and climate prediction.

subject: OCN
title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

subject: OCN
title: Elemental Composition Changes
description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Marine Geochemistry
description: Seminar on a broad topic; discussion and critique of research papers.

subject: OCN
title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.

subject: OCN
title: Math Techniques for Oceanographers
description: (3 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Introduction to numerical methods, data analysis, error propagation, box models, linear and nonlinear least squares, perturbation theory, numerical integration.

subject: OCN
title: Methods in Microbiology Oceanography
description: (1 8-hr Lab) Modern methods for sampling microbial populations from the sea and for quantifying biomass and in siturates of metabolism. Integrated field projects, theme varies.
prereq_raw: OCN 621 or OCN 623 , and OCN 626 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves I
description: Survey of wave types-acoustic, capillary, gravity, inertial, vorticity. Basic wave concepts emphasized: phase and group velocities, standing waves, energy conservation, dispersion, refraction, diffraction. Rotation and boundary effects are covered: reflection, basin modes, trapping, tides.

subject: OCN
title: Ocean Waves II
description: Baroclinic gravity waves, inertial waves, mid-latitude Rossby waves, topographic waves, equatorial waves.

subject: OCN
title: Marine Hydrodynamics
description: Introduction to classical hydrodynamics and continuum mechanics. Techniques for solution of Navier Stokes equations on various scales of oceanic motion; potential theory, dynamic modeling, and viscous and rotational processes.

subject: OCN
title: Satellite Oceanography
description: Techniques of satellite observations of the ocean, including temperature, pigment concentration, currents, and winds; analysis of a satellite data set as term project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Oceanographic Instrumentation and Technology
description: Measurement techniques in physical oceanography, including pressure, temperature, salinity, oxygen, optical sensors, current meters, navigation systems, ocean acoustics, and mooring structures. Includes a laboratory research project.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either OCN 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent.

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either OCN 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent

subject: OCN
title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Nino/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I
description: Basic concepts and equations to describe large-scale ocean circulation; numerical models; boundary layers; models of wind-driven circulation of a homogeneous ocean.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics II
description: Thermodynamics of stratified fluids; convection; mixing; models of the thermohaline circulation; the role of eddies in the large-scale ocean circulation.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Environmental Data Science
description: Advanced applications of environmental data science: combine data with Bayesian inference, predictions using artificial neural networks, and analyze data in space and time using the Python language with biological and geophysical datasets.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN, ATMO, and ERTH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: OCN
title: Paleoceanography
description: Study of the paloeceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere, and biosphere.

subject: OCN
title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
description: Combined lecture/discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
prereq_raw: previous course in marine science, or consent.

subject: OCN
title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
description: Introduction to modeling biological and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on biological production. Students will learn biological-physical dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.

subject: OCN
title: Data Science Fundamentals in R
description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

subject: OCN
title: Advanced Statistics in R
description: (2-hr Lec, 1-hr Lab) In-depth introduction to the modern statistical methods necessary for analyzing biological/ecological data, including GLMs, GAMs, mixed models, ordination, etc. Students will learn how to perform these methods in R.

subject: OCN
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Biological Oceanography
description: Seminar. Literature and concepts in one of several active fields considered in detail.
repeatable_raw: 3 times, credits earned up to 12 credits.

subject: OCN
title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest.

subject: OCN
title: Seminar
description: Oceanographic topics of current interest.

subject: OCN
title: Proposal Development
description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal.
prereq_raw: two of the following: OCN 621 , OCN 626 , OCN 627 (or concurrent), or OCN 628 (or concurrent); or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: OCN majors only.

subject: OCN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: OEST
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: GES, ERTH, and MET majors only.

subject: OEST
title: The College Experience
description: Required for entering SOEST majors to develop skills and applications for a successful college experience. Students will examine academic goals and implement strategies to achieve goals including time management and career exploration.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SOEST majors only.

subject: OEST
title: Natural Hazards
description: Science of natural hazards: impact on human civilization of events in the lithosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere (e.g., earthquakes, hurricanes, red tides, and floods), and impact of humans on their exposure to and mitigation of the hazards.

subject: OEST
title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

subject: OEST
title: Contemporary Issues in Energy Systems
description: Introductory experience in energy systems including current status of fossil fuel, renewable energy technologies, energy utilization and conservation; environmental and policy aspects.

subject: OEST
title: Ethics in Scientific Research
description: Introduction to issues of ethics in scientific research and scientific misconduct.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ERTH, GES, or ATMO majors only.

subject: OEST
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Introduction to the principles of sustainability analysis through execution of Life Cycle Analysis applied to products, processes, or systems. LCA and the evaluation of environmental impact will be presented. Personal computer or laptop (Word 97 or higher) OS, and minimum of 4GB RAM.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and PHYS 170 ) with a minimum grade of C-; Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: OEST
title: Undergraduate Directed Research
description: Student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. Student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: OEST
title: Earth Sciences Professional Development Education
description: Specialized Earth Science topics workshops designed for in-service teachers who wish to learn new approaches and content areas in geology and geophysics, meteorology and oceanography. Credits earned cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

subject: OEST
title: Communicating Ocean Sciences
description: Application of current learning theory and pedagogical practices in formal and informal learning environments to improve communication and instructional skills. Graduate students from multiple science disciplines welcome. Requires knowledge of biology, earth sciences, and/or chemistry.
prereq_raw: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry or marine science, an interest in ocean science, and enthusiasm for teaching science; or consent.

children.text: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry
marine science, an interest in ocean science,

subject: OEST
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy.

subject: OEST
title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Technology—Man in the Sea
description: Survey of human activities in the ocean, from the most traditional to the most innovative technical and engineering accomplishments.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture
description: Introduction to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the human interaction with the ocean using multiple perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: ORE
title: Surf Science and Culture Lab
description: Practical laboratory dedicated to wave science covering generation, propagation, transformation, and coastal processes related to surfing and the ocean environment through technology.

subject: ORE
title: Mineral and Energy Resources
description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

subject: ORE
title: Buoyancy and Stability
description: Ship nomenclature and geometry, hydrostatic principles of surface ships and underwater vehicles in free-floating, partially waterborne, and damaged conditions. Subdivision of ships. Launching.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean and Resources Engineering Laboratory
description: Design, construction, and evaluation of an engineering system. Laboratory and field experience and data analysis supplemented with appropriate theory.

subject: ORE
title: Oceanography for Ocean Engineers
description: Physical, chemical, biological, and geological ocean environments for ocean engineers. Introduction to ocean dynamical processes and general circulation. Ocean measurement techniques, theory of underwater acoustics. Sonar, swath bathymetry, and tomography applications.

subject: ORE
title: Water Wave Mechanics
description: Governing equations in free surface flow, deterministic and probabilistic wave theories, wave transformation, wave-induced coastal currents, tides, ocean engineering operational sea state, and design wave criteria.

subject: ORE
title: Probability and Statistics for Ocean Engineers
description: Probability and statistical analysis including distributions, multiple regression and correlation, autocovariance, cross-spectra, and practical applications in ocean engineering.

subject: ORE
title: Hydrodynamics of Fluid-Body Interaction
description: Hydrodynamics of ships, coastal and offshore structures. Wave forces by potential theory and by Morison’s equation. Method of source distribution for potential flow problems. Flows with prescribed body motion, fixed and freely floating bodies.

subject: ORE
title: Dynamics of Ocean Structures
description: Response of floating platforms and vessels to wave action, spectral analysis in sea keeping. Frequency and time domain analyses of rigid body motions in six degrees of freedom.

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

subject: ORE
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: ORE
title: Structural Analysis in Ocean Engineering
description: Structural and finite element analyses and design of ocean structures to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loading of the sea. Considerations include material type, safety factor, stress concentration, and fatigue.

subject: ORE
title: Environmental Fluid Dynamics
description: Fluid dynamics for coastal and estuarine environments. Turbulent mixing processes in homogeneous and stratified fluids. Buoyancy driven flows, internal hydraulics, topographic effects and estuarine circulation. Spill and pollutant dispersal.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Instrumentation and Technology
description: Overview of past, present, and emerging technologies and instrumentation that support oceanographic and marine operations. Will cover the design, operation, and maintenance of the mechanical, electrical, and computing components of these systems.

subject: ORE
title: Applications in Ocean Acoustics
description: Using sound to observe the ocean. Fundamentals of propagation. Topics include marine mammals, navigation and communication, seismics, ships, wind and rain, ocean dynamics, flow and biological imaging and measurement, seafloor mapping, and the forward/inverse problem.

subject: ORE
title: Autonomous Marine Systems
description: Identifies the unique challenges faced by autonomous underwater and surface vehicles, and analyzes approaches to address those challenges. Topics include hydrodynamic vehicle modeling, propeller theory, subsystem integration, and motion control strategies.
prereq_raw: MATH 307 or MATH 311 (or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 (or equivalent), or instructor consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

children.text: ( or equivalent), and ECE 351 or ME 451 ( or equivalent), or instructor consent

subject: ORE
title: Coastal and Harbor Engineering
description: Planning and design of seawalls, groins, jetties, breakwaters, and layout of ports. Design requirements for harbor entrances and channels. Littoral drift and sedimentation problems. Navigation and mooring requirements.

subject: ORE
title: Nearshore Processes and Sediment Transport
description: Sediment transport by waves and currents in coastal areas and its effect on morphological processes. Effect of man-made structures on littoral drift and shoreline.

subject: ORE
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
prereq_raw: ORE 607 ; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable.

subject: ORE
title: Marine Mineral Resources Engineering
description: Activities in marine minerals development are examined in a multidisciplinary systems approach involving engineering, Earth and environmental sciences and economics.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: ORE
title: Ocean Engineering and Resilience in a Changing Climate
description: Focus on understanding the changing ocean conditions (e.g. waves and sea levels) relevant to the resilience of practical ocean engineering applications.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ORE
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

subject: ORE
title: Directed Reading or Research
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing and consent.

subject: ORE
title: Thesis Research
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: candidacy for MS in ocean and resources engineering.

subject: ORE
title: Nonlinear Water Wave Theories
description: Higher-order theories. Forced oscillations. Stoke’s theory. Nonlinear shallow-water wave equations and hydraulic jumps; effects of rotation. Internal waves. Analytical techniques necessary will be developed as course progresses.

subject: ORE
title: Mathematical and Numerical Methods in Ocean Engineering
description: Formulation and application of analytical and numerical methods for simulating and solving ocean engineering problems. Mathematical and computational fundamentals; numerical interpolation, differentiation, and integration; accuracy and stability; solutions to ordinary and partial differential equations.

subject: ORE
title: (Alpha) Capstone Design Project
description: Major design experience based on knowledge and skills acquired in earlier course work and incorporating realistic constraints that include economic, environmental, ethical, social, and liability considerations. Emphasis is placed on teamwork and consultant-client relationship. (B) coastal engineering; (C) offshore engineering; (D) ocean resources engineering; (E) oceanic engineering.

description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting and permanent faculty.

title: Seminar in Ocean and Resources Engineering
description: Attendance at 15 approved seminars is required along with submission of notes.

subject: ORE
title: Dissertation Research

subject: PACE
title: Problems of War and Peace
description: Introduction to the problems individuals and political communities currently face with respect to war, peace, and international conflict. Includes questions of human nature, economy, morality, nuclear deterrence, arms control and disarmament, and alternatives to war.

subject: PACE
title: Survey of Conflict Management
description: Survey of contemporary conflict management and resolution: negotiation, mediation, conciliation, ombuds, fact-finding, facilitation techniques, arbitration, and litigation.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Governing, Policy, and Political Journalism
description: Survey of the institutions of democratic governance and the role of journalism in covering and analyzing public policy.

subject: PACE
title: Survey Peace and Conflict Studies
description: Survey of basic concepts, ethical relationships, methods, and debates in modern peace research and the oral skills needed for conflict resolution studies.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Personal Peace: Stories of Hope
description: Interviewing, writing, and publishing stories of those who have overcome great difficulties to find personal peace.
prereq_raw: grade of B or better in ENG 100 or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Environmental Governance
description: Centers around the ethical dilemmas of environmental and climate challenges and examines available mechanisms for solving them. Develops written communication skills through a critical lens from a political ecology and environmental justice perspective.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Model United Nations
description: Simulation of United Nations organizations, especially General Assembly and/or Security Council.

subject: PACE
title: Greek and Roman War Literature
description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Aggression, War, and Peace
description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

subject: PACE
title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course; or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Media Communications and Conflict
description: Uses an ethical lens to see the role of news media in influencing conflict, and introduces conflict-sensitive communication movements working to resolve conflicts. Writing/discussion used as mediums for reflecting on ethical dilemmas.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: The Meaning of War
description: Exploration of ethical questions related to the many facets of war—e.g., patriotism, tribalism, holy war, self—sacrifice, cowardice, media coverage, propaganda, torture, genocide, pillage, suicide tactics, battlefield immunity.

subject: PACE
title: Directed Reading
description: Directed reading in peace and conflict resolution.

subject: PACE
title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction
description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. No experience necessary.

subject: PACE
title: Media Ethics
description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects through writing assignments.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: JOUR majors only.

subject: PACE
title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawaiʻi
description: (75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students) History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing only.

subject: PACE
title: History of Peace Movements
description: Examination of two centuries of U.S., European, Australian, and Hawaiian peace, thought, and action. Also surveys early Christian and secular attitudes to war. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PACE
title: Gandhi, King, and Nonviolence
description: Life and thought of Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King, Jr.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Terrorism
description: Multidisciplinary approach to the origins, dynamics, and consequences of international terrorism, including the psychological, legal, ethical and operational concerns of counterterrorism.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Human Rights: International and Comparative Perspectives
description: Introduction to international, regional, and domestic human rights law; comparative perspectives on the theoretical origins of human rights and policy debates on the protection of human rights, dispute resolution, and enforcement mechanisms.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level social sciences course, or consent.

children.text: level social sciences course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Negotiation
description: Negotiation theory, negotiation skills and application of negotiation in conflict prevention, conflict management and conflict resolution with an emphasis on oral communication and contemporary ethical issues.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Leadership for Social Change
description: In-depth study of current models and emerging theories of ethical leadership in community service; development of tangible leadership skills, including communication, conflict resolution, team-building, and management skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE

description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PACE

description: Provides an exploration of peacebuilding, its contributions to community and its intersectionality with the arts to influence non-violent conflict resulting in cultural performance for all to engage and enjoy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Statecraft and Diplomacy in East Asia
description: Examines the history and architecture of diplomacy and statecraft in East Asia.

subject: PACE
title: Race and Gender in Global Affairs and Diplomacy
description: Focuses on the impact of race and gender on global affairs and diplomacy. Students will learn and apply various ethical approaches to address racism and sexism and move toward more just diplomatic practices.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Mediation
description: Learn the core components of the mediation process and the tools for empowering mediation participants to reach customized resolutions. Emphasis on learning and applying the skills through exercises and mock mediation sessions.

subject: PACE
title: Protest Under Occupation
description: Explore nonviolent protests when one Independent State controls the territory of another Independent State (or international organization, such as the United Nations), without the transfer of sovereign title. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Indigenous Nonviolent Action in the Asia-Pacific
description: Study of nonviolent methods (i.e., United Nations structures, international law, boycotts, and peaceful protest) used to gain political goals and examines their successes, failures, and the prospects for those that remain ongoing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Introduction to Facilitating Organizational Change
description: Explores the characteristics of organizations from different perspectives including structural, political, ethical, and cultural frames from organizational theory and practice. Focuses on how to design organizational change strategies and facilitate their implementation.
prereq_raw: any 200-level DS course (with a minimum grade of C+).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Advocating for Children: Rights and Welfare
description: Multi-disciplinary advocacy for children’s rights and welfare in various social and political systems; the role of families, justice, economics, media, race, culture, environment on policy-making for children.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Culture and Conflict Resolution
description: Conflict resolution techniques for major world culture. Emphasis on cultures of the Pacific Basin, Pacific Islands, and Asia.

subject: PACE
title: International Law and Disputes
description: Management, prevention, resolution of international disputes and the role of international law.
prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent.

subject: PACE
title: ’Ike Kūpuna: Introduction to Indigenous Frameworks for Peace Building
description: Survey of the concepts and major theories of indigenous epistemology that can create social change.

subject: PACE
title: Managing Human Conflict
description: Introduction into the field of conflict analysis and resolution through the examination of theory and roleplay. Major theories of conflict studies are considered and the forms of conflict resolution, such as negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Research and Peace
description: Introduction to and survey of the interdisciplinary field of peace research, combining theory, methodology, and empirical aspects. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACE
title: Topics in Peace and Conflict Resolution
description: Recent issues, practices in peace and conflict resolution.

subject: PACE
title: Hiroshima & Peace
description: 10-day intensive course at Hiroshima City University, Japan, in the 2-weeks before the annual August 6 commemoration of the atomic bombing. Home-stay with Japanese family.
prereq_raw: any 200 level social science course, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing.

children.text: level social science course, or consent

subject: PACE
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PACE
title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills.

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

title: Teaching Model United Nations

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PACE
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

subject: PACE
title: Seminar: Social Studies
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field.

subject: PACE
title: Mediation: Theory and Practice
description: Combined lecture, discussion, and mediation simulations. Theory of ADR field. Theory of major different models of mediation, both in the U.S. and internationally. Application of mediation process to categories of disputes, family, workplace, and international.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Dispute Resolution System Design
description: Conflict prevention, management and resolution in the workplace. Design and implementation of effective systems integrating ADR and recent advances in dispute resolution methodology to government, health, nonprofit, educational, private sector and other institutions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing, or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Conflict Management for Educators
description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes.

subject: PACE
title: Family Mediation
description: Theory and skills for practicing divorce and custody mediation. Negotiation and conflict intervention skills used by social workers, lawyers, and other intervenors in family conflict. Focus on Hawaiʻi’s divorce and custody laws and practices.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PACE
title: Collaboration Between Sectors
description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems.

subject: PACE
title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or departmental approval.

subject: PACE
title: Topics: Conflict Theory
description: Recent issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PACE
title: Conflict Resolution Practicum
description: Practice in conflict resolution skills. Open to candidates for Certificate in Conflict Resolution.

subject: PACE
title: Political Ecology
description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

subject: PACE
title: Advanced Topics: Conflict Theory
description: Advanced seminar covering issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Worlds: An Introduction to Pacific Islands Studies
description: Introduces students to the geography, societies, histories, cultures, contemporary issues, and arts of Oceania, including Hawaiʻi. Combines lectures and discussion that emphasize Pacific Islander perspectives and experiences.

subject: PACS
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Oceania
description: Uses interdisciplinary approaches to examine the causes, impacts, and responses to climate change in Oceania, while drawing on examples and lessons from the broader Asia-Pacific with an emphasis on a writing intensive assessment.

subject: PACS
title: Islands of Globalization
description: Combined lectures, service-learning. Examines the nature and impact of globalization on Pacific Island societies, viewed from the perspective of islanders who engage with global forces and processes, and create strategies to survive. Limit 20 students.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Islands Movement and Migration
description: Combined lecture and service-learning activities. Examines the diaspora of Pacific Islanders. Includes a service-learning activity examining cultural, political, and economic status of groups of Pacific Islanders living in other Pacific places. Limit of 20 students.

subject: PACS
title: Arts in Oceania—An Introduction
description: Practical and theoretical study of arts in Oceania in relevant cultural contexts.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Communities in Hawaiʻi
description: Examines Pacific Islander communities’ experiences in Hawaiʻi through service learning, reading, writing, lecture, and discussion. Concerns about housing, employment, education, health, language, and culture are central.

subject: PACS
title: Contemporary Issues in Oceania
description: Combines lectures and discussions to examine contemporary political, social, and economic issues in the Pacific Islands region. It also develops and strengthens students’ written communication skills by emphasizing reading, writing, and referencing.

subject: PACS
title: Thinking Through Pacific Arts, Ritual, and Performance
description: Lecture, discussion, and workshop series surveys arts, ritual, and performance practices throughout the Pacific. Engaging with Pacific traditions of thought, and creative approaches to research, students also return findings to Pacific communities.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACS
title: Climate Change, Resilience, and Sustainability in Oceania
description: Examines Pacific Island experiences and responses to climate change, contrasting Indigenous and local impacts with regional and global models, emphasizing resilience, sustainability, and community strategies confronting rising seas, biodiversity loss, pollution, and ecological disruption.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACS
title: Islands and Archipelagos
description: Applies an island studies perspective to critically evaluate the commonalities and differences across islands and archipelagos in several world regions. Examines how island geographies influence social identities and movements and are impacted by environmental conditions.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PACS
title: Literature of the Pacific
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: PACS
title: Pacific Islander Collaborative Research
description: Engage in intensive collaborative research with a Pacific Islander community in Hawaiʻi, culminating in a research paper and public presentation. Oral communication is an essential component of this course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: PACS
title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
description: Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawaiʻi, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand.

subject: PACS
title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of Pacific literature.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course.

subject: PACS
title: Moving Images in the Pacific Islands
description: Critically examines indigenous and foreign representations of the Pacific Islands and is designed to make film a central focus of inquiry for students interested in the contemporary Pacific.

subject: PACS
title: Culture and Consumption in Oceania
description: Lecture on changing patterns of consumption in Oceania, and the historical, political, cultural, artistic, and economic forces shaping such practices.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing, or consent.

subject: PACS
title: Learning Oceania
description: Graduate seminar. Introduction to the nature and origins of Pacific Studies as an organized field of study. Epistemological, conceptual, political and ethical issues facing students of the region today.

subject: PACS
title: Re/Presenting Oceania: Pacific and American Perspectives
description: Graduate seminar. Critical analysis of the way physical, social and cultural aspects of Oceania have been represented in scholarly and popular media.

subject: PACS
title: Researching Oceania: Creative and Conventional Methods of Inquiry
description: Graduate seminar. Literacy, theory and method in the creation of a Master’s research project.

subject: PACS
title: Women in Oceania
description: Will look at feminist theory, ethnography, culture, activism and globalization in the context of writing, research and film on or by Women in Oceania.

subject: PACS
title: Community Fisheries in Oceania
description: Explores Pacific communities’ fisheries management, cultural practices, and reciprocal relationships, highlighting their beliefs, traditions, and innovations in sustaining marine resources for present and future generations.

subject: PACS
title: Topics in Histories of Oceania
description: Reading and research on major issues, topics, and themes in the history of Oceania.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PACS
title: Reviewing Oceania: An Introduction to Systematic Literature Review
description: Introduction to systematic literature review. Material will include theoretical and hands-on use of software for reference management and MAXQDA for qualitative data analysis.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only, or permission of instructor.

subject: PACS
title: Graduate Seminar: Change in the Pacific
description: Interrelationship of change in selected Pacific Islands regions, institutions, and processes.

subject: PACS
title: Master’s Portfolio Project
description: Independent study for students working on MA portfolio projects. A grade of satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in PACS.

subject: PALI
title: Elementary Pali I
description: Reading simple texts from Pali canon. Grammar taught as needed for the reading.

subject: PALI
title: Elementary Pali II
description: Continuation of PALI 381 .

subject: PALI
title: Intermediate Pali I
description: Continuation of PALI 382 . Reading various Hinayâna texts.

subject: PALI
title: Intermediate Pali II
description: Continuation of PALI 481 .

subject: PAS
title: Overseas Study
description: Registration allows student to maintain enrolled status at UH Mānoa while taking courses abroad.

subject: PATH
title: Immunopathology Seminar
description: Autoimmune diseases and transplantation immunity.

subject: PATH
title: Directed Research
description: Pathology of aging, nutrition, alcoholism, and immunology. Open to selected undergraduate students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit II Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for first-year medical students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Concurrent Elective
description: Elective course for second-year medical students.

subject: PATH
title: Unit V Block Elective
description: Required elective for second-year medical students, objectives to be determined by contract. One option is a review of USMLE Part I.

subject: PATH
title: Pathology Practicum
description: Required autopsy experience involving dissection and microscopic examination of tissues and detailed evaluation of disease process.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: third- or fourth-year standing.

subject: PATH
title: (Alpha) Unit VII Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: advanced topics in clinical immunology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: anatomic pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: clinical pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Unit VII Electives in Pathology: extramural elective in pathology
description: Individualized instruction in laboratory medicine for the practicing physician, clinical and anatomic pathology: (B) advanced topics in clinical immunology; (C) anatomic pathology; (D) clinical pathology; (E) pathologic aspects of aging, nutrition, and/or alcoholism; (F) extramural elective in pathology.

subject: PATH
title: Introduction to Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
description: Provides an introduction to the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine and the role pathologists and the laboratory play in the diagnosis and management of disease.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD students only.

subject: PATH
title: Electives in Pathology
description: Individualized instruction in clinical and/or anatomic pathology. Third-year elective.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Seminars
description: Interactive weekly lecture/seminar designed to teach topics in pediatrics and supplemented by small group 2-hour encounters with faculty clinicians in pediatric emergency medicine, inpatient pediatric, and enonatology to gain exposure in pediatric hospital care.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Medical students only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatric Shadowing Encounters
description: Clinical Shadowing — Students are paired with Pediatric Subspecialists in chosen area(s) for 8-10 half days. Required: Log book file describing one concept that the student learned during each of the sessions.

subject: PED
title: Introduction to Research Methodology, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology
description: Interactive seminar series to cover the following topics: data types, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, selecting a statistical test, data distributions, measures of data spread, statistical test assumptions, standard deviation vs. standard error, etc.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Medical students only.

subject: PED
title: Pediatrics Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, covering evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of childhood diseases. Emphasis on primary prevention, normal growth and development of the neonate to adolescent, and arrangement of pediatric care, including outpatient, inpatient, and emergency room experiences.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.
coreq_raw: MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532, PSTY 532 , and SURG 532 .

subject: PED
title: (Alpha) Electives in Pediatrics
description: Fourth-year elective in pediatric sub-specialty areas in which medical students may receive clinical experiences and an in-depth study of selected sub-specialty areas within the field of pediatrics. (B) adolescent medicine; (C) ambulatory pediatric care; (D) pediatric child abuse; (E) clinical genetics; (F) Sub-Internship in neonatology; (G) pediatric cardiology; (H) Sub-Internship in pediatric emergency medicine; (I) Sub-Internship in pediatric hematology/oncology; (J) Sub-Internship in infectious diseases; (K) Sub-Internship in pediatrics—general ward in pediatrics; (M) extramural electives in pediatrics; (N) pediatric rheumatology; (P) developmental behavioral pediatrics; (Q) pediatric international preceptorship; (R) Sub-Internship in pediatric critical care; (S) pediatric radiology; (T) pediatric ultrasound; (U) pediatric nephrology; (V) pediatric sports medicine; (W) pediatric neurology; (X) pediatric pulmonology; (Y) pediatric palliative care.
repeatable_raw: 2 times per alpha, up to 36 credits; 1 time by exception only for (D), (W), (X), (Y); not repeatable for (Q).
