subject: PEPS
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: The World of Insects
description: Biology/ecology of insects with emphasis on relationships to plants, animals, and especially people in Hawaiʻi and the tropics. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: ( BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Invasive Pest Species
description: Ecological, economic and sociological impacts of invasive species on tropical ecosystems; characteristics of invasive species and vulnerability of habitats; ethical issues on impacts of management options on evolution, biodiversity and eco-stability and human life. Open to nonmajors.

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology
description: Biology, diversity, and ecology of insects with emphasis on Hawaiian fauna. Classification to order level.
prereq_raw: ( BOT 101 or ZOOL 101 or BIOL 171 ) with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: General Entomology Laboratory
description: Laboratory in the biology and classification to family level of Hawaiʻi’s insects and arthropods.
prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

subject: PEPS
title: Agricultural Biosecurity and Food Safety
description: Introduction and overview to concepts of agricultural biosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), the global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

subject: PEPS
title: Tropical Fruit Production
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices and recent innovations in tropical and subtropical fruit crops, emphasizing botanical aspects and commercial production in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Pathogens and Diseases
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Classification, morphology, ecology, and biology of bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and viruses that attack economic crops. Etiology and control of plant diseases.
prereq_raw: PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or BOT 101 or MICR 130 , or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

subject: PEPS
title: Turfgrass Pest Management
description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawaiʻi, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

subject: PEPS
title: Foundations of Pest Management
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles and concepts of insect pest management; biological, cultural, physical, and chemical control; sampling protocol; pests of fruit and vegetable crops, turf and urban landscape plants, urban structures, and environments including medically important insects.
prereq_raw: one of the following: PEPS 250 or PEPS 363 , BIOL 171 , BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; or consent.

children.text: or PEPS 363 , BIOL 171 , BIOL 172 , or BOT 101 ; or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Disease Epidemiology and Management
description: Epidemiological principles and integrated disease management of important pathogens and diseases affecting key crops in various agroecosystems in Hawaiʻi and the global tropics. This course develops writing skills.

subject: PEPS
title: Applied UAS Operations for Agriculture and Environment
description: Applies operations with uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), mission planning, safety, photogrammetry and GIS, personnel management, and payload operation. Focus on topics required for commercial certifications as a remote pilot, agricultural operator, and pesticide applicator.
prereq_raw: completion of FS/FQ, DP, DB, and DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: STEM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

children.text: DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-

subject: PEPS
title: Insects as Food & Feed
description: Biology, ecology, and nutritional value of edible insects. Explores the use of edible insects as alternative protein sources for human consumption and animal feed as solutions to global food security.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Undergraduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Environmental Law
description: Exploration of federal laws, regulations, and precedents that govern our interaction with the environment. Analysis of laws regulating air, water, toxins, pests, endangered species, and environmental justice.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior or senior standing.

subject: PEPS
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: (2 Lec, 1-3-hr hybrid Lab) Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 or BIOL 265 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Weed Science
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 152 and TPSS 200 / SUST 211 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect-Plant Interactions
description: Study of the coevolutionary relationships between insects and plants, with emphasis on the behavior, physiology, and symbiotic relationships of insects. Discussed in the context of sustainable agriculture, anthropogenic change, and climate change.
prereq_raw: PEPS 363 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Topics in Plant & Environmental Protection
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. May be offered by visiting faculty, extension faculty or research faculty.

subject: PEPS
title: PEPS Capstone
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development, Directed Research, field studies, employment with cooperating businesses, government or schools are all options.

subject: PEPS
title: Directed Research
description: Conduct original research in environmental protection sciences. Limited to qualified undergraduate students.

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Agrosecurity and Food Safety
description: Concepts of agrosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

subject: PEPS
title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Fungi and Nematodes
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr. Lab) Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology and management of plant diseases caused by fungi, oomycetes, and nematodes. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

subject: PEPS
title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Bacteria and Viruses
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology, and management of plant diseases caused by bacteria and viruses. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.
prereq_raw: PEPS 605 (with a minimum grade of B).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B )

subject: PEPS
title: Professional Development
description: Lecture/ discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases
description: Iterative and interactive course integrating plant pathogen and pest biology with diagnostic and management approaches. Will use biological information about pathogens, anthropods, and abiotic stresses to diagnose diseases, disorders, or other injuries of plants.
prereq_raw: ( PEPS 605 and PEPS 606 ) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases Laboratory
description: Diagnosis and management of plant pathogen and pest problems in laboratory and field. Taught concurrently with PEPS 615 .
prereq_raw: ( PEPS 605 and PEPS 606 ) with a minimum grade of B, or equivalent.

subject: PEPS
title: Plant Biochemistry
description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest.
prereq_raw: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect Nutrient Regulation
description: Focuses on nutrient intake and utilization by insects with emphasis on herbivory and agricultural pests. A multitude of environmental factors that influence nutrient regulation will be discussed.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect Physiology
description: (2 Lec) Study of the principal physiological and biochemical functions in insects, with emphasis on hormonal interactions.

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Entomophagy
description: This advanced course examines the scientific, technological, and socio-economic dimensions of entomophagy–the use of insects and insect-derived materials as sustainable sources of food and feed for an expanding global population.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Molecular Plant-Fungal Interactions
description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only.

subject: PEPS
title: Seminar in Plant Pathology
description: Seminar on research and topics in plant pathology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Systematics and Phylogenetics
description: Classification and study of diversity among insects and other life forms. Use of morphological and molecular characters to reconstruct evolutionary histories.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Insect Ecology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Insects as living units in an environment of physical and biotic factors.

subject: PEPS
title: Biological Control of Pests
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental concepts. Critical study of major biological control projects.
prereq_raw: PEPS 421 or consent. Recommended: PEPS 662 ; and ZOOL 631 or ZOOL 632 .

children.text: Recommended: PEPS 662 ; and ZOOL 631 or ZOOL 632

subject: PEPS
title: Biological Control of Weeds
description: Examine approaches to weed biological control of invasive plants in various environments with different agents (insects, pathogens, and vertebrates), integration with other management tactics, sociopolitical aspects, and history of the practice.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PEPS
title: Invertebrate Microbiology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) In-depth study of the molecular and cellular interactions between microbes and animals. Topics will cover types of symbioses, gut microbiome, parasites, and agricultural pathogens, and disease and human health disease.

subject: PEPS
title: Seminar in Entomology
description: Seminars on research and topics in entomology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Special Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in plant and environmental protection sciences at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in entomology or tropical plant pathology.

subject: PEPS
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research, critical reviews in environmental protection sciences, entomology, or plant pathology.

subject: PEPS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant Nematology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Advanced study of nematode taxonomy, genetics, behavior, host interactions, and sustainable management in an integrated lecture-laboratory.
prereq_raw: PEPS 605 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant Virology
description: Characterization, genome organization, gene expression, and molecular mechanisms of plant viruses.
prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
prereq_raw: PEPS 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B or better ) or consent

subject: PEPS
title: Proposal/Defense Seminar
description: Thesis/ dissertation proposal and defense seminars.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PEPS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Public Health
description: Introduces public health concepts with an emphasis on principles and tools for population health, disease prevention, health professions and healthcare systems, and public health professions and systems.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Issues in Hawaiʻi
description: Application of general public health concepts and tools with broader public health issues as they relate to the State of Hawaiʻi.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Global Health
description: Introduction to the basic principles of global PH. Topics include the application of these principles to global PH issues, exploration of links between health, economic, and social status, health disparities and global interventions.

subject: PH
title: Quantitative Reasoning for Public Health
description: Inductive and deductive reasoning; tabular, symbolic, verbal, and graphical forms of functions and relations; graphs and pictorial representations of data; interpretations of probabilistic data; surveys and statistical studies as related to public health.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Student Success in the College Experience
description: Required for entering PH majors to gain strategies for a successful college experience while studying public health. Students will examine academic and career goals and implement strategies to achieve them.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Public Health Issues
description: Seminar will explore current issues and case studies in epidemiology, issues and causes of chronic and infectious diseases, how the environment interacts with health, and how social and behavioral factors affect personal health.

subject: PH
title: Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Seminar to work with faculty in applying evidence-based knowledge on social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Epidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion on the fundamental principles of epidemiology, exploring patterns of disease, threats to health and EPI methods for prevention, control, and treatment.
prereq_raw: PH 201 , and PH 210 or MATH 140X or MATH 161 or higher; or instructor approval.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Youth Risk and Protection—Public Health Research, Practice, and Policy
description: Application of public health, related to youth health risks and protective factors using an eco-developmental framework.

subject: PH
title: The United States Health Care System
description: Overview of the U.S. health care system. Topics will include health economics, health service expenditures, comparative health systems, health policy, and issues of cost containment, access, and quality of care.

subject: PH
title: Public Health and the Environment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with environmental effects on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Sophomore standing and above.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Biology and Pathophysiology
description: Explores the biological basis of human disease and the role public health measures play in reducing both the extent and impact of chronic and acute diseases on individuals and society.
prereq_raw: PH 201 , and one of the following: BIOL 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 or FSHN 185 .

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Biostatistics
description: Basic biostatistics methods in public health and biomedical research. Topics covered include data collection, data analyses, and interpretation of statistical results. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Epidemiology
description: Students will gain a deeper understanding of the core concepts used in epidemiologic research and practice. Upon completion, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct an epidemiologic study. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health I: Health Promotion for Individuals and Groups
description: Focus on the application of social and behavioral theory in health education, and how health promotion programs are constructed for various populations with an emphasis on cultural diversity and social determinants of health.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Behavioral Health II: Health Promotion in Communities
description: Introduction to health education and health promotion programming in public health, and to social/behavioral theories used to develop health interventions that affect communities, institutions, and policies. Introduction to common program planning models.

subject: PH
title: Tobacco & Community Disparities
description: Assessing the facilitators and barriers of smoking initiation, cessation, and exposure to second-hand smoke within communities. Use of photovoice and its application to policy and addressing disparities.

subject: PH
title: Health Policy and Management
description: Examines the role that health policy and management plays in population-based public health practice, including the delivery, quality, and costs of health care and the structure, process, and outcomes of health services delivery. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
prereq_raw: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200 ; or consent.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health—an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: ( PH 201 , or ANSC 200 , or BIOC 141 , or BIOL 101 , or BIOL 171 , or BOT 101 , or ERTH 101 , or GES 102 , or OEST 101 , or OCN 102 , or ATMO 150, or SOC 180 ) with a minimum grade of C or better; or consent.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Environmental Microbiology
description: Lecture/discussion. Will define the nature and biological activities of microorganisms in different environments and evaluate the effects of these microbes on human activities and health. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Social Determinants of Indigenous Peoples’ Health
description: Examines indigenous peoples’ health inequities using social determinants of health framework: considers this approach within the historical, political, cultural, and social context of Indigenous population’s health status to generate solutions.

subject: PH
title: Application of Public Health Principles in Research and Practice
description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health projects and associated methods while working to develop a written applied learning project literature review. Students will present their findings at a public forum.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Applied Learning Experience
description: Allows students to execute an independent, mentor-supervised, applied learning project as implementation of skills learned in previous public health coursework. Applied project is a required component of the public health undergraduate degree program.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Undergraduate Capstone Seminar
description: Synthesis of public health knowledge, skills, and practice acquired during the public health undergraduate degree. Students also reflect on, finalize, and present written applied learning experience projects at a public form. Senior standing and higher.
prereq_raw: completed public health applied learning experience and consent.

children.text: completed public health applied learning experience

subject: PH
title: (Alpha) Current Issues and Topics in Public Health
description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

subject: PH
title: Current Issues and Topics in Public Health: biostatistics
description: Current and emerging issues and varying topics related to public health. (B) biostatistics; (E) epidemiology; (H) health policy and management; (S) social and behavioral health sciences; (T) public health.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing and above.

subject: PH

subject: PH
title: Public Health Foundations
description: Focus will provide a broad introduction to the field of public health and orientation to overarching issues in the field.

subject: PH
title: U.S. Health Care Services and Policy
description: Overview of the historical, conceptual, ethical and political context for health care delivery in the U.S. Explores current trends, practices and issues in the delivery of health care services in both private and public sector.

subject: PH
title: Public Health Biology
description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management.

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals to One Health
description: Familiarizes students with the fundamentals of One Health—an interdisciplinary field of study linking ecosystems to human and animal health. It uses contemporary examples and emphasizes oceans and human health connections.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Introduction to Health Promotion Theory and Methods
description: Individual and community health; implications for public health practice, individual and social change processes.

subject: PH
title: Health Economics
description: Integrated concepts in health economics and its application towards health policy issues; market failures in health care; factors affecting U.S. health care spending potential impact on equity/efficiency stemming from changes in health care delivery.

subject: PH
title: Cultural Competency in Health Care
description: Presents both analytical and practical approaches to cultural competency domains, concepts, models, frameworks, patterns and communication that occur in cross-cultural healthcare situations.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Activism
description: Examines how Indigenous Peoples and their allies (individually and collectively) accomplish social change in society.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Health Seminar
description: Examines public health through an Indigenous lens, integrates competencies across all public health disciplines, and will apply them in context of working for and with Indigenous communities to improve health and wellness.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy
description: Examines major federal and local policies that impact health and health care delivery in the U.S. and other nations; considers effectiveness of these policy-making institutions for improving population health; covers methods in policy analysis.

subject: PH
title: Grant Writing in Public Health
description: Lecture/ discussion on grant writing with public health focus. Includes basic components of grant proposals, assessing appropriate funding opportunities, data sources/resources for justifying grants, and the funder’s perspective. Student will prepare a brief foundation grant proposal.

subject: PH
title: Program Planning, Management, Evaluation, and Leadership
description: Foundation to inform, educate, and improve health for individuals, communities, and populations. Knowledge/acquisition of skills through program planning, management, evaluation and leadership that span the social-ecological range from individual-level to population-level programs.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: EPID and PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Needs Assessment
description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.

subject: PH
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

subject: PH
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.

subject: PH
title: Global Health and Human Security
description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulnerability in the global context with a special focus on problems with high likelihood and risk in the Pacific.

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics I
description: Introduction to statistical methods for public health sciences. Probability, experimental design, t tests and analysis of variance, 2X2 contingency tables, linear regression, introduction to life tables.

subject: PH
title: Biostatistics II
description: Poisson distribution, Fisher’s exact test, contrasts in ANOVA, two way ANOVA, multiple linear regression and analysis of covariance, path analysis, logistic regression, method of maximum likelihood, likelihood ratio tests.
prereq_raw: PH 655 , completion of one semester of calculus; or consent.

children.text: completion of one semester of calculus;

subject: PH
title: Computer Applications in Public Health
description: Applications of computers to problems common to public health. Emphasis on data analysis and processing using existing computer programs.

subject: PH
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, and urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology I
description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods. Topics covered include: outbreak investigation, measures of morbidity and mortality, measurements of risk, biological variability, screening, measurements of error, sampling, statistical significance, study design, and association and causation.

subject: PH
title: Principles of Epidemiology II
description: Lecture/ discussion on: design and interpretation of experimental and observational studies; causation and casual inference; biases in study design; random error and statistics role in epidemiology; and epidemiological data analysis.

subject: PH
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

subject: PH
title: Seminar in Infectious Disease Control
description: Strategies for controlling important infectious diseases in the Pacific area. Emphasis on epidemiology, ecology, and public health principles.
prereq_raw: PH 663 (or concurrent) and one semester in microbiology, or consent.

subject: PH
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

subject: PH
title: Epidemiological Study Design Critique
description: Critique of study design using published public health literature. Emphasis on exchange of ideas, alternative approaches; stresses epidemiology as science of public health.

subject: PH
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

subject: PH
title: Leading and Managing Health Programs
description: Assess how to organize community partnerships to create and communicate a shared vision for a changing future; discuss solutions to organizational and community challenges; maximize motivation to reach public health goals.

subject: PH
title: Native Health Ethics, Law, and Policy
description: Review theories and laws concerning health care ethics, policy, and practice using Indigenous case studies. Topics include Indigenous health systems, advocacy, and the intersecting issues of self-determination, ethics, agenda setting, and the policy cycle.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
description: Applications of evidence-based knowledge about the social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians.

subject: PH
title: Community Engaged Research and Practice
description: Explores collaborative and engaged approaches with communities in public health research and practice. With a focus on Indigenous Peoples’ health, we delve into Indigenous knowledge and empowerment in evaluation, needs assessment, intervention, and health promotion.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Hawaiʻi Public Health Policies on Infectious Diseases
description: Examines quarantine/isolation of patients infected with Hanson’s disease. Focus on PH policies before 1823 and after; analysis of other infections in Hawaiʻi and the world to examine differences in policies and their effect on the public.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Managing Global Health Service Delivery
description: Provides knowledge, skills, attitudes and resources that health managers require to manage and maintain the quality of partnerships, facilities, programs, community services, people, drugs, and information in limited resources settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners.

subject: PH
title: Environmental Determinants of Health
description: Environmental factors in personal and community health; implications for public health practice. Consideration of major issues from local, U.S., and international perspectives.

subject: PH
title: Global Nutrition
description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

subject: PH
title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH
title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Nutritional Epidemiology
description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

subject: PH
title: Global Health Challenges
description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change.

subject: PH
title: Fundamentals of Environmental Epidemiology
description: Examines the complex relationship between environmental contaminants and human health. Emphasis on environmental epidemiology study design, environmental exposure monitoring and risk assessment, disease and environmental exposure mapping, and spatial data analysis and modeling with GIS.

subject: PH
title: Preparation for Public Health Practice
description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health workforce readiness and professional skills while exploring possible field experience options.
prereq_raw: PH 600 and completion of 9 graduate PH credit hours.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

children.text: completion of 9 graduate PH credit hours

subject: PH
title: Promoting Physical Activity
description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

subject: PH
title: Health Communication
description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material, and a practical training in motivational counseling skills.

subject: PH
title: Health Promotion Research
description: Focus on research methods commonly used in health promotion. Topics will include randomized trials, quasi-experimental design, sampling, measurement, and correlational studies. Labwork will focus on the use of SPSS to analyze data for applied research problems.

subject: PH
title: Community-Based Participatory Research
description: Explores ways academic and lay communities collaborate on research, key theoretical perspectives in the development of CBPR, and the challenges in implementing CBPR approaches. Format includes lectures, discussions, readings, writing assignments, and a fieldwork project.

subject: PH
title: Systematic Literature Review in Public Health
description: Imparts skills in conducting a systematic review of the literature. Students provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work. Intended for doctoral students to complete their qualifying paper.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only. Consent or PhD in PH or EPID only. Class Standing Restrictions: Doctoral students only.

subject: PH
title: Indigenous Applied Research Methods

restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only.

subject: PH

description: Advanced application of health disparities research methodologies to address health and social injustices faced by Indigenous people. Grounded in survey design, implementation, and analyses through a public health and Indigenous lens.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PH majors only or consent. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Qualitative Research for Public Health Sciences
description: Provides a basic understanding of qualitative research approaches, methodologies, and techniques and for public health research and practice (needs assessment, program development, and evaluation strategies).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PH
title: Statistical Methods in Epidemiological Research
description: Multiple variable statistical methods currently used in chronic disease epidemiology. Logistic regression, conditional logistic regression, proportional hazards regression modelling, generalized estimating equation-based methods, delta method approximations, exact tests.

subject: PH
title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
description: Will cover selected topics in chronic diseases with critical analysis of the current epidemiologic literature. Methodologic issues, contemporary findings and recommendations for future research will be discussed.

subject: PH
title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.

subject: PH

description: Provide an understanding of the relationship between health behaviors and outcomes including psychological, physiological, and quality of life aspects. It will also focus on the major theories of behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed on understanding concepts, principles, explanations, and how these are translated into practical interventions for adoption and maintaining behavior change.

subject: PH
title: Social Epidemiology
description: Examine the epidemiologic study of the social distribution and social determinants of states of health, including the identification of social-environmental exposures and their relation to physical and mental health outcomes.

subject: PH
title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
description: Covers modern methods for longitudinal data analysis. Topics include random effects and growth curve models, generalized linear models for longitudinal data including generalized estimating equations, and generalized linear mixed models.

subject: PH
title: Survival Analysis
description: Construction and interpretation of various types of life tables, treatment of censored data, proportional hazards, relative risk regression models, and parametric survival analysis.

subject: PH
title: Neuroepidemiology
description: Lecture/discussion providing an overview of the epidemiology of neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and their risk factors, and methodological considerations for the study of these diseases.

subject: PH

subject: PH

description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

subject: PH

description: Will explore several aspects of human health through the perspective of how natural selection and evolution influence disease risk, with the aim of improving treatment and prevention.
prereq_raw: PH 663 (with a minimum grade of B).
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PHIL

description: (LED) Introduction to critical thinking and its application in everyday life. The materials progress from logic and the structure of argument to fallacies and the nature of science.

subject: PHIL

description: Sport, from ancient ritual to modern spectacle, embodies ethics, aesthetics, and identity. This course examines Western and non-Western traditions, exploring sport as bodily cultivation, cultural practice, and philosophical lens on human flourishing and social division.

subject: PHIL

description: Everyone wants to be happy. What is happiness? How do we become happy? Students examine and practice proposals from ancient philosophy and tragedy and recent psychology about the ingredients, methods, and difficulties of living well.

subject: PHIL
title: Introduction to World Philosophy I
description: Introduction to philosophy as it has manifested itself differently across cultures throughout the world. Focus on the development of philosophical thought from its beginnings up until 1500 CE.

subject: PHIL

description: Philosophy attempts to understand the human being and the societies they form. Introduces students to the notion of world philosophy, focusing upon thinkers who have helped to shape our present.

subject: PHIL

description: What is happiness? reality? the best political community? Students explore ancient Greek and Roman philosophical responses to these and other fundamental questions, and develop skills of writing, reading, and oral communication.

subject: PHIL
title: Medieval to Enlightenment Philosophy
description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on translations of texts originally written by men and women in post-classical Latin and Arabic. Significant attention is paid to developing writing skills.

subject: PHIL
title: Modern Philosophy
description: Introduction to the history of philosophy based on texts or translations of “modern” works, that is works originally written in a modern European language.

subject: PHIL
title: Women Philosophers
description: Introduces students to the ideas of women philosophers.
prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

subject: PHIL
title: Existentialism: Freedom, Being, Death
description: Introduction to major thinkers and fundamental concepts and debates of Existentialism, taking Existentialism as a global movement expressed in philosophical texts, literature, and film. Significant attention is paid to developing writing skills.

subject: PHIL
title: Philosophy and Science Fiction
description: Will use important works of science fiction and philosophy to explore philosophical questions, such as the nature of personal identity and the meaning of human life.

subject: PHIL

prereq_raw: one PHIL 100-level course or consent of instructor.

subject: PHIL

prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or BUS or BLAW, or consent.
