subject: PHYS
title: Individual Work in Advanced Physics
description: Limited to students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Applications of Mathematics in Physical Sciences
description: Mathematical methods, techniques; applications to problems in physical sciences.
prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A , and MATH 307 or MATH 311 ; or consent. Recommended: upper division mathematics course.

subject: PHYS
title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
description: Laws of thermodynamics, heat transfer, kinetic theory, statistical mechanics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics I
description: Crystal structure: lattice vibrations; phonon effects; electronic processes in solids (metals, semiconductors, and superconductors).

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Physics II
description: Energy-band calculations, optical processes, Josephson effect, theories of dielectrics and magnetism, physics of color centers, order-disorder transformation.

subject: PHYS
title: Electromagnetic Waves
description: Field equations, plane, spherical and guided waves.

subject: PHYS
title: Physical Optics
description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
prereq_raw: PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C) or ECE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-), or consent.

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) or ECE 372 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) , or consent

subject: PHYS
title: General Relativity & Cosmology
description: Introduction to general relativity & cosmology. Spacetime metrics, geodesics, Einstein field equations, black holes. Geometry of the universe, redshift, cosmological distances. Cosmological models, dark matters, dark energy. Big Bang nucleosynthesis, recombination, cosmic microwave background, inflation.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274 ; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent). Recommended: ASTR 242 .

subject: PHYS
title: Electronics for Physicists
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Investigation of Kirchhoff’s Laws, electromagnetic circuit theory. Fourier analysis and stability theory with circuits. Applications to physical measurements are stressed. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Electronics for Physicists
description: Introduction to high performance solid state instrumentation by means of practical research electronics: printed circuit board design/fabrication; complex programmable logic design/verification; integrated circuit SPICE simulation. Detector fabrication and test emphasis during final project.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics I
description: Wave mechanics, Schroedinger equation, angular momenta, potential problems.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274 , PHYS 310 , PHYS 350 , PHYS 400 (or concurrent); either MATH 244 or MATH 253A ; and either MATH 311 or MATH 307 ; or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory I
description: Advanced experiments involving nuclear spectroscopy, angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization, chaos, measurement of speed of light, numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274L and PHYS 480 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics II
description: Continuation of PHYS 480 ; atomic physics, scattering, perturbation theory.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Physics Laboratory II
description: Advanced experiments involving measurement of the muon lifetime, crystal x-ray diffraction, nuclear magnetic resonance, the Mössbauer effect, and numerical simulations. Development of professional writing skills; preparation of formal reports in style of scientific journal articles.
prereq_raw: PHYS 274L , PHYS 480 , and PHYS 480L ; or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Professional Ethics for Physicists
description: Seminar on ethical principles and their application to physics, astronomy, and closely-related fields. Participants present and discuss current and historical examples of ethical issues. Emphasis on developing oral communication skills.
prereq_raw: PHYS 310 or ASTR 300 (or concurrent), or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PHYS, ASTP, and ASTR majors only.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern Physics
description: Introduction to nuclear and elementary-particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
description: Mathematical tools of theoretical physics. Continuation of PHYS 400 but with an independent selection of topics.

subject: PHYS
title: Analytical Mechanics
description: Dynamics of particles, particle systems; rigid bodies; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations; special relativity.

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics I
description: Potential theory, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, boundary value problems.
prereq_raw: PHYS 450 ; and PHYS 600 (or concurrent), or MATH 402 .

subject: PHYS
title: Electrodynamics II
description: Relativistic electrodynamics, radiation by charged particles.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Optics
description: Contemporary advanced applications in optics including nonlinear optics and optical parametric oscillators, atomic lasers and laser systems, and free-electron lasers.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.
prereq_raw: PHYS 400 or PHYS 481 or PHYS 600 and MATH 402 .

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Mechanics
description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar
description: Discussions and reports on physical theory and recent developments.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PHYS
title: Condensed Matter Seminar
description: Results and discussions of current topics in condensed matter physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Atomic and Solid-State Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in atomic, surface, and solid-state physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Seminar on Elementary Particle Physics
description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in elementary particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: PHYS
title: Topics in Particles and Fields
description: Topics in current theoretical research; e.g., unified field theories, general relativity, gravitation, and cosmology.

subject: PHYS
title: Special Topics: Experimental Physics
description: Topics in current experimental research in low-energy physics, high-energy physics, cross-disciplinary physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Advanced Topics in Condensed Matter Theory
description: Topics in condensed matter theory, e.g., group theory, many-body techniques, renormalization group, density functional theory, other topics of current interest.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics I
description: Equilibrium thermodynamics; Gibbs ensembles; quantum statistics; ideal and non-ideal Fermi; Bose and Boltzmann gases; phase transitions; and critical phenomena.

subject: PHYS
title: Statistical Physics II
description: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics, transport theory, fluctuation dissipation theorem, many-body Green’s function methods, normal Fermi and Bose liquids, superfluidity, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Modern General Relativity
description: Differential geometry, special relativity, Einstein equations, gravitational phenomena, equivalence principles, black holes, gravitational waves, cosmology, relativistic stars, experimental tests, computational techniques.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate students only in PHYS or ASTR.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory I
description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics.

subject: PHYS
title: Quantum Field Theory II
description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Nuclear and Particle Physics II
description: Quantum chromodynamics; electroweak interactions; the standard model. Techniques of particle physics.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, electron-electron interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Solid-State Theory
description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

subject: PHYS
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: PLAN
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: PLAN
title: Survey of Urban Sociology
description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Introduction to Planning
description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawaiʻi planning—research problems from a multidisciplinary approach. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Reading in Planning
description: Independent research on topics in urban and regional planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Examines resilience thinking as it relates to making cities resilient to environmental hazards in the context of climate change. Draws on relevant theories, policy, and case studies in urban planning. Emphasis on instruction in writing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Geography
description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.
prereq_raw: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330 , or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.
prereq_raw: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Principles of Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
prereq_raw: PLAN 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312 , or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: GIS for Community & Environmental Planning
description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Housing, Land, and Community
description: Analyzes housing availability, particularly affordable housing, and its relationship to land use and community building. Examines public policies impacting housing, land use, community development, and ways they can be improved. Emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: PLAN
title: Public Policy and Planning Theory
description: Designed to a) impart a historic and comparative perspective on the evolution of urban and regional planning in public policy; b) explore the spatial and built environment dimensions of society, planning and policy; c) assess the justifications for planning and differing processes of planning in the U.S. and Asia-Pacific with a focus on the role of the planner in policy formulation and implementation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or with permission.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Methods
description: Introduction of the basic methods in planning, including problem definition, research design, hypothesis testing, statistical reasoning, forecasting and fundamental data analysis techniques required by the planning program and the planning profession.
prereq_raw: one of ECON 321 , GEO 380 , or SOC 476 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN and ARCH majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Advanced Planning Theory
description: Advanced planning theory for PhD students (others by petition) to prepare for careers in planning education and/or high level professional practice. Covers key contemporary planning policy issues and themes from the perspective of values, explanations of the real world, policy alternatives and implementation. Students must have passed PLAN 600 or equivalent (by petition) with a B or better.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: PhD students only or by consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Economics
description: Reviews and builds skills in applying basic theories and principles of urban and regional economics in contemporary U.S., Hawaiʻi and Asia-Pacific.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Qualitative Methods in Planning
description: Provides a general introduction to qualitative research methods for planning and planning research. Includes data collection methods (focus groups, interviews, ethnography, participant observation, and participatory action research) and various analytic methods and approaches.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Models
description: Allocation, decision, derivation, and forecasting models used in the analysis of demographic, economic, land use, and transportation phenomena in urban and regional planning.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Comparative Planning Histories
description: Provides students with an overview of the history of urban and regional planning in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, and the role that planning has played in shaping contemporary urban settlements.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: PLAN
title: Introduction to Public Policy
description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation.

subject: PLAN
title: Politics and Development: China
description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

subject: PLAN
title: Causality in the Social Sciences: A Relatively Gentle Introduction
description: An introduction to the statistical methods used to identify plausibly causal effects with non-experimental data.
prereq_raw: PLAN 601 with a minimum grade of A- or equivalent.

subject: PLAN
title: Community Planning and Social Policy
description: Social issues and conditions; consequences of social policies experienced by different groups; community social plans and programs organized by various kinds of agencies and organizations.

subject: PLAN
title: Foundations in Indigenous Planning
description: Examines the gaps in conventional planning curricula by centering Indigenous planning, with emphasis on Native Hawaiian knowledge. Students explore culturally grounded frameworks often marginalized in conventional urban and regional planning discourse.
prereq_raw: PLAN 600 with a minimum grade of B.

subject: PLAN
title: Housing
description: Housing delivery systems as an aspect of urban and regional planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Community-Based Planning
description: Planning and programmatic aspects of community-based development projects. East-West and local planning perspectives on participatory development and intentional communities.

subject: PLAN
title: Community Economic Development
description: Community-based economic development approaches and methods explored with an emphasis on low income communities.

subject: PLAN
title: Multiculturalism in Planning and Policy
description: Graduate seminar focuses on issues of governance, policy and planning in diverse multicultural societies. Differences in backgrounds, languages, privilege, preferences and values are often expressed in planning and policy controversies such as affirmative action and land use planning. Will examine these controversies and explore theories of governance in a multicultural setting.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Planning and Policy
description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PLAN
title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

subject: PLAN
title: Coastal Planning and Management
description: Theory and practice of coastal planning and management in the U.S. and abroad. Case studies investigate topics such as coastal land conservation, marine protected areas, coastal hazards, fisheries, and aquaculture.

subject: PLAN
title: Environmental Valuation and Policy
description: Build valuation skills to assess best use, conservation, and policies relating to environmental amenities. Provides an overview of policy solutions to environmental degradation used by planners.

subject: PLAN
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/ Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via video-conferencing.

subject: PLAN
title: Topics in Resource Management
description: Issues, analytic techniques and management strategies for different resource systems including land, water, energy, coastal resources, forests and fisheries. Course focus varies from year to year.

subject: PLAN
title: Negotiation and Mediation in Planning
description: Applicability and limitations of selected approaches; role of planners; impact on planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Environmental Problems
description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

subject: PLAN
title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills.
prereq_raw: one of the following courses with a minimum grade of B: PLAN 627 ; or PACE 429 , PACE 447 , PACE 477 , PACE 647 , PACE 652 , or PACE 668 ; or COMG 455 or SOC 730 ; or LAW 508 ; or MGT 660 .
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

children.text: courses with a minimum grade of B : PLAN 627
; or PACE 429 , PACE 447 , PACE 477 , PACE 647 , PACE 652 , or PACE 668 ; or COMG 455 or SOC 730 ; or LAW 508 ; or MGT 660

subject: PLAN
title: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia
description: Key issues and policies in urban planning, rural-urban relations, rural regional planning, and frontier settlement in Asia and the Pacific.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning in Hawaiʻi and Pacific Islands
description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PLAN
title: Globalization and Urban Policy
description: Urbanization and urban policies in the Asia and Pacific region with focus on the international dimension of national and local spatial restructuring.

subject: PLAN
title: Shelter and Services in Asia
description: Examines government and non-government organizations’ responses to urban and rural shelter issues and services in Asia.

subject: PLAN
title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

subject: PLAN
title: Environment and Development
description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

subject: PLAN
title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Policies and Programs
description: Land use public policy planning in urban and regional settings. Growth management and land use guidance systems.

subject: PLAN
title: Neighborhood and Community Land Use Planning
description: Land use planning for urban neighborhoods and small towns. Theory and practice of neighborhood planning. Neighborhood and community dynamics, reinvestment, and stabilization.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Urban Infrastructure
description: Introduction to the planning of various urban infrastructures. Explores approaches and tools to plan, evaluate, and regulate urban infrastructure systems in support of sustainable and resilient cities and communities.

subject: PLAN
title: Project Planning and Management
description: Examines project management in theory and practice and the roles and responsibilities of the project manager. Focuses on planning, organizing, and controlling the efforts of projects.

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Planning
description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Transportation Policy and Planning
description: Theory and practice of urban transportation planning in developed and developing countries with an emphasis on the U.S., Asia, and Pacific region.

subject: PLAN
title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

subject: PLAN
title: Research Design Seminar
description: Research design and preparation of thesis proposal. Normally taken after admission to candidacy in MURP.
prereq_raw: ( PLAN 600 or PLAN 601 or PLAN 603 ) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Policy Implementation and Program Evaluation
description: Implementation and evaluation in public policy analysis; philosophical and methodological issues; impact of policies and plans; use of evaluation research in program implementation.

subject: PLAN
title: Applied Geographic Information Systems: Public Policy and Spatial Analysis
description: Use of advanced and specialized spatial methods and models in urban and regional planning. Uses GIS software and builds upon PLAN 601 . Skills are useful applied to planning, economic development, and environmental planning and resource management.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Research Methods
description: Advanced methods and deterministic and stochastic models used in urban and regional planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Collaboration Between Sectors
description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems.

subject: PLAN
title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or departmental approval.

subject: PLAN
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
description: Overview to the field of disaster management and humanitarian assistance with a specific focus on risk reduction. Includes background knowledge and skills for preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and adaptation to hazards and threats.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Disaster Science: Understanding Hazards and Disasters
description: Combined lecture/discussion focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and and planning.

subject: PLAN
title: Humanitarian Assistance: Principles, Practices and Politics
description: Combined lecture/discussion aimed at understanding the theoretical basis and working structure of humanitarian assistance programs and international responses to natural and human-induced disasters.

subject: PLAN
title: Information Systems for Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
description: Combined lecture/laboratory in disaster management focusing on essential methodological and practical issues that are involved in spatial analyses using GIS and other information technologies to inform decision making related to natural hazards, disasters, and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.
prereq_raw: PLAN 473 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: PLAN
title: Disaster Recovery: Theory and Practice
description: How do communities recover from disaster? Provides students with an overview of recovery theory and an understanding of how planners, policy makers, and ordinary citizens rebuild communities, cities, and nations following catastrophic events.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: PLAN
title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

subject: PLAN
title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PLAN
title: Historic Preservation Planning
description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

subject: PLAN
title: Site Planning
description: Fundamental principles that guide site planning, including planning and design determinants of the site taking into account its regional context, site-specific characteristics and applicable codes, ordinances, and standards.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN and ARCH majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Land Use Management and Control
description: Survey course of public land use management.

subject: PLAN
title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: LAND, ARCH, and PLAN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Reading and Research
prereq_raw: Consent of instructor and department chair.

subject: PLAN
title: Thesis Research
description: Limited to MURP students under Plan A.

subject: PLAN
title: Homeland Security: Terrorism
description: Combined lecture/discussion in disaster management and humanitarian assistance track focusing on developing a multidisciplinary understanding of international terrorism and anti-terrorism planning and response.

subject: PLAN
title: Seminar in Planning Theory
description: Special topics in theory, history, analysis.

subject: PLAN
title: Seminar in Planning Practice
description: Project planning, programming, and similar topics.

subject: PLAN
title: Planning Practicum
description: Team experience in defining and addressing a current planning problem; identification, substantive review, research design, preparation and presentation of analysis. Topic varies. Limited to 10 students.

subject: PLAN
title: Directed Project
description: Individual project in analysis, plan preparation and evaluation, and policy/program evaluation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Urban Design Studio
description: Group experience in defining urban and regional design problems and potentials, developing and evaluating alternatives, formulating strategies for implementation.
prereq_raw: ( PLAN 600 and PLAN 601 ) with a minimum grade of B, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PLAN and ARCH majors only.

subject: PLAN
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: PhD student only.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Discussion of politics as an activity and of political problems, systems, ideologies, processes.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Science
description: Discussion of politics as an activity and of political problems, systems, ideologies, processes.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to World Politics
description: Power and contemporary world politics since 1945 with emphasis on the U.S. role.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to American Politics
description: American political processes and institutions, as seen through alternative interpretations. Emphasis on opportunities and limitations for practical political participation.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Indigenous Politics
description: Foundations in Indigenous politics from diverse cultural perspectives and across regions. Addresses political issues facing Indigenous peoples at global and local levels, with attention to Indigenous epistemologies, languages, movements, and institutions.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Global Politics
description: Foundations in global politics from political, historical, and multicultural perspectives.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawaiʻi and the Asia-Pacific region.

subject: POLS
title: Politics and Public Policy
description: Perspectives on the role of government in guiding economies and civil societies with particular emphasis on the recent U.S.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Political Futures
description: Introduction to political future studies. Using science fact and fiction, shows how past and present images of the future influence people’s actions.

subject: POLS
title: Introduction to Hawaiʻi Politics
description: Introduction to political history, institutions, processes, and issues in Hawaiʻi grounded in Native Hawaiian perspectives.

subject: POLS
title: Media and Politics
description: Influences and effects of media on politics. Setting public agendas, interpreting events, manipulating the political process, political learning through popular culture.

subject: POLS
title: Reading and Writing Politics
description: Develop skills needed to read and write political texts. Weigh competing views; read and analyze texts for what they do and do not say; craft and defend evidence-based arguments; practice writing mechanics and style.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: POLS majors only or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Problems of War and Peace
description: Introduction to the problems individuals and political communities currently face with respect to war, peace, and international conflict. Includes questions of human nature, economy, morality, nuclear deterrence, arms control and disarmament, and alternatives to war.

subject: POLS
title: Political Design and Futuristics
description: Possible social and political alternatives for the future. Conditions likely if present trends continue, formulation of visions of better futures, means for their achievement.

subject: POLS
title: Race and Politics
description: Racial inequality in the U.S.; mechanisms of institutional racism in employment, education, criminal justice, electoral politics.

subject: POLS
title: Hawaiʻi Politics
description: Introduction to and critical study of institutions, governments, and political processes in Hawaiʻi. Attends to race, class, gender, sexuality, indigeneity and nationality. Grounded in Native Hawaiian perspectives, with an emphasis on comparative study and dialogue.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: POLS
title: Native Hawaiian Politics
description: Critical study of issues in contemporary Native Hawaiian politics, with an emphasis on application and active engagement.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or consent.

subject: POLS
title: (Alpha) Topics in Hawaiʻi Politics
description: Intensive examination of particular institutions, processes, and issues. (B) the military in Hawaiʻi; (C) political thought in Hawaiian; Taught in Hawaiian; (D) politics of food.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher or consent.

description: Intensive Intermediate Portuguese course covers content of PORT 201 and PORT 202 combined. Hybrid format combines 3 credits online and 3 credits face to face.

subject: PORT
title: Conversation
description: Intensive practice in spoken Portuguese, focusing on the preparation and completion of oral tasks and presentations. 40 or more of the grade is based on 3-4 oral communication presentations.

subject: PORT
title: Third-Level Portuguese Abroad
description: Intensive, formal instruction at the third-year level in Portuguese language: reading, writing, pronunciation, grammar, or conversation in a Portuguese-speaking country.

subject: PORT
title: Fourth-Level Portuguese Abroad
description: Intensive formal instruction at the fourth-year level in Portuguese language, linguistics, culture, civilization, film, or literature in a Portuguese-speaking country.

subject: PPC
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.

subject: PRAK
title: Introduction to Prakrit I
description: Survey of principal Prakrit languages; selected readings and analysis.
prereq_raw: PALI 381 , PALI 382 , SNSK 281, and SNSK 282; or equivalent.

subject: PRAK
title: Introduction to Prakrit II
description: Continuation of PRAK 481 .

subject: PSTY
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Individualized directed readings and/or research in mental health and psychiatry under the supervision of an instructor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors.

subject: PSTY
title: Psychiatry Longitudinal Clerkship
description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, including knowledge, skills, attitudes for assessment, diagnosis, and management of psychiatric problems in medical practice, inpatient, and emergency room settings. Emphasis on development and application of psychosocial cultural formulations in all areas of psychiatric and medical practice.
prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses.
coreq_raw: FMCH 532 , MED 532 , OBGN 532 , PED 532 , SURG 532 , and SURG 535.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: MD majors only.
