subject: PSTY
title: Philosophy & Human Suffering
description: To see how various philosophies and religions have tackled the question, “why is there suffering in the world?” Read short excerpts from “classic” texts and discuss in a welcoming atmosphere and draw own conclusions. Medical students only.

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Psychology
description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Psychology
description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Personal Development
description: The application of psychology to the understanding, management, and enhancement of one’s life.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Gender
description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to gender and its impact on the lives of women and men: socialization of gender, mental health, racial identity, majority-minority status, sexual orientation, life-span issues and violence.

subject: PSY
title: Survey of Research Methods
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab) Survey of standard methods and related conceptual issues employed in psychological research. Both experimental and non-experimental methods will be reviewed.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Behavioral Psychology
description: Outline of basic learning principles. A general, unified approach to study of human personality and behavior. Based upon a learning conception; various areas of psychology and the other social sciences are treated.

subject: PSY
title: Statistical Techniques
description: Frequency distributions; graphic methods; central tendency; variability; correlation; reliability; tests of significance.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Psychobiology
description: Survey of study of behavior from a natural sciences viewpoint. Evolution, ethological analysis of behavior genetics, neural mechanisms, drugs and behavior, biological development.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Psychology
description: Emotional, mental, physical, social development from infancy to adulthood; interests and abilities at different age levels.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Personality
description: Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: History, theories, nature of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Community Psychology
description: Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stress, health, intergroup relations, culture, ethnicity, social competence, and community empowerment.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
description: Psychology applied to education, including cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching, learning, development, and research. Develops knowledge and written communication skills through an introduction to classroom assessment, instruction, motivation, classroom management, and standardized testing.

subject: PSY
title: Learning and Motivation
description: Theoretical interpretations; survey of major theorists and contemporary controversial issues; major influences in classical and instrumental conditioning.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Emotion
description: Survey of traditional views and leading theories, and research in related topics.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: Survey of cognitive processes involved in perception, attention, memory, language, problem-solving, reasoning, judgment, intelligence and consciousness, among others.

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Coverage of the relationship between the brain and body on learning and memory, stress, motivated and regulatory behavioral functions, and mental disorders.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Coverage of the principles of pharmacology in relation to the effects of drug actions on the brain and behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Sensation and Perception
description: In-depth coverage of the basic principles involved in sensing and perceiving our environment.

subject: PSY
title: Social Development of Children
description: Survey of the social and emotional development of children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Development and Aging
description: Overview from a multidisciplinary, life-span perspective. Includes research techniques, personality development, family relationships, occupational attainment, death.

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Psychological theories and cultural systems; understanding of own and other cultures; psychological and cultural perception of social motivation; cultural similarities and differences in interpersonal relations.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
description: Psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, and societal regulation of intimate relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Abnormal Psychology
description: Nature and causes of psychological disorders.

subject: PSY
title: Consumer Behavior
description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

subject: PSY
title: History of Psychology
description: Origin and development of contemporary points of view.
prereq_raw: PSY 100 . Recommended: 9 credit hours in psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar on the Psychology of Knowledge
description: Selected topics in the psychology of knowledge and mind from Western and/or non-Western perspectives.
repeatable_raw: In different topics up to 9 credit hours.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum in Psychology
description: Supervised psychological experience in school, clinic, hospital, industry, social welfare, government, etc.

subject: PSY
title: Teaching General Psychology
description: Supervised experience.
prereq_raw: PSY 100 , at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology, and written consent.

children.text: at least 12 additional credit hours in psychology,

subject: PSY
title: General Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research.

subject: PSY
title: Psychometrics: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory, research, or methodology relevant to individual differences, measurement, or aspects of psychometrics.

subject: PSY
title: Experimental Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research, in cognitive psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Psychobiology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in psychobiology, physiological psychology, or sensory processes.

subject: PSY
title: Clinical Child and Adolescent Psychology
description: Social and emotional maladjustment in children and adolescents, developmental disabilities, pediatric psychology, psychological interventions with children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Development Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in developmental psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in social psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology
description: Psychological principles for understanding and dealing with wellness and illness. Theories and research on stress-related disorders; prevention of stress through lifestyle and healthy behaviors.
prereq_raw: PSY 100 or consent. Recommended: PSY 220 or PSY 322 .

subject: PSY
title: Communicating Social Support
description: Survey of major theories, concepts, research, and application regarding communication and social support in interpersonal relationships and professional relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Teaching Personal Development
description: Supervised experience in leading a seminar in personal development.
prereq_raw: PSY 170 and 12 additional credits in PSY and written consent.

children.text: additional credits in PSY and written consent

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Topics in Adjustment/Treatment/Prevention
description: In-depth coverage of some area of theory and research in clinical psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

subject: PSY
title: Special Topics in Psychology
description: Covers topics of current or special interest not covered in regular course offerings or advanced topics seminars.

subject: PSY
title: Methodologic Foundations of Psychology
description: Methods used in psychological research; observational, correlational, and experimental types of design.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Regression
description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences and the general linear model with a focus on regression. Topics include correlation, bivariate and multiple regression, mediation, and moderation. Requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: PSY
title: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) and Related Methods
description: Introduction to ANOVA and its extensions from both traditional and general linear model approaches. Topics include single and multi-factor ANOVA, multiple comparisons, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), and repeated-measures ANOVA.

subject: PSY
title: Factor Analysis and Structural Equation Models (SEM)
description: Theories and applications to latent variables models. Topics include path analysis, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, structural equation models (SEM), multi-sample SEM, mean structure, latent growth curve models, and multilevel SEM. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

subject: PSY
title: Multivariate Analysis
description: Analysis of multiple dependent variables. Topics include multivariate normal distribution, Hotelling’s 72, multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA), discriminant analysis, cluster analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis (PCA).

subject: PSY
title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
description: Test theories and applications in education and social sciences. Topics include the true score model; reliability; generalizability theory; validity; item response theory; and applications in research. Class requires knowledge in ANOVA and regression.

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Psychometrics
description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include unidimensional and multidimensional models of item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, scaling methods, and current issues in psychometrics.

subject: PSY
title: Categorical Data Analysis
description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables. Topics include contingency tables; logistic regression; log-linear models; and introduction to generalized linear models.

subject: PSY
title: Analysis of Multilevel Models and Longitudinal Data
description: Theories and applications of analysis of nested (clustered) data. Topics include fixed and random effects, intra-class correlation, cross-sectional multilevel models, and multilevel models, and multilevel models with repeated measures and longitudinal data. Requires basic knowledge of regression.

subject: PSY
title: Principles of Learning
description: Survey of the principles of learning, including important discoveries in the development of the study of learning, major theories, and both basic and applied research in contemporary literature.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Psychology
description: In-depth survey of the computational and representational structures and processes of cognition. Special attention devoted to consideration of the relationship between brain, mind, and computation.

subject: PSY
title: Thinking
description: Provides an introduction to higher cognition (thinking and reasoning) and its foundations, particularly as they relate to the larger field of cognitive science.

subject: PSY
title: Comparative Cognition
description: Survey of the historical and contemporary study of cognition across species, including learning, memory, attention, navigation, reasoning, social interaction, and communication.

subject: PSY
title: Selected Topics in Comparative Psychology
description: Intensive review of comparative, communicative, sensory, or learning mechanisms in animals.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopharmacology
description: Basic principles of pharmacology as they apply to the brain and specific psychological disorders such as anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorders, schizophrenia, psychosis, memory, and drug use.

subject: PSY
title: Behavioral Neuroscience
description: Relation of central and peripheral nervous systems to behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Developmental Foundations
description: Historical, theoretical, and methodological foundations of developmental psychology.

subject: PSY
title: Cognitive Development
description: Familiarizes students with current research and theory in cognitive development through readings of original journal articles and monographs.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology
description: Theories and research in social cognition and behavior.

subject: PSY
title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Application of psychological theories to cross-cultural phenomena; assessment of cross-cultural processes and social motivations; culture and personality; research evaluation and design.

subject: PSY
title: Psychology and Social Issues
description: Conflict, dissent, community issues, problems; social change and its relation to mental disorder.

subject: PSY
title: Applied Social Psychology
description: Problems in use of social psychology principles in human affairs; multidisciplinary considerations.

subject: PSY
title: Social Psychology of Love and Sex
description: Seminar in psychosocial aspects of human sexual relationships. Social psychology of cognitive, emotional and physiological arousal, interpersonal attraction, mate selection, and antecedents and consequences of intimate relationships.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
description: Preparation for becoming a clinical psychologist with emphasis on scientist-practitioner model, professional ethics, diversity and professional development.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate student in psychology or consent of instructor.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment I
description: Psychometric theory; ethics; diversity issues; principles and methods of cognitive-intellectual, neuropsychological, and personality assessment.

subject: PSY
title: Introduction to Assessment II
description: Administration and interpretation of cognitive-intellectual and personality assessment devices.
prereq_raw: PSY 670 and PSY 671 or consent and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program.

subject: PSY
title: Advanced Assessment
description: Conceptual and methodological foundations of clinical applications of assessment.
prereq_raw: PSY 671 and PSY 672 and enrollment in Clinical Studies Program, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PSY majors only.

subject: PSY
title: Treatment Research
description: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to clinical treatment research methods and findings.
prereq_raw: PSY 670 (or concurrent) and PSY 671 , or consent.

subject: PSY
title: Psychopathology
description: Comprehensive study of the mental disorders across the lifespan.

subject: PSY
title: Child Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of children and adolescents.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Practicum
description: Supervised clinical assessment and treatment of adults.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum in Clinical Psychology
description: This supervision-style class will cover cases and issues related to students’ clinic work, supervision, or educational goals while training in external practicum sites.

subject: PSY
title: Cultural Community Psychology
description: Graduate seminar on cultural considerations and issues in the history, methods, theories, interventions, and professional roles in community psychology. Small class size (up to 10). Open to graduate students.

subject: PSY
title: Practicum: Behavioral Change and Community
description: Supervised experience in educational, mental health, correctional, consulting, or community action agencies.

subject: PSY
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis. Minimum of six credit hours is required.

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in History and Theory of Psychology

subject: PSY
title: Seminar in Quantitative Psychology
description: Specific and newly emerging topics in statistics, including casual inference, analysis of missing data, and statistical machine learning. Content varies and focuses on advanced topics not covered in other PSY methods and statistics courses.
prereq_raw: PSY 610 (with a minimum grade of B) or instructor consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PSY majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or instructor consent

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychometrics
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Experimental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Developmental Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Social Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Child Treatment
description: Psychological interventions for youth, as well as parent training.

subject: PSY
title: Adult Treatment: Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy
description: Training in cognitive-behavioral strategies for treating adults.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Enrolled in Clinical Studies Program only. PSY major only.

subject: PSY
title: Health Psychology: Behavioral and Biological Bases
description: Psychological and biological bases of health psychology and behavioral medicine. Overview of cognitive, behavioral, and psychophysiological mechanisms; theories and methods of prevention in physical disease.

subject: PSY
title: Research in Clinical Psychology
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Community Psychology Research
description: Supervised reading, discussion, research projects in areas of special interest.

subject: PSY
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: PUBA
title: Survey of Public Policy and Analysis
description: Students will learn about the policy making process, the results of policy decisions and how public policy is assessed, analyzed, and responded to. Also discusses important policy issues that currently fill the political landscape.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: PUBA
title: Research Methods for Policy Evaluation
description: Explores methodological approaches to the evaluation of public policies and strengths and weaknesses of various social science research methods. Students will learn how to employ them to determine the effectiveness of various public policies.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PUBA
title: Foundations of Nonprofit Management
description: Broad overview of nonprofit organizations, including what it means to be a nonprofit, strategies of nonprofit organizations, and the management of nonprofits. Topics include advocacy, leadership, and evaluating success. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: PUBA
title: Multicultural Leadership in Public Service
description: Develop students’ culturally agile leadership to allow them effectively lead in work on international, regional, and local projects and problems of compelling public interest that cross cultures. Junior standing or higher.

subject: PUBA
title: Practicum and Internship
description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent.

subject: PUBA
title: Directed Reading and Research in Public Administration
description: Independent research and reading on topics in public administration, public service, and community development.

subject: PUBA
title: Introduction to Research Approaches for Public and Nonprofit Organizations
description: Introduction to research approaches for conducting and evaluating the effectiveness of programs in the public and nonprofit sectors; performance measurement to inform managerial decision making.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only.

subject: PUBA
title: Introduction to Public Administration
description: Develop a comprehension of the history and foundation of public administration. Topics include economic, political, and social dynamics; decision-making and leadership theories, management challenges, human resources, budgeting, program evaluation, policy, and technology.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Organizations: Theory and Change
description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Leadership and Ethics
description: Applies leadership and ethical theories to public and non-profit sectors, focusing on ethical leadership; emphasizes critical thinking to address value conflicts; and teaches moral reasoning as a practical professional skill.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Effective Communication in Public Administration
description: Knowledge and skills to effectively communicate in the public sector. Focus on communication foundations and skills, levels and contexts of public sector communication, and handling challenges such as diverse and multi-cultural settings.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Personnel Management
description: Understand the pivotal role that effective human resource management (also known as personnel management) plays in improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include managing diversity, employment law and discrimination, performance appraisal, and labor-management relations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Administration Research Methods
description: Introduction to research methods for public administrators to understand the principles and methods used to conduct and analyze valid research. Examples are oriented to the field; theory and hands-on practice utilized.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Budgeting
description: Institutions and issues related to public-sector budgeting at federal, state, and local levels. Process of developing public budgets and constraints on public policy reflected in budgets.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA majors only.

subject: PUBA
title: Policy Analysis and Implementation
description: Explore contemporary policy issues relating to public administration practice. Develop analytic techniques and models of public policy-making processes, administrative rules, and policy implementation strategies. Learn how social forces, political, and economic pressures influence policy orientation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA majors only.

subject: PUBA
title: Reforming Public Organizations
description: Looks at the challenges and opportunities for changing public organizations so that they may be more successful in meeting their public responsibilities and better places for people to work. Focus is on the creation of positive images of organization and effective change strategies.

subject: PUBA
title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PUBA
title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change.

subject: PUBA
title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public institutions using economic lens. Rationale of property, contract, and tort law; evolution of administrative law, economic efficiency of common law system, effects of legal rules on economic behavior.

subject: PUBA
title: Collaboration for Public and Nonprofit Leaders
description: Theories, skills, and tools needed to effectively manage networks in government and nonprofit organizations; explores how to administer, assess performance, and evaluate success in these dynamic new partnerships.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only or consent.

subject: PUBA
title: Managing Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
description: Examines rationales, impacts, and various dimensions of diversity and inclusion beyond race and gender. Students learn and apply public management tools used to foster workplace diversity and inclusion.

subject: PUBA
title: ICT Policy and Planning
description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

subject: PUBA
title: Public Policy and Advocacy
description: Designed to deepen students’ ability to understand and influence the policy process in Hawaiʻi and the U.S.. Topics include theories of the policy process, and advocacy strategies, legal constraints, and coalition building.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA majors only or approval of instructor.

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management
description: Fundamental aspects of managing a nonprofit organization: overview of the nonprofit sector; mission and scope of nonprofit organizations; organizational structures and functions; resource and volunteer development; major management issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: PUBA
title: Nonprofit Management Practices and Tools
description: Skills and tools needed by nonprofit managers. Topics include but are not limited to grant-writing, strategic planning, business practices, program evaluation, and advocacy.

subject: PUBA
title: International Perspectives on Public Administration
description: Key dimensions of public administration systems on a global scale; historic and contemporary forces shaping national systems; the dimensions that distinguish them, the opportunities and constraints for comparison and the transfer of knowledge and experience.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or departmental approval.

subject: PUBA
title: Indigenous Governance
description: Overview of indigenous governing systems, particularly in the Americas and the Pacific. Students will learn the legal frameworks and principles of these systems, and how services are provided to citizens.

subject: PUBA
title: Special Topics
description: Topics of current interest in the field of public service and public administration, taught by regular and visiting faculty.
repeatable_raw: Up to 6 credits for different topics

subject: PUBA
title: MPA Practicum
description: Placement in public, private, and nonprofit organizations to observe and analyze organizational functions and processes while undertaking projects of use to the host agency.
prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B: PUBA 602 , PUBA 603 , and PUBA 604 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA majors only.

children.text: with a minimum grade of B : PUBA 602

subject: PUBA
title: Certificate Practicum
description: Students in the nonprofit management track of the certificate will learn by doing and observing in a nonprofit organization selected in consultation with the student’s advisor.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PUBA graduate certificate students only.

subject: PUBA
title: Capstone Seminar
description: Culminates public administration core courses by incorporating theoretical, analytical, and practicum observations into examination of public issues of importance to Hawaiʻi and the region.
prereq_raw: ( PUBA 601 , PUBA 602 , PUBA 607 ) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: QHS
title: Mathematic Preparation for Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Mathematics preparation for quantitative health sciences. Includes selective topics in linear algebra, advanced calculus and probability theory.

subject: QHS
title: Directed Reading/Research
description: Directed reading/research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through quantitative methodologies and/or the process of conducting a research study.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistics Concepts for Clinical Researchers
description: Provide biostatistical concepts to clinical researchers. Students will obtain the ability to demonstrate an understanding of key biostatistical concepts in clinical research; and interpret statistical findings most commonly reported in clinical and healthcare literature.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: QHS
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

subject: QHS
title: Generalized Linear Model
description: Statistical theory of Linear Model and Generalized Linear Model, algorithms use for estimation, inference concepts, and assessment of goodness-of-fit. Covers Proportional Hazard Model and Generalized Estimating Equations.
prereq_raw: QHS 601 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: QHS
title: Data Management and Visualization for Health Sciences
description: Data management and visualization is essential to all aspects of health sciences. Through hands-on experiences in R, will introduce data processing, manipulation, visualization and reproducibility, with an emphasis on clinical, medical, and health science problems.

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: QHS
title: Bioinformatics II
description: Focus on bioinformatics approaches for functional genomics related to DNA, RNA, and protein. It will provide of virus, bacteria, and human genome and bioinformatics approaches to human disease.
prereq_raw: QHS 610 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: QHS
title: Machine Learning for Biomedical Data Science
description: Introduction to machine learning techniques with a focus on hands-on training. Topics include supervised, unsupervised, and ensemble methods, using R and/or Python to explore data, train models, and evaluate performance in practical projects.

subject: QHS
title: Introduction to Clinical Trials
description: Introduction to clinical trials. Topics include history, definitions/terminology, adverse events, FDA and government regulatory agencies, ethics; monitoring committees, recruitment, introduction to protocol development, basis designs.

subject: QHS
title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
description: Covers basic and advanced statistical methods utilized in clinical trials design, conduct, and data analysis. Topics cover statistician’s role in drug development and DSMB, statistical theory in phases I-IV clinical trial designs and analysis.
prereq_raw: QHS 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B or consent

subject: QHS
title: Introduction to Clinical Research
description: Provides an overview of concepts, methodology, and various practical aspects of clinical research.

subject: QHS
title: Translational Research Methods
description: Focus on translational research methods through selected genetic and acquired diseases including cancer, neurodevelopmental, inflammatory immune, and metabolic conditions with insight into analyses of DNA, RNA, genomics-proteomics, cell and animal models, and advanced imaging.

subject: QHS
title: Quantitative Health and Clinical Research Seminar
description: Provides overview of research related to health in Hawaiʻi and advances in quantitative health and clinical research. Topics include ethnic disparities in health, social and cultural factors, ethics, biostatistics and bioinformatics.

subject: QHS
title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective.

subject: QHS
title: Secondary Data Analysis
description: Will allow students who are new to using secondary data to become comfortable with accessing the data, forming hypotheses, and designing study proposals. Will introduce examples with basic and advanced techniques.
prereq_raw: QHS 601 (or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B- .

children.text: ( or equivalent) with a minimum grade of B-

subject: QHS
title: Medical Genetics
description: Focus on heritable disorders, genetic mechanisms, patterns of inheritance, phenotype-genotype correlations, genetic/environmental factors, clinical diagnoses, genomic and precision medicine.

subject: QHS
title: Special Topics in Quantitative Health Sciences
description: Special topics in quantitative health sciences. Reflects special research interest of QHS faculty or guest lecturers.

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting
description: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of the biostatistician as both consultant and collaborator with biomedical researchers, guide students in enhancing problem-solving and communication skills, and provide opportunity to observe real-life biostatistical consultations.
prereq_raw: QHS 601 and QHS 602 (or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) with minimum grades of B, and consent

subject: QHS
title: Biostatistical Consulting Practicum
description: Under the supervision of biostatistics faculty members, students will have the opportunity to provide statistical consultations to biomedical researchers and gain hands-on experience conducting biostatistical analysis in solving real-life analytic problems.
prereq_raw: QHS 675 (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of B.

subject: QHS
title: Critical Appraisal of Clinical Research Literature
description: Introduces key literature appraisal concepts and processes. Students will practice and sharpen their skills by engaging in the review and discussion of a set of clinical research publications representing major study designs.
prereq_raw: QHS 640 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: QHS
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through the process of conducting a research study.

subject: QHS
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.
repeatable_raw: seven times or up to 8 credits.

subject: RE
title: Principles of Real Estate
description: Principles affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources, including legal, physical, economic elements; valuation; market analysis; finance; investments, and public and private externalities affecting the allocation and utilization of real estate resources.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate and Environmental Law
description: Property rights, land tenure, agency, contracts and negotiation theory, title conveyancing and escrow, mortgage instruments, fair housing, state and federal environmental policy.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Appraisal/Analysis
description: Analysis of real property, including feasibility analysis, market analysis, income property capitalization, and general real estate valuation techniques.

subject: RE
title: Administration of Real Property Assets
description: How business firms and investors manage their real property assets in terms of the legal, financial, and physical dimensions of real property. Case studies in hotels, condominiums, and office buildings in the environment in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Business majors only.

subject: RE
title: Current Topics in Real Estate Analysis
description: Consideration of various special concepts and problems in real estate.

subject: RE
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Reading and research in a special area within the major field under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Finance and Investment
description: Financial and investment techniques used to evaluate real property and real estate security investments.

subject: RE
title: Real Estate Investment Analysis
description: Development of strategic business plans for the optimization of a firm’s real property assets. Includes facilities utilization audits, contingency planning, and the impact of new techniques.

subject: REL
title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

subject: REL
title: Introduction to the World’s Major Religions
description: Buddhism, Christianity, Confucianism, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism, Shinto, Taoism and indigenous traditions of Hawaiʻi and/or Oceania.

subject: REL
title: Religion and the Meaning of Existence
description: Basic ideas and issues in contemporary religious thought about the meaning of existence.

subject: REL
title: Religion and the Meaning of Existence
description: Basic ideas and issues in contemporary religious thought about the meaning of existence.

subject: REL
title: Introduction to World Mythology
description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Social Justice
description: Religious persons and organizations play significant roles in fighting for issues of social justice worldwide. Introduces students to the relationship between religions and social justice in China, South America, U.S., and Hawaiʻi.

subject: REL
title: Religion and the Environment
description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems.

subject: REL
title: Understanding the Old Testament (Hebrew Bible)
description: Examines the Old Testament (Hebrew Bible) as an expression of the religious life, history, and thought of ancient Israel and as a sacred text within later Judaism and Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Understanding the New Testament
description: Origin and development of early Christian message as set forth in the New Testament; special attention to Jesus and Paul.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Indian Religions
description: Historical survey of the teachings and practices of major religious traditions of India.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Chinese Religions
description: Taoist, Confucian, Buddhist and folk beliefs and practices in their social and historical context.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Japanese Religions
description: Broad survey, with primary focus on Shinto, Buddhist, and modern sectarian movements, analyzed in relation to social and cultural themes of major historical periods.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Hawaiian Religion
description: Major teachings and practices from ancient times to present, their cultural influence; analysis of religious texts; relation to other traditions of Oceania and to Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Buddhism
description: Survey of major forms and practices.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Judaism
description: Survey from origin to modern times with an emphasis on writing-based analysis of Jewish thought in Talmudic and Medieval Periods

subject: REL
title: Understanding Islam
description: Historical survey of the beliefs and practices of Islam as a world religion, including the prophet Muhammad, scriptures, philosophy and science, theology, law, major sectarian movements, relations with other religious traditions, and fundamentalism.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Christianity
description: History of ideas concentrating on events, persons, and issues with the greatest impact on the evolution of Christianity.

subject: REL
title: Understanding Ancient Religions
description: Comparative and historical survey of the religious beliefs and practices in ancient times throughout Egypt, Mesopotamia, Syria-Canaan, Anatolia, Persia, Greece, and Rome.

subject: REL
title: Viking Religion
description: Introduction to the Scandinavian religions in the Viking Age, their depiction in popular culture, and reconstruction in the form of new religious movements.

subject: REL
title: Priestesses and Prophetesses
description: Legendary priestesses and prophetesses from ancient to modern religions around the world including ancient Sumeria, Egypt, Greece, China, India, the Middle East, Japan, and Hawaiʻi. This course develops written communication skills.

subject: REL
title: Myth, Religion, and Society
description: Survey of major theories and methods for analyzing myth, ritual, and religious practice, drawing on anthropology, history, philosophy, political science, psychology, and sociology. Emphasis on developing core analytical skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Biblical Hebrew I
description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or consent.

subject: REL
title: Biblical Hebrew II
description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; essay-based analysis of literary forms, with attention given both to stories important to the development of the Abrahamic religions and writing-based interpretation of religious traditions.
prereq_raw: REL 301 / CLAS 301 with C- or better.

subject: REL
title: Creation and Evolution
description: An exploration of interactions between science and religion with a focus on cosmogonies.

subject: REL
title: Indigenous & Decolonial Approaches to Religion and Culture
description: Introduction to indigenous and decolonial approaches to the study of religion and culture. Includes a critical assessment of tools and terminology traditionally used in academia. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Animals
description: Critical study of the ethical treatment of nonhuman animals and the religious beliefs and practices associated with them throughout history and across various cultures. Emphasis on teaching oral communication.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Zen (Ch’an) Buddhist Masters
description: Study of lives, teachings, practices of Zen masters in China, Japan, Korea, and the West.

subject: REL
title: Global Christianity
description: Christianity as a transcultural religion, through the study of Christian art, literature, ritual, and theology in diverse cultures; including the Near East, Africa, Latin America, and the Pacific.
prereq_raw: REL 150 , REL 201 , or REL 210 ; or consent.

subject: REL
title: Ka Baibala ʻŌlelo Hawaiʻi (The Bible in Hawaiian)
description: Survey of and selected readings from the Hawaiian Bible (Baibala Hemolele). Conducted in Hawaiian.

subject: REL
title: Cults and New Religions
description: Study of cults and new religious movements in America, the Pacific, and East Asia; examining types, causes, and functions of these movements.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Conflict in American History
description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Religion, Politics, and Society
description: Exploration of the diverse approaches and perspectives that American religious groups embrace in addressing controversial and diverse issues of contemporary American life. Emphasis on considering and discussing ethical approaches and practicing oral communication.

subject: REL
title: Christian Ethics in Modern Life
description: The meaning of Christian faith for the moral life with reference to contemporary moral issues.

subject: REL
title: Sufism: Mystical Traditions of Islam
description: Introduction to the history, literature, and worldview of Sufism. Students will encounter the following topics in relation to Islamic mysticism: asceticism, monotheism, philosophy, love, union, sainthood, ecstatic experience, and spiritual uses of art.
prereq_raw: REL 209 or REL 383 or PHIL 330 or HIST 354 , or consent.

subject: REL
title: Witches and Witchcraft
description: Persecution of witches, witchcraft in Europe, 1300-1700, examined as crisis of church and theology; origins, effects on church and society.
prereq_raw: one of REL 201 , HIST 151 , HIST 152 , PSY 100 , or consent.

subject: REL
title: Islam in History
description: Examination of the historical connections between Islam and other civilizations will focus on the role of Islam in world history.

subject: REL
title: Women and Religion
description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through reading autobiographies, films, and primary texts, and through the development of research and writing skills.
prereq_raw: REL 149 or WGSS 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151 .

subject: REL
title: Heroes and Villians in Religious Literature
description: Explores the depictions of heroes and villains in the religious literature of the world. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: REL
title: Love, Sex, and Religion
description: Love and sex as themes in religions of Asia and the West.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Art
description: The uses of art in religion are studied with historical examples.

subject: REL
title: Prophecies of the Last Days
description: In-depth look at ancient Judeo-Christian apocalyptic texts and the communities in which they originated, followed by a survey of the medieval and modern day heirs of apocalyptic traditions.

subject: REL
title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Written communication emphasis.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: REL
title: Classical Hindu Mythology
description: Study of myths and narratives of classical Hinduism through the Sanskrit epics Rāmāyana and Mahābhārata; exploring major concepts such as dharma, karma, and yoga. Intensive, interpretive writing, and peer-review exercises, will hone students’ writing skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or consent.

subject: REL
title: Mysticism East and West
description: Mystic traditions of the West from desert monasticism to Renaissance mystics compared with those of South and East Asia. Focuses on the ethical lives of these mystics, and developing oral communication skills. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Hawaiian Gods
description: The traditions and practices related to one or more major indigenous gods, or class of gods, will be studied by the interpretation and analysis of primary texts. Develops written communication skills.

subject: REL
title: On Death and Dying
description: Aspects of death and dying; relation to our culture and society, to understanding of each other and of ourselves.

subject: REL
title: Life and Teachings of Jesus
description: Critical study of synoptic gospels and of extra-Biblical sources with an emphasis on teaching students to present their research in both written and oral formats.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

subject: REL
title: Health/Medicine in Religion
description: Issues of health and disease in the light of religious beliefs and practices with a focus on ethical matters shaping policies in the U.S. and the world.

subject: REL
title: Religion and Food
description: Writing-based seminar exploring foodways as a basic component in the practice of religions. Examines theoretical issues, foodways as creators of community and identity, sustainability, and other ethical issues, abstinence and fasting, and healing.

subject: REL
title: Anthropology of Buddhism
description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

subject: REL
title: Spiritual Ecology
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Sacred Places
description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Seminar on research in sociological aspects of religious sectarianism, historical and current; special reference to Hawaiʻi.

subject: REL
title: Seminar on Buddhism
description: Selected historical, thematic, and textual research topics in Buddhism; topics and geographical focus to be announced each semester.

subject: REL
title: Daoism: Philosophy and Religion
description: Seminar on religious Taoism, its historical development and its role in the present-day context. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

subject: REL
title: Field Methods in Religion
description: Introduction to theoretical and methodological approaches to doing fieldwork in the study of religion. Application of these in studying Hawaiʻi’s diverse religious environment.

subject: REL
title: Buddhism in Japan
description: Major features and trends in thought, institutions, and practices in the context of Japanese history and culture, 6th-20th century.

subject: REL
title: Polynesian Religions
description: Introduction to field, comparison of several traditions; beliefs and practices from analysis of texts. Historical interactions with Christianity. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: REL
title: Seminar in Religion
description: Topics preannounced each semester.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: upper division standing or consent.

description: Forms of juvenile deviance; conditions and processes that result in alienation and deviance of youth. Juvenile corrections as institutionalized societal responses.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to the Sociology of Punishment
description: Multiple social theories about different forms of formal and informal punishments and social control across different societies and times.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Sociology of the Family
description: Family patterns, mate selection, parent-child interaction, socialization of roles, legal sanctions, trends in organization, functions.

subject: SOC
title: East Asian Popular Cultures
description: East Asian popular culture, with a focus on Korea and Japan, as well as the Chinese language sphere. Analyzes social forces shaping pop culture industries, artists, and productions in the region from a global perspective.

subject: SOC
title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
description: (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics.

subject: SOC
title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
description: (3 Lec, 2 50-min Lab) Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics. Restricted to students in the honors program and required for students taking the honors track in sociology.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Urban Sociology
description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawaiʻi.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Health
description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or WGSS 202 , or POLS 110 ; or consent.

children.text: -level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or WGSS 202 , or POLS 110 ; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Inequality and Stratification
description: Introduction to social stratification theory and research; definition and measurement of socioeconomic status; racial, ethnic and gender inequality; differences in lifestyles and life chances; social mobility.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Work
description: Work from viewpoint of individuals; meaningfulness versus productivity; how work, economics, and the industrial system affect individual goals.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Change
description: Causes, processes, and effects of social change and movements, using a variety of cases in and outside the US. Develops written communication skills.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Social Policy
description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.
