subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociological Theory
description: Major theorists and their influences, from Comte to today.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Law
description: Law as a political enforcement of the social order; how it is organized and operates; determinants of effectiveness; ways it adapts to and facilitates changing social conditions.

subject: SOC
title: Criminology
description: Concepts used in crime, law enforcement, criminal justice, and corrections. Types of criminal behavior; costs and effects of control.

subject: SOC
title: Drugs and Society
description: Use of mood- and mind-altering drugs in America among adults, youth, and cross-culturally. Illicit drug culture, psychedelics, and perception; social norms and deviant behavior.

subject: SOC
title: Deviance and Social Control
description: Interrelations of deviance, criminology, juvenile delinquency, corrections, social control, sociology of law. Key concepts, theories.

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice Organizations
description: Examines major criminal justice organizations-police, courts, and prisons. Using organizational theory, identifies the role of organizational goals, structure, resources, legitimacy, culture, and front-line workers in shaping criminal justice policy and practice.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Social Psychology
description: Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Happiness in Unsettled Times
description: Combines theoretical, scientific and ‘hands-on’ learning to explore how happiness and well-being can be cultivated, even in this challenging era of extreme global climate events.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Education
description: Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on the American system; including business, military, and religious institutions’ role in educating people. Significant time will be spent practicing and developing writing skills.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.

subject: SOC
title: Survey of Medical Sociology
description: Social factors in disease and treatment; illness behavior, roles of patients and healers; nature of healing professions; use of medical services; alternative systems of medical organization.

subject: SOC
title: Chinese Society and Culture
description: Social institutions, family, community, education, stratification, government, economy; impact of modernization and revolution on their contemporary transformation.

subject: SOC
title: Japanese Society and Culture
description: Persistence and change in economy, policy, religion, education, family, and other institutions of modern Japan.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Korea
description: Social institutions, family, education, religion, cultural values, social classes, economic development, social movements, gender relations, North-South relations, and unification issues.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Gender
description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

children.text: -level SOC course, WGSS 151 or any 200 - or 300 -level WGSS course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or consent.

children.text: -level SOC course, or WGSS 151 or any 200 - or 300 -level WGSS course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Law, Politics and Society
description: Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does.
prereq_raw: SOC 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

children.text: level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics
description: Explores how food, body, and other “matter of life” are imbedded in biopolitics from the feminist perspectives.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS or ES course, or consent

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Urban Sociology
description: Urbanization in developed and developing countries, the rural-urban continuum, structure and process of metropolitan regions, theories of urban location and growth, housing and urban renewal.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Social Stratification
description: Approaches to research in social inequality: community studies; historical and cross-cultural analyses of poverty, working class, middle class, power structure, social mobility, etc.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Population and Society
description: Global and U.S. patterns of population growth; composition and distribution, elementary demographic techniques; development issues and population policy.

subject: SOC
title: Economy and Society
description: Study of the dominant trend of economic change and its impact on society; globalization of economic activities and transformation of industrial society to postindustrial one; corporate restructuring and downsizing and their impact on employment and income distribution; gender relations in workplaces; the impact of globalization on the newly industrializing countries.

subject: SOC
title: Technology and Society
description: Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption; impact on society; innovation.

subject: SOC
title: Gender and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or one 300-level WGSS or ES course; or consent.

children.text: -level WGSS or ES course; or consent

subject: SOC
title: Organizations and Society
description: Schools, hospitals, industries, prisons, and government agencies analyzed in terms of self-actualization, alienation, human relations, communication, leadership, organizational conflicts.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Criminology & Delinquency
description: Advanced topics related to crime, juvenile delinquency, and criminal justice explored sociologically.

subject: SOC
title: Punishment & Society
description: Institutions, organizations, and individuals charged with carrying out punishment in the criminal justice system and beyond.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Law and Social Change
description: Interrelationships between legal orders and other social institutions; use of “law” to change major status relationships, e.g., boss-worker, woman-man, child-adult.

subject: SOC
title: Women and Crime
description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Prisons
description: Prisons, jails, and other detention facilities across historical, social, and/or international contexts.

subject: SOC
title: Social Structure and the Individual
description: Effects of social institutions on individuals. Role of socioeconomic status, cultural background, family structure, peer group, schools, and occupational roles in socialization.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Gender Violence
description: Historical and structural theories of gender-based violence, including domestic and sexual abuse, prostitution, trafficking, cross-cultural perspectives, social policy and practices. Junior standing or graduate standing only.

subject: SOC
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 , WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Marriage and the Family
description: Theory and methods of studying social interaction in marriage and the family; examination of marriage, mating, love, and choice. Empirical research emphasizing Hawaiʻi.

subject: SOC
title: Marriage and Family: A Feminist Perspective
description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 , or WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course; or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sociology of Aging
description: Social and research issues significant to delivery of long-term care services to the elderly; cost, quality, availability of services, evaluation of programs, role of family, formal and informal care services.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Medical Sociology
description: Application of sociological theories and concepts to medical social situations and behavior; problems of obtaining data for research.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Religion
description: Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawaiʻi.

subject: SOC
title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawaiʻi
description: Historical and contemporary social processes involved in race, racism, and inter-ethnic relations in Hawaiʻi. Focus on intersection of Asian and/or Pacific Island cultures with Native Hawaiian culture.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of the Arts
description: Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Sports and Society
description: Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society.

subject: SOC
title: Popular Culture
description: Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines, etc.; relation to sociological theories and studies.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Survey Research
description: Survey research design and analysis, including theory selection instrument construction, sampling techniques, data collection, computerized data analysis, and writing up research reports of the findings.

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics
description: Common statistical procedures emphasizing univariate and bivariate description; some attention to multivariate techniques and statistical inference, within context of research procedures.

subject: SOC
title: Social Statistics Laboratory
description: Required lab for computer applications for analysis of sociological data.

subject: SOC
title: Analysis in Field Research Methods
description: Techniques for collecting and analyzing qualitative data. Participant observation; small groups in natural settings; community studies. Grounded theory; theories of everyday life; reality construction.

subject: SOC
title: Discussion Group Leader-Freshman Seminar
description: A unique opportunity for students to gain leadership, teaching, and public speaking skills as a SOC 100 leader for a section of 10 freshmen students while being mentored weekly by a faculty course coordinator.

subject: SOC
title: Politics of Multiculturalism
description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent.

subject: SOC
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester;
repeatable_raw: 2 times, up to 12 credits. Consent of instructor.

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology
description: Topics course that explore current issues and try new ideas.

subject: SOC
title: Topics in Sociology: Student Projects
description: Students create their own study group and solicit an advisor from faculty. Consult department for assistance.

subject: SOC
title: Professional Development Seminar
description: Introduces sociology as a professional field. Provides skills for successful graduate degree completion, building a research agenda, preparing work for publication, and navigating the employment market for sociologists.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Sociology majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Statistics for Regression Analysis
description: Dealing with the multiple linear regression and logistic regression models, focusing on modeling, i.e., specification of the explanatory variables to answer different research questions. Emphasis on applications using statistical package programs. SOC 605L is required.

subject: SOC
title: Regression Analysis Laboratory
description: Lab for computer analysis skills is required for students taking SOC 605 .

subject: SOC
title: Research Methods and Design
description: Emphasis on theory selection, theory construction, and choice of research strategies.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Methods of Content Analysis
description: Content analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze text systematically. Covers sampling and case selection; manual and computer-assisted methods of coding and analyzing textual data; writing reports using content analysis data.

subject: SOC
title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar Qualitative Research
description: Advanced seminar on conducting fieldwork in natural social settings with emphasis on qualitative techniques, political and ethical considerations, data management and assessment, interpretation and reflexive writing.

subject: SOC
title: Classical Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociological theory from 19th-century to the 1960s, including intellectual contexts and historical development.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociology theory from the 1960s to the present, including intellectual contexts and historical development.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Organizational Analysis
description: Theoretical approaches to organizations; organizational structure and process; organizational pathologies and effectiveness; the organization and its environment.

subject: SOC
title: Medical Sociology
description: Covers the major paradigms in medical sociology for analyzing social epidemiology, the political economy of health systems, health service organizations, health and wellness behaviors, illness perception and help-seeking, doctor-patient interaction, and adaptations to illness.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Stress and Health
description: Analysis of current theory and empirical research on relationship of stress and health; sociological, psychological, and community psychiatry models and current issues.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Mental Health and Illness
description: Examines sociological research and theories about mental health and illness. A key question in medical sociology will be addressed: What is the relationship between society and mental health?

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Stratification
description: Classical theories of social class, contemporary developments; crucial research issues, appropriate methodologies.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Classified graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Criminology
description: Major current theories, history of their development, elaborations of typologies, implications for treatment modalities.

subject: SOC
title: Criminal Justice System
description: Examination of the criminal justice system; the exercise of discretion and limits placed upon it.

subject: SOC
title: American Punishment
description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison-industrial complex.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Introduction to Human Population
description: Comparative analysis of quantitative and qualitative aspects of population; factors affecting size, distribution, and composition; impact of population size and composition on society.

subject: SOC
title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

subject: SOC
title: Teaching Seminar
description: Examines research on teaching, learning, and ethics, as well as practical skills for teaching at the university level. Syllabi and teaching philosophies are developed, which are useful for the academic job market.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: SOC
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Evaluation Research
description: Research design, data collection, field problems and analysis in the evaluation of social programs. Examples from criminal justice, corrections, drug treatment, mental health, and public health.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Statistics
description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research.

subject: SOC
title: Cultural Analysis
description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
description: Substantive areas that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other courses.

subject: SOC
title: Advanced Medical Sociology
description: Application of theoretical paradigms and methodologies to the examination of selected research topics in the field of medical sociology.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Aging, Culture, and Health
description: Overview of the major theories, perspectives, and empirical findings relating to aging in various cultural contexts.
prereq_raw: SOC 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SOC, PSY, NURS, SW, PH majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Family and Gender
description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures.

subject: SOC
title: Comparative Study of East Asia
description: Comparative analysis of social organization, social processes, and change of both capitalist and communist countries of East Asia, with each other and other areas of the world.

subject: SOC
title: Social Change—Pacific Islands
description: Analysis of social change; transformation from subsistence societies to commodified, wage-labor societies with participation in world economy.

subject: SOC
title: Modern Japanese Society
description: Social and behavioral studies of Japanese values, social organization, and personality development. Problems of value conflict, political protest, world role, tradition, and social change.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Modern Chinese Society
description: Developmental policies, social change, and impact on modern Chinese social institutions. Includes China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. May include social and demographic change, population, social stratification, gender, and family problems.

subject: SOC
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Race and Ethnicity
description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Up to 2 times in different alphas.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Race and Ethnicity: anti-racism studies
description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.

repeatable_raw: Up to 2 times in different alphas.

subject: SOC

description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Up to 2 times in different alphas.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Race and Ethnicity: race, place, and inequity
description: An examination of how ideas of “race” and “ethnicity” are constructed, and how this reflects and shapes social structures and relationships: (B) anti-racism studies; (C) ethnic identity and nationalism: cooperation and conflict; (D) race, place, and inequality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.
repeatable_raw: Up to 2 times in different alphas.

subject: SOC
title: Conflict Analysis/Resolution
description: Seminar on the analysis of conflict resolution. Faculty from law, planning, political science and guest practitioners will present multidisciplinary analysis and intervention strategies on contemporary conflicts.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Structure and the Individual
description: Intensive study and individual research projects in a selected topic. Theoretical and methodological issues in relating social and individual levels of analysis. Recommended: SOC 612 .

subject: SOC
title: Seminar in Social Movements
description: Study of sociology of social movements, plus independent student research.

subject: SOC
title: Development in Asia
description: Theories and available research methods examined for applicability to developing areas; specific examples from Asia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SOC
title: Urban Sociology
description: Demographic trends in urban growth: nature and dimensions of urbanization and urbanism; ancient, American, and Third World cities; ecological theories of urban growth; lifestyles.

subject: SOC
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral dissertation.

subject: SOCS
title: First Year Experience
description: Brings together topics, discussion, and peer support to increase success at UH Mānoa and the College of Social Sciences. The emphasis is on knowledge, skills, and behaviors leading to graduation and sharing the first-year experience.

subject: SOCS
title: Leadership and Social Issues
description: Fosters understanding of key societal and community issues, social science perspectives on them, the qualities of effective leadership, and invites examination of personal responsibilities, intentions, and abilities to make a difference on those issues.

subject: SOCS
title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

subject: SOCS
title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

subject: SOCS
title: Statistical Analysis for Social Sciences
description: Statistical reasoning in the analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, inference measures of association, decomposition of variance, and regression analysis. Lab required.
prereq_raw: any 100 level social science course or consent.

children.text: level social science course or consent

subject: SOCS
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: SOCS
title: Introduction to Digital Media for the Social Sciences
description: Incorporates hands on instruction for creating informational media content, to include learning how to use camera and sound equipment, learning how to edit and create graphics, and learning presentation techniques.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SOCS
title: Intermediate Digital Media and Production
description: Focus on theoretical and practical methods for media design and production of high-quality creative digital content. Emphasis on social media strategies and oral communication skills to attract mass online audiences.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: SOCS
title: Social Sciences Service Learning and Micro Internship
description: For students undertaking service-learning or micro-internship options separately or for another class. Discussions and research related to learning experiences and issues encountered while in the field.

subject: SOCS
title: Pilina: Topics in Indigenous Social Sciences
description: Explores pilina (relationship, connection) of selected topics and issues of interest in the social sciences through Indigenous voices, perspectives, and scholarship.

subject: SOCS
title: Advanced Digital Media for Social, Cultural, and Community Engagement
description: Advanced digital media techniques for creating high-quality video content that promotes social, cultural, and community engagement. Focus on writing and oral skills with emphasis on visual storytelling and distribution on broadcast and social media platforms.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: SOCS
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester;
repeatable_raw: 2 times, up to 12 credits. Consent of instructor.

subject: SOCS
title: Topics in Teaching Innovations
description: Examination and critical analysis of contemporary curriculum and instruction issues in social sciences. Concepts, theories, principles underlying active learning, critical thinking, values inquiry, assessment, and multidisciplinary approaches to integration of knowledge.

subject: SOCS
title: Ocean Policy and Management
description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

subject: SPAN

subject: SPAN

description: Conversation, grammar, reading.

subject: SPAN

description: Course content of SPAN 101 and SPAN 102 covered in one semester. Three two-hour sessions per week.

subject: SPAN

subject: SPAN
title: Intermediate Spanish II
description: Continuation of SPAN 201 . Oral practice and grammar study; increasing emphasis on reading and written composition. Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 202 and SPAN 259 .

subject: SPAN
title: Intensive Spanish for Business
description: SPAN 201 and SPAN 202 content combined, oriented to business Spanish. Three 50-minute sessions per week plus online work.

subject: SPAN
title: Intermediate Spanish Abroad I
description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the second-year level in Spanish language and culture in a Spanish-speaking country. Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 201 and SPAN 258.

subject: SPAN
title: Intermediate Spanish Abroad II
description: Continuation of SPAN 258 . Students cannot receive credit for both SPAN 202 and SPAN 259.

subject: SPAN
title: Legends, Stories, and Current Events
description: Development of language skills through reading of literary and cultural texts.
prereq_raw: SPAN 202 (or concurrent) or SPAN 203 or SPAN 259 .

subject: SPAN
title: Language and Writing I
description: Improvement of Spanish vocabulary, language accuracy, and expression of ideas in Spanish through writing.
prereq_raw: SPAN 202 or SPAN 203 or SPAN 259 , or consent.

subject: SPAN
title: Conversation I
description: Intensive practice in spoken Spanish, focusing on the preparation and completion of oral tasks and presentations. Not open to (near)-native speakers.

subject: SPAN
title: Conversation II
description: Continuation of SPAN 303 .

subject: SPAN
title: Introduction to Spanish-English Translation
description: Practical introduction to written Spanish-English translation through the translations of texts from Spanish to English and the reverse. Includes an emphasis on composition and style.

subject: SPAN
title: (Alpha) Spanish in Use
description: Spanish language as used in specific professions; (B) marketing, tourism & business; (C) health & public safety. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SPAN
title: Spanish in Use: marketing

subject: SPED
title: Individuals with Extensive Support Needs
description: Etiology, characteristics, and development of individuals with extensive support needs; historical, theoretical, and legal issues affecting individuals with extensive support needs; multicultural, family, and consumer issues; professional and ethical issues in providing services.

subject: SPED

description: Characteristics and educational provisions for gifted children and youth with particular attention to psychological aspects of creativity.

subject: SPED
title: Education Program for the Gifted/Talented
description: Utilization and evaluation of teaching/learning models for gifted/talented students, including consideration of roles, expectancies for learning, and organizational procedures.

subject: SPED
title: Developing Oral Language and Phonetic Awareness in Students with Disabilities
description: Focuses on the sound-symbol correspondences of language and the relationship of phonemic awareness and the phonological system of language to the reading process in students with disabilities and other diverse learners.

subject: SPED
title: Strategies for Reading Difficulties
description: Overview of methods, programs, and strategies for reading instruction designed to improve the performance of students, grades K-12, who experience difficulties in reading acquisition, fluency, and comprehension.

subject: SPED
title: Literacy (Writing) for Students - Mild/Moderate Support Needs
description: Research-based practices, programs, and strategies for writing instruction for students with mild/moderate support needs. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with disabilities while enhancing students’ writing abilities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: BEd in SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Vocabulary Comprehension, Fluency & Writing Interventions for Students with Disabilities
description: Development of and intervention for fluent reading vocabulary acquisition, comprehension and writing in students with disabilities. Explicit and systematic instruction of core aspects of reading and writing.

subject: SPED
title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
description: Knowledge and skills for relating effectively with families and professionals on behalf of the children and youth with and without disabilities. Coverage of the context in which family members and school personnel interact.

subject: SPED

description: (3 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Elementary
description: Teaching elementary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction. Collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar in Special Education
description: Study of issues, trends, and research into special education programming and service delivery.

subject: SPED
title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers including criteria for evaluation and planning.
prereq_raw: HDFS 230 (or concurrent) and HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Preschool Children–Special Needs
description: Examination of application of current research and practices for serving preschool children with special needs.

subject: SPED
title: Physical and Medical Needs: Students with Extensive Support Needs
description: Learning to teach students with physical and medical needs, with a focus on developing independence. Instructional and assistive strategies in collaboration with related service providers.

subject: SPED
title: Non-School-Age Individuals with Extensive Support Needs
description: Effective planning, instruction, and support for non-school-age individuals (infants, toddlers, and adults) with extensive support needs across natural environments.

subject: SPED
title: Secondary Transition for Students with Disabilities
description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for postsecondary education, employment, and community living.

subject: SPED
title: Introduction to Assessment and Instruction-Extensive Support Needs
description: Assessment methods and tools, instructional and assistive strategies, and special procedures to support the participation of students with extensive support needs in inclusive settings.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Mild/Moderate Support Needs
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate support needs. Stress on program development to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities into general education environment.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment, Planning, and Instruction for Students with Extensive Support Needs
description: Techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with extensive support needs. Focus on program development to facilitate the inclusion of students with disabilities into general education settings

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Practices Across the Curriculum-Mild/Moderate Support Needs
description: Strategies for teaching science, math, and social studies to students with mild/moderate support needs in secondary settings; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, and curriculum development.

subject: SPED
title: Assistant-Level Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis at the assistant level supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

subject: SPED

description: Addresses instructional/assistive technologies and strategies that support inclusion for special/general education; application of Universal Design for Learning to support diverse student access to the PreK-12 general curriculum.

subject: SPED
title: Classroom Organization and Management
description: Knowledge and skills related to basic organizational management of an inclusive classroom, including scheduling, grouping, and stress and time management; techniques of applied behavior management, emphasizing behavior change and practical implementation of learning principles.

subject: SPED
title: Theoretical Basis for Teaching Special-Needs Students
description: Survey of biophysical, behavioral, social/ecological, psychodynamic/psychoeducational, cognitive/developmental, counter-theoretical approaches to teaching exceptional students. Opportunity for the development and/or strengthening of one’s own theoretical frame of reference.

subject: SPED
title: Characteristics/Strategies for Teaching At-Risk Students
description: Survey of educational, behavioral, and emotional characteristics of students who are at-risk for school failure and strategies to work with such students.

subject: SPED
title: Intensive Behavioral Interventions
description: Principles of behavior, emphasizing positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems and improving behavior and learning for students with extensive support needs.

subject: SPED

prereq_raw: one of SPED 480, LTEC 414 , or LTEC 442 .

Focus on understanding special education law necessary in providing services to students with disabilities in a variety of placements. Appropriate for special/general education teachers, administrators, or related service providers.

subject: SPED

subject: SPED

description: Collaboration skills necessary to function as team members and to ensure the success of students with disabilities in inclusive school and community settings.

subject: SPED

prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent.

subject: SPED

prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent.

subject: SPED

Taught in ASL and English.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment and Data-Based Decision Making
description: Assessment methods focused on curriculum-based measurement and diagnostic assessment. Connecting formal and informal assessment to instructional decision making. Formulating and implementing plans to meet the learning needs of students who require mild to moderate support.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Assessment and Instruction—Severe Disabilities and Autism
description: Basic principles of assessment, instruction, and curriculum development; application of formal and informal assessment procedures for goal selection, formulating instructional plans, and adapting instructional materials to accommodate learning needs of students with severe disabilities and autism.

subject: SPED
title: Family-Centered Approaches in Deaf Education
description: Prepare teachers to deliver family-centered home-based services to families of deaf children using the SKI-HI model. Course will be taught in ASL and English.
prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Collaboration–Working with Deaf Students in Inclusive Settings
description: Collaboration skills for working with general education teachers, specialists, paraprofessionals, families and community members to support the success of deaf students in inclusive settings. Taught in ASL and English.
prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Transition Strategies for Deaf Students
description: Collaborative model for facilitating the transition of deaf and hard-of-hearing students to develop appropriate transition plans and effective plans of study. Taught in ASL and English.
prereq_raw: SPED 606 , SPED 607 and SPED 608 ; or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Adaptations and Special Procedures- Students/Severe Disabilities/Autism
description: Adaptations and special intervention procedures to support the participation of individuals with severe motor, communication, and/or adaptive behavior disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. Includes lab work.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SPED majors only.

subject: SPED
title: Strategies Across Content Area
description: Strategies for teaching math, science, and social sciences to students of all ages with mild/moderate disabilities; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, curriculum development.

subject: SPED
title: Language Arts Strategies: Students with Mild/Moderate Support Needs
description: Basic concepts related to language, language development, and recognition of language-related learning difficulties of students with mild/moderate support needs; strategies for teaching language arts curricula (listening, speaking, reading, writing) to students of all ages.

subject: SPED
title: Children’s Literature for Deaf Students
description: Introduction to English literature translated into American Sign Language (ASL) including discussion of ASL literature genres, the importance of translation, selection of literature; story reading, book reading, and retelling. Taught in ASL.

subject: SPED
title: Teaching Skills for Social Competence
description: Issues in social development, self-determination, and social skills competence training for children and youth with disabilities; experience in group social skills training and development of individualized programs.
prereq_raw: either SPED 485 or SPED 630 , and either SPED 611 or SPED 614 ; or consent.

subject: SPED
title: Field Experiences in Special Education
description: Students spend a minimum of nine hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Practicum
description: Supervised education/community experiences; minimum of 20 hours weekly with special-needs population (MR, LD, SED, SMH); pre-school through postsecondary settings (public/private). Related seminar or equivalent and completion of SPED core required.

subject: SPED
title: Internship
description: Supervised education/community experiences with special needs populations, preschool through postsecondary settings.

subject: SPED
title: Clinical Practice Special Projects
description: Development and implementation of a field-based research professional development project under the direction of the student’s advisor; limited to students enrolled in the interdisciplinary program.

subject: SPED
title: Positive Behavior Support
description: Principles and laws governing human behavior and positive methods for addressing significant challenging behaviors for diverse students. Emphasis on functions of behavior, experimental techniques for documenting behavior change, and use of technology for improving behavior.

subject: SPED
title: Early Intervention for Special Populations
description: Issues important to early childhood special education. Early screening and assessment, working with families, curriculum options/models, program evaluation.

subject: SPED
title: Language/Communication Assessment and Intervention
description: Current research in typical language learning, assessment, planning, implementation, and evaluation of verbal behavior for individuals with social and communication needs, including complex communication needs. Procedures for developing functional communication objectives in ongoing routines/activities.

subject: SPED
title: Motor Development/Intervention for Students with Severe Disabilities
description: Normal/abnormal motor development; description/etiology of physically disabling conditions influencing motor development; analysis/application of assessment/ intervention strategies to promote motor development; positioning and handling skills.

subject: SPED
title: Inclusive Physical Activity
description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

subject: SPED
title: Procedures for Early Childhood Special Education
description: Assessment and intervention strategies to promote behavior change with young children with disabilities. Promoting child skill gains and integrated programming options.

subject: SPED
title: Topics and Issues in Reading Difficulties
description: Introduction of foundational knowledge of language and literacy development. Current topics and issues related to literacy development in students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Introduction of basic linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for beginning or struggling readers. Covers evidence-based practices for teaching literacy to students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Advanced Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
description: Advanced linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for older students. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with Dyslexia or related reading difficulties.

subject: SPED
title: Seminar on Mild/Moderate Disabilities

subject: SPED

restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SPED

subject: SPED

prereq_raw: successful completion of all required courses or consent.
coreq_raw: STE 405 (B, C, D, F, G, H, I, J, KI, L, M, or P)

subject: STE
title: Supervision of the Observation- Participation Student
description: Basic guidelines for developing effective team relationships between the professional teacher and the observation-participation student.
prereq_raw: two years’ teaching experience and consent.

subject: STE
title: Observation and Assessment in Early Childhood Education
description: Introduction to the purposes, theories, and methods of early childhood assessment. Emphasizes observation, documentation, and assessment to provide evidence of children’s development and learning and how to use assessment to guide teaching and learning.

subject: STE
title: Observation and Assessment in Early Childhood Education Lab
description: Field experience in early childhood settings to facilitate young children’s growth and learning.

subject: STE
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
description: Continuation of STE 415 : focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children.

subject: STE
title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
description: Continuation of STE 415L .

subject: STE
title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education
description: Planning child-centered, responsive programs for children. Focuses on play, learning environments, integrated thematic instructional design, guidance, assessment, and family engagement in early childhood and early elementary to promote enjoyment, growth, and development.

subject: STE
title: Supervision of Student Teaching
description: Principles and methods; role of supervisor; human resources supervision in student teaching. Open to teachers interested in pre-service teacher education.
prereq_raw: three years teaching experience and consent.

subject: STE
title: Family and Community Centered Partnerships
description: Knowledge and appreciation for the complex characteristics of children, families, and communities. Analysis and development of skills for creating respectful, reciprocal relationships with children and families from diverse backgrounds. Lecture/lab.
prereq_raw: STE 318 (or concurrent), or HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: STE
title: Advanced Supervision of Student Teaching
description: Advanced principles and methods: clinical supervision, observation recording, analysis, interpretation of classroom teaching; human resources supervision in student teaching.
prereq_raw: STE 420 , successful supervision of two or more student teachers, and consent.

subject: STE
title: Cooperative Vocational Education
description: Planned work-experience program for special areas of vocational technical education. Acceptable type of wage-earning employment. Minimum of six 40-hour weeks or 240 work hours required.

subject: STE
title: Foundations of Vocational Education
description: Historical and philosophical foundations of vocational technical education, overview of federal and state legislation and contemporary practices. Special emphasis on vocational education program in Hawaiʻi.

subject: STE
title: Office and Marketing Technology
description: Understanding and use of word processing, spreadsheet, and database software for business applications. Explore software across the office and marketing content areas.

subject: STE
title: Multicultural and Social Justice Education
description: Exploring social justice and multilingual, multicultural education with attention to Hawaiʻi as our place of learning and teaching.

subject: STE
title: Hawaiian Studies, Methods
description: Examination of issues in Hawaiian and U.S. views of education and their application to the teaching of Hawaiian studies. Field experience required.

subject: STE
title: Education of Exceptional Children in Regular Classroom
description: Practices that facilitate teaching special needs students in regular classrooms. Techniques for meeting academic needs, managing behavior, motivating students, increasing peer interactions, communication between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms, Secondary
description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/ talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

subject: STE
title: Issues in Computer Education
description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

subject: STE
title: Directed Activity
description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, teaching, and/or projects.

subject: STE
title: Common Core State Standards in ELA: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of ELA content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the ELA practices of the Common Core State Standards.

subject: STE
title: Common Core State Standards in Mathematics: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of mathematics content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the mathematical practices of the Common Core State Standards.

subject: STE
title: (Alpha) Practicum in Curriculum Development: Natural Science
description: For in-service teachers to upgrade subject matter and develop teaching methods and materials for instruction.
