subject: SUST
title: Dynamic Earth
description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment
description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards.

subject: SUST
title: The Natural Environment Lab
description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

subject: SUST
title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Biology & Society Laboratory
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawaiʻi. Not a BIOL major elective.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to the Environment, Climate Change, & Sustainability
description: Introduction to the environment, climate change, and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning exercises that address sustainable development and the three pillars of sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
prereq_raw: SUST 112 (or concurrent) or GES 102 (or concurrent) or OCN 102 (or concurrent).

subject: SUST
title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Cities
description: How do we plan cities to meet long-term social, economic, and environmental needs? Students will learn about sustainability as it relates to issues like energy, transportation, housing, land, water, and food. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability in a Changing World
description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawaiʻi/Oceania. Active learning environment.

subject: SUST
title: Humans and the Environment
description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

subject: SUST
title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world. Students who successfully completed CHEM 100 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in SUST 120/ CHEM 110 without instructor override. Students who successfully complete SUST 120/ CHEM 110 with a grade of C or better will not be allowed to enroll in 100 without instructor override.

subject: SUST
title: Politics & Poetics of Climate Change in Asia
description: Examines the causes and impacts of, and responses to, climate change in Asia through interdisciplinary approaches: natural sciences, politics, economics, as well as legal, cultural, and creative/artistic dimensions.

subject: SUST
title: Politics and Poetics of Climate Change in Oceania
description: Uses interdisciplinary approaches to examine the causes, impacts, and responses to climate change in Oceania, while drawing on examples and lessons from the broader Asia-Pacific with an emphasis on a writing intensive assessment.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Food and Energy Field Course
description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawaiʻi for sustainable development.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental History
description: Explores the influence of nature-climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms-on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

subject: SUST
title: Religion and the Environment
description: Examines the roles contemporary religious groups play in ground movements for sustainability. Introduces students to key scholars, religious leaders, and activists who are implementing sustainable solutions to pressing environmental problems.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change
description: Introduction to the science of climate change focusing on Earth’s past, present and future, specifically, the causes, consequences, and record of past changes; future projections, mitigation, and adaptation. Appropriate for both science and non-science majors.
prereq_raw: ERTH 101 or ERTH 103 or ERTH 104 or ERTH 106 or ERTH 111 or ERTH 130 or ATMO 101 or GES 102 , or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Historical Ecology of Hawaiʻi
description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Science
description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi as a model system.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupuaʻa
description: Examination of the ahupuaʻa system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the mālama ʻāina track designed to build critical writing skills.

subject: SUST
title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

subject: SUST
title: Organic Food Crop Production
description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiians
description: The social system, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians in a Pacific context. Transformation of the Hawaiian system by a capitalist economy. Native Hawaiian regeneration and quest for sovereign governance as an Oceanic society.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: SUST
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Environmental Humanities
description: Introduction to the environmental humanities, which rests at the intersection of the arts, humanities, and environmental studies.

subject: SUST
title: Topics in Sustainability
description: Emphasizes understanding of interconnectivity of human and natural systems, and critical thinking towards proposed solutions.
repeatable_raw: Repeatable on different topics up to six credit hours.

subject: SUST
title: Global and Local Perspectives on Severe Weather
description: Dynamics and structure of the main types of severe weather (tropical cyclones, supercell storms, tornadoes, flash floods, hailstorms, fog, etc.); future changes due to climate change; risk assessment; severe weather in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: ATMO, GES, GG, GEO, GES, NREM, or OCN students only.

subject: SUST
title: Introduction to Planning
description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawaiʻi planning—research problems from a multidisciplinary approach. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Issues
description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
prereq_raw: one of BIOL 101 , BIOL 123 , or GEO 101 ; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Conservation Ethics
description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resources Management
description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
prereq_raw: ( NREM 251 / TPSS 251 or NREM 210 / TPSS 210 ; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172 ) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
description: Introduction to natural resource and environmental public policy at U.S. federal, Hawaiʻi state, local, and international levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments, and contemporary ethical issues.
prereq_raw: NREM 210 / PEPS 210 / SUST 210 or NREM 251 / SOCS 251 / TPSS 251 or ( BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or ( ERTH 101 or higher); and NREM 220 / SUST 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses.

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology
description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-in-practice in Hawaiʻi and elsewhere.

subject: SUST
title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Issues
description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Water and Society
description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Ethics
description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
prereq_raw: SUST 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103 .

subject: SUST
title: Mālama ʻāina Resource Management Visual Technologies
description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

subject: SUST
title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Governance
description: Centers around the ethical dilemmas of environmental and climate challenges and examines available mechanisms for solving them. Develops written communication skills through a critical lens from a political ecology and environmental justice perspective.
prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environment and Agriculture
description: Overview of environmental issues related to agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts. Ethical issues on impact of agriculture on the environment will be discussed.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiʻi and the Pacific
description: Hawaiʻi as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

subject: SUST
title: Globalization and Environment
description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Global Environmental Politics
description: Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance.

subject: SUST
title: Communicating Sustainability
description: Application of project-based science communication, strategic communication, and digital media techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.
prereq_raw: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

subject: SUST
title: Geography, Environment, and Society
description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change, Resilience, and Sustainability in Oceania
description: Examines Pacific Island experiences and responses to climate change, contrasting Indigenous and local impacts with regional and global models, emphasizing resilience, sustainability, and community strategies confronting rising seas, biodiversity loss, pollution, and ecological disruption.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Culture and Environment
description: Critically examines changing views of nature, nature-culture relationships, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

subject: SUST
title: Economics of Global Climate Change
description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
prereq_raw: SUST 120 or SUST 130 or SUST 131, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future.

subject: SUST
title: Society and Environment
description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

subject: SUST
title: Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

subject: SUST
title: Inter-woven Structures
description: Studio investigation of threads under tension. Thematic lens of environmental vulnerability and resiliency. Exploration of art practice as embodied knowledge. Specific attention to weaving as meaning and place-making. Engages writing as a significant tool for analysis.

subject: SUST
title: Human Values and the Environment
description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts-literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics-in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawaiʻi
description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Development
description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawaiʻi. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.

subject: SUST
title: Economic Change and Hawaiʻi’s People
description: Hawaiʻi’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

subject: SUST
title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.
prereq_raw: SUST 220 / NREM 220 or ECON 130 or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

children.text: - or 300 -level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course, or consent

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Marketing
description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable

subject: SUST
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Law and Politics
description: Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawaiʻi and the U.S. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Politics of the Ocean
description: Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. Sophomore standing or higher.
prereq_raw: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Literature and the Environment
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of intersections between literature and the environment, including issues such as climate change, technology, pollution, land and land use, interspecies relationships.
prereq_raw: One ENG DL course or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Internship for Sustainability and Social Justice
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience in addressing sustainability issues.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: History of the Indian Ocean World
description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants.

subject: SUST
title: Climate, Air Quality, & Policy
description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legla aspects of pollution control.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

subject: SUST
title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

subject: SUST
title: The Ocean Economy
description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

subject: SUST
title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

subject: SUST
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
description: Examines resilience thinking as it relates to making cities resilient to environmental hazards in the context of climate change. Draws on relevant theories, policy, and case studies in urban planning. Emphasis on instruction in writing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Community and Natural Resource Management
description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
prereq_raw: two social science courses (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: two social science courses ( with a minimum grade of C-

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

subject: SUST
title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

subject: SUST
title: Agriculture, Food and Society
description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to non-majors.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Geochemistry
description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/ agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

subject: SUST
title: Environment, Resources and Society
description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

subject: SUST
title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

subject: SUST
title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making. Engages writing as a significant tool for art-making and analysis.

subject: SUST
title: Installation/Performance—Material in Context
description: Studio investigation of the transformation of space (ecological, social, political, psychological) through artist intervention. Experiments in non-object based interventions and into the evocative potential of materials. Engages writing and oral expression as significant analytical tools.

subject: SUST
title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation. Senior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro. Junior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Biocultural Ecology and Conservation
description: Examines some perspectives on Ecology within the context of Indigenous and Local Knowledge systems, and some approaches to conservation by Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities.
prereq_raw: BIOL 265 or BIOL 301 or BIOL 305 / BOT 305 or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results.

subject: SUST
title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level.

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

subject: SUST
title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: BIOL 172 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or consent

subject: SUST
title: Topics in Comparative Ethnic Conflict: Hawaiian Sovereignty in Pacific Context
description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution. Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context; focuses on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawaiʻi; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
prereq_raw: HWST 207 / SUST 217 or HWST 307 / SUST 317 or HWST 356 / SUST 356

subject: SUST
title: ʻāina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

subject: SUST
title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

subject: SUST
title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O’ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.
prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

subject: SUST
title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawaiʻi. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.
prereq_raw: SUST 217 / HWST 207 or SUST 317 / HWST 307 or SUST 356 / HWST 356 .

subject: SUST
title: Global Ethnic Conflict
description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent.

subject: SUST
title: GIS for Community & Environmental Planning
description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Forest Ecology
description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).
prereq_raw: ( SUST 311 / NREM 310 and NREM 380 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: SUST
title: American Environmental History
description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

subject: SUST
title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

subject: SUST
title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change with an emphasis on writing and ethical reasoning.

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Topics in Sustainability
description: Emphasizes understanding of interconnectivity of human and natural systems, and critical thinking towards proposed solutions.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Problem Solving
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Senior-level capstone for NREM and related majors. Ecosystem management within problem-solving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: NREM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability Capstone
description: Capstone for undergraduate students in interdisciplinary studies focusing on sustainability. The capstone experience provides an opportunity for students to gain knowledge and research experience in an applied setting.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: IS majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Senior standing or higher.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

subject: SUST
title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Seminar on Water in History
description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

subject: SUST
title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
prereq_raw: grade of C- or above in ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
prereq_raw: NREM 301 / SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainable Business Management
description: Overview of sustainable business management in the firm’s functional areas, including sustainable strategic planning, climate risk assessment, sustainable asset financing, supply chain management, fair trade, and green/ethical consumption behavior management.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Planning and Policy
description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Flood Mitigation
description: Design and solutions to coastal flood mitigation problems. Topics include climate adaptation; engineering solutions and best practices to mitigate coastal risk under different ocean hazard scenarios; and ecological approaches to mitigate coastal risk.
prereq_raw: consent; knowledge of AutoCAD and ORE 661 desirable.

subject: SUST
title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Modeling
description: Coastal modeling using the SMS Surface-Water Modeling software. Applications to solving coastal problems for different ocean hazard scenarios by applying models for tides, waves, coastal circulation, wave-current interaction, sediment transport, and/or morphology change.

subject: SUST
title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/ Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via video-conferencing.

subject: SUST
title: Coastal Geology
description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.

subject: SUST
title: Urban Environmental Problems
description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

subject: SUST
title: Planning in Hawaiʻi and Pacific Islands
description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawaiʻi, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent.

subject: SUST
title: Resource Economics
description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

subject: SUST
title: Environmental Resource Economics
description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

subject: SUST
title: Land Systems Science
description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socioecological system function.
prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461 .

subject: SUST
title: Seminar: place-based education
description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field. (P) place-based education.
prereq_raw: graduate and/or undergraduate courses in education and/or social sciences or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: COE-related majors only.

subject: SUST
title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: KāNāwai Lawaiʻa: Hawaiʻi’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance.

subject: SUST
title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

subject: SUST
title: He Aliʻi Ka ʻāina; Land, Resources, and Leadership
description: Seminar focused on leadership challenges in Mālama ʻāina to bridge ancestral and contemporary systems to better steward resources, produce abundance, work with and in community, and pivot large institutions for a better Aloha ʻāina future.

subject: SUST
title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

subject: SUST
title: Sociology of Sustainability
description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Marine Renewable Energy
description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
prereq_raw: ORE 607 ; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable.

subject: SUST
title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SUST
title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

subject: SUST
title: Political Ecology
description: Introduction to political ecology. Content will examine the historical development of and contemporary scholarship in political ecology from a human and environmental geography perspective.

subject: SUST
title: Topics in Biocultural Diversity and Conservation
description: Biological, cultural, and linguistic conservation are intimately linked, but rarely studied simultaneously. Adopts a trans-disciplinary view of diversity and conservation of nature, cultures, and languages, along with issues in anthropology, law, and ethics.

subject: SW
title: The Field of Social Work
description: Orientation to the profession of social work; historical development, values and philosophy, scope and aims.

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice I
description: Orientation to practice principles, concepts, values, knowledge base, and their application.
prereq_raw: SW 200 (complete with C or better) and majors only.

children.text: ( complete with C or better) and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice II
description: Introduction to practice skills with individuals, families, groups, and communities. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
prereq_raw: SW 302 (complete with C or better) and majors only.

children.text: ( complete with C or better) and majors only

subject: SW
title: History of Social Welfare
description: Historical developments and implications of social welfare activities, institutions, and policies and European backgrounds; introduce social welfare developments in selected non-European countries. Recommended: SW 200 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare as a Social Institution
description: Study of U.S. social welfare institutional structures, programs, and policies addressing human need; focus on Hawaiʻi’s legislative processes and social service programs; emphasis on oral communication inherent to advocacy, legislative, and policymaking processes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment
description: Examination of complex sociocultural factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others. Challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment. Recommended: SW 200 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior and the Social Environment II
description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.
prereq_raw: SW 360 with a grade of C or better. Recommended: SW 200 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: An examination of current trends in the field of social welfare.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education I
description: Introduction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: SW 302 , SW 325 , SW 326 (or concurrent), SW 360 , and SW 361 (or concurrent) complete with C or better; and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better; and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice III
description: Use of problem-solving processes and ethical models of decision-making in practice with individuals, families, groups, and communities.
prereq_raw: SW 303 , SW 326 , and SW 361 complete with C or better; and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better; and majors only

subject: SW
title: General Social Work Practice IV
description: Examination of practice methods and intervention models; identification and analysis of issues related to practice. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
prereq_raw: SW 402 (C or better) and majors only.

children.text: ( C or better) and majors only

subject: SW
title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
prereq_raw: PH 201 or SW 360 or WGSS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200 ; or consent.

subject: SW
title: Research Development in Social Welfare
description: Introduction to and application of language of research, theoretical concepts underlying advancement of knowledge, practical steps in research.
prereq_raw: completion of required junior-level SW courses (i.e., SW 302 , SW 303 , SW 325 , SW 326 , SW 360 , SW 361 , and SW 391 ) with C or better.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.
