subject: SW
title: Native Hawaiian Perspectives: A Cultural Context for Well-Being
description: To preserve the cultural knowledge of kupuna as it relates to health and wellbeing. Disseminate cultural knowledge of health and well-being to social work students and students in allied health professions.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW or Social Welfare students only.

subject: SW
title: Ke Aʻo Mau: Learning Preserved
description: To provide a holistic examination of issues and to explore culturally-anchored resolutions and practices to achieve social justice and health and well-being.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW, Social Welfare, or PH students only.

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Provides students with a body of knowledge, skills, and values that facilitate social work with Native Hawaiians.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW or Social Welfare students.

subject: SW
title: Social Services with Children
description: Study of current social services for children in the U.S. with focus on familiarization of child welfare programs and services in Hawaiʻi.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Concepts and Issues in Gerontology
description: Aging and its effect on the individual, family groups, associations, and communities. Impact of aging on social service delivery systems, public policy and role of social work.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: senior standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: An examination of current trends and issues in social work.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education II
description: Intermediate instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: SW 391 complete with C or better, and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better, and majors only

subject: SW
title: Undergraduate Field Education III
description: Advanced instruction to field education; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to the field experience.
prereq_raw: SW 490 complete with C or better, and majors only.

children.text: complete with C or better, and majors only

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Planned individualized study or research in special area related to social work practice interest. Up to 3 credit hours.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: majors only, senior standing, and consent of program chair and faculty advisor.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Individuals
description: Beginning practice course introduces students to the basic processes of social work and the roles and skills needed for generalist practice. Relevant theories of social work practice with individuals are explored for the efficacy with various problems and for their applicability to practice with various ethnocultures, social classes, and oppressed populations. Interviewing and interpersonal skill development are incorporated.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Families and Groups
description: Practice course builds upon the generalist framework and foundation content presented in 606. Special emphasis is given on models for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of practice with families and groups. Relevant theories of groups and the principles of group dynamics and group work methods are examined in regard to task, therapeutic, psychoeducational, and social development groups. Family content includes structural, behavioral, communication/experiential, and culturally-specific theories of intervention.

subject: SW
title: Social Welfare Policy and Services
description: Examines in a historical and comparative framework the economic, social, political, organizational, and administrative factors influencing the development, formulation, and implementation of social welfare policies in the U.S. Provides opportunity for the application of various models of social policy analysis in major areas of social welfare programming and service delivery.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Communities and Organizations
description: Community conceptualization; organized roles of developer, enabler, broker, mediator, and advocate; diagnostic and problem-solving technology; the special characteristics of the social worker as community organizer; matrix of structural objectives; sources and use of power; how to build an organization; and interorganizational negotiation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Organization and Administration in Social Work
description: Introduction to formal organization theory. Social service administration examined and implications for service delivery systems developed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Policies, Programs and Services on Aging
description: Explores policies, programs, and services for older adults. Students learn about the aging network, assess older adults’ needs, link older adults to appropriate services in the community, and track legislative bills that address older adults’ quality of life.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Death and Dying
description: Physical, social, cultural, psychological, and spiritual dimensions of dying, death, and bereavement.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Social and Cultural Aspects of Aging
description: Overview of aging from the biopsycho, socioeconomic and cultural perspectives. Explores common theories of aging. Emphasis on bridging the gap between the realm of concepts and theories, and the world of practice in gerontology.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Introduction to Scientific Methods and Principles in Social Work
description: Understanding and interpreting results of nomothetic and idiographic research; design principles and statistical analyses and their relationship to practices; use of published research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Research Designs and Data Analyses for the Evaluation of Practice Effectiveness
description: Extending the study of scientific methods introduced in SW 640 . Covers the range of empirical research methods and data analytic procedures suitable for knowledge building and practice evaluation at all levels of intervention from case to program.

subject: SW
title: Quantitative Methods I
description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences. Introduction to general linear model as principle of data analysis. Course requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

subject: SW
title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.

subject: SW
title: Multivariate Methods
description: Multivariate forms of multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of co-variance. Multiple discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis are discussed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment I
description: Examination of complex factors that privilege some and oppress/marginalize others; challenges commonly held tropes and complicates the discourse regarding individual, family, group, organizational and community development within the social environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment II
description: Focus on human development across the lifespan with attention given to unique challenges and opportunities faced in each phase. Emphasis is placed on “populations at risk” and the strengths and assets unique to diverse populations.

subject: SW
title: Treatment of Chemical Dependency
description: Introduction to treatment of alcoholism and other chemical dependencies. Application of social work strategies in work with individuals and families in the disease and recovery process.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Diagnosis and Assessment in Clinical Practice
description: Augments existing courses, enhances practicum, and satisfies students’ expressed need for firmer understanding and working knowledge of the DSM, the prevailing diagnostic system for psychological disorders in the United States.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SW
title: Child Welfare as a Field of Social Work
description: Emphasis on the developments in child welfare; issues, concerns with regard to needs and rights, and the application of social work services to problems associated with needs for protection. Review of historical, theoretical, empirical, and legal findings for skill development in intervening in dysfunctional parent/ child interaction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Community and Public Health Practice
description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Topics in Social Welfare
description: Current trends in field of social welfare. Recent courses have focused on forensic social work, immigrants and refugees, and leadership in human services. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Marriage and Family Therapy
description: Introduction to couple and family therapy offers an overview of family systems perspective, theory and technique relevant to informing effective social work case planning, case management, advocacy, and interaction with clients.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education I
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
prereq_raw: SW 606 (or concurrent)(with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C )

subject: SW
title: Generalist Field Education II
description: Field education is the signature pedagogy of social work education. Students will engage in supervised social work practice and have the opportunity to apply generalist knowledge, skills, values, and ethics to practice.
prereq_raw: SW 690 and SW 607 (or concurrent) and SW 631 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of C).

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of C )

subject: SW
title: Health and Aging
description: Biological and physiological changes associated with aging. Social and psychological factors associated with health maintenance. Major threats to health, changing patterns of morbidity and mortality of the aged.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Directed Reading and Research
description: Students, on the basis of special interest, select a faculty member to work with on a problem for which planned individualized study or research is deemed advisable.

subject: SW
title: Thesis Research
description: Independent research under supervision of a thesis committee. Includes formal proposal and defense of finished research.

subject: SW
title: Methods of Group Psychotherapy
description: Designed specifically to train students in the theory and practice of leading psychotherapy groups; it includes historical developments, research, theories, and application of group psychotherapy, group techniques and exercises.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Therapeutic Strategies with the Older Adult
description: Focuses on interdisciplinary strategies with older adults: individual, family, and group therapy; eclectic mental health approaches; case management; and environmental intervention. Emphasis placed on the use of these strategies as preventive, as well as supportive, measures for the well, transition, and frail elderly. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Advanced practice course for students specializing in social work with children and families. Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of both theoretical formulations and therapeutic techniques for practice in the field of family and child welfare. Emphasis placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of common child and family practice situations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice with Children and Families
description: Designed for students in the child and family concentration and builds upon past knowledge and skill development in practice classes and in the practicum. Students integrate, demonstrate, and extend earlier learning, acquire new knowledge, and learn and practice new skills. Organized around student case presentations in a consultation format. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Didactic and experiential learning activity focuses on the major role functions of the social worker in the health field including assessment, contracting, counseling, advocacy, case management, discharge planning, family group work, community and team building. Covers health care policy, research directions in practice and social work management issues.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Health Care
description: Through the use of case studies developed by the students, social work practice is examined in three areas of health care: primary care provided in health departments and medical groups, hospital-based services, and long-term care. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings. Focused on engagement and assessment while emphasizing cultural, person in environment, and strengths-based approaches.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice in Mental Health
description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings, with a focus on history and policy in the U.S. and Hawaiʻi, as well as culturally-grounded and evidence-based practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Work Practice with Older Adults
description: Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of theoretical formulations and intervention strategies for working with older adults and their families. Emphasis on diversity/justice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in Social Work with Older Adults
description: Designed for gerontology specialization students to gain advanced knowledge for working with diverse older adults and their families. Emphasis on strength perspectives on aging.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Policy Analysis
description: Students pursue in-depth a specific topic in the areas of social planning, social policy analysis, evaluation of social programs, administration, supervision, and consultation. Selectively a comparative perspective is introduced and case studies used to illustrate concepts, principles, and techniques, with implications for practice. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Social Work and the Law
description: Knowledge of judicial systems and law relevant to social work practice in corrections, child-family welfare, health, and mental health. Skills for effective participation in the legal process are acquired in moot court and in practice for testifying.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Review of Research in Social Work
description: In-depth study of research in a substantive area. Each seminar will be devoted to a particular topic: e.g., foster care of children, effectiveness of social work intervention, etc.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project—Plan B
description: Independent research (group of two to seven students or by an individual student) undertaken under the sponsorship of a faculty advisor. Elements are selection of a topic related to the practice of social work or knowledge relevant to that practice, utilization of empirical research methodology in collecting and analyzing original data, and preparation of a scholarly paper.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project–Plan B
description: Same as SW 743 .

subject: SW
title: Individual or Group Research Project–Plan B
description: Same as SW 743 .

subject: SW
title: Analysis and Development of Knowledge for Social Work
description: Focuses on developing an understanding of philosophy of science, theory development, social work epistemology, and the analysis and development of knowledge for social work practice.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.

subject: SW
title: Quantitative Methods II
description: Empirical research methodology with emphasis on design principles and measurement theory; design and measurement issues and problems in cross-cultural research.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent.

subject: SW
title: Qualitative Research: Philosophical, Methodological and Analytic Approaches
description: Theories and methods of qualitative research; problem formulation, informant selection, study design, data collection and analysis utilizing qualitative approaches.
prereq_raw: SW 640 or SW 651 or equivalent; departmental approval.

subject: SW
title: Dissertation Seminar
description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent.

subject: SW
title: Seminar in International Social Work
description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning for those Hawaiians experiencing problems in today’s society. Meets seminar requirement.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing.

subject: SW
title: Seminar on Women and Health
description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: graduate standing or consent.

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education I
description: Instruction in the field is continued. The field experience in the second year provides an opportunity for the student to test out concepts, principles, theories, and alternate approaches in actual practice settings.
prereq_raw: SW 717 (or concurrent) or SW 722 (or concurrent) or SW 724 (or concurrent) or SW 726 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B -).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B -)

subject: SW
title: Specialist Field Education II
description: Continuation of SW 790 .
prereq_raw: SW 790 and; SW 718 (or concurrent); or SW 723 (or concurrent); or SW 725 (or concurrent); or SW 727 (or concurrent) (all with a minimum grade of B-).

children.text: ( all with a minimum grade of B- )

subject: SW
title: Advanced Social Welfare Policy Analysis and Change
description: Builds on SW 630 and emphasizes a more thorough and comprehensive examination of major policies, programs, and populations central to a concentration (Health, Mental Health, Gerontology, Child and Family). Students learn a more focused and applied analysis of the relationship between social policy, research, and social work practice.
prereq_raw: SW 606 and SW 607 ; SW 630 and SW 631 ; SW 640 and SW 650 ; SW 659 and SW 660 ; SW 690 and SW 691 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SW majors only.

subject: TAHR
title: International Exchange Study/Research
description: Study overseas in an approved international or similar exchange program.

subject: TAHR
title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

subject: TAHR
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: TAHR
title: Extension Education & Outreach
description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program development and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: TAHT
title: First Year Tahitian I
description: Basic core skills of listening, speaking and grammar of spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

subject: TAHT
title: First Year Tahitian II
description: Continuation of TAHT 101 .

subject: TAHT
title: Second Year Tahitian I
description: Intermediate core skills of listening, speaking and knowledge of grammar for spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

subject: TAHT
title: Second Year Tahitian II
description: Continuation of TAHT 201 .

subject: TAHT
title: Third-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of TAHT 202 . Conversation, advanced reading, composition.

subject: TAHT
title: Third-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of TAHT 301 .

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of TAHT 302 . Advanced conversation, reading, and writing with focus on modern formal and colloquial Tahitian styles. The language in the realms of storytelling, radio, folklore, traditional and modern writing. Survey of modern and classical language.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
description: Continuation of TAHT 401 .

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
description: Fulltime formal instruction at the University of French Polynesia in Tahiti. Fourth-year level in Tahitian language and culture.

subject: TAHT
title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
description: Continuation of TAHT 458 .

subject: THAI
title: Elementary Thai I
description: First semester of elementary Thai. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Thailand.

subject: THAI
title: Elementary Thai II
description: Continuation of THAI 101 . Emphasizes reading, writing, listening, and speaking modern standard Thai. Structural points are introduced inductively. Regular on-line lab work and review of audiovisual materials.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Elementary Thai
description: Content of 101-102 covered in one semester. Emphasis on the development of communicative competence in both oral and written language and exposes students to the culture of Thailand.

subject: THAI
title: Intermediate Thai I
description: Continuation of THAI 102 . Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script.

subject: THAI
title: IntermediateThai II
description: Continuation of THAI 201 . Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script.

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Intermediate Thai
description: Content of 201-202 covered in one semester. Emphasis on the continued development of competence in both oral and written language for more advanced communication, travel, and further study.

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of THAI 202 . Advanced conversation and reading, emphasis on modern written texts. Regular on-line lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Third-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of THAI 301 .

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Third-Level Thai
description: Continuation of THAI 202 . Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading; emphasis on modern written texts. Lab work.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai I
description: Continuation of THAI 302 / THAI 303 . Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

subject: THAI
title: Fourth-Level Thai II
description: Continuation of THAI 401 .

subject: THAI
title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Thai
description: Continuation of THAI 303 . Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

subject: THAI
title: Thai Language in the Media
description: Development of reading and aural comprehension of authentic Thai language used in print and broadcast media through reading Thai newspapers, viewing and listening to Thai television and radio programs. Oral and written reports.

subject: THAI
title: Structure of Thai
description: Introduction to information structure of Thai as a basis for developing reading skills. Analysis of rhetorical, sentence, and word structure from different types of written texts.

subject: THAI
title: Structure of Thai
description: Continuation of THAI 451 .

subject: THAI
title: (Alpha) Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story
description: Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story: 1930-1969
description: Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Short Story: 1970-present
description: Selected readings in Thai short stories from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.

subject: THAI
title: (Alpha) Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel
description: Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.
prereq_raw: THAI 402 , THAI 461B or THAI 461C , or consent.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel: 1930-1969
description: Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.
prereq_raw: THAI 402 , THAI 461B , or THAI 461C , or consent.

subject: THAI
title: Readings in Thai Contemporary Prose Literature: the Novel: 1970-present
description: Selected readings in Thai novels from early 1930s to present. Oral and written reviews. (B) 1930-1969; (C) 1970-present.
prereq_raw: THAI 402 , THAI 461B or THAI 461C , or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Stage, Screen, and New Media Writing
description: Introduction to college level writing and information literacy for and about the stage (theatre, dance, performance), the screen (film, television), and new media (digital platforms, social media).

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to World Drama and Theatre
description: (2 Lec, 1 1-hr Lab) Performance traditions of Africa, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and the Pacific from the 5th century B.C. to the present. Analysis of political, religious, and technological conditions of theatre. Includes practical theatre workshop. Emphasis on writing instruction.

subject: THEA
title: Live on Stage
description: Students view locally-produced theatre and dance productions and write performance reviews. Readings, writing, and class discussion will guide students to understand each performance. Performances include theatre, dance, musical theatre, opera, and performance art.

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Hula
description: Designed for students with no hula experience. Introduces students to the basic foundational skills of hula and emphasizes the importance of language, basic body movements and vocal techniques.

subject: THEA
title: (Alpha) Beginning Practicum
description: Beginning workshop experience in the practical application of performing arts skills. (B) performance; (C) stagecraft; (D) costume; (E) performing arts management; (F) directing dramaturgy stage management choreography.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to the Art of the Film
description: Introduction to the aesthetics of silent and sound movies. Technical subjects analyzed only as they relate to theme and style.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Long-Form Improvisation
description: Introduction to long-form improvisation as developed by companies such as Second City and iO Chicago. Focus will be on games, situations, creating characters, and forming narratives from those elements.

subject: THEA
title: Development of the Sound Film
description: Growth and changes in aesthetics of the sound film from 1929 to present; films by Renoir, Welles, Eisenstein, etc.

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Voice and Movement
description: Introduction to vocal and movement techniques to increase self-awareness and potential for self-expression.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Acting for Stage and Screen
description: Beginning acting techniques for theatre and screen media including exercises, improvisations, monologues, and scenes. Focus on voice, relaxation, body awareness, and freedom from self-consciousness. Emphasis on writing instruction as appropriate to discipline.

subject: THEA
title: Acting I: Foundations and Techniques for Stage and Screen
description: Fundamentals of contemporary acting styles for stage and screen, including self-awareness, character, and scene work.
prereq_raw: THEA major or THEA 221 , or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA and THDN majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Pidgin/HCE Drama
description: Introduction to Hawaiian Creole English (HCE) multicultural comedy and drama in Hawaiʻi. Emphasis on acting exercises, local dialects, and the performance of Pidgin/HCE plays.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Stage Production
description: Survey class introducing theater management, lighting, costuming, scenery, and other aspects of theatre that relate to producing stage performances.

subject: THEA
title: Theatre Production Lab
description: Lab observations and projects illustrating basic principles of theatre production.

subject: THEA
title: Film/TV Production Process
description: Entry-level course details three phases of the production process for film and video projects: pre-production, production, and post-production.

subject: THEA
title: Principles of Design
description: Introduction to general design principles as applied to theatre. Will introduce the language and tools of visual literacy and visual communications via individual projects and collaboration.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Voice Function and Singing Styles
description: Students will study how the singing voice works in various styles, including classical, musical theater, jazz, choral, and pop/rock. Students will learn historical contexts, aural characteristics, and musical vocabulary through lecture, discussion, and listening.

subject: THEA
title: Intermediate Hula
description: Intermediate level hula course for students with some hula experience that builds upon existing cultural knowledge, performance and language skills. Students will prepare costumes and adornments for a public performance.

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre I: Script Analysis
description: Script analysis methods for world drama. Develops written and oral communication skills. Required of all majors.
prereq_raw: One of THEA 101 , THEA 221 , THEA 222 , THEA 240 ; or consent.

subject: THEA
title: World Theatre II: Myth to Drama
description: Myth and ritual into drama, 1000 BCE-1700 CE. Development of secular drama from sacred and ritual beginnings. Required of all majors.

subject: THEA
title: Experimental Art and Animation
description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
prereq_raw: CINE 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or CINE 353 / DNCE 353 / THEA 353 (or concurrent) or CINE 356 / DNCE 356 / THEA 356 (or concurrent).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: SCA, ART, THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only.

subject: THEA
title: Playwriting
description: One-act plays; practice in writing in dramatic form.
prereq_raw: Grade of B or better in composition or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Screenplay Writing
description: Characterization, structure, theme, image, and other components of writing for film.
prereq_raw: THEA 201 and grade of B or better in composition, or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Auditioning
description: Preparation of material from different audition situations, including monologues, cold readings, dance, singing, and TV/film.

subject: THEA
title: Acting II: Advanced Scene Study
description: Further exploration of character development and dramatic action through textual analysis.

subject: THEA
title: Film/TV Acting
description: Acting techniques for film and TV production. Students appear in scenes from TV and film scripts.
prereq_raw: One of THEA 101 , THEA 221 , THEA 222 , COM 201 , or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Film/TV Acting
description: Advanced acting techniques for film and TV production. Taping/filming of scenes and full-length scripts.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Asian Acting Styles
description: Principles of acting based on traditional Asian models. Voice, movement exercises.

subject: THEA
title: Taiji (T’ai Chi) for Actors I
description: Basic Taijiquan (T’ai Chi Ch’uan) movement training.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: THEA
title: Taiji Round Form for Actors
description: Introduction to basic Asian movement skills through learning the Wu-style taijiquan round form, a faster and more fluid version of the full 108 taiji sequence of forms.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to non-majors. Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to the Performing Arts of Southeast Asia
description: Introduction to the history and development of major performing arts genres in Southeast Asia: theatre, dance-drama, opera, music, puppetry, ritual, and modern spoken drama. Topics include cultural identity, multiculturalism, modernization, and tourism. Online course.

title: (Alpha) Topics in Theatre Production
description: Workshop in principles, techniques, and application of contemporary theatre production practices. (B) entertainment electrics: lighting, sound, special effects, projections, and related areas; (C) technical production: technical direction, technical design, construction, rigging, and related areas; (D) scenic painting: techniques of scene painting for theatre through reading, drawing exercises, color theory, and practical projects; (E) props and crafts: techniques to create props for theatre.
prereq_raw: any course in THEA or DNCE, or production experience; or consent.
repeatable_raw: 1 time for different alphas, each alpha can be taken one time.

subject: THEA
title: Lighting I: Beginning Lighting Design
description: Basic principles of lighting design and associated technologies. Includes functions and properties of light, lighting and control equipment, working procedures, and drafting and paperwork techniques.

subject: THEA
title: Scenic I: Beginning Scenic Design
description: Workshop introducing the basic principles and approaches of scenic design for theatre and dance, with emphasis on the creative process.
prereq_raw: a course in THEA or DNCE, production experience, or consent. (Consent required for production experience option)

subject: THEA
title: Introduction to Costume Construction
description: Workshop on basic principles of costume construction for theatre and dance. Professional practices, materials, and methods.

subject: THEA
title: Costumes I: Beginning Costume Design
description: Basic principles and approaches to costume design for theatre and dance. Visual communication methods, creative process, historical research, and organizational practices.

subject: THEA
title: Stage Makeup Workshop
description: Western and traditional Asian makeup theory and application practice. Western corrective, period, and old age makeup. Asian may include Jingju, Kabuki, Wayang.

subject: THEA
title: Performance and Medicine
description: Survey of key texts on medicine and performance, and on how these two areas intersect, including representations of medicine and illness in contemporary drama and performance-based practices within medicine.

subject: THEA
title: Curtain Up! Broadway Musicals, Then and Now
description: Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the “Hamilton” phenomenon, exploring their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts. Course develops written communication skills.

subject: THEA
title: Movement Improvisation
description: Introduces movement improvisation to all levels and disciplines. Movement studies will explore improvisation approaches, devices, elements, exercises, and implications to gain skills in and appreciation for the art of improvisation.

subject: THEA
title: Beginning Directing
description: Basic practical course in how to direct a play. Students will direct scenes. Emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: THEA, DNCE, THDN majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: upper division theatre majors or consent.

subject: THEA
title: Advanced Hula I
description: Advanced level hula course for students with hula experience that builds upon existing cultural knowledge, performance and language skills presented in THEA 288 / DNCE 288 .

title: Directed Reading/Studies
description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision.

subject: TIM
title: International Exchange Programs
description: UH Mānoa School of Travel Industry Management majors participating in approved international exchange programs.

subject: TIM
title: Internship I
description: Introduction to travel industry. Discussion of job search strategies, TIM internship requirements, career and academic planning.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Travel Industry Management
description: Overview of travel industry and related major business components. Analysis of links between hotel, food, transportation, recreation, and other industries comprising tourism.

subject: TIM
title: Food and World Cultures
description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

subject: TIM
title: Food and World Cultures
description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

subject: TIM
title: Internship II
description: A minimum of two hundred hours of travel industry experience. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

subject: TIM
title: Internship III
description: A minimum of two hundred hours of travel industry experience. Position must be different from TIM 200 position and of a more responsible nature or in a different organization. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

subject: TIM
title: Legal Environment of the Travel Industry
description: Origin, development, and principles of common, statutory, constitutional, international, and maritime law relating to the travel industry, including applicable ethical precepts.

subject: TIM
title: Information Systems Technology
description: Computer applications in the travel industry; operation and evaluation of specific travel industry systems and applied business systems. TIM majors only.
prereq_raw: TIM 101 ; and either ICS 101 , or both LTEC 112 and LTEC 113 .

subject: TIM
title: Management of Service Enterprises
description: Principles and philosophies of management with special emphasis on those principles and theories that are most relevant to management in service-based industries. Students may not earn credit for TIM 303 and BUS 315 . TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Principles of Travel Industry Marketing
description: Concepts, problems, processes of marketing within the travel industry; development of marketing strategies including product, place, promotion, and price for travel institutions. Students may not earn credit for TIM 304 and BUS 312 . TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
description: Cash flow determination and management strategies for financing hospitality ventures and expansion. Determining the financial viability of proposed and existing operations through traditional and state-of-the-art techniques. TIM majors only.
prereq_raw: TIM 101 , ACC 200 and ACC 210 ; and NREM 203 , MATH 203 , MATH 215 , MATH 241 , or BUS 250 .

subject: TIM
title: Human Resource Management: Travel Industry
description: Comprehensive overview of human resources management (HRM) with emphasis on the supervision in the travel industry, including HRM as a firm’s strategic asset, contemporary theories, issues and developments, to improve employee recruitment productivity and retention.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Institutional Purchasing
description: Procurement responsibilities in hospitality management. Emphasis on institutions supplying hospitality operations and legislation which controls standards of industrial supplies and goods.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM and FSHN majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Club Management
description: Introduction to club and institutional management, including operations, services, and facilities.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Foodservice Management
description: Critical and essential aspects of managing foodservice operations including principles of food safety and sanitation, procedural knowledge in front and back of the house and guest relations.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Hotel Management
description: Comprehensive understanding of hotel management and functional departments including front office, accounting, housekeeping, food and beverage, marketing, security and safety. Simulation of management trainee programs by hotel chains. Synthesis of concepts, tools and theories of decision-making relevant to hotel operations.
prereq_raw: TIM 101 , TIM 302 , and TIM 303 (with a minimum grade of C- in TIM 302 and TIM 303 ).
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- in TIM 302 and TIM 303 )

subject: TIM
title: Quality Food Management
description: Explore various aspects of the quality in foodservice operations and develop strategies to measure and improve the quality.

subject: TIM
title: Events Planning and Marketing
description: Introduction to special event planning processes and techniques. Emphasis on designing, planning, marketing, management, staging events, legal compliances, risk management, financial control, and successful event evaluation.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: TIM
title: Quantity Foods and Institutional Purchasing
description: Quantity food and beverage operations, menu development and costing, dietary menu claims, purchasing procedures, inventory control, procurement, transportation, legislation. Institutional foodservice sanitation, Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and National Restaurant Association Certification.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.
prereq_raw: ECON 120 or ECON 130 or ECON 131 ; or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Sociocultural Issues in Tourism
description: Issues arising from the impacts of tourism on societies and cultures. Class discussions of the ethical dimensions of such impacts. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Geography of Global Tourism
description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions. Emphasis on Writing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: TIM
title: Travel Distribution Management
description: History, development, operations, and management of travel distribution organizations including: travel agents, tour operators and wholesalers, specialty channelers, meeting planners, incentive houses, travel associations, and other destination management organizations. Evolution and economics of the distribution of travel products through destination databases and electronic commerce.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Hotel/Resort Facilities and Design
description: Comprehensive understanding of facilities management and design including maintenance systems, sustainable development options and design and environmental management.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality Sales & Negotiation
description: Personal selling by hospitality and tourism firms engaged in business-to-business marketing. Emphasis will be placed on negotiation case studies, exercises, and role-plays.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Introduction to Tourism Transportation
description: Introduction to managerial and operational issues related to all modes of transportation used by tourists into or within a tourist destination. Passenger behavior; transport infrastructure; transport networks; regulation; sustainable transport.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Principles of Logistics
description: Management of logistics systems: inventory control, warehousing, materials management, physical distribution, transportation. Emphasis on Hawaiʻi’s location and unique problems.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Air Transportation Management
description: Marketing, management and strategies used by airlines, airports, catering, and aircraft manufacturers.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Surface Transportation Management
description: Management of surface transportation such as cars, buses, intercity rail, etc. Includes marketing, ownership and financing, supply chain, operations, regulation and promotion, and human resources. Emphasis on written communication.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Economics in Travel Industry
description: Microeconomic theory of consumer behavior and demand production cost analysis, market structure and pricing in travel companies. Economic impact of tourism. Students may not earn credit for TIM 365 and BUS 313 .
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: TIM Study Abroad
description: Study abroad instructional experience emphasizing international travel, tourism and hospitality-related topics at equivalent, accredited programs. Content varies depending on locus of instruction and instructor. Course qualifies as either a TIM or general elective with pre-approval or department.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

Restricted to majors.

subject: TIM
title: Resort, Spa and Wellness Management
description: Principles of resort and spa development. Essential aspects of understanding the leadership and interrelationships of managing/operating and marketing resorts, spas, and wellness.

subject: TIM
title: Resort Mixed Use Development
description: Critical and essential aspects of developing and managing resort mixed use facilities. Includes multidimensional and dynamic interrelationships of site development and facilities, business mix, management structures and systems, and industry practices.
prereq_raw: TIM 313 or TIM 369 ; and TIM 314 . Recommended: TIM 333 and TIM 401 .

subject: TIM
title: Revenue Management in Travel Industry
description: An in-depth comprehensive introduction to the theory and practice of revenue management and provides recognition of thorough knowledge of the fundamental metrics and methodologies used within the hotel industry.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only.

subject: TIM
title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: TIM
title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

subject: TIM
title: Destination Development and Marketing
description: Analysis of key factors in the marketing and management of tourism destinations, including destination branding, product development, integrated marketing, stakeholder relations, and the role of destination marketing/marketing organizations. Emphasis on written communication.

subject: TIM
title: Strategic Management for the Travel/ Hospitality Industry
description: Strategic management in the travel/hospitality industry. Case study analysis, discussion and written reports, covering strategies, management problems and industry issues. Emphasis on writing instruction.
prereq_raw: TIM 301 , TIM 302 , TIM 303 , TIM 304 , TIM 305 and graduating senior.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Transportation
description: Advanced level of discussion in terms of transportation, including management, economics, strategy, regulation, operating performance, fleet management, and network management. Emphasis on written communication.

subject: TIM
title: Environmental Management Systems
description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: TIM
title: Research Application in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Analysis of methodologies appropriate for research in travel industry management. Survey of the literature of applied techniques and approaches including exploratory approaches. Familiarization with research design and implementation of development of research proposals.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Strategic Marketing in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: In-depth study of marketing principles and problems related to travel industry organizations. Emphasis on strategic marketing. Research applications, international and domestic marketing of travel industry services.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Information Technology, e-Commerce, and Travel Industry in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Planning, implementation, management, evaluation, and impact of information and electronic communication technologies, including e-commerce applications in the travel industry. Analysis of new information technology use as an area of research and strategic application.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Managerial Accounting for Travel Industry
description: Advanced study of management accounting within travel industry: responsibility accounting, pricing decisions, concepts and application of central systems, financial planning, price level impacts, performance evaluation.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality Management
description: Advanced human relations and operating issues; use of accounting, behavioral, financial, marketing, and informational systems in managing hospitality organizations.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Managerial Economics in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Advanced study analysis of economics and management of passenger transportation systems serving the travel industry. Emphasis on topics such as government policy, transport economics, marketing and management, and the relationships between transportation systems and tourism development.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Global Tourism Analysis
description: International trade theory and regional analysis methodologies applied to tourism and the service industry, including travel balance account, inter-regional transactions flow, economic impacts, environmental economics, demand theory and forecasting.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Financial Management in Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation
description: Applications of financial analysis to both the domestic and international travel industry.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TIM majors only. Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TIM
title: Hospitality, Tourism, and Transportation Field Studies
description: Integration of concepts and application of knowledge and skills from other courses to a selected field study project.
prereq_raw: Any two 600-level TIM courses completed and a third concurrent; or consent.

subject: TIM
title: Professional Paper
description: Independent project or paper under faculty supervision in lieu of Plan A, TIM 700 thesis. Requires proposal approved by supervisor and graduate chair prior to registration.
prereq_raw: Three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent.

subject: TIM
title: Seminar: Travel Industry Management Policy
description: Integration of learning through analysis of policy issues, trends, and problems in the travel industry.
prereq_raw: Three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent.

subject: TIM
title: Directed Reading
description: Independent study of approved, advanced reading with faculty supervision. Requires proposal prepared by student and approved by supervisor and graduate chair before registration.

subject: TIM
title: Thesis Research
description: Independent supervised research. Formal and oral written presentation of research findings.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Tourism Management
description: Sustainable management of global tourism to minimize its negative impacts and optimize its positive ones. Deliberation and analysis of major issues related to global tourism from the perspectives of ethics and sustainability. PhD students only.
prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Hospitality Management
description: Advanced hospitality management aims to critically explore the key areas that comprise hospitality management, integrate theories and practice, and explore the linkages between hospitality research, management, and business strategies. PhD students only.
prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

subject: TIM
title: Advanced Topics in Global Transportation Management
description: Transport economics and management, and their applications for the travel and tourism industry. Focuses on analytical thinking, problem-solving. and research skills using transportation issues. PhD students only.
prereq_raw: TIM 601 with a minimum grade of B.

subject: TONG
title: Beginning Tongan
description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

subject: TONG
title: Beginning Tongan
description: Continuation of TONG 101 .

subject: TONG
title: Intermediate Tongan
description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

subject: TONG
title: Intermediate Tongan
description: Continuation of TONG 201 .

subject: TPSS
title: (Alpha) Plants for People
description: The origins: social, cultural, and ceremonial traditions; culture; food and nutritional properties. Processing of a variety of tropical horticultural plants are presented, with tasting sessions and optional field trips. Topics will rotate among (B) beverage crops (e.g., coffee, tea, chocolate, kava, fruit juices); (C) herbs, spices, and flavoring (selection of examples to be determined); (D) tropical fruits (assortment offered depends on availability during semester); (E) ornamental plants (flowers, houseplants, popular landscape plans, bonsai, ethnic ornamentals). Does not count towards TPSS major.
