subject: TPSS
title: Sustainable Food and Energy (Field Course)
description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawaiʻi for sustainable development.

subject: TPSS
title: Natural History Field Trips on Hawaiʻi Island
description: Field trips for Natural history and Conservation of the Hawaiian Islands.

subject: TPSS
title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi as a model system.

subject: TPSS
title: Aquaponics
description: Basic online course integrates aquaculture (raising fish and prawns) with hydroponics plant cultivation in water. Includes the basic design and construction of an aquaponics feed system.

subject: TPSS
title: Organic Food Crop Production
description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

subject: TPSS
title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

subject: TPSS
title: Tropical Production Systems
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Comparisons and contrasts of crop management systems, techniques, and technologies in protected and open field production of tropical crops.

subject: TPSS
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science
description: Origin, development, properties, management of tropical soils; classification of Hawaiian soils.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Minimum prerequisite grade of C or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Fundamentals of Soil Science Laboratory
description: Field and analytical methods for exploring the origin, development, properties, and management of soils, with an emphasis on tropical and Hawaiian soils.
prereq_raw: ( CHEM 161 and CHEM 161L ) with a minimum grade of C.

subject: TPSS
title: Current Topics in Plant Science
description: Undergraduate seminar that provides the presentation and discussion of topics of current relevance to students preparing for careers in applied plant sciences. Oral focus designation.
prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 or NREM 210 , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Farm & Food Marketing
description: Problems, agencies, functions, costs, prices, regulations affecting marketing: proposed improvements.

subject: TPSS
title: Applied Statistics for Food and Landscape Systems
description: Designed for students interested in developing a critical framework for understanding different ways of measuring, visualizing, and interpreting the different goals humans have for agroecosystems.

subject: TPSS
title: Renewable Energy and Society
description: Combined lecture/discussion regarding the ability of renewable energy technologies to meet local, national, and global energy demands and their potential impacts on the environment and society.

subject: TPSS
title: Managerial Accounting
description: Principles and methods of agricultural accounting. Preparing and interpreting financial statements. Sources and costs of credit, capital budgeting, tax management, estate planning.
prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Tropical Landscape Practices
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Concepts and techniques of landscape installation and management in the tropics.
prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 369 ; or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Enterprise Management
description: Introduction of practical concepts and methods used in business management. Introduce broad range of business strategies. Understand the critical role each strategy plays. Facilitate student’s practice of analytical and critical thinking through case studies.

subject: TPSS
title: Landscape Architecture History
description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.

subject: TPSS
title: Landscape Graphics Studio
description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.

subject: TPSS
title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale.

subject: TPSS
title: Horticulture: Theory and Practice
description: Techniques of culture and management of horticulture crops.

subject: TPSS
title: Ornamental Plant Materials
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Identification, origin, use, and cultural requirement of trees, shrubs, vines, and groundcovers used in Hawaiian landscapes.

subject: TPSS
title: Genetics: Theory to Application
description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

subject: TPSS
title: Vegetable Crop Production
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Crop biology, requirements, and production techniques for commercial vegetable production in Hawaiʻi will be stressed.

subject: TPSS
title: Flower and Foliage Crop Production
description: Biology and production of cut flowers, blooming potted plants, foliage plants under field and protected cultivation in Hawaiʻi and globally.

subject: TPSS
title: Tropical Fruit Production
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices and recent innovations in tropical and subtropical fruit crops, emphasizing botanical aspects and commercial production in Hawaiʻi and beyond.

subject: TPSS
title: Turfgrass Management
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Adaptability and selection, establishment, and cultural practices of grasses for various types of turf.

subject: TPSS
title: Cultural Biogeography
description: Co-evolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems.

subject: TPSS
title: Extension Education & Outreach
description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program develoopment and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher, or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Introduction to Social, Ethical and Political Issues Associated with Biotechnology
description: Introduces concepts of biotechnology, fundamental issues associated with use of this technology, with special emphasis on agricultural biotechnology.
prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 or BIOL 171 or NREM 210 , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Turfgrass Pest Management
description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawaiʻi, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Propagation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Theoretical and applied aspects of seed and vegetative propagation technology involving fruits, flowers, vegetables, and landscape plants.

subject: TPSS
title: Tropical Seed Science
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of seed science, seed physiology, seed production, and genetic modification. Hawaiʻi’s seed industry and biotechnology.

children.text: ( recommended) and TPSS 420 ( recommended), or consent

subject: TPSS
title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
prereq_raw: ECON 130 or NREM 220 / SUST 220 , and ECON 321 or NREM 310 ; or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Nursery Management
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Management practices in production and operations of commercial nurseries in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 364 ; or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: TPSS
title: The Biology of Fungi
description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.
prereq_raw: BOT 201 or BIOL 172 with a minimum grade of C; or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental Soil Chemistry
description: Study of soil chemical processes such as weathering, adsorption, precipitation, and ion exchange; causes of soil acidity, alkalinity, and salinity; reactions between soils and fertilizers, pesticides, or heavy metals. Management strategies to minimize environmental contamination by nitrate, phosphate, and trace elements such as As, Pb, and Se.

subject: TPSS
title: Applied UAS Operations for Agriculture and Environment
description: Applied operations with uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), mission planning, safety, photogrammetry and GIS, personnel management, and payload operation. Focus on topics required for commercial certifications as a remote pilot, agricultural operator, and pesticide applicator.
prereq_raw: completion of FS/FQ, DP, DB, and DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: STEM majors only.

children.text: DY core requirements with a minimum grade of C-

subject: TPSS
title: Tissue Culture/Transformation
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Application of plant tissue culture for plant scientists; study of the growth and development of plant tissues in culture as influenced by chemical and environmental factors, and the regeneration of plants following plant transformation by biolistics and other molecular approaches.

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainable Nutrient Management in Agroecosystems
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Biological, chemical, and physical processes governing the cycling of nutrients in agroecosystems, crop and livestock production, and the effects on surrounding unmanaged ecosystems.
prereq_raw: ( TPSS 304 and CHEM 161 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Breeding and Genetics
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Unique aspects of plant genetics and applications to crop improvement, with emphasis on breeding plants in Hawaiʻi.

subject: TPSS
title: Soil Plant Environment
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Bio-physical processes in the soil-plant-atmosphere continuum that influence crop growth and development. Methods to estimate the impact of soil and climate on crop performance. Use of crop models to simulate effects of planting date, plant spacing and density, fertilizer rate, rainfall or irrigation, and daily weather on crop yield and farm income.
prereq_raw: TPSS 304 and either PHYS 151 or PHYS 170 , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Irrigation and Water Management
description: Basic soil-water-plant relationships, irrigation water requirements, irrigation efficiencies, different methods of irrigation, planning, design and management of an irrigation system, fertigation and impact of irrigation on soil and water quality.
prereq_raw: NREM 203 (or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 (or equivalent), or consent.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 304 / TPSS 304 ( or equivalent), or consent

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Physiology
description: Integration of form and function from cellular to whole plant levels in processes from seed germination, through photosynthesis, growth, and morphogenesis, to flowering and senescence.

subject: TPSS
title: Principles of Plant Physiology Lab
description: (1 3-hr Lab) Principles of experimentation in plant physiology, includes individual investigations.

subject: TPSS
title: Post-Harvest Physiology
description: Comparative physiological and biochemical processes during growth, maturation, ripening, and senescence in fruits, vegetables, and flowers related to changes in quality and storage life. Tropical commodities emphasized.
prereq_raw: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 , BIOL 171 , or BOT 201 ; CHEM 152 ; or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Nutrient Diagnosis in the Tropics
description: Designed for students to identify essential nutrients required by plants; diagnose nutrient disorders in plants; and propose environmentally sound solutions to correct disorders.

subject: TPSS
title: Life in the Soil Environment
description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
prereq_raw: TPSS 371 / PEPS 371 / SUST 371 or BIOL 375 , or MICR 351 , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
description: Laboratory to accompany TPSS 480 . Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171L and BIOL 172L , or MICR 351L , or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Weed Science
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.
prereq_raw: ( TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and CHEM 152 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Plants in Design
description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.

subject: TPSS
title: Experimental Topics
description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

subject: TPSS
title: Internship
description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

subject: TPSS
title: Internship Experience
description: Internship field experience for TPSS majors.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TPSS majors only.

subject: TPSS
title: Directed Studies
description: Supervised individual instruction in field laboratory and library.

subject: TPSS
title: Crop Modeling
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Principles of modeling crop growth and development, model types, techniques, simulation. Modeling influence of climate/environment on phenology, growth, development of horticultural crops.

subject: TPSS
title: Experimental Design
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Advanced Soil Microbiology
description: (3 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Study of biochemical and biogeochemical transformations mediated by soil microorganisms, emphasis on processes important to plant growth productivity and environmental quality.

subject: TPSS
title: Nutrition of Tropical Crops
description: (1 2-hr Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Mineral nutrition of plants in relation to plant metabolism, mechanisms of ion uptake, long-distance transport of solutes, and interactions at the root-soil interface. Special emphasis on problems associated with tropical crops.

subject: TPSS
title: Professional Development
description: Lecture/discussion targets students exiting from graduate degree programs and provides preparation as a career professional; topics include establishing a professional identity; CV and cover letters, job-seeking due diligence, and negotiation skills.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TPSS
title: Molecular Genetics of Crops
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Applications of molecular genetics to crop improvement.
prereq_raw: ( TPSS 453 and MBBE 402 ) with a minimum grade of C-, or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Quantitative Genomics and Evolution
description: Overview and lab-based course exploring theory and methods to understand genome evolution and adaptation; focus will be on a range of organisms.

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Biochemistry
description: Comprehensive study of chemical constituents and biochemical processes unique to the plant kingdom with emphasis on selected aspects of current interest.
prereq_raw: MBBE 402 (with a minimum grade of C) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C ) or consent

subject: TPSS
title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawaiʻi and the tropics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TPSS majors only.

subject: TPSS
title: Advanced Soil Chemistry
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Physio-chemical processes in soils and soil solutions, with emphasis on ionic equilibria, mineral stability, organic complexation, and surface sorption of major plant nutrients and heavy metals.

subject: TPSS
title: Soil Plant Nutrient Relations
description: (2 Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Soil-plant interactions, emphasis on characteristics of tropical soils and plants influencing nutrient uptake by plants. Diagnostic methods to identify nutrient deficiencies and element toxicity.
prereq_raw: TPSS 450 (with a minimum grade of C-) or consent.

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- ) or consent

subject: TPSS
title: Information Research Skills
description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

subject: TPSS
title: Communications in the Sciences
description: (3-hr Lec/Lab combination) Laboratory-type course for improving communication abilities in the sciences and engineering. Presentations to lay audiences are emphasized. Hands-on experience in techniques and methods is provided.

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TPSS and LAND majors only.

subject: TPSS
title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TPSS majors only.

subject: TPSS
title: Orchidology
description: (2 Lec, 1 3-hr Lab) Classification, culture, cytogenetics, breeding of orchids.
prereq_raw: Consent. Recommended: TPSS 200 / SUST 211 and TPSS 402 .

subject: TPSS
title: Graduate Seminar
description: Presentation of research reports; reviews of current literature in plant and soil sciences.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing or consent.

subject: TPSS
title: Sustainability of Food Systems
description: Explores sustainability and resilience of food systems with an emphasis on Hawaiʻi, using interdisciplinary approaches to assess impacts.

subject: TPSS
title: Plant Growth and Development
description: Contemporary literature is used as the basis for understanding the physiology for whole plant growth and development. Aspects covered include vegetative and reproductive development, seed dormancy, senescence, abscission, and relevant biochemical and molecular processes.

subject: TPSS
title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

subject: TPSS
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in TPSS program.

subject: TPSS
title: Directed Research
description: In-depth study of specialized problems.

subject: TPSS
title: Special Topics
description: Specialized topics from various areas of plant and soil research such as experimental techniques, growth regulation, morphogenesis, genetics and breeding, culture and nutrition of tropical crops.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health: Preparing for the Next Pandemic
description: Focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study of a global health problem that is optimally approached from a One Health perspective.
prereq_raw: ANSC 200 , BIOL 101 , MICR 130 , PH 201 , or consent of instructor.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Journal Club
description: Students gain critical reading skills in the presentation and discussion of published literature on One Health-related topics.

subject: TRMD
title: Principles of Medical Parasitology
description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.
prereq_raw: MICR 351 with a grade of B or higher or equivalent.

subject: TRMD
title: International Training in Biosciences Research
description: Combines weekly lectures by faculty for discussion of the 9 Steps of Research and completion of training courses for working with human subjects, including research ethics, laboratory safety, blood-borne pathogens, and principles of health disparity. MHIRT cohort only.

subject: TRMD
title: Health Disparities
description: Overview of biosciences research related to health and health disparities in a global setting as well as in Hawaiʻi. Workshop topics include health research, Native Hawaiian health, global health, and cultural competency. MHIRT cohort only.

subject: TRMD
title: Summer Research Experience
description: Hands-on research experience at assigned international sites. Students learn research and analytical skills in the field and laboratory setting, and present data to peers and faculty upon completion of the training. MHIRT cohort only.

subject: TRMD
title: Medical and Urban Entomology
description: (2 Lec, 1-3-hr hybrid Lab) Biology, ecology, health and economic impacts, and control of urban insect pests and medically important arthropods that act as vectors of diseases.
prereq_raw: ( PEPS 363 or BIOL 265 ) with a minimum grade of C, or consent.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Practicum
description: Provide certificate students with real-world experience and opportunity to integrate and apply classroom learning in a professional environment. Intended for students who prefer to pursue a supervised, practical experience rather than a research-based project.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Seminar
description: Weekly presentations and discussions on current events and research in the field of One Health. Presentation topics may include research progress, literature reviews, or research proposals.

subject: TRMD
title: Reading and Research
description: Directed reading and research in laboratory; diagnostic aspects of bacterial, parasitic, and viral infections.

subject: TRMD
title: Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Elective for fourth-year medical students for advanced study of selected topics within the field of tropical medicine and medical microbiology.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Fourth-year standing or MD degree.

subject: TRMD
title: One Health Elective
description: Foundation in One Health concepts and practical application to management of disease through recognition of the interconnection of human, animal, and ecosystem health. MD student at JABSOM only.
prereq_raw: Completion of MD 3rd year clerkships and consent.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Medical students only.

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: infectious diseases
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: parasitology
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: epidemiology
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Topics in Infectious Diseases: immunology
description: Elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: (Alpha) Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: infectious diseases
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: parasitology
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: epidemiology
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Selected Research Topics in Infectious Diseases: immunology
description: Research elective for medical students; (B) infectious diseases; (C) parasitology; (D) epidemiology; (E) immunology. MD majors only.

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TRMD
title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate standing only.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology I: Medical Parasitology
description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.

subject: TRMD
title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Micro II
description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

subject: TRMD
title: Tropical Medicine Laboratory Rotations
description: Practical experience in use of equipment and procedures in infectious disease and immunology research; introduction to research in tropical medicine.

subject: TRMD
title: Neurovirology
description: Seminar on neuroinvasive viruses giving basics of viruses causing nervous system diseases and discussing recent advances in the research field of neurovirology.

subject: TRMD
title: Infectious Disease Microbiology III
description: Basic structure, physiology, epidemiology, and genetics of pathogenic bacteria as well as the host response to these organisms. Correlation of these characteristics to disease pathogenesis in humans and animal models.

subject: TRMD
title: Advances In Medical Immunology
description: Presentations/discussions of current literature concerning recent advances in immunology relevant to disease and to disease processes.

subject: TRMD
title: Infection and Immunity
description: Combined lecture/discussion of interactions of pathogens with the innate and acquired immune systems. Topics will include the role of novel receptors in pathogen detection, inflammation in disease pathogenesis, pathogen immune evasion, and neuroimmunology.

subject: TRMD
title: Ecological Epidemiology
description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

subject: TRMD
title: Vaccinology
description: History/evolution of vaccines, current and next generation vaccines, vaccine immunology, adjuvants, vaccine strategies, vaccines for viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases, vaccine-proof-of-concept and downstream developmental studies; vaccine safety production processes.
prereq_raw: ( TRMD 604 and TRMD 605 ) with a minimum grade of B.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Genetics and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
description: An evolutionary perspective to examine the interactive responses between infectious agents and the immune system. Topics will include natural selection, life history evolution, population genetics of pathogens and hosts, and anti-microbial resistance.
prereq_raw: TRMD 604 (or concurrent) and TRMD 605 (or concurrent), or consent.

subject: TRMD
title: Bioinformatics I
description: Provides fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with strong emphasis on hands-on training. Topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phytogeny, and genomics including microarray and RNA-sequence analysis.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.
repeatable_raw: 1 time, but credit earned one time only.

subject: TRMD
title: Advances in HIV/AIDS
description: History of HIV, basic biology and virology, epidemiology, HIV pathogenesis and immunology, clinical features, and co-morbidities. Treatment and prevention of HIV/AIDS, including research methods, statistics, cultural competence, genetics, pathophysiology, drug and vaccine development.

subject: TRMD
title: Fundamentals of Biostatistics
description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Parasitology
description: Consideration of ultrastructure, physiology, biochemistry, in-vitro cultivation and host-parasite relationship of parasites of medical importance.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Virology
description: In-depth study of the major groups of viruses pathogenic for human; virus replication, host range, pathogenesis, immunology, and epidemiology.

subject: TRMD
title: Advanced Medical Bacteriology
description: Role of bacteria in infectious diseases, with emphasis on clinical aspects and identification of etiological agents.

subject: TRMD
title: Epidemiology of Tropical Infectious Diseases
description: Epidemiology of infectious diseases as it relates to tropical medicine. Lecture/seminar format.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: TRMD graduate standing or consent.

subject: TRMD
title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

subject: TRMD
title: Plan B Master’s Project
description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Graduate standing in TRMD.

subject: TRMD
title: Directed Research
description: Directed research in medical microbiology (bacteriology, parasitology, virology).

subject: TRMD
title: Thesis Research
description: Research for master’s thesis.

subject: TRMD
title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

subject: TRMD
title: Dissertation Research
description: Research for doctoral thesis.
prereq_raw: Approval of department faculty is required.

subject: UNIV
title: University Experience
description: An introduction to the university community; topics include critical thinking, the value of higher education, cultural and transition issues; emphasis on writing.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic and Personal Exploration
description: Introduction to goal setting, time management, major exploration, academic planning, service-learning opportunities, student/faculty meetings, financial literacy, and encourages frequent self-reflection.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic and Career Exploration
description: Introduces exploratory students to major and career exploration resources, guides students in developing personal, academic, and career goals and plans, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Develops written communication skills.

subject: UNIV
title: Introduction to Majors and UH Mānoa
description: Major exploration providing incoming students with an understanding of the tools to navigate UH Mānoa and explore the programs of study available. Introduction to career development, goal setting, and action planning. Freshmen only.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory majors only.

subject: UNIV
title: Topics in Learning Techniques & Technologies
description: Student-centered topics on techniques and technologies used for successful learning. Emphasizes the cultivation of learning dispositions and strategies for achievement in higher education and beyond.

subject: UNIV
title: Your Academic Journey
description: Provides exploratory students with the knowledge/skills to thrive in college and beyond. Utilizes writing as a tool for research, analysis, exploration, and reflection. Topics include major and career exploration, personal interests, and goal-setting. May not be taken concurrently or after UNIV 340 . Freshmen and sophomores only.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory designations only.

subject: UNIV
title: ACE Mentoring: Facilitating Student Development
description: Theoretical foundations in student learning and holistic development. Practical leadership skills acquisition and application through the facilitation of a seminar for new freshmen. Emphasis on developing proficiency in writing and public speech.

subject: UNIV
title: Academic Exploration Through Advising
description: Major exploration designed to assist exploratory students in the process of researching personal, career, and educational goals through writing and the impact of these goals on the decision-making process. Emphasis on written self-reflection and identity. Sophomore standing.

subject: UNIV
title: Major Exploration: Strategic Review
description: Designed to guide students who, as designated, require additional support in selection of best fit major.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory students only.

subject: UNIV
title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Training Course
description: Intensive course designed for peer advisor trainees to learn General Education requirements, university policies and procedures, and campus resources. Trainees also develop skills and strategies necessary to provide quality advising to their fellow students.

subject: UNIV
title: Collaborative Learning: Foundations of Tutoring
description: Theory and practice of collaborative learning in academic contexts. Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: UNIV
title: Topics in Major and Career Exploration
description: Major and career development for Exploratory students, using written and oral communication to facilitate learning across varied topics.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: UNIV
title: Major Exploration: Major Selection for Seniors
description: Specially designed for designated seniors to review, reflect upon, and analyze their choice of major in order to ensure selection of best fit major and graduate efficiently with that major.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Exploratory students only. Class Standing Restrictions: Seniors only.

subject: UNIV
title: Mānoa Peer Advisor Leader Training and Leadership Practicum
description: A reflective apprenticeship in which Peer Advisor Leaders solidify their understanding of advising and learn more about leadership and deepen their facilitation, communication, collaboration, and leadership skills by mentoring a cohort of peer advisor trainees.
prereq_raw: UNIV 350 (or equivalent course) (with a minimum grade of B).

children.text: ( or equivalent course) ( with a minimum grade of B )

subject: UNIV
title: Directed Study
description: Individual reading or research.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: URDU
title: Reading and Writing in Urdu
description: Introduces students to the Nastaliq (Urdu) script, alphabets, their various forms, and combination rules. Reading and writing is emphasized.

subject: UROP
title: Transformational Research Experiences for Early Undergraduates
description: Introduction to exploring discover-based investigation, with hands-on experiences in a wide range of science fields. Divided into 4-week learning modules led by researchers at several UH Mānoa research facilities on and off campus.

subject: UROP
title: Faculty Mentored Research and Creative Work Project
description: Directed research for undergraduate students conducting faculty-mentored research or creative work projects.
prereq_raw: Consent of UROP director and student faculty mentor.

children.text: of UROP director and student faculty mentor

subject: VIET
title: Elementary Vietnamese I
description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets one hour, three times a week.

subject: VIET
title: Elementary Vietnamese II
description: Continuation of VIET 101 .

subject: VIET
title: Intermediate Vietnamese I
description: Continuation of VIET 102 . After completion, most students should be able to use all major sentence patterns to produce sounds, combinations of sounds, tones, and intonation and have some understanding of Vietnamese culture.

subject: VIET
title: Intermediate Vietnamese II
description: Continuation of VIET 201 .

subject: VIET
title: Third-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of VIET 202 . Emphasis on increased proficiency and cultural understanding through interaction with Vietnamese media, including newspapers, radio, film, etc.

subject: VIET
title: Third-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of VIET 301 .

subject: VIET
title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of VIET 302 . Emphasis on cultural understanding through modern literary Vietnamese.

subject: VIET
title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
description: Continuation of VIET 401 .

subject: VIET
title: Introduction to Vietnamese Literature
description: Selected readings in major genres; emphasis on analysis. Modern literature.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to LGBTQ Studies
description: Introduction to a survey of the key terms, texts, and histories of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities with special attention to Hawaiʻi and Oceania.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures, with a focus on gender, race, class, and sexual dynamics; exploration of women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics.

subject: WGSS
title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures. Focus on gender, race, class, sexual dynamics, and women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics. Honors students only.

subject: WGSS
title: History of Gender, Sex, and Sexuality in Global Perspectives to 1500 CE
description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from prehistory to 1500 CE. Examines ancient world civilizations from multiple perspectives stressing issues and forces still influential today.

subject: WGSS
title: History of Gender, Sex and Sexuality in Global Perspective, 1500 CE to the Present
description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from 1500 CE to present. Examines world cultures from multiple perspectives, stressing issues and forces of continuing influence.

subject: WGSS
title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to nonmajors.

subject: WGSS
title: Psychology of Gender
description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to women’s lives: socialization of gender, mental health, violence against women, achievement motivation, lifespan issues, domestic violence.

subject: WGSS
title: Priestesses and Prophetesses
description: Legendary priestesses and prophetesses from ancient to modern religions around the world including ancient Sumeria, Egypt, Greece, China, India, the Middle East, Japan, and Hawaiʻi. This course develops written communication skills.

subject: WGSS
title: Women Philosophers
description: Introduces students to the ideas of women philosophers.
prereq_raw: any course 100 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women Writers of World Literature
description: Major women writers of world literature examined in context of female literary tradition.
prereq_raw: ENG 100 , ENG 100A , or ESL 100 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Sexual Identity in Literature
description: Selected themes in major works of various types, cultures, periods. Requires a minimum of 3,000 words of writing.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, War, and the Military
description: The military as it includes and excludes women as soldiers, nurses, wives, prostitutes, and victims. Women and war economics; feminism, war, and peace.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 362 , WGSS 375 or SOC 362 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Health
description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or WGSS 202 , or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or POLS 110 ; or consent.

children.text: -level SOC course, or POLS 110 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Indigenous Women’s Health
description: Examines issues of indigenous women’s health pre and post colonial in Hawaiʻi, Asia, and the Pacific regions.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 305 ; or HWST 107 , HWST 270 or HWST 285 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: U.S. Women’s History
description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work, women in social movements, changing norms regarding gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences of women. Emphasis on ethical issues and oral communication.

subject: WGSS
title: Sex and Gender
description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual difference; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Social Policy
description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent.

children.text: - or 300 -level course, or SOC 100 or any 200 -level SOC course; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Sport
description: Explores the influence of gender in sport from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives. Through extensive writing, students examine gendered experiences of participants, spectators, and employees in sports organizations.

subject: WGSS
title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation.
prereq_raw: one ES or WGSS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Intersectional Feminist Geographies
description: Explores space and place from intersectional feminist perspectives including Indigenous, Black, island, post-colonial and queer geographies. Focuses on contemporary case studies in gender and sexuality.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Sophomore standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: 20th-Century Literature by Women
description: Twentieth-century women writers and their works; novels, short stories, poems, autobiographies. Interrelations of gender and literature.
prereq_raw: (one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 ), and WGSS 245 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance, ethical considerations of genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, Ideas, and Society
description: Status of women in American society today in light of the cultural, historical, and philosophical forces that have produced it.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Religion
description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through reading autobiographies, films, and primary texts, and through the development of research and writing skills.
prereq_raw: WGSS 149 or REL 149 or REL 150 or HIST 151 or WGSS 151 .

subject: WGSS
title: Queer Dance Exploratory
description: Queer dance exploration in movement practices and performance.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: Open to all majors.

subject: WGSS
title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawaiʻi
description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawaiʻi; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
prereq_raw: any ANTH, SOC, or WGSS course.

subject: WGSS
title: Seminar: Women and International Development
description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment; ethical considerations of economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty. Open to nonmajors.
prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Sociology of Gender
description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawaiʻi and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher.
prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and the Media
description: Role and representation of women and non-binary communities in the media. Feminist alternatives to mainstream media and dominant narratives. Emphasis on oral communication to empower marginalized voices.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality; emphasis on teaching gender and sexuality through writing and oral communication.
prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Island Feminisms: Art, Literature, and Culture
description: Examines island feminisms and explores ways women have engaged in various forms of cultural production (art, literature, film). Interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transnational. Key themes discussed: settler-colonialism, race, gender, and sexuality.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Politics
description: Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries; female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 (or concurrent) or WGSS 362 (or concurrent) or any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent); or consent.

children.text: level POLS course (or concurrent) ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
description: Intersecting processes of racial and gender oppression and privilege; institutional contexts and lived experiences; ethical issues in past and present anti-racist feminist thought and activism in the United States and in Hawaiʻi.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or ES 101 or junior standing.

subject: WGSS
title: Sexualities
description: Multi-disciplinary course that draws from various disciplines in Social Science to explore human sexualities. Significant focus on ethical dilemmas and the utilization of ethical frameworks anchored in utilitarianism, rights, justice, virtue, and the common good.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 315 or WGSS 350 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
description: Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change.
prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or POLS 390 (or concurrent) or POLS 382 , WGSS 151 , or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Directed Reading

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and the Geopolitics of Korean Popular Culture
description: Using South Korean popular culture as a case study, this lecture/discussion/seminar examines the relationship between popular culture and a range of forces including: politics, international relations, military, social movements, fandoms, and industries.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Women, Gender, & Sexuality in Performance
description: Feminist and performance studies approaches to performances by women and other genders; focus on the representation and status of women

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Work
description: Gender and race of paid and unpaid work in the formal and informal sectors of the economy; carework in households; unemployment; ethics of revaluing feminized work; labor rights: scope: local and global.
prereq_raw: one 300-level WGSS or ES course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy
description: Examination of basic feminist issues in philosophy, and of responses to them.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality and Digital Media
description: Students learn how gender and sexuality are constructed online and produce a website to post their analysis and contribute to knowledge production about gender and sexuality in cyberspace.

subject: WGSS
title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: junior standing or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Seminar in the Biology of Women
description: Embryological, anatomical, and physiological development of human female; hormonal, neural, and behavioral determinants of female sexual behavior; psychobiology of pregnancy, ovariectomy, and menopause.
prereq_raw: WGSS 350 or BIOL 172 or BIOL 350 , or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Fashion, & Globalization
description: Explores ethics of the present and historic expansions of the fashion industry and its environmental impact globally. Examines how gender/race/class shape garment production and consumption and fashion activism in world regions. Emphasis on oral/written communication.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Madness
description: Interdisciplinary critical examination of the relationship between gender and mental health. Psychological research, feminist theory, autobiography, literature, and cinema.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 202 , WGSS 245 , PSY 202 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Crime
description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: - or 300 -level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Justice and Law
description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 381 , or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Violence
description: Interdisciplinary course will examine western constructs of gender violence on its correlates with ethnicity, class, sexuality, nation, and empire.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 202 , WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 , WGSS 460 , WGSS 462 , or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
description: Interdisciplinary approach to feminist perspectives on environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as political movement with reference to race and coloniality; cross-cultural comparison of differently-imagined relationships to non-human others, with emphasis on ethics and writing.
prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WGSS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.”
prereq_raw: any 300 level WGSS or POLS course, or consent.

children.text: level WGSS or POLS course, or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Methods and Research
description: Overview of feminist issues with dominant theories of knowledge and major methodologies employed in the social sciences; and exploration of role of gender theory and feminist politics in feminist research.

subject: WGSS
title: Queer Theory
description: Intensive survey of the key theories, texts, and questions of the interdisciplinary fields that make up queer theory.
prereq_raw: WGSS 141 or WGSS 151 or WGSS 392 or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and Consumption in a Global World
description: Students learn theories of the global economy, histories of consumerism, constructions of gendered public spaces, and how the cultural production of consumers and consumer culture functions in the process of globalization.

subject: WGSS
title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: - or 300 -level WGSS course, SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawaiʻi
description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai’i. The course develops written communication skills.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS or ES; or consent by instructor.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Junior standing or higher.

children.text: at least one course in WGSS

subject: WGSS
title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries. Recommended: at least one WGSS course.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent.

children.text: - or 300 -level WGSS course, or SOC 300 ; or consent

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Education
description: Examines historical and current gender issues in education as they intersect with ethnicity and class. We pay close attention to the writing process and the skills needed to compose a well-written research paper.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender, Sexuality, and Global Popular Culture
description: A study of gender, race, and sexuality as constructed in contemporary global popular culture, including music, films, novels, television shows, and internet culture.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or WGSS 202 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism, Nation and Empire
description: Examines U.S. feminist movements in the 19th and 20th century by exploring how U.S. racism, nationalism and imperialism have provided the context from which feminism emerged.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Globalization in Asia
description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 360 , WGSS 361 , WGSS 439 , AMST 310 , AMST 316 , AMST 318 , AMST 373 , AMST 455 , POLS 339 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g. with class, religion, ethnicity).

subject: WGSS
title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender in Action Cinema
description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Film
description: Exploration of film as a philosophical and artistic form in the context of gender, race, and sexuality.
prereq_raw: one of WGSS 151 , WGSS 175 , WGSS 176 , or THEA 201 ; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Indigenous Feminisms
description: Examines the origins and futures of Indigenous feminist theory and praxis. Topics explored include cultural revitalization, colonialism, and sexual violence in Indigenous communities, citizenship and sovereignty, and contemporary Native gender roles and identity.

subject: WGSS
title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
description: Intensive study of selected questions and issues in the construction and representation of sexuality and gender in specific genres, social and cultural contexts, or thematic/figurative clusters.
prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course; or consent.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Disasters
description: Explores disasters and their consequences for women, with attention to gender, race, sexuality, and class.
prereq_raw: at least one course in WGSS, or consent of instructor.
grade_option_raw: A-F only. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Social Sciences Internship
description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories.

subject: WGSS
title: Women and Revolution
description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

subject: WGSS
title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration. Junior standing or higher.

subject: WGSS
title: Selected Topics
description: Problems and issues for reading and research: feminist theory, criticism, affirmative action, etc.
prereq_raw: any WGSS course in appropriate area.

prereq_tree.text: any WGSS course in appropriate area

subject: WGSS
title: Teaching Women’s Studies
description: Strategies for teaching women’s studies; addressing complex issues of gender, race, nation, class, sexuality and culture in a contemporary multiethnic campus environment. Emphasis on classroom techniques, teaching pedagogies, and hands-on experience.
prereq_raw: WGSS 151 and one or more WGSS course with a grade of B or better in all relevant courses, instructor recommendation; or consent.

description: Introductory graduate seminar designed to develop common vocabulary and explore the core debates in transnational feminist teaching and research to encourage critical reflection about teaching assumptions, approaches, and techniques in the contemporary college or university environment.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Faculty Seminar Series
description: Seminar/discussion to introduce students pursuing the Graduate Certificate to the Women’s Studies faculty and their areas of research, and to initiate student’s graduate studies in a women’s studies field.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Women in American Culture
description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Research and Methods of Inquiry
description: Examination of an emergent body of literature about how to shape questions concerning gender, sex, race, class, colonialism, and other vectors of power. Includes methods from social sciences and humanities and debates in the philosophy of science.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Theory
description: Selected ideas from contemporary feminist theory concerning power, knowledge, and self; articulating women’s voice; deconstructing gender.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance.

subject: WGSS
title: Writing and Publishing in an Interdisciplinary Field
description: Writing-intensive and publishing-focused class, students learn how to publish in an interdisciplinary field. Readings and assignments are designed to help students succeed in academic publishing.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminism and Its “Others”
description: Relationship between feminist and other sites of critical insight and scholarship that have contributed to creating anticolonial, antiracist, antihomophobic theory, method and action. Questions the legacy of feminist coalition practices and engages the ongoing transformations that have begun to produce new alliances and coalitions that disrupt traditional boundaries of identity and power.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Topics in Feminist Social Policy Research
description: Feminist social scientists from a variety of fields have explored issues of gender, social change and social justice. Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: WGSS
title: Feminist Criminology
description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

subject: WGSS
title: Advanced Queer Theory
description: Advanced graduate seminar on the key ideas within queer theory. Students will become familiar with theories of queer relationality, queer of color critique, globalization of sexuality, disability and transgender studies, and queer indigeneities.
prereq_raw: undergraduate or graduate course work in women’s, gender, sexuality, or LGBTQ studies.

subject: WGSS
title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

subject: WGSS
title: Research in Feminist Studies: Capstone Experience
description: Provide women’s studies graduate certificate students with an opportunity to design, develop and complete a research project culminating in a publishable quality work and a professional quality seminar presentation.

subject: ZOOL
title: Animal Physiology
description: Lecture/laboratory introduction to animal physiology, especially vertebrates. Topics include nerve and muscle physiology, metabolism, circulation, respiration, excretion, and thermoregulation in a project-driven format. Labs develop skills in experimental biology, morphology, data analysis, and scientific writing.

subject: ZOOL
title: Comparative Physiology
description: Physical-chemical cellular mechanisms underlying function of organ systems; general principles inferable from study of adaption to diverse environments.
prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172 , and MBBE 402 (or concurrent) or BIOC 441 (or concurrent); or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Introduction to Neuroscience
description: Nerve cells, their signaling capabilities and the developmental organization of nervous systems, both invertebrate and vertebrate, for sensory reception, integration, behavioral command and learning; insights from on-going research using molecular, genetic, biophysical, and imaging methods.

subject: ZOOL
title: Avian Biology
description: Broad coverage of the morphology, physiology, ecology, behavior, and evolution of birds, emphasizing the relation of birds to general theory in biology.

subject: ZOOL
title: (Alpha) Seminar in Zoology
description: Reports on research, reviews of literature, or research experience. Required of students majoring in zoology or entomology. (B) general zoology; (D) animal behavior; (E) ecology; (F) physiology; (G) developmental biology; (H) marine biology.

subject: ZOOL

description: (1 3-hr Lab) Group or individual research projects depending on interest of students.

subject: ZOOL
title: Genetics of Behavior and Evolution
description: Introduction to concepts and techniques in the genetics of behavior. Techniques include next gen sequencing, GWAS, and more. Students may use real data to analyze associations between genotype and phenotype.
restrictions_raw: Class Standing Restrictions: Graduate students only.

subject: ZOOL
title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology
description: Lectures, readings and presentations on sensory systems and behavior of fishes.
prereq_raw: ZOOL 430 , ZOOL 606 , BIOL 306 , BIOL 465 ; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology Laboratory
description: Laboratory study of fish sensory systems and behavior.
prereq_raw: ZOOL 430 , ZOOL 606 , BIOL 306 , BIOL 465 ; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Topics in Development and Reproductive Biology
description: Discussion and survey of literature on specific topics; some field and lab work may be required.

subject: ZOOL
title: Quantitative Genomics and Evolution
description: Overview and lab-based course exploring theory and methods to understand genome evolution and adaptation; focus will be on a range of organisms.

subject: ZOOL
title: Seminar on Science Teaching
description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audio-visual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

subject: ZOOL

description: Principles of ecology of marine biota and environment.
restrictions_raw: Major Restrictions: graduate standing in zoology, oceanography, or botany; or consent.

description: (1 Lec, 1 2-hr Lab, 1 Discussion) Formal quantitative approach in identifying, designing, performing, analyzing, and interpreting ecological field problems.
prereq_raw: ZOOL 439, ZOOL 439L, and ZOOL 631 ; or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Evolution in Marine Systems
description: Fundamental elements of modern evolutionary theory and research, with a strong focus on marine organisms and ecosystems.

subject: ZOOL
title: Introduction to Statistical Modeling in Biology
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Statistical methods for biological research. Covers: probability; likelihood-based inference; hypothesis testing; linear and generalized linear models; common statistical tests; statistical programming.
prereq_raw: MATH 215 or MATH 216 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A or NREM 203 (or equivalent), or consent.

subject: ZOOL
title: Advanced Biometry
description: (3 Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Multivariate statistical methods: multiple regression and correlation; multiway anova; general linear models; repeated measures and multivariate anova; loglinear analysis and logistic regression.

subject: ZOOL
title: Cellular Neurophysiology
description: Biophysical and membrane mechanisms of conduction, synaptic transmission, and other electrical responses of nerve cells.

subject: ZOOL
